analyze: This procedure provides the step-by-step operational instructions that IAM Engineering follows to implement the identification, authentication, session management, and authenticator management requirements defined in the Example Org Authentication & Credential Management Standard.

Executing this procedure ensures that only uniquely identified and authenticated users, devices, and processes gain access to Example Org systems, and that the resulting configurations and evidence are captured and retained.

This procedure is performed by IAM Engineering on all Example Org authentication infrastructure, including the [Identity Provider], [Directory Service], [MDM Solution], [PKI], and all systems that enforce logon, session, and banner controls.

It applies to privileged accounts, non-privileged accounts, non-organizational (external) users, and devices that connect to Example Org networks, and runs continuously as account, session, and authenticator events occur.
- Administrative access to the [Identity Provider], [Directory Service], [MDM Solution], [Endpoint Management Console], and [Web/Application Gateway]
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for change records and exception tracking
- Access to the [PKI] and [Certificate Authority] for public key-based authentication steps
- Access to the [Documentation Repository] for policy, plan, and evidence retention
- An approved [System Security and Privacy Plan] for each in-scope system, where the Standard requires plan-documented values
- Current CISA phishing-resistant authentication guidance and the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite
Open the [Identity Provider] administration console and navigate to the authentication/lockout policy settings.
Set the maximum consecutive invalid logon attempts to `[Assignment: organization-defined number]` within a `[Assignment: organization-defined time period]`.
Set the enforced threshold to five (5) consecutive invalid attempts within a fifteen (15) minute window for all account types.
Apply the policy to all authentication endpoints and verify enforcement with a test account by exceeding the threshold and confirming the lockout triggers.
Export the resulting configuration and file it as part of the Authentication policy configuration export.
In the [Identity Provider] lockout policy, configure the automated action taken when the maximum unsuccessful attempts are exceeded.

Select and configure at least one of: automatic lock for a minimum of thirty (30) minutes; lock until released by an administrator; delay the next logon prompt per `[Assignment: organization-defined delay algorithm]`; notify the system administrator; or `[Assignment: organization-defined action]`.
Configure administrator notification so that a lockout event generates an alert to the IAM Engineering on-call channel via the [Ticketing System].
Document the administrator release process: verify the requester's identity per the identity verification steps in this procedure, then unlock the account from the [Identity Provider] console.
Record the configured action in the Authentication policy configuration export.
Open the [MDM Solution] console and select the device compliance policy applied to `[Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices]`.
Configure the device wipe setting to purge or wipe information after ten (10) consecutive unsuccessful logon attempts.
Set the purge technique per `[Assignment: organization-defined purging or wiping requirements and techniques]` (e.g., full device wipe versus work-profile wipe).
Assign the policy to all enrolled mobile device groups and verify enforcement on a test device.
Capture the resulting policy in the Authentication policy configuration export.

In the [Identity Provider] or [Endpoint Management Console] biometric authentication settings, set the maximum consecutive unsuccessful biometric attempts to `[Assignment: organization-defined number]`.
Configure the fallback behavior on exhaustion (revert to the primary authenticator or lock per the lockout steps above).
Verify enforcement with a test enrollment and record the setting in the Authentication policy configuration export.

In the [Identity Provider], configure the post-lockout authentication path to permit `[Assignment: organization-defined authentication factors]` different from the primary factors once the consecutive invalid attempt threshold is exceeded.
Apply an independent limit of `[Assignment: organization-defined number]` consecutive invalid attempts through the alternative factors during a `[Assignment: organization-defined time period]`.
Test the full path: exceed the primary threshold, authenticate via the alternative factor, and confirm both limits are enforced independently.

Compose the banner text in the [Identity Provider] logon configuration so it states that: system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; unauthorized use is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.

Include the statements that users are accessing a U.S. Government system and accessing a system that contains U.S. Government information, consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and guidelines.
Configure the banner to display before access is granted and to remain on screen until the user acknowledges the usage conditions and takes an explicit action to log on or further access the system.

For publicly accessible systems, configure the notification to display under `[Assignment: organization-defined conditions]` before further access, include references to monitoring/recording/auditing only where consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems, and include a description of authorized uses of the system.
Confirm the displayed banner on each authentication portal, capture screenshots, and retain them with the Authentication policy configuration export.
In the [Identity Provider] session policy settings, set the concurrent session limit for each account/account type to one (1) session.

For any role requiring more than one concurrent session, confirm the requirement is expressly documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan before raising the limit for that account type.
Test with two simultaneous logins on a test account to confirm the earlier session is blocked or terminated as configured.
Retain the session configuration in the Authentication policy configuration export.
In the [Endpoint Management Console] and [MDM Solution], configure automatic device lock after fifteen (15) minutes of inactivity for both remote and internal access connections.
Configure the lock screen to conceal previously visible information with a publicly viewable image, per `[Assignment: organization-defined image]`.
Publish the user requirement — via [Ticketing System] knowledge base article and onboarding material — that users must initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended.

Verify that the device lock releases only after the user reestablishes access using the established identification and authentication procedures (username/password plus MFA), and never without re-authentication.
Document, in the workstation use procedure maintained in the [Documentation Repository], the proper functions to be performed on workstations accessing electronic protected health information.
Specify in the same document the manner in which those functions are to be performed and the physical attributes of the surroundings of each workstation or workstation class that can access ePHI.
Disseminate the procedure to all staff with ePHI-accessing workstations and obtain acknowledgment through the [Ticketing System] workflow.
Update the document when workstation classes, locations, or functions change.
In the [Identity Provider] and [Web/Application Gateway] session policies, configure automatic session termination after `[Assignment: organization-defined conditions or trigger events]` occur.
Configure electronic session termination after a predetermined time of inactivity on all systems that maintain ePHI.

Enable a user-initiated logout capability on every information resource that uses authentication to gain access; for ARC-AMPE scope, confirm the resources are defined in the applicable security and privacy plans.

Configure an explicit logout message confirming termination of the authenticated session; use the standard message documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (e.g., "Your session has been terminated").

Configure an explicit warning message indicating the session will end in `[Assignment: organization-defined time]`, and confirm that the time-until-end value is specified in the applicable security and privacy plan.
Export the session policy configuration into the Authentication policy configuration export.
In the [Directory Service] and application access controls, configure access so only persons or software programs granted access rights per § 164.308(a)(4) can reach systems maintaining ePHI.
Reconcile the access list against approved access rights before enabling access, and verify with a negative test using an account outside the authorized list.
In the [Directory Service], assign a unique name and/or number to every user for identifying and tracking identity; never reuse identifiers across users.
Uniquely identify and authenticate all organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.

Employ identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines, requiring system/network authenticators and unique user identifiers for all organizational users.
Configure the [Service Desk] workflow so that any help desk transaction with information security and privacy implications requires verified user identification before action.

For non-organizational users, uniquely identify and authenticate them or the processes acting on their behalf, using identity proofing compliant with NIST SP 800-63 at IAL-2/AAL-2 and requiring unique user identifiers (see the non-organizational user steps below).
Document, in the [Documentation Repository], the procedure for obtaining necessary ePHI during an emergency (e.g., break-glass account activation, approver chain, and post-event review).
Implement the emergency access mechanism in the [Identity Provider] and test it as `[Assignment: organization-defined test frequency]` requires.
Log each emergency activation in the [Ticketing System] and review it after the event.
Enable a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information at rest and in transit on all systems maintaining ePHI.
Verify the implementation uses the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards wherever the system contains PII.

IAM Engineering develops, documents, and disseminates the identification and authentication policy (addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance) and the supporting procedures to `[Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]`.
The designated official `[Assignment: organization-defined official]` manages the development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures.

Review and update the policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following `[Assignment: organization-defined events]`, including assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Maintain all HIPAA Security Rule policies and procedures in written (electronic) form in the [Documentation Repository], with a written record of any required action, activity, or assessment.
Retain required documentation for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
Make the documentation available in the [Documentation Repository] to all persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains.
Review the documentation periodically and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of ePHI.
In the [Identity Provider], enable an MFA enforcement policy on all privileged account roles and administrative consoles.
Select only phishing-resistant methods per current CISA guidance (e.g., FIDO2 security keys or PIV smart cards).
Enroll each privileged account holder, verify enrollment in the MFA admin console, and export the MFA enrolment report.
Confirm enforcement by attempting privileged access without the second factor and verifying denial.
In the [Identity Provider], enable MFA for all non-privileged, non-consumer account types.
For consumer accounts, where MFA is not mandated, promote voluntary enrollment and record the current enrollment rate from the MFA enrolment report.
Export the MFA enrolment report covering all non-privileged account types and retain it as process evidence.

Where shared accounts or authenticators are employed, configure the [Identity Provider] or [Privileged Access Solution] so each user is individually authenticated before access to the shared account or resource is granted.
Maintain the list of shared accounts and their authorized users in the [Documentation Repository].

For MFA to local, network, and remote access to both privileged and non-privileged accounts, configure the [Identity Provider] so one factor is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access.

Verify the separate device meets `[Assignment: organization-defined strength of mechanism requirements]`, and for ARC-AMPE scope that it implements the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography.
Record the approved separate-device authenticator types in the Authentication policy configuration export.

In the [Identity Provider] and [Web/Application Gateway], enable replay-resistant mechanisms (e.g., nonce or timestamp-based challenge/response, or protocol-level replay protection such as SAML/OIDC nonce validation) for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
Verify with a captured-traffic replay test that a replayed authentication is rejected.
Configure the [Identity Provider] to provide single sign-on for `[Assignment: organization-defined system accounts and services]`.
Register each in-scope service as a relying party and confirm session behavior matches the concurrent session and termination settings above.
Configure the [Identity Provider] to accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials, including from other federal agencies.
Validate certificates against the [PKI] trust anchor and check revocation status before granting access.
In the [Identity Provider], enable the out-of-band mechanisms `[Assignment: organization-defined out-of-band authentication]` under `[Assignment: organization-defined conditions]`.
Test the out-of-band flow end to end and record the configuration in the Authentication policy configuration export.
Implement, through the [Identity Provider] authentication flow and the [Service Desk] verification script, procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed.
Require the verification steps before initial account issuance, on any help desk transaction with security implications, and on credential re-issuance.
Uniquely identify and authenticate `[Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices]` before establishing a `[Selection: local; remote; network]` connection.

For devices requiring authentication, use at minimum shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access; confirm the approved device types are defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.

Where cryptographically based bidirectional authentication is required for `[Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices]`, configure mutual certificate-based authentication (mTLS) via the [PKI] and verify both directions during a connection test.

Where addresses are allocated dynamically, standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration per `[Assignment: organization-defined lease information and lease duration]`, and audit lease information when assigned to a device in the [DHCP/DNS Service] logs.
Handle device identification and authentication based on attestation by `[Assignment: organization-defined configuration management process]`.
Verify the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving an authenticator as part of initial distribution, using the identity verification procedures in this document.

Establish initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization, ensuring sufficient strength of mechanism for the intended use and compliance with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL/AAL/FAL level 1 for Certification Class B, level 2 for Certification Class C, and level 3 for Certification Class D.

Implement administrative procedures — documented in the [Documentation Repository] and executed via the [Ticketing System] — for initial authenticator distribution, lost/compromised/damaged authenticators, and revocation.
Change all default authenticators (including vendor-supplied passwords) prior to first use, and immediately upon system installation.

Change or refresh authenticators per `[Assignment: organization-defined time period by authenticator type]` or when `[Assignment: organization-defined events]` occur; change or refresh authenticators immediately when they are known or suspected to be compromised.
For group or role accounts, change the authenticator whenever membership in those accounts changes; add this to the joiner/mover/leaver workflow in the [Ticketing System].

Protect authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification; require individuals to take, and have devices implement, specific controls `[Assignment: organization-defined authenticator protection controls]`; and protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information their use permits access to.

Require developers and installers of system components to provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation; verify at acceptance before the component joins production.

Encrypt authentication assertions when passed through third parties such as a browser (e.g., SAML assertions encrypted using XML-Encryption, or OpenID Connect ID Tokens encrypted using JSON Web Encryption) — configure this in the [Identity Provider] federation settings.

Comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B for authenticator management; pair Organizational System/User Account passwords with MFA (strongly recommended for Organizational ACA Consumer Account passwords), and strongly recommend a policy requiring Organizational System/User Account passwords be changed or refreshed at least once every six (6) months.

In the [Identity Provider] password policy settings, enforce password composition and complexity of `[Assignment: organization-defined composition and complexity rules]`, compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B: minimum eight (8) characters for ACA Consumer Accounts and all other accounts, and minimum twelve (12) characters for Administrator/Privileged Accounts; block dictionary words, allow passphrases, configure temporary passwords to trigger an immediate change to a permanent password, and apply `[Assignment: organization-defined mobile device complexity exception]` for mobile devices per organizational risk tolerance.

Maintain the list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords in the [Password Screening Service], update it per the frequency defined in the applicable security/privacy plans (not to exceed one (1) year), and update it immediately when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly.
Configure the password change flow to verify at creation and update that new passwords do not appear on the compromised password list.
Configure all authentication endpoints to transmit passwords only over cryptographically protected channels (TLS) and disable any cleartext authentication protocols.

Store passwords using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash; verify the storage configuration in the [Directory Service] and record the algorithm in the Authentication policy configuration export.
Require immediate selection of a new password upon completion of any account recovery, enforced in the [Identity Provider] recovery workflow.
Allow user selection of long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters; set maximum length high enough to permit passphrases.

Deploy automated tools to assist users in selecting strong password authenticators (e.g., the password strength meter built into the [Identity Provider] enrollment page) and enable them on all password creation and change screens.

Enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key for all public key-based authentication (hardware-backed key storage or protected key store), and map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group in the [Identity Provider].

When PKI is used, validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status information (CRL/OCSP) via the [Certificate Authority].
Implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation, and confirm the cache refreshes per `[Assignment: organization-defined revocation cache refresh]`.

Implement `[Assignment: organization-defined security controls]` to manage the risk of compromise due to individuals having accounts on multiple systems (e.g., SSO through the [Identity Provider] and consistent MFA enforcement).
Inventory multi-account holdings per user via the [Directory Service] and apply the controls to each account.
Use only the external organizations `[Assignment: organization-defined external organizations]` to federate credentials; configure each as a trusted identity provider in the [Identity Provider].
Bind identities and authenticators dynamically using the rules `[Assignment: organization-defined binding rules]`.
Use only General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management; verify product approval before procurement in the [Ticketing System].

Require issuance of `[Assignment: organization-defined types of and/or specific authenticators]` to be conducted `[Selection: in person; by a trusted external party]` before `[Assignment: organization-defined registration authority]` with authorization by `[Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]`.

For biometric-based authentication, employ mechanisms that satisfy `[Assignment: organization-defined biometric quality requirements]`, verified at enrollment in the [Identity Provider] biometric enrollment flow.
Enable presentation attack detection mechanisms in the biometric authentication path and validate them with spoof-attempt testing before go-live.
In the [Endpoint Management Console] and [Identity Provider], prohibit the use of cached authenticators after `[Assignment: organization-defined time period]`.
Verify on a test endpoint that cached credentials expire at the configured limit and full re-authentication is required.

Establish and apply an organization-wide methodology for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms — networks, operating systems, browsers, and applications — executed through the [Endpoint Management Console].
Baseline the approved trust store content, distribute it, and audit deviations.
Employ `[Assignment: organization-defined password managers]` to generate and manage passwords, and protect the stored passwords using `[Assignment: organization-defined controls]`.
Distribute the password manager via the [Endpoint Management Console] and disable any policy requiring memorized rotation where the manager is in use.

In the [Identity Provider] logon pages and all application authentication prompts, verify that authentication feedback (typed passwords, secret answers, one-time codes) is obscured and not echoed in cleartext.
Review each authentication surface and file confirmation in the Authentication policy configuration export.
Implement mechanisms for authentication to each cryptographic module that meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines.
Verify all systems containing PII use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards, and record module modes of operation in the Authentication policy configuration export.

Uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users, or processes acting on their behalf, using identity proofing and authentication compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 at IAL-2/AAL-2, with system/network authenticators and unique user identifiers.

Accept only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant; document and maintain the list of accepted external authenticators in the [Documentation Repository], reviewing it whenever a federation partner is added or removed.

Verify each external credential is certified as compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 document suite by an approved accreditation authority and meets or exceeds those guidelines; use General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management.
Conform to `[Assignment: organization-defined identity management profiles]` for identity management, defined using NIST SP 800-63-compliant identity proofing and authentication processes.
Accept and verify federated or PKI credentials that meet `[Assignment: organization-defined policy]` before mapping them to local accounts in the [Identity Provider].
Implement `[Assignment: organization-defined measures]` to disassociate user attributes or identifier assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties.

In the [Identity Provider], configure forced re-authentication when `[Assignment: organization-defined circumstances or situations]` occur, including when authenticators, credentials, or roles change; when security categories of systems change; when execution of privileged functions occurs; and after a fixed time period of `[Assignment: organization-defined re-authentication period]`.
For ARC-AMPE scope, confirm each circumstance is defined in the applicable security and privacy plan before enabling the trigger.
Test each trigger (e.g., perform a privileged function and confirm the session requires re-authentication) and retain test results with the Authentication policy configuration export.

IAM Engineering is authorized and accountable to perform all steps in this procedure end to end, including configuration, verification, evidence capture (MFA enrolment report and Authentication policy configuration export), and handoffs to participant teams such as the [Service Desk] and [Endpoint Management] staff.

Exceptions to any step must be requested through the [Ticketing System] and are reviewed and approved by `[Assignment: organization-defined official]` in coordination with IAM Engineering before they take effect.

analyze: Executing this procedure enables Security Operations to detect, respond to, document, and report security and privacy incidents in a consistent, repeatable manner, and to maintain the policy, plan, training, and testing artifacts that sustain Example Org's incident response capability.
It produces and retains incident tickets with timelines and tabletop exercise reports as evidence of an operating capability.

This procedure is performed by Security Operations, with participation from the ISSO, Privacy Office, Legal Counsel, Human Resources, Public Relations/Communications, System Owners, and designated external partners, across all Example Org systems that process organizational or regulated data.
It governs the full incident lifecycle: preparation, detection and analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, reporting, and post-incident improvement.
- Access to the [Incident Ticketing System] with permissions to open, update, and close incident tickets.
- Access to the [SIEM] and [Security Monitoring Platform] for log review, correlation, and alerting.
- Access to the [Document Management System] where the incident response policy, plan, and procedures are published.
- Access to the [Training Platform] for assigning and recording incident response training.
- Access to [Forensic Toolkit] and secured evidence storage with write-protection capability.
- A designated Incident Response Official named in the appropriate security and privacy documents.
- Current contact information for the ISSO, Privacy Office, Legal Counsel, Human Resources, CMS, and external partners.
- The current Example Org Information Security Standard: Incident Response, Incident Handling and Breach Notification Standard and Procedures, and Privacy Incident and Breach Response Plan.
- Approval from the Business Owner for the current incident response plan.

Security Operations drafts or updates the organization-level incident response policy, ensuring it addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that it is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Security Operations drafts or updates the supporting incident response procedures that facilitate implementation of the policy and the associated incident response controls.
Security Operations submits the draft policy and procedures to the designated Incident Response Official for review.

Upon approval, Security Operations publishes the policy and procedures in the [Document Management System] and disseminates them to all organization-defined personnel or roles with incident response responsibilities.
Security Operations records the dissemination (distribution list, date, version) in the [Document Management System].
Security Operations identifies the official responsible for managing the development, documentation, and dissemination of the incident response policy and procedures.
Security Operations confirms the official(s) responsible for managing incident response for systems are named in the appropriate security and privacy documents.
Security Operations updates the naming records in the [Document Management System] whenever the designation changes.
Security Operations schedules a review of the incident response policy and procedures at least every one (1) year.

Following any assessment or audit finding, security or privacy incident, or change to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines, Security Operations initiates an out-of-cycle review of the affected policy or procedure content.
Security Operations documents the review outcome, applies updates, and re-disseminates changed documents per the dissemination step above.
Security Operations actively monitors for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect incident response policies, on a continuous basis.

At least every one (1) year, Security Operations reviews the incident response policies and procedures to confirm they remain effective and support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle.
Security Operations incorporates guidance from the Privacy Office for handling incidents involving Personally Identifiable Information (PII) into the procedures.
Security Operations records the monitoring and review outcomes in the [Document Management System].
Security Operations maintains and applies the implemented policies and procedures that address security incidents and prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.
Security Operations verifies, during each incident and each periodic procedure review, that the executed actions map to these policies and procedures.
Security Operations identifies suspected or known security incidents through monitoring and reported alerts.
Security Operations responds to each identified incident and mitigates, to the extent practicable, the harmful effects of incidents known to the organization.
Security Operations documents each security incident and its outcome in an incident ticket with timelines in the [Incident Ticketing System].
Security Operations maintains the incident response policies and procedures in written (electronic permitted) form in the [Document Management System].
Security Operations retains this documentation for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
Security Operations makes the documentation available to persons responsible for implementing the procedures.

Security Operations reviews the documentation periodically and updates it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.

Security Operations regularly reviews records of information system activity, including audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports, using the [SIEM] and [Security Monitoring Platform].
Security Operations records the review outcome and any resulting actions in the [Incident Ticketing System].
Security Operations applies the FedRAMP Incident Evaluation and Communication rules when implementing each incident response control in this procedure.
Security Operations verifies, at each control review, that evaluation and communication practices conform to the FedRAMP rules.
Security Operations assigns incident response training, consistent with the individual's assigned roles and responsibilities, through the [Training Platform].
Security Operations ensures each individual completes the training within one (1) month of assuming an incident response role or responsibility or acquiring system access.
Security Operations verifies completion in the [Training Platform] before the one (1) month deadline and escalates non-completion to the individual's manager.
Security Operations schedules refresher training through the [Training Platform] within one (1) year of the individual's prior training.
When system changes require it, Security Operations delivers additional incident response training to affected personnel.
Security Operations tracks completion status in the [Training Platform] and escalates overdue training.
Security Operations reviews and updates incident response training content every one (1) year.
Following defined events or incidents, Security Operations reviews the training content and updates it to reflect lessons learned.
Security Operations records the content review and version history in the [Training Platform].
Security Operations formally maintains and records, in the [Training Platform], the personnel participating in incident response training.
Security Operations ensures the training includes privacy education and awareness associated with sending sensitive information (e.g., confidential, proprietary, financial, or PII).
Security Operations ensures the training teaches personnel how to recognize when sensitive information such as PII is involved, so they can coordinate with the designated privacy official.
Security Operations incorporates simulated events into incident response training to facilitate the required response by personnel in crisis situations.
Security Operations conducts the simulations in the [Training Platform] or [Training Environment] and records participation.
Security Operations provides an incident response training environment using the organization-defined automated mechanism ([Training Environment]).
Security Operations verifies the environment is available to trainees and reflects current procedures before each training cycle.
Security Operations delivers training on how to identify and respond to a breach, including the organization's process for reporting a breach.

Security Operations ensures the breach reporting process taught complies with CMS' policy and plan for preparing for and responding to a breach of PII, applying the training frequency specified in AT-02.

Security Operations tests the effectiveness of the incident response capability for the system at least every one (1) year, using appropriate organization-defined tests (checklists, walk-throughs, discussion-based or tabletop exercises, simulations, or comprehensive exercises).

Security Operations may use the organization's documented response to an actual incident as part of the test; any response capabilities not exercised during the previous actual incident response must be additionally exercised or simulated as part of the test.
Security Operations documents the test results, including the tabletop exercise report, and retains it as evidence.
Security Operations tests the incident response capability using the organization-defined automated mechanisms ([Security Testing Platform]).
Security Operations records the automated test outputs with the test documentation.

Security Operations coordinates incident response testing with the organizational elements responsible for related plans, including business continuity plans, disaster recovery plans, continuity of operations plans, contingency plans, crisis communications plans, critical infrastructure plans, and occupant emergency plans.
Security Operations invites representatives of those elements to relevant tests and records their participation in the test documentation.
Security Operations determines the effectiveness of incident response processes using measures and metrics that are accurate, consistent, and in a reproducible format.
Security Operations uses the metrics to drive continuous improvement of the incident response processes and records the metrics with each test cycle.

Security Operations implements the incident handling capability consistent with the incident response plan, executing in order: preparation; detection and analysis; containment; eradication; and recovery.
Security Operations opens an incident ticket with timelines in the [Incident Ticketing System] at detection and updates it through each lifecycle phase.

Security Operations ensures the rigor, intensity, scope, and results of incident handling activities are comparable and predictable across the organization by applying the same documented handling steps to every incident.
Security Operations coordinates incident handling activities with contingency planning activities, notifying the contingency planning owners when an incident may trigger contingency actions.
Security Operations records the coordination in the incident ticket.
After each incident, Security Operations conducts a lessons-learned review of the ongoing incident handling activities.
Security Operations incorporates the lessons learned into the incident response procedures, training, and testing, and implements the resulting changes.
Security Operations records the changes and their implementation in the [Document Management System] and [Training Platform].

Security Operations documents relevant information related to security and privacy incidents in accordance with the current Example Org Incident Handling and Breach Notification Standard and Procedures, inclusive of CMS reporting requirements and timelines.
Security Operations retains the documentation as incident tickets with timelines in the [Incident Ticketing System].
Security Operations preserves evidence through technical means, including secured storage and "write" protection of evidence media.
Security Operations uses sound forensics processes and utilities ([Forensic Toolkit]) that support legal requirements.
Security Operations determines and follows a chain of custody for forensic evidence, recording each transfer of custody in the incident ticket.
Security Operations identifies the vulnerability exploited during the security and privacy incident.
Security Operations implements safeguards to reduce risk and vulnerability exploit exposure, including isolating or disconnecting affected systems.
Security Operations records the vulnerability, safeguards applied, and residual risk in the incident ticket.
Security Operations coordinates incident response activities, including forensic malware analysis, with the Information System Security Officer (ISSO).
The security operations center performs actions to reduce the risk that an information security and/or privacy incident will occur and to respond appropriately to each incident or breach.
The security operations center maintains primary responsibility for incident detection, including internal security monitoring and analysis of network traffic and logs.

Security Operations maintains contact information for individuals within the organization and CMS who have incident handling responsibilities in the system Incident Response Plan, updating it whenever contacts change.
Security Operations supports the incident handling process using the organization-defined automated mechanisms ([SIEM], [Incident Ticketing System]).
Security Operations verifies the automated mechanisms are operational before and during each incident.
Security Operations includes the organization-defined types of dynamic reconfiguration for the organization-defined system components as part of the incident response capability.
Security Operations exercises the reconfiguration actions during containment as incident conditions require and records the actions taken in the incident ticket.
Security Operations identifies the class of each incident based on attack vector (e.g., attack via external media, the web, improper system use, loss of equipment).

Security Operations takes actions in response to the incident class to ensure continuation of organizational missions and business functions, selecting from: graceful degradation; information system shutdown; fall back to manual mode or alternative technology whereby the system operates differently; employing deceptive measures; alternate information flows; or operating in a mode reserved solely for when systems are under attack.
Security Operations aligns incident response actions with business continuity processes so business continuity planners are made aware of incidents and their impacts.
Security Operations applies the written guidelines for prioritizing incidents and applying appropriate responses, and records the classification and chosen response in the incident ticket.
Security Operations correlates incident information and individual incident responses in the [SIEM] to achieve an organization-wide perspective on incident awareness and response.
Security Operations reviews correlated data during each incident to identify related activity across systems.
Security Operations implements and maintains the configurable capability to automatically disable the system if the organization-defined security violations are detected.
Security Operations defines and reviews the violation triggers in the [Security Monitoring Platform] and verifies the disablement capability functions during testing.
Security Operations implements the incident handling capability for incidents involving insider threats.
Security Operations coordinates closely with the organization's legal and human resources offices throughout the handling of each insider threat incident.
Security Operations records the coordination and legal/HR guidance in the incident ticket.
Security Operations coordinates the incident handling capability for insider threats with the organization-defined organizational entities.
Security Operations documents each entity's involvement in the incident ticket.
Security Operations coordinates with the organization-defined external organizations to correlate and share the organization-defined incident information.
Security Operations records the shared information and the cross-organization perspective gained in the incident ticket.
Security Operations employs the organization-defined dynamic response capabilities to respond to incidents as conditions evolve.
Security Operations records each dynamic response action taken in the incident ticket.
Security Operations coordinates incident handling activities involving supply chain events with the other organizations involved in the supply chain.
Security Operations documents the coordination and each party's actions in the incident ticket.
Security Operations establishes and maintains an integrated incident response team that can be deployed to any location identified by the organization within the organization-defined time period.
Security Operations verifies team roster, availability, and deployment readiness and records the verification with the team's maintenance records.
Security Operations analyzes malicious code and/or other residual artifacts remaining in the system after the incident, using [Forensic Toolkit].
Security Operations analyzes anomalous or suspected adversarial behavior in or related to the organization-defined environments or resources.
Security Operations records the analysis findings in the incident ticket.
Security Operations establishes and maintains the security operations center as the persistent monitoring and response function for the organization.
Security Operations verifies SOC staffing, tooling ([SIEM], [Security Monitoring Platform]), and coverage and records the verification.
Security Operations coordinates with Public Relations/Communications to manage public relations associated with an incident.
Security Operations supports the employment of measures to repair the reputation of the organization and records the communications actions in the incident ticket.

Security Operations tracks and documents every incident, maintaining records about each incident, its status, and other pertinent information necessary for forensics as well as evaluating incident details, trends, and handling.
Security Operations maintains these records as incident tickets with timelines in the [Incident Ticketing System] and keeps each ticket's status current until closure.
Security Operations tracks incidents and collects and analyzes incident information using the organization-defined automated mechanisms ([SIEM], [Incident Ticketing System]).
Security Operations reviews the collected incident information for trends and records the analysis.

Security Operations requires personnel to report suspected incidents to the organizational incident response capability within the timeframe established in the current Example Org Incident Handling Procedure.
Security Operations publishes the reporting channel ([Incident Reporting Channel]) to all personnel and confirms the requirement during incident response training.
Security Operations reports incident information to the organization-defined authorities.

Security Operations reports suspected incident information to CMS within the timeframe established in the Example Org Incident Handling Procedure and applicable current legally binding agreements (e.g., Computer Matching Agreement, Information Exchange Agreement, Data Usage Agreement, Business Agreement, or Interconnection Security Agreement).
Security Operations records each report, its recipient, and its timestamp in the incident ticket.
State Administering Entities report potential or confirmed security incidents within one (1) hour of discovery by completing the CMS ACA Security and Privacy Incident Response Template.
The State AE notifies the CMS IT Service Desk via email to cms_it_service_desk@cms.hhs.gov or by calling 1-800-562-1963.
CMS and State AE personnel work together for the duration of the incident, and CMS personnel notify any affected federal agencies.
Security Operations verifies the report was completed and records the notification timestamp in the incident ticket.
Security Operations reports incidents using the organization-defined automated mechanisms, including email, posting on web sites, and automated incident response tools and programs.
Security Operations confirms each automated report was delivered and records the confirmation in the incident ticket.
Security Operations reports system vulnerabilities associated with reported incidents to the organization-defined personnel or roles.
Security Operations records the vulnerability report and recipients in the incident ticket.

Security Operations provides incident information to the provider of the product or service and other organizations involved in the supply chain or supply chain governance for systems or system components related to the incident.
Security Operations records the information shared and with whom in the incident ticket.

Security Operations confirms, via contract or other arrangement, that business associates (and subcontractors) are required to report to the covered entity any security incident of which they become aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information as required by § 164.410.

Security Operations confirms the plan sponsor of a group health plan is required to report to the group health plan any security incident of which it becomes aware, in addition to implementing reasonable and appropriate administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for electronic protected health information.
Security Operations logs each business associate or plan sponsor report in the [Incident Ticketing System] and handles it through the standard incident lifecycle.

Security Operations provides an incident response support resource, integral to the organizational incident response capability, that offers advice and assistance to users of the system for the handling and reporting of incidents.

The support resource may include help desks, assistance groups, the automated [Incident Ticketing System] to open and track incident response tickets, and access to forensics services or consumer redress services when required.

For PII-related incidents, Security Operations engages the forensic, technical, policy, and legal expertise of Information Assurance Officers/Managers, Privacy Officers, Legal Counsel, and external or internal IT help desks.
Security Operations increases the availability of incident response information and support using the organization-defined automated mechanisms to the maximum extent possible.
Security Operations publishes self-service incident reporting and guidance through the [Incident Reporting Channel] and verifies its availability.
Security Operations establishes a direct, cooperative relationship between the organization's incident response capability and external providers of system protection capability.
Security Operations identifies organizational incident response team members to those external providers and updates the identification when team membership changes.

Security Operations develops the incident response plan providing a roadmap for implementing the incident response capability, describing the structure and organization of the capability, the high-level approach for how the capability fits into the overall organization, and the unique requirements of the organization relating to mission, size, structure, and functions.

Security Operations ensures the plan defines reportable incidents, provides metrics for measuring the incident response capability, defines the resources and management support needed to maintain and mature the capability, and addresses the sharing of incident information.
Security Operations ensures the plan explicitly designates responsibility for incident response to the applicable ISSO, approved by the Business Owner.
Security Operations submits the plan for review and approval by the applicable ISSO and approval by the Business Owner at least every one (1) year.

Security Operations distributes copies of the plan to incident response personnel, including all personnel with a role or responsibility for implementing the plan (such as the CISO, CIO, ISSO, Senior Privacy Official, Incident Management/Response Team, PII Breach Response Team, Operations Centers personnel, appropriate legal officials, and public relations or communications officials).
Security Operations records distribution in the [Document Management System].

Security Operations updates the plan to address system and organizational changes or problems encountered during plan implementation, execution, or testing, at a minimum every one (1) year or when incident response event(s) demonstrate a change/update is needed to improve the plan.
Security Operations communicates plan changes to all personnel with a role or responsibility for implementing the plan.
Security Operations protects the plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification using access controls in the [Document Management System].
Security Operations, with the Privacy Office, develops and implements the Privacy Incident and Breach Response Plan.
Security Operations maintains the plan in the [Document Management System] and exercises it alongside the incident response plan.

Security Operations ensures that, for breaches involving PII, the incident response plan includes a process to determine if notice to individuals or other organizations, including oversight organizations, is needed.

Security Operations ensures the plan includes an assessment process to determine the extent of the harm, embarrassment, inconvenience, or unfairness to affected individuals and mechanisms to mitigate such harms.
Security Operations ensures the plan identifies applicable privacy requirements and records the assessment outcomes in the incident ticket.

Security Operations owns this procedure end to end and performs the detection, handling, documentation, reporting, training, and testing steps on a continuous basis, coordinating with the ISSO, Privacy Office, Legal Counsel, Human Resources, Public Relations/Communications, System Owners, business associates, plan sponsors, CMS, and supply chain partners as participants in individual steps.

Exceptions to any step in this procedure require review and approval by the designated Incident Response Official and the applicable ISSO, with Business Owner approval required for incident response plan exceptions.
Example Org Information Security Standard: Incident Response
