analyze: Executing this procedure operationalizes the account management, access enforcement, identity proofing, and personnel security requirements of the Example Org Identity Lifecycle & Access Review Standard, ensuring that every identity is provisioned, monitored, reviewed, and deprovisioned under documented control.
It produces the evidence of that control — the identity provider user export, the HR active-employee roster, and access review tickets with sign-off — on a quarterly cycle.

IAM Engineering performs this procedure end to end for all user, service, privileged, temporary, and shared accounts across Example Org's identity and access infrastructure, with HR, System Owners, the Authorizing Official, and the Privacy/Security Officer participating in defined steps.
It applies to all systems that store, process, or transmit organizational data, including electronic protected health information (ePHI) and Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
- Administrative access to the [Identity Provider] and to each connected target system's account administration interface.
- Read access to the [HR System] to obtain the active-employee roster and termination/transfer notifications.
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for access request, review, and sign-off workflows.
- Access to the [SIEM] and [Logging Platform] for account action auditing and atypical usage monitoring.
- Access to the [Privileged Access Management (PAM) System] for privileged account administration.
- Contact list of designated account managers, System Owners, and the Authorizing Official.
- The current Example Org Identity Lifecycle & Access Review Standard and the organization-level access control policy it derives from.
- Approved identity proofing methods and, where applicable, connectivity to the Federal Data Services Hub (FDSH) Remote Identity Proofing (RIDP) Service.

IAM Engineering maintains the organization-level access control policy and this procedure in written (electronic) form in [Document Management System], covering purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance.
IAM Engineering disseminates the policy and procedures to all applicable personnel and roles via [Document Management System] distribution and records acknowledgment in [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering makes the documentation available to every person responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains, and retains each version and every documented action, activity, or assessment for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later. `[HIPAA 164.316(b)(1) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(ii)]`

The designated access control policy official (see Step 2) reviews and updates the policy and procedures at least every one (1) year, and additionally following assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, and changes to applicable laws (including privacy laws), Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines. `[ARC-AMPE AC-1 | NIST 800-53 AC-1]`
IAM Engineering reviews the documentation periodically and updates it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of ePHI. `[HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)]`

IAM Engineering actively monitors for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect access control policies — using [Regulatory Monitoring Source] — and confirms that organization, mission/business process, and system access control policies remain effective, updating them as required.

IAM Engineering verifies that the policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system life cycle and the life cycle of the information on the system, and documents that verification in the policy review record.

The Authorizing Official designates, in writing, an official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the access control policy and procedures, and records the designation in [Document Management System].
IAM Engineering updates the roles and contact list in this procedure whenever the designation changes.

IAM Engineering documents, in the account management section of the access control policy, the types of accounts allowed (user, service, privileged, temporary, emergency, shared/group under Section 8 conditions) and the types specifically prohibited (guest, anonymous, and shared accounts for access to PII).
IAM Engineering assigns a named account manager for each system and records the assignment in [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering documents the prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership — including job code, need-to-know, and approval requirements — in the [Identity Provider] group/role definitions.

For each account, IAM Engineering specifies in the [Identity Provider] the authorized user, group and role membership, access authorizations (privileges), and required attributes (e.g., employment status, contractor flag, individual status per Section 27).

IAM Engineering creates, enables, modifies, disables, and removes accounts only in accordance with the policy, this procedure, and the documented prerequisites and criteria, executing each action through the [Identity Provider] and logging the request in [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering monitors the use of accounts via [SIEM] dashboards and the quarterly review in Section 5.
The requesting supervisor submits an account creation request in [Ticketing System], including intended system usage and required attributes.
IAM Engineering verifies the request against the HR active-employee roster (or contractor engagement record) and the documented group/role membership criteria.
The designated approving personnel or role (the System Owner, or the Authorizing Official for shared/group accounts per Section 8) approves or rejects the request in [Ticketing System].

Upon approval, IAM Engineering provisions the account in the [Identity Provider], assigns the identifier per Section 26, and confirms the account's authorizations match the approved request before enabling it.
IAM Engineering authorizes access to the system only on the basis of a valid access authorization, intended system usage, and other required attributes recorded in the ticket.
Each quarter, IAM Engineering exports the full user account list from the [Identity Provider] (the identity provider user export) and the active-employee roster from the [HR System].

IAM Engineering reconciles the export against the roster, flagging accounts with no matching active employee or approved contractor record, expired accounts, policy-violating accounts, and accounts inactive for 60 days or more.
IAM Engineering opens an access review ticket in [Ticketing System] per system, attaching the identity provider user export and HR active-employee roster as evidence.

The assigned account managers and System Owners review each flagged account and confirm, in the ticket, whether access remains required; IAM Engineering disables or removes accounts not confirmed as required, per Section 11.
The System Owner signs off on the access review ticket in [Ticketing System]; IAM Engineering retains the signed-off tickets as the access review evidence of record.
IAM Engineering confirms the review completed within the 90-day maximum interval between reviews and records the completion date in the ticket.
HR records terminations and transfers in the [HR System]; the [HR System] integration notifies IAM Engineering and the account managers automatically.

IAM Engineering confirms that notification of accounts no longer required reaches account managers and designated personnel within twenty-four (24) hours, notification of user termination or transfer within eight (8) hours, and notification of system usage or need-to-know changes within eight (8) hours; where the automated mechanism fails, IAM Engineering sends the notification manually via [Ticketing System] within the same intervals.
IAM Engineering logs each notification and the resulting account action in [Ticketing System].
When an individual is removed from a group that uses a shared or group account, the account manager notifies IAM Engineering via [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering changes (rotates) the shared account's authenticator in the [Identity Provider] or [PAM System] and distributes the new credential only to current, authorized group members.
IAM Engineering records the rotation, the triggering removal, and the recipient list in the ticket.
Before any shared or group account is created, the requesting Business Owner documents the business need and obtains advance approval from the Authorizing Official in [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering verifies the system security plan describes how the accounts are used and includes compensating processes and procedures to uniquely attribute account user activities (e.g., session recording via [PAM System], individual check-out of credentials).

IAM Engineering permits the shared/group account only when both the approved business need and the compensating attribution controls are in place, and re-verifies both conditions during the quarterly review in Section 5.

IAM Engineering removes or disables default user accounts on all systems; where a default account must remain active, IAM Engineering renames it and documents the exception in the system security plan.

IAM Engineering implements centralized control of user access administrator functions through the [Identity Provider] and [PAM System], so that access administration is not performed through scattered, system-local accounts.

IAM Engineering regulates contractor access by provisioning contractors only through the Section 4 approval flow, defining the security requirements contractors must agree to and support, and limiting contractor access to the minimum required.

IAM Engineering prohibits the use of guest, anonymous, and shared accounts for providing access to PII, and configures role definitions so each user receives only the minimum amount of PII necessary to perform their duties.

IAM Engineering implements and maintains policies and procedures ensuring all workforce members have appropriate access to ePHI and that workforce members without access cannot obtain it, enforced through the [Identity Provider] role model.
IAM Engineering applies the authorization and supervision procedures in this document to workforce members who work with ePHI or in locations where ePHI might be accessed.

During provisioning (Section 4) and the quarterly review (Section 5), IAM Engineering determines that each workforce member's access to ePHI is appropriate for their assigned duties, recording the determination in the access review ticket.

IAM Engineering documents, reviews, and modifies each user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process in the [Identity Provider], based on the organization's access authorization policies; granting of ePHI access occurs only through these documented mechanisms.

If Example Org operates a health care clearinghouse as part of a larger organization, IAM Engineering implements policies and procedures — enforced as firewall/segmentation rules and separate identity boundaries — that protect the clearinghouse's ePHI from unauthorized access by the larger organization.

IAM Engineering configures the [Identity Provider] to disable non-consumer accounts within twenty-four (24) hours when the accounts have expired, are no longer associated with a user or individual, are in violation of organizational policy, or have been inactive for sixty (60) days.

IAM Engineering runs a daily reconciliation between the [Identity Provider] and the [HR System] to detect accounts no longer associated with an active individual and triggers disablement within the 24-hour window.
IAM Engineering verifies disablement executed and records the action in [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering provisions temporary and emergency accounts only through [Ticketing System] with an expiration date recorded at creation.
IAM Engineering configures the [Identity Provider] to automatically disable temporary and emergency accounts after no more than ninety-six (96) hours from last use.
IAM Engineering verifies the automatic disablement fired for each such account and documents the verification in the ticket.

IAM Engineering configures the [Identity Provider], [PAM System], and target systems to automatically audit account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions, forwarding events to the [SIEM].
IAM Engineering reviews the [SIEM] account-action reports as part of the quarterly review in Section 5 and investigates any account action without a corresponding approved ticket.

IAM Engineering includes, in the organizational user security policy distributed per Section 1, the requirement that users log out when the time period of inactivity will exceed twenty-four (24) hours; this is a user responsibility, not an automated control.
IAM Engineering confirms the logout requirement is present in the current published user policy during the annual policy review in Section 1.
IAM Engineering establishes and administers privileged user accounts in the [PAM System] according to a role-based access scheme tied to documented job responsibilities.

IAM Engineering monitors privileged role and attribute assignments and all changes to roles or attributes via [SIEM] alerts, and revokes access when a privileged role or attribute assignment is no longer appropriate.
IAM Engineering establishes application-specific privileged user accounts under a role-based scheme based on user responsibilities associated with application use.

IAM Engineering inspects administrator groups, root accounts, and other system-related accounts on demand and at least once every fourteen (14) days to ensure unauthorized accounts have not been created, and inspects application-specific privileged user roles at least once every thirty (30) days, recording each inspection in [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering configures [SIEM] rules to detect atypical account usage, such as access at times of day or from locations inconsistent with normal usage patterns.

IAM Engineering reports detected atypical usage to the designated personnel or roles (account managers and System Owners) and, where the usage may indicate an incident, to the incident response team via [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering documents the disposition of each atypical usage report in the ticket.

Upon notification from HR, the Security Officer, or management that an individual poses a significant risk, IAM Engineering disables that individual's accounts in the [Identity Provider] within one (1) hour of discovery.
IAM Engineering confirms disablement across all connected systems and records the discovery time, disablement time, and notifying party in [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering enforces approved authorizations for logical access using the technical access control policies of the [Identity Provider] and each target system, allowing access only to persons or software programs that have been granted access rights.
Where encryption is used as an access control mechanism, IAM Engineering verifies it meets the approved and latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards before deployment.
IAM Engineering configures operating system controls to disable public "read" and "write" access to all system-related files, objects, and directories that contain sensitive information.
IAM Engineering protects data stored in the information system with system access controls and encrypts data residing in non-secure areas.

When contracting with external service providers, IAM Engineering isolates PII — and the software and services that receive, process, store, or transmit PII — within the service provider environment to the maximum extent possible, so that other service provider customers sharing physical or virtual space cannot gain access to that data or those applications.

IAM Engineering configures the [Identity Provider] attribute-sync rules so that changes to security attributes of subjects and objects (e.g., job code, clearance, department) automatically trigger revocation of the affected access authorizations.
IAM Engineering defines the timing rules governing revocations in the attribute-sync configuration and verifies revocations executed after each attribute change during the quarterly review.

Before releasing information outside the system, IAM Engineering verifies the receiving external organization provides information security and privacy safeguards commensurate with those implemented by Example Org, documented in an approved agreement.

IAM Engineering applies the organization-defined controls to validate the appropriateness of the information designated for release, and records the validation in [Ticketing System] prior to execution of the release.

IAM Engineering implements, in consultation with the senior privacy official and legal counsel, the mechanisms enabling individuals to access their PII/PHI elements defined in applicable security/privacy plans: individual authentication and identification, accounting of disclosures, notice of privacy practices, request forms and application interfaces.

IAM Engineering delivers the accessed PII/PHI in a readable form and format, consistent with published policies, procedures, and applicable federal and state privacy requirements for processing access requests.
IAM Engineering logs each access request and its fulfillment in [Ticketing System] as part of the accounting of disclosures.

IAM Engineering documents, for each specific workstation or class of workstations that can access ePHI, the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings.

IAM Engineering enforces the documented workstation access designations through the [Identity Provider] (network and application access) and physical access controls, and reviews the documentation during the annual policy review in Section 1.
IAM Engineering identifies and documents the duties of individuals requiring separation and defines system access authorizations in the [Identity Provider] to support that separation.

IAM Engineering divides critical mission functions and information system support functions among separate individuals or groups, including separating information system testing functions (user acceptance, quality assurance, information security) from production functions.

IAM Engineering ensures an independent entity — not the Business Owner, ISSO, System Developer(s)/Maintainer(s), or System Administrator(s) responsible for the system — conducts information security testing.

IAM Engineering ensures audit functions are not performed by the security personnel responsible for administering access control, and verifies these separations in role assignments during the quarterly review in Section 5.

IAM Engineering configures all roles in the [Identity Provider] to allow only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.

IAM Engineering disables all file system access not explicitly required for system, application, and administrator functionality, ensuring only authorized users can access files, directories, drives, workstations, servers, network shares, ports, protocols, and services expressly required for the performance of job duties.

IAM Engineering provides contractors with minimal system and physical access, requires them to agree to and support organizational security requirements, and participates in assessing contractors' ability to adhere to and support the organization's security policy during the contractor selection process.

IAM Engineering restricts the use of database management utilities to authorized database administrators, prevents users from accessing database data files at the logical data view, field, or field-value level, and implements table-level access control.

IAM Engineering disables all system and removable media boot access unless explicitly authorized by the Authorizing Official for compelling operational needs; where authorized, IAM Engineering ensures boot access is password protected.

The System Owner explicitly authorizes, in [Ticketing System], access for organization-defined individuals or roles to security functions (deployed in hardware, software, and firmware) and to security-relevant information — including setting/modifying audit logs and auditing behavior, boundary protection system rules, access authorizations, authentication parameters, and system configurations and parameters — for security administrators, system and network administrators, system security officers, system maintenance personnel, system programmers, and other privileged users.
IAM Engineering restricts privileged accounts on the system to the organization-defined personnel or roles so authorized, enforced via [PAM System] group membership.

IAM Engineering requires users of system accounts (or roles) with access to security functions or security-relevant information to use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions; where use of a privileged account for such functions is unavoidable and feasible, IAM Engineering ensures the use is audited.

IAM Engineering reviews the privileges assigned to all users with privileges no less often than every ninety (90) days to validate the need for such privileges, and reassigns or removes privileges as necessary to correctly reflect organizational mission and business needs, recording the review and sign-off in the access review ticket.

IAM Engineering configures operating system and application controls to prevent software from executing at higher privilege levels than the users executing the software, except software explicitly documented as an exception in the system security plan.
IAM Engineering configures the [PAM System] and target systems to log the execution of privileged functions, forwarding logs to the [SIEM].
IAM Engineering configures role-based controls to prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions, and verifies the configuration during the quarterly privilege review in Section 25.

IAM Engineering receives authorization from the designated personnel or roles before assigning an individual, group, role, service, or device identifier, selecting an identifier that identifies the intended party and assigning a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.

IAM Engineering prevents reuse of identifiers for two (2) years, ensuring previous identifier-based access authorizations (e.g., access to sensitive files or folders) are removed from the system before the identifier is reused.

IAM Engineering uniquely identifies each individual using organization-defined characteristics identifying individual status — including contractors and foreign nationals — recorded as attributes in the [Identity Provider].
IAM Engineering verifies identifier uniqueness and the 2-year non-reuse rule during the quarterly review in Section 5.
IAM Engineering implements procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to ePHI is the one claimed, executed as part of every account registration.

IAM Engineering identity proofs users who require accounts for logical access to systems based on the appropriate identity assurance level in applicable standards and guidelines, resolves user identities to a unique individual, and collects, validates, and verifies identity evidence.

IAM Engineering identity proofs all users requiring logical access accounts — including non-privileged (consumer) accounts — to Identity Assurance Level 2 (IAL-2) or higher per the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines suite; for ACA Consumer Accounts, IAM Engineering may use the Federal Data Services Hub (FDSH) Remote Identity Proofing (RIDP) Service in lieu of otherwise meeting IAL-2.

IAM Engineering requires that the registration process for any account — including non-privileged (consumer) accounts — includes supervisor or sponsor authorization, captured in [Ticketing System] before provisioning.

IAM Engineering requires that evidence of individual identification be presented to the registration authority for all accounts, and validates and verifies that evidence through organization-approved methods of validation and verification that comply with applicable agreements with CMS.
IAM Engineering retains the identity proofing evidence and verification record with the account registration ticket.

Upon notification of employment termination from the [HR System], IAM Engineering disables the terminated individual's system access in the [Identity Provider] within the same day as termination; for individuals terminated for cause, IAM Engineering executes termination actions immediately and, in certain situations, disables the system accounts before notifying the individuals of the termination actions.
IAM Engineering terminates or revokes all authenticators and credentials associated with the terminated individual, including tokens in [PAM System] and certificates in [Certificate Authority].

IAM Engineering implements these procedures for terminating access to ePHI when the employment of, or other arrangement with, a workforce member ends, or as required by determinations made under the workforce clearance procedure.

HR conducts an exit interview that includes a discussion of information security topics, addressing non-disclosure of information security and privacy information; IAM Engineering confirms the interview occurred via [Ticketing System].

HR retrieves all security-related organizational system-related property from the terminated individual — hardware authentication tokens, system administration technical manuals, keys, identification cards, and building passes

analyze: Executing this procedure ensures that identities, accounts, and access rights across Example Org systems are established, reviewed, modified, and terminated in a controlled, documented, and auditable manner, so that only authorized individuals retain access to organizational systems and electronic PHI.

This procedure is performed by IAM Engineering, with participation from HR, supervisors/sponsors, system and application owners, and the [Authorizing Official], across all Example Org identity provider accounts, application accounts, privileged accounts, and workstations that create, store, transmit, or access organizational data, including electronic PHI.
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for logging account and access review actions
- Current HR active-employee roster export from [HR System]
- Approved Access Control Policy and the Identity Lifecycle & Access Review Standard on file
- Current [Authorizing Official] designation for approvals requiring AO sign-off
- [Account Approval Authority] roster identifying who may approve account creation, modification, and privileged access requests
- Access to system security plans (SSPs) for in-scope systems
- Access to [Privileged Access Management Tool] or equivalent privileged-account inventory, if deployed
- [Data Loss Prevention/Release Control Tool] access, where information release review is required

IAM Engineering drafts or updates the Access Control Policy, addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and standards.
The designated [Access Control Policy Owner] reviews and approves the policy and associated procedures.
IAM Engineering disseminates the approved policy and procedures to all personnel and roles identified in the Standard via the [Identity Provider] or [Document Management System].

IAM Engineering reviews and updates the policy and procedures at least every 1 year, and additionally following an assessment/audit finding, a security or privacy incident, or a change in applicable law, regulation, or policy.
IAM Engineering logs each review and its outcome in the [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering maintains documented procedures for authorization and supervision of workforce members who work with electronic PHI.
Before granting access, the supervisor or [Account Approval Authority] completes a workforce clearance check to determine the appropriateness of the requested access for the individual's role.
IAM Engineering records the clearance decision and the granted access in the [Ticketing System].
Upon notice from HR that employment or the workforce arrangement has ended, IAM Engineering executes the termination procedure defined in Step 40 (PS-4) to remove access.
IAM Engineering documents access authorization procedures for granting access to workstations, transactions, programs, and processes involving electronic PHI.
IAM Engineering establishes each user's initial right of access based on the documented authorization policy, recording the decision in the [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering reviews and, as needed, modifies each user's right of access at the quarterly access review (see Step 10) or upon a triggering event (transfer, termination, role change).

If Example Org operates a health care clearinghouse component within a larger organization, IAM Engineering implements and documents policies and procedures that segregate the clearinghouse's electronic PHI from unauthorized access by the larger organization.
IAM Engineering configures each in-scope system to permit access only to persons or software programs that have been granted access rights in the [Identity Provider].
IAM Engineering assigns a unique name and/or number to each user at account creation to identify and track that user's identity across all systems.

IAM Engineering establishes emergency access procedures for each system holding electronic PHI and documents the activation steps in the system security plan; these are implemented when an emergency access event occurs.
System/application owners configure automatic logoff after a predetermined period of inactivity, as specified in the system security plan.
System/application owners implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic PHI at rest and in transit, consistent with the system security plan.
IAM Engineering configures each in-scope system to require authentication of any person or entity requesting access to electronic PHI before granting that access.
IAM Engineering verifies, at account provisioning and at each quarterly review, that authentication mechanisms in place correctly bind the credential to the claimed identity.

IAM Engineering maintains all access-related policies, procedures, and records of required actions, activities, and assessments in written (which may be electronic) form in the [Document Management System].
IAM Engineering retains this documentation for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
IAM Engineering makes the documentation available to all personnel responsible for implementing the procedures it describes.
IAM Engineering reviews and updates the documentation in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic PHI, in addition to the quarterly review cycle.
IAM Engineering, together with the system/application owner, documents the proper functions permitted on each workstation or workstation class that can access electronic PHI.
IAM Engineering documents the manner in which those functions must be performed and the physical attributes required of the workstation's surroundings.
IAM Engineering disseminates the workstation use policy to affected personnel and records acknowledgment in the [Ticketing System] or [Learning Management System].
IAM Engineering defines and documents the account types allowed and specifically prohibited on each in-scope system in the system security plan.
IAM Engineering assigns an account manager for each system.
IAM Engineering documents prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership for each system.
For each account, IAM Engineering records the authorized user, group/role membership, and access authorization in the [Identity Provider].
The [Account Approval Authority] approves each account creation request before IAM Engineering provisions the account.
IAM Engineering creates, enables, modifies, disables, and removes accounts according to the documented policy and criteria, and monitors account use on an ongoing basis.
IAM Engineering authorizes access only where a valid access authorization, intended system usage, and any other required attribute are documented and approved.
IAM Engineering aligns all account management actions with the personnel termination procedure (Step 40) and transfer procedure (Step 41).
When an account is no longer required, the requesting manager or system owner notifies the account manager and [Account Approval Authority] within 24 hours.
When HR notifies IAM Engineering of a user termination or transfer, IAM Engineering notifies the account manager and [Account Approval Authority] within 8 hours.
When a user's system usage or need-to-know changes, the requesting manager notifies IAM Engineering and the account manager within 8 hours.
IAM Engineering logs each notification and the resulting account action in the [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering reviews all accounts on all systems quarterly (at least every 90 days) for compliance with account management requirements, using the identity provider user export and the HR active-employee roster as source data.
IAM Engineering reconciles the identity provider user export against the HR active-employee roster to identify accounts belonging to individuals no longer employed.
IAM Engineering opens an access review ticket in the [Ticketing System] for each discrepancy and obtains sign-off from the account owner or manager before closing it.

Where shared or group accounts are deployed, IAM Engineering changes the shared authenticator whenever an individual is removed from the associated group, and records the rotation in the [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering configures the [Identity Provider] to support automated creation, modification, disabling, and removal of system accounts.
IAM Engineering verifies quarterly, during the account review (Step 10), that automated account management mechanisms are functioning as configured.
IAM Engineering configures temporary and emergency accounts in the [Identity Provider] with an automatic expiration or disablement trigger of no more than 96 hours from last use.
IAM Engineering verifies expiration of each temporary/emergency account and logs the disablement event in the [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering configures the [Identity Provider] to disable non-consumer accounts within 24 hours of expiration, loss of association with a user, or a detected violation of organizational policy.
IAM Engineering configures the [Identity Provider] to disable accounts that have been inactive for 60 days.
IAM Engineering reviews disablement events during the quarterly account review (Step 10) and confirms each disabled account is logged in the [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering enables audit logging in the [Identity Provider] for all account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions.
IAM Engineering verifies quarterly that the audit log is capturing these events and retains the log per the retention schedule in Step 6.
IAM Engineering documents, as a user-policy requirement, that users must log out of any session exceeding 24 hours of expected inactivity.
IAM Engineering disseminates this requirement through the Access Control Policy and confirms user acknowledgment via the [Learning Management System] or [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering establishes and administers privileged user accounts, including application-specific privileged accounts, using a role-based access scheme documented in the [Identity Provider] or [Privileged Access Management Tool].
IAM Engineering monitors privileged role assignments and any changes to roles or attributes on an ongoing basis.
IAM Engineering inspects administrator groups, root accounts, and other system-related privileged accounts on demand and at least every 14 days.
IAM Engineering inspects application-related privileged roles at least every 30 days.
IAM Engineering revokes privileged access immediately when the role or attribute assignment is no longer appropriate, and logs the revocation in the [Ticketing System].
Before provisioning a shared or group account, the requesting owner submits a documented business need to the [Authorizing Official] for advance approval.
IAM Engineering does not provision the shared/group account until AO approval is recorded in the [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering documents, in the system security plan, the account's use and the compensating processes (e.g., check-out logging, session recording) that provide unique attribution of individual user activity within the shared account.
IAM Engineering monitors system accounts for atypical usage patterns using the [Identity Provider] or [SIEM Tool].
IAM Engineering reports detected atypical usage to [Designated Security Personnel] and, where necessary, to the applicable incident response team.
IAM Engineering logs the report and any resulting action in the [Ticketing System].
Upon discovery or notification that an individual poses a significant risk, IAM Engineering disables that individual's account(s) in the [Identity Provider] within 1 hour of discovery.
IAM Engineering logs the disablement, the reporting party, and the justification in the [Ticketing System].
IAM Engineering configures each in-scope system to enforce approved access authorizations for logical access to information and system resources, consistent with the Access Control Policy.
IAM Engineering verifies enforcement configuration during the quarterly account review (Step 10).
When a subject's or object's security attribute changes, IAM Engineering revokes the resulting invalid access authorization according to the timing rules documented in the Access Control Policy.
IAM Engineering records the revocation event and its timing in the [Ticketing System].

Before releasing information outside the system, IAM Engineering or the data owner confirms that the receiving system, component, or external organization provides information security and privacy safeguards commensurate with those Example Org implements.
IAM Engineering or the data owner validates the appropriateness of the specific information designated for release using [Data Loss Prevention/Release Control Tool] or documented manual review.
IAM Engineering logs the release authorization in the [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering provides a documented mechanism (e.g., a request process through [Ticketing System] or a self-service portal) enabling individuals to access the PII/PHI elements about themselves defined in the applicable system security or privacy plan.
IAM Engineering verifies the requester's identity per Step 5 before releasing the requested elements.
IAM Engineering identifies and documents duties requiring separation in a [Separation-of-Duties Matrix].
IAM Engineering defines system access authorizations for each role so that no individual can independently execute both halves of a separated duty.
IAM Engineering verifies separation-of-duties compliance during the quarterly account review (Step 10).
IAM Engineering provisions each account with only the access necessary to accomplish the individual's assigned organizational tasks.
IAM Engineering reviews and adjusts access grants that exceed least-privilege requirements as part of the quarterly account review (Step 10).

IAM Engineering restricts access to security functions (hardware, software, firmware) and security-relevant information — including setting/modifying audit logs and auditing behavior, boundary protection rules, access authorizations, authentication parameters, and system configurations/parameters — to explicitly authorized personnel.
The [Account Approval Authority] approves each request for this access before IAM Engineering provisions it.
IAM Engineering issues each user with security-function access a separate non-privileged account for use when performing nonsecurity functions.
IAM Engineering verifies during privileged account review (Step 16) that users are using the non-privileged account for nonsecurity tasks.
IAM Engineering restricts assignment of privileged accounts on each system to the personnel or roles designated in the system security plan.
IAM Engineering confirms this restriction during the privileged account inspection cycle (Step 16).
IAM Engineering reviews the privileges assigned to all users with privileges at least every 90 days to validate continued need.
IAM Engineering reassigns or removes privileges that no longer reflect organizational mission or business need, and records each change in the [Ticketing System] as a signed-off access review ticket.

System/application owners configure each system so that software does not execute at a higher privilege level than the user executing it, except where explicitly documented in the system security plan.
IAM Engineering reviews documented exceptions during the quarterly account review (Step 10).
IAM Engineering enables logging of privileged function execution in the [Identity Provider] or [SIEM Tool] for all in-scope systems.
IAM Engineering retains these logs per the retention schedule in Step 6.
System/application owners configure technical controls in each system to block non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.
IAM Engineering tests this restriction as part of the quarterly account review (Step 10).

IAM Engineering, with system/application owners, identifies the user actions that may be performed without identification or authentication, consistent with mission and business functions, and records them in an [Unauthenticated Actions List].
IAM Engineering documents the supporting rationale for each such action in the applicable system security plan.
IAM Engineering obtains authorization from the [Account Approval Authority] before assigning an identifier to an individual, group, role, service, or device.
IAM Engineering selects an identifier that correctly identifies the individual, group, role, service, or device, and assigns it in the [Identity Provider].
IAM Engineering prevents reuse of an identifier for 2 years, removing any previous identifier-based access authorizations before the identifier may be reused.

At registration, IAM Engineering records the individual status characteristics defined in the applicable system security or privacy plan (e.g., contractor, foreign national, non-organizational user) against the identifier in the [Identity Provider].
IAM Engineering uses this characteristic tag when applying access rules that depend on individual status.

Before issuing any account — privileged, non-privileged, or consumer — IAM Engineering identity-proofs the requesting user to Identity Assurance Level 2 (IAL-2) or higher per NIST SP 800-63, or, for ACA Consumer Accounts, via the Federal Data Services Hub Remote Identity Proofing Service.
IAM Engineering resolves the user's identity to a unique individual before account creation.
IAM Engineering records the proofing outcome in the [Ticketing System] prior to account provisioning.
For every account request, including non-privileged/consumer accounts, IAM Engineering requires supervisor or sponsor authorization before beginning registration.
IAM Engineering records the sponsor's authorization in the [Ticketing System] before provisioning the account.
For every account request, including non-privileged/consumer accounts, IAM Engineering requires the individual to present evidence of identification to the registration authority.
IAM Engineering records the type of evidence presented in the [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering validates and verifies presented identity evidence using organization-approved, CMS-agreement-compliant validation and verification methods, applying this requirement to all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts.
IAM Engineering records the validation/verification outcome in the [Ticketing System] before completing registration.
HR notifies IAM Engineering of an individual's termination as soon as the action is confirmed.
IAM Engineering disables the individual's system access in the [Identity Provider] the same day as termination.
IAM Engineering terminates or revokes all authenticators and credentials associated with the individual.
The individual's supervisor or HR conducts an exit interview covering the organization-defined information security topics, including non-disclosure of information security and privacy information.
IAM Engineering or Facilities retrieves all security-related organizational system-related property from the individual.

IAM Engineering retains organizational access to information and systems formerly controlled by the terminated individual and logs completion of all steps in a signed-off access review ticket in the [Ticketing System].
HR notifies IAM Engineering of an individual's reassignment or transfer as soon as the action is confirmed.
The individual's new and former supervisors, with IAM Engineering, review and confirm the ongoing operational need for the individual's current logical and physical access authorizations.
IAM Engineering removes or disables all system accesses no longer required within 24 hours of the formal transfer action.
IAM Engineering modifies remaining access authorizations to correspond to the individual's new operational need.

IAM Engineering notifies the account manager and [Account Approval Authority] of the completed transfer action within 24 hours, and logs the action as a signed-off access review ticket in the [Ticketing System].

IAM Engineering owns this procedure end to end and is the only team authorized to create, modify, disable, or remove accounts and to execute the review, termination, and transfer actions described above.

The [Authorizing Official] and [Account Approval Authority] review and approve exceptions, shared-account requests, and privileged-access decisions; HR and individual supervisors initiate and confirm termination and transfer triggers but do not themselves modify system access.

analyze: This procedure provides the step-by-step operational instructions Platform Engineering follows to maintain Example Org's configuration baselines, control changes to production and non-production systems, and keep the governing configuration management policy and procedures current.
Executing it produces the evidence artifacts this process is accountable for: change tickets with approvals, and the baseline configuration and drift report.

Platform Engineering performs this procedure continuously across all Example Org systems, devices, appliances, and applications, including development and test environments and systems issued for high-risk travel.
Other teams (Security, Privacy, and system owners) participate in reviews and approvals, but Platform Engineering owns the process and its handoffs end to end.
- Access to the [Change Management System] with permissions to raise, review, and approve change tickets.
- Access to the [Configuration Management Software] and the [Hardware/Software Asset Management System] used to maintain and compare baseline configurations.
- Membership roster for the [Configuration Change Control Board], including the designated security and privacy representatives.
- A named official designated to manage the configuration management policy and procedures, recorded in the appropriate security and privacy documents.
- An established [status page or electronic bulletin board] approved and accepted by the system owner for communicating significant changes to CMS and business partners.
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for logging drift findings and emergency changes.
- Current copies of the *Example Org Information Security Standard: Change & Configuration Management* and the configuration management policy.

Confirm the configuration management policy addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that it is maintained at the organization level as a single, authoritative document.

Verify that the procedures facilitating implementation of the policy (this document) are documented, current, and disseminated to all personnel and roles with configuration or change responsibilities.
Make the documentation available to every person responsible for implementing it.

Confirm the designated official responsible for developing, documenting, and disseminating the policy and procedures is named in the appropriate security and privacy documents; if the designation has changed, update the security and privacy documents.

Review and update the configuration management policy and procedures at least every one (1) year, and additionally whenever any of the following trigger events occurs: assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; or changes to applicable laws (including privacy laws), executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines.

Actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws and regulations that affect configuration management policies; when a change is identified, open a review ticket in the [Ticketing System] and update the policy before the next scheduled review if needed.
Apply FedRAMP Significant Change Notification rules whenever configuration management policy or procedures change in a way that constitutes a significant change to the system or its environment.

Confirm the policy and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards throughout the system life cycle and for the information on the system; document any gaps and remediate them via the change control process below.

Store the policy, these procedures, and all records of actions, activities, and assessments required by the HIPAA Security Rule in written (electronic) form, and retain them for 6 years from the date of creation or the date last in effect, whichever is later.
Review this documentation periodically and update it in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.

Document and maintain a current baseline configuration for every system, device, appliance, and application, including security update posture, under configuration control in the [Configuration Management Software].

Review and update the baseline configuration at least every one (1) year, when major system changes or upgrades occur, when critical security patches are applied, when emergency changes occur (e.g., unscheduled changes, system crashes, replacement of critical hardware components), and whenever system components are installed or upgraded.

Configure the [automated mechanisms] (e.g., the [Hardware/Software Asset Management System], [Software Asset Management System], and [Configuration Management Software]) so they capture everything needed to verify the baseline, including access controls that give the automation the information it requires, and run them as part of the Continuous Monitoring Program to maintain the currency, completeness, accuracy, and availability of the baseline.
Produce and retain the baseline configuration and drift report from the automated comparison as evidence of baseline currency.

Retain at least one (1) previous version of each baseline configuration — the most recent older generation — to support emergency rollback; retain additional previous versions based on risk tolerance.

Maintain a baseline configuration for development and test environments that is managed separately from the operational baseline configuration, with development and testing performed in environments separate from operational systems to minimize risk to production.

Before an individual travels to a location deemed to be of significant risk, issue them a system or system component configured to a stringent baseline (e.g., latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption).

When the individual returns, apply return safeguards: perform a detailed inspection for physical tampering, then purge or reimage the hard disk drive and removable media before reconnecting the system.

Document the types of changes to the system that are configuration-controlled (e.g., changes to baseline settings, security configurations, critical components) and record this determination alongside the baseline documentation.

Route every proposed configuration-controlled change through a change request form in the [Change Management System], including an explicit security and privacy impact analysis for the Board to consider.

Convene the [Configuration Change Control Board] sufficiently frequently to accommodate proposed change requests, and coordinate change control activities with the requirements of other appropriate organization officials whenever those activities occur.

Require security and privacy representatives (which may include the [Information System Security Officer], [Chief Information Security Officer], and/or the [Senior Official for Privacy]) as members of the Board reviewing each request.
Document the Board's approval or disapproval decision on the change ticket in the [Change Management System]; retain the change ticket with its approvals as evidence.

Use the [Change Management System]'s automated mechanisms to document proposed changes, notify approval authorities and request approval, highlight proposed changes not approved or disapproved within [Approval Response Window], prohibit implementation of changes until designated approvals are received, document all changes, and notify designated personnel when approved changes are completed.
Retain records of configuration-controlled changes for no less than one (1) year after the change.
Test, validate, and document each approved change in the separate test environment before finalizing its implementation.
Implement the approved change in production only after testing is documented on the change ticket.

Update the current system baseline to reflect the change and deploy the updated baseline across the installed base using the [automated deployment mechanisms], then regenerate the baseline configuration and drift report.
Monitor and review activities associated with configuration-controlled changes — approvals, implementation steps, and outcomes — via the change ticket record and the Continuous Monitoring Program.

Review changes to the system [Change Review Frequency] to determine whether unauthorized changes have occurred, and additionally whenever drift is reported by the automated monitoring mechanisms; log any unauthorized change in the [Ticketing System] as a security incident.

Configure the [Detection & Response tooling] to implement the defined security responses automatically if baseline configurations are changed in an unauthorized manner (e.g., alerting, reverting the configuration, disabling the change source).

Verify that all cryptographic mechanisms used to provide the defined controls (e.g., encryption modules, key management configurations) are tracked under configuration management and changed only via the change control process.

Establish and maintain an approved means of communication — such as an electronic bulletin board or web status page, accepted by the system owner — for notifying the business owner and associated service consumers of significant changes to or developments in the information system or environment of operations that may affect business agreements or contracts with CMS and business partners.

When a significant change meeting this threshold is approved, post the notification to the [status page or electronic bulletin board] and follow CMS change reporting procedures, utilizing the CMS change notification form for the specific entity type.
Platform Engineering is authorized and accountable to execute all steps above end to end, including baseline maintenance, change ticket handling, drift review, and evidence retention.

Approvals and disapprovals of configuration-controlled changes rest with the [Configuration Change Control Board], which must include the designated security and privacy representatives; exceptions to any step in this procedure require Board approval and documented rationale on the change ticket.

analyze: This procedure provides the step-by-step operational instructions for implementing the physical and environmental protection requirements defined in the Physical & Environmental Security Standard, covering facility access control, physical monitoring, environmental and power protection, and equipment/media control.
Executing this procedure produces the evidence artifacts — the Badge access review and Data centre environmental monitoring records — that demonstrate compliance with the Standard.

This procedure is performed by Facilities / Physical Security, with participation from Information Security, HR, the Privacy Office, and the incident response capability, across all facilities that house electronic information systems, including data centres, wiring closets, and designated alternate work sites.
It applies to all personnel, visitors, contractors, and maintenance staff who request or hold physical access to those facilities.
- Access to the [Badge Access Control System] with administrative rights for Facilities / Physical Security personnel
- Access to the [Visitor Management System] and [Video Surveillance System]
- Access to the [Environmental Monitoring System] covering the data centre
- Access to the [Physical Access Audit Log System] and [Ticketing System]
- The current System Security and Privacy Policy naming the designated official for physical and environmental protection policy (per [NIST PE-1 | ARC PE-1 AE Mandatory])
- The current Physical & Environmental Security Standard and the organization's physical and environmental protection policy
- The organization-defined list of acceptable forms of identification for visitor access `[Assignment: Acceptable Forms of Identification]`
- Contact roster for organization-defined notification personnel, emergency responders, and the incident response capability
- Current vendor documentation for power, emergency lighting, fire protection, and water damage protection equipment, plus applicable local, state, and federal testing requirements

Facilities / Physical Security develops and documents the organization-level physical and environmental protection policy addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, ensuring consistency with applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Facilities / Physical Security documents these implementing procedures to facilitate execution of the policy and its associated controls, and disseminates both to all applicable personnel and roles.

Facilities / Physical Security confirms the designated official responsible for the development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures is named in the System Security and Privacy Policy; if not, submit a change to the [Ticketing System] to have the official documented.

Facilities / Physical Security reviews and updates the policy and procedures at least every one (1) year, and additionally following assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, and changes to applicable laws, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines.

Facilities / Physical Security actively monitors for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy affecting physical and environmental protection, and reviews at least annually to confirm the policies and procedures remain effective.

Facilities / Physical Security validates, during each review, that the policy and associated controls support privacy throughout the system life cycle and limit unnecessary or inappropriate access to Personally Identifiable Information (PII).

Facilities / Physical Security maintains all policies, procedures, and required documented actions, activities, and assessments in written (electronic or paper) form in the [Documentation Repository].
Facilities / Physical Security retains all required documentation for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
Facilities / Physical Security makes current documentation available to every person responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains, via the [Documentation Repository].

Facilities / Physical Security reviews documentation periodically and updates it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
Facilities / Physical Security develops, obtains approval for, and maintains the list of individuals with authorized access to the facility where the system resides.

Facilities / Physical Security issues authorization credentials (badges) through the [Badge Access Control System] only to individuals on the approved access list, and authorizes access based on the individual's position or role.

Facilities / Physical Security conducts the Badge access review quarterly (this satisfies the requirement to review the access list at least every six [6] months), reconciling the active badge list in the [Badge Access Control System] against the approved access list and current HR role assignments.

When access is no longer required (transfer, termination, or role change), Facilities / Physical Security removes the individual from the facility access list and deactivates the credential in the [Badge Access Control System], retaining the Badge access review evidence.

At visitor reception, verify two forms of identification from the organization-defined list of acceptable forms of identification `[Assignment: Acceptable Forms of Identification]` before granting visitor access.

Restrict unescorted access to the facility to personnel holding security clearances, formal access authorizations, a need for access to all information contained within the system, or the organization-defined physical access authorizations `[Assignment: Unescorted Access Authorizations]`.

Facilities / Physical Security, with Information Security, implements physical safeguards for all workstations that access electronic protected health information to restrict access to authorized users.

Facilities / Physical Security documents, per workstation or workstation class, the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are performed, and the physical attributes of the workstation surroundings.

Facilities / Physical Security applies position or role–based physical restrictions (placement, cabling locks, screen positioning, or lockable enclosures) so only authorized users can operate these workstations.

Facilities / Physical Security enforces physical access authorizations at all entry and exit points, verifying individual access authorizations before granting access and controlling ingress and egress using the [Physical Access Control System] and/or guards.

Facilities / Physical Security controls access to areas designated as publicly accessible using the defined physical access controls or security safeguards, and escorts visitors and controls visitor activity in the organization-defined circumstances `[Assignment: Visitor Escort Circumstances]`.

Facilities / Physical Security secures all keys, combinations, and other physical access devices in controlled storage, inventories all physical access devices every ninety (90) days, and changes combinations and keys at least every one (1) year — or earlier after any security-relevant event, lost key, compromised combination, or transfer/termination of a key or combination holder.

Facilities / Physical Security controls access to the data center/facility using door and window locks, security personnel, or physical authentication devices (e.g., biometrics and smart card/PIN combination), and restricts access to grounds/facilities to authorized persons only.
Facilities / Physical Security stores and operates servers only in physically secure environments, granting access to explicitly authorized personnel only.

Facilities / Physical Security creates and maintains restricted areas, security rooms, or locked rooms controlling access to areas containing PII, requiring two barriers to access PII under normal security (secured perimeter/locked container, locked perimeter/secured interior, or locked perimeter/security container); where non-authorized employees may have access after hours, protected information must be containerized.

Facilities / Physical Security enforces physical access authorizations to the system itself — in addition to facility controls — at the organization-defined physical spaces `[Assignment: System-Level Physical Spaces]`.

Facilities / Physical Security performs security checks at the physical perimeter for exfiltration of information or removal of system components at the organization-defined frequency `[Assignment: Perimeter Security Check Frequency]`.
Facilities / Physical Security staffs guards at the organization-defined physical access points to the facility 24 hours per day, 7 days per week.

Facilities / Physical Security installs lockable physical casings on the organization-defined system components `[Assignment: Components Requiring Lockable Casings]` and employs the organization-defined anti-tamper technologies `[Assignment: Anti-Tamper Technologies]` to detect and/or prevent physical tampering or alteration of hardware components within the system.
Facilities / Physical Security limits access using physical barriers and employs access control vestibules at the organization-defined locations `[Assignment: Access Control Vestibule Locations]`.

Facilities / Physical Security controls physical access to the organization-defined system distribution and transmission lines within facilities using the defined security controls or safeguards `[Assignment: Line Access Controls]`.

Facilities / Physical Security disables any physical ports not in use (e.g., in wiring closets and patch panels), verifying port status during the periodic wiring closet inspection recorded in the [Ticketing System].

Facilities / Physical Security controls physical access to output from the organization-defined output devices `[Assignment: Output Devices]` so unauthorized individuals cannot obtain the output, and links individual identity to receipt of output (e.g., badge-in release or logged retrieval acknowledgment) via the [Physical Access Audit Log System].

Facilities / Physical Security monitors physical access to the facility where the system resides to detect and respond to physical security incidents, using physical intrusion alarms and surveillance equipment ([Video Surveillance System]).

Facilities / Physical Security reviews physical access logs at least monthly (every thirty [30] days), and additionally upon occurrence of the organization-defined events or potential indications of events `[Assignment: Log Review Trigger Events]`.

Facilities / Physical Security configures the monitoring systems to recognize the organization-defined classes or types of intrusions `[Assignment: Intrusion Classes]` and initiate the defined response actions using the defined automated mechanisms `[Assignment: Automated Response Mechanisms]`.

Facilities / Physical Security employs video surveillance of the defined operational areas `[Assignment: Surveillance Areas]`, reviews video recordings at the defined frequency `[Assignment: Video Review Frequency]`, and retains recordings for the defined period `[Assignment: Video Retention Period]`.

Facilities / Physical Security monitors physical access to the system itself — in addition to facility-level monitoring — at the organization-defined physical spaces `[Assignment: System-Level Physical Spaces]`.

Facilities / Physical Security coordinates the results of reviews and investigations with the organizational incident response capability, escalating suspected incidents through the [Ticketing System].

Reception staff and guards record every visitor in the [Visitor Management System]; each record must include the visitor's name and organization, the visitor's signature, form of identification, date of access, time of entry and departure, purpose of visit, and the name and organization of the person visited.
Facilities / Physical Security maintains and reviews visitor access records using the defined automated mechanism ([Visitor Management System]) at least monthly (every thirty [30] days).
Facilities / Physical Security reports anomalies in visitor access records to the defined personnel or roles `[Assignment: Anomaly Recipients]` via the [Ticketing System].
Facilities / Physical Security retains visitor access records for at least one (1) year.

Facilities / Physical Security submits the policy for collection and retention of visitor access records to the privacy office and/or the senior official for privacy for review, and limits PII in visitor records to the elements identified in the privacy risk assessment.
Facilities / Physical Security protects power equipment and power cabling for the system from damage and destruction (conduit, cable trays, restricted routing).

Facilities / Physical Security permits only authorized maintenance personnel to access infrastructure assets, including power generators; heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems; cabling; and wiring closets, verifying authorization against the access list before entry.

Facilities / Physical Security employs redundant power cabling paths physically separated by the defined distance `[Assignment: Redundant Cabling Separation Distance]`, and employs automatic voltage controls for the defined critical system components `[Assignment: Critical Components for Voltage Control]`.
Facilities / Physical Security provides the capability of shutting off power to the defined system or individual system components `[Assignment: Emergency Shutoff Scope]` in emergency situations.
Facilities / Physical Security places emergency shutoff switches or devices in the defined locations by system or component to facilitate access for authorized personnel.
Facilities / Physical Security protects the emergency power shutoff capability from unauthorized activation (covers, locked enclosures, or restricted access).

Facilities / Physical Security implements and maintains a main power switch or emergency cut-off switch for data centers, server rooms, and mainframe rooms, prominently marked and protected by a cover, and inspects it during quarterly facility walkthroughs.

Facilities / Physical Security provides an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) to facilitate orderly shutdown of the system and/or transition to long-term alternate power in the event of primary power loss.

Facilities / Physical Security provides an alternate power supply, activated manually or automatically, that can maintain minimally required operational capability during an extended loss of primary power; where required, the alternate supply must be self-contained — not reliant on external power generation — and capable of maintaining minimally required or full operational capability.

Facilities / Physical Security tests emergency power equipment on a schedule complying with manufacturer recommendations and local, state, and federal requirements, and no less often than every three (3) years, recording results in the [Documentation Repository].
Facilities / Physical Security employs and maintains automatic emergency lighting that activates on power outage or disruption and covers emergency exits and evacuation routes within the facility.
Facilities / Physical Security provides emergency lighting for all areas within the facility supporting essential mission and business functions.

Facilities / Physical Security tests emergency lighting equipment on a schedule complying with manufacturer recommendations and local, state, and federal requirements, and no less often than every three (3) years, recording results in the [Documentation Repository].
Facilities / Physical Security employs and maintains fire detection and suppression systems supported by an independent energy source.

Facilities / Physical Security ensures fire detection systems activate automatically and notify the defined personnel or roles `[Assignment: Fire Notification Recipients]` and defined emergency responders in the event of a fire.

Facilities / Physical Security ensures fire suppression systems activate automatically and notify the defined personnel or roles and defined emergency responders, and employs an automatic fire suppression capability whenever the facility is not staffed on a continuous basis.

Facilities / Physical Security schedules fire protection inspections by authorized and qualified inspectors at the defined frequency `[Assignment: Fire Inspection Frequency]`, and resolves identified deficiencies within the defined period `[Assignment: Fire Deficiency Remediation Deadline]`.

Facilities / Physical Security tests fire protection equipment on a schedule complying with manufacturer recommendations and local, state, and federal requirements, and no less often than every three (3) years, recording results in the [Documentation Repository].

Facilities / Physical Security maintains temperature, humidity, and pressure levels within the facility where the system resides at acceptable vendor-specified levels consistent with the ASHRAE document *Thermal Guidelines for Data Processing Environments*.

Facilities / Physical Security monitors environmental control levels at the defined frequency `[Assignment: Environmental Monitoring Frequency]` using the [Environmental Monitoring System], producing the Data centre environmental monitoring records as evidence.

When an environmental control alert occurs, Facilities / Physical Security evaluates the alert level and follows the prescribed guidelines for that level, alerts component management of possible loss of service and/or media, reports damage, provides remedial action, and implements the contingency plan if necessary.

Facilities / Physical Security employs the defined automatic environmental controls `[Assignment: Automatic Environmental Controls]` in the facility to prevent fluctuations potentially harmful to the system.

Facilities / Physical Security employs environmental control monitoring that provides an alarm or notification of changes potentially harmful to personnel or equipment to the defined personnel or roles `[Assignment: Environmental Alert Recipients]` via the [Environmental Monitoring System].

Facilities / Physical Security protects the system from damage resulting from water leakage by providing master shutoff or isolation valves that are accessible, working properly, and known to key personnel; document valve locations and brief key personnel on them.

Facilities / Physical Security tests water damage protection equipment on a schedule complying with manufacturer recommendations and local, state, and federal requirements, and no less often than every three (3) years, recording results in the [Documentation Repository].

Facilities / Physical Security employs automated water detection near the system that alerts the defined personnel or roles `[Assignment: Water Alert Recipients]` using the defined automated mechanisms via the [Environmental Monitoring System].
Facilities / Physical Security authorizes and controls all system components entering and exiting the facility, logging each item in the component movement register.

Facilities / Physical Security maintains records of the system components, and of the movements of hardware and electronic media and the person responsible for each movement, in the [Asset Tracking System].

Facilities / Physical Security implements procedures governing the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media containing electronic protected health information into and out of the facility, and movement of these items within the facility.

Facilities / Physical Security implements procedures addressing final disposition of electronic protected health information and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored, and procedures for removal of electronic protected health information from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use.

Before movement of equipment, the requesting team creates a retrievable, exact copy of electronic protected health information when needed, confirmed by Facilities / Physical Security prior to releasing the item.
Facilities / Physical Security determines and documents the alternate work sites allowed for use by employees, in coordination with Information Security.
Facilities / Physical Security defines the controls employed at alternate work sites in the appropriate System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP) and implements them.
Facilities / Physical Security assesses the effectiveness of controls at alternate work sites and records the assessment results in the [Documentation Repository].

Facilities / Physical Security provides employees at alternate work sites a means to communicate with information security and privacy personnel in case of incidents, and publicizes the contact channel to affected personnel.

Facilities / Physical Security positions system components within the facility to minimize potential damage from the defined physical and environmental hazards `[Assignment: Positioning Hazards]` (e.g., away from water sources, exterior walls, and high-traffic areas) and to minimize the opportunity for unauthorized access.
Facilities / Physical Security re-evaluates component placement whenever facility layout changes or new hazards are identified, recording placement decisions and changes in the [Ticketing System].

Facilities / Physical Security establishes — and implements as needed — procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operations plan in the event of an emergency; step 2 of the facility access list procedure is bypassed only under these documented emergency procedures, with the access logged and reconciled afterward.

Facilities / Physical Security documents all repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility that are related to security (e.g., hardware, walls, doors, and locks) in the [Ticketing System], retaining the records per the documentation retention procedure above.

Facilities / Physical Security is accountable for this procedure end to end: it executes all steps, produces the Badge access review and Data centre environmental monitoring records, coordinates handoffs with HR, Information Security, the Privacy Office, reception staff, guards, maintenance personnel, and the incident response capability, and answers for the outcome.
Exceptions to any step in this procedure require review and written approval by Facilities / Physical Security in consultation with Information Security, documented in the [Ticketing System].
