analyze: Executing this procedure establishes, maintains, approves, and protects Example Org's information security program governance artifacts — the organization-wide program plan, risk management strategy, planning and personnel security policies, system security and privacy plans, rules of behavior, access agreements, and supporting facility, media, acquisition, and workforce controls — and keeps them current, coordinated, and traceable to applicable frameworks.

This procedure is performed by the Security Program / GRC team, with participation from the senior risk-accountable official, the Senior Information Security Officer, Human Resources, system owners, contracting personnel, and facilities staff, and applies to all organizational systems, workforce members, facilities, and external providers that create, receive, maintain, or transmit organizational information, including electronic protected health information (ePHI).
- A named senior official with responsibility and accountability for the risk being incurred to organizational operations, assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
- A named Senior Information Security Officer (e.g., CISO) with the mission and resources to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain the organization-wide information security program.
- Access to the [Document Management System] for authoring, storing, and permissioning governance documents.
- Access to the [GRC Tool] for tracking reviews, approvals, and control designations.
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for tracking review tasks and trigger events.
- Access to the [Identity Provider] for verifying access grants and revocations.
- Access to the [HR System] for workforce onboarding, transfer, and termination data.
- Access to the [Contract Management System] for business associate and external provider agreements.
- Access to the [Physical Access Control System] and facility maintenance records.
- The current ARC-AMPE System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP) template.
- Current enterprise architecture documentation and the roster of contractor personnel.
- The prior year's Approved policy set with review dates and the current Program plan and org chart.

The Security Program / GRC team drafts the organization-wide information security program plan in the [Document Management System], providing an overview of the requirements for the security program and describing the security program management controls and common controls in place or planned for meeting those requirements.
Ensure the plan identifies and assigns roles and responsibilities, documents management commitment, addresses coordination among organizational entities, and addresses compliance.
Circulate the draft to each organizational entity responsible for information security and incorporate their coordination feedback before finalizing.

Submit the plan to the senior official with responsibility and accountability for the risk being incurred to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, and reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, and obtain their documented approval.
Disseminate the approved plan to all personnel with program responsibilities via the [Document Management System].
Apply access controls in the [Document Management System] so the plan is protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification; restrict write access to the Security Program / GRC team.
Record the approved plan as part of the Program plan and org chart evidence artifact and update the Approved policy set with review dates in the [GRC Tool].
The Security Program / GRC team schedules the program plan review annually and executes it against the current Program plan and org chart.

Following any of the following events, initiate an out-of-cycle review: system architectural or design changes; assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws (to include privacy laws), Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

Actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect the information security program plans, using [Legal/Regulatory Monitoring] sources, and log identified changes in the [Ticketing System].
Review the plan at least every one (1) year to ensure it remains effective, and update it to reflect monitored legal and policy changes.
Ensure the updated plan supports cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and for the information on the systems it governs.
Re-obtain senior official approval for the updated plan and update the Approved policy set with review dates.
The Security Program / GRC team designates, in writing, the officials responsible for the development of system-level information security program plans.
Record each designation in the [GRC Tool] and ensure the named officials are identified in the appropriate security and privacy documents (e.g., each system's SSPP).
Communicate the designations to the named officials and their management chain.
Maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the rule in written form (electronic form is permitted), stored in the [Document Management System].
Maintain a written record of any action, activity, or assessment required by the rule to be documented, filed alongside the related policy in the [Document Management System].

Retain the required documentation for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later; configure [Document Management System] retention rules accordingly.

Make the documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains, via [Document Management System] access grants managed by the Security Program / GRC team.

Periodically review the documentation and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information, recording each review in the Approved policy set with review dates.

Senior leadership appoints a senior information security officer (e.g., senior agency information security officer or chief information security officer) with the mission and resources to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain an organization-wide information security program.
The Security Program / GRC team records the appointment and the officer's authority and resourcing in the Program plan and org chart.

Separately identify and document the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the required policies and procedures for the covered entity or business associate [HIPAA 164.308(a)(2)], and record that identification in the Program plan and org chart.

The Security Program / GRC team develops a comprehensive strategy to manage security risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation associated with the operation and use of organizational systems, and privacy risk to individuals resulting from the authorized processing of personally identifiable information.
Publish the strategy in the [Document Management System] and disseminate it to the personnel and roles defined in the strategy.
Implement the risk management strategy consistently across the organization, embedding its risk determination and acceptance steps into the [GRC Tool] workflows used by all teams.
Review and update the strategy at least every one (1) year, or as required, to address organizational changes; document the review outcome and re-approve the updated strategy.

The Security Program / GRC team develops, documents, and disseminates to the organization-defined personnel or roles an organization-level planning policy addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, consistent with applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Develop procedures to facilitate the implementation of the planning policy and the associated planning controls, and publish both in the [Document Management System].
Designate the official who manages the development, documentation, and dissemination of the planning policy and procedures, and record the designation in the [GRC Tool].

Review and update the planning policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, including assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws (to include privacy laws), Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Designate the officials responsible for the management of planning controls for systems and ensure they are named in the appropriate security and privacy documents.

Actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect planning policies, and review them at least every one (1) year to ensure the planning policies remain effective.
Ensure the planning policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and for the information on the systems.
Update the Approved policy set with review dates to reflect the completed review.

The Security Program / GRC team conducts an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the organization, and documents the assessment results in the [GRC Tool].
Implement security measures sufficient to reduce the risks and vulnerabilities identified to a reasonable and appropriate level, tracking each measure to closure in the [Ticketing System].
Maintain policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(i)], and verify they are reflected in the Approved policy set with review dates.

Implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports [HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D)]; the Security Program / GRC team pulls these records from [Logging/Monitoring Platform] and [Ticketing System] and records the review outcomes.
For each system, the designated system-level plan official develops a security and privacy plan using the ARC-AMPE SSPP template; the completed SSPP must be consistent with that template.

Ensure the plan explicitly defines the constituent system components; describes the operational context in terms of mission and business processes; identifies the individuals fulfilling system roles and responsibilities; identifies the information types processed, stored, and transmitted; provides the security categorization with supporting rationale; describes specific threats of concern; provides the results of a privacy risk assessment for systems processing PII; describes the operational environment and any dependencies on or connections to other systems; provides an overview of the security and privacy requirements; identifies any relevant control baselines or overlays; describes the controls in place or planned (including rationale for tailoring decisions); includes risk determinations for security and privacy architecture and design decisions; and includes security- and privacy-related activities requiring planning and coordination with the organization-defined individuals or groups.
Ensure the plan is consistent with the organization's enterprise architecture.
Submit the SSPP to the authorizing official or designated representative for review and approval prior to plan implementation, and record the approval in the [GRC Tool].

Distribute copies of the approved plan to the organization-defined personnel, roles, or stakeholders via the [Document Management System], and communicate subsequent changes to the plans to the same audience.
Review the SSPP at least every one (1) year or following significant changes.
Update the SSPP to address changes to the system and environment of operation or problems identified during plan implementation or control assessments.
Protect the SSPP from unauthorized disclosure and modification using [Document Management System] access controls, with write access limited to the plan official and the Security Program / GRC team.

The Security Program / GRC team establishes rules of behavior describing the responsibilities and expected behavior of all individuals requiring access to the system (including contractors) for information and system usage, security, and privacy.

Include in the rules of behavior restrictions on: use of social media, social networking sites, and external sites/applications; posting organizational information on public websites; and use of organization-provided identifiers (e.g., email addresses) and authentication secrets (e.g., passwords) for creating accounts on external sites/applications [NIST PL-4(1) | ARC-AMPE PL-4(1) AE Mandatory].

Before authorizing access to information and the system, require and capture a documented acknowledgment — such as an electronic or physical signature, or an electronic agreement check box in [Identity Provider] onboarding — indicating the individual has read, understands, and agrees to abide by the rules of behavior.
Review and update the rules of behavior at least every one (1) year.
When the rules are revised or updated, require individuals who acknowledged a previous version to read and re-acknowledge the revised rules before retaining access.

The Security Program / GRC team, with Facilities, implements policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information.

Implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and the facilities in which they are housed, while ensuring properly authorized access is allowed [HIPAA 164.310(a)(1)], administered through the [Physical Access Control System].

Establish (and implement as needed) procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operations plan in the event of an emergency [HIPAA 164.310(a)(2)(i)].
Implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft [HIPAA 164.310(a)(2)(ii)].

Implement procedures to control and validate a person's access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control, and control access to software programs for testing and revision [HIPAA 164.310(a)(2)(iii)].

Implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility that are related to security (for example, hardware, walls, doors, and locks), recording them in the facility maintenance log [HIPAA 164.310(a)(2)(iv)].

The Security Program / GRC team, with the enterprise architecture function, develops security and privacy architectures for the system that describe the requirements and approach for protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of organizational information; the requirements and approach for processing PII to minimize privacy risk to individuals; how the architectures are integrated into and support the enterprise architecture; and any assumptions about, and dependencies on, external systems and services.

Review and update the architectures at least every one (1) year or following a significant change — which can include system architectural or design changes; assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; or changes in applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines — to reflect changes in the enterprise architecture.
Reflect planned architecture changes in security and privacy plans, Concept of Operations (CONOPS), criticality analysis, organizational procedures, and procurements and acquisitions.
The Security Program / GRC team selects a control baseline for the system and records the selection and rationale in the SSPP.
Tailor the selected baseline by applying the specified tailoring actions, documenting each tailoring decision.

Do not remove or reduce any of the controls included within the ARC-AMPE baseline; do not add AC 2(8) to the control baseline, because access to PII may only be granted to officers and employees with a need for the information in performance of their duties, and dynamic account creation may not support independent verification of that need.

Add controls to the ARC-AMPE baseline only where they do not conflict with or create less stringent standards than the baseline, and only as the result of a risk-informed decision based on mission and business functions, environments of operation, threats, vulnerabilities, and other conditions affecting the organization.

Treat parameter values that do not start with "organization-defined" as minimum parameter values, modifiable only to create more stringent standards; assign values for parameters that start with "organization-defined," considering applicable regulations, statutes, administrative rules, and similar guidance for safeguarding systems and information.
Record the tailored baseline and parameter assignments in the SSPP and the [GRC Tool].

The Security Program / GRC team develops, documents, and disseminates to the organization-defined personnel and roles an organization-level personnel security policy addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, consistent with applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Develop procedures to facilitate the implementation of the personnel security policy and the associated personnel security controls.
Designate the official who manages the development, documentation, and dissemination of the personnel security policy and procedures, and record the designation in the [GRC Tool].

Review and update the personnel security policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, including assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws (to include privacy laws), Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Designate the officials responsible for the management of personnel security for systems and ensure they are named in the appropriate security and privacy documents.

Actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect personnel security policies, and review them at least every one (1) year to ensure the personnel security policies remain effective.

Ensure the personnel security policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and for the information on the systems, and update the Approved policy set with review dates.

The Security Program / GRC team, with Human Resources, implements policies and procedures to ensure all members of the workforce have appropriate access to electronic protected health information and to prevent workforce members who do not have such access from obtaining it.
Implement procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with ePHI or in locations where it might be accessed [HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(A)].

Implement procedures to determine that a workforce member's access to ePHI is appropriate [HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(B)], using role definitions maintained in the [HR System] and entitlements in the [Identity Provider].

Implement procedures for terminating access to ePHI when a workforce member's employment or other arrangement ends, or as required by clearance determinations [HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(C)], executed through the [Identity Provider] deprovisioning workflow.

The Security Program / GRC team develops and documents access agreements for organizational systems, including access authorization requests, nondisclosure agreements, acceptable use agreements, privacy training and awareness, and rules of behavior.

Ensure the access agreements contain provisions consistent with the ACA and the requirements of 45 CFR § 155.260 – Privacy and security of personally identifiable information, paragraphs (b)(2) and (c).
Review and update the access agreements as part of the system security authorization or when a contract is renewed or extended, but at a minimum at least every one (1) year.

Verify that individuals requiring access to organizational information and systems sign the appropriate access agreements (paper or electronic) prior to being granted access; check the signed-agreement record in [HR System] or [Identity Provider] before approving the access request.
Require individuals to re-sign access agreements to maintain access when the agreements have been updated or at least every one (1) year, tracked via the [GRC Tool] re-acknowledgment queue.

For classified information requiring special protection, verify individuals have a valid access authorization demonstrated by assigned official government duties, satisfy associated personnel security criteria, and have read, understood, and signed a nondisclosure agreement [NIST PS-6(2)].

Notify individuals of applicable, legally binding post-employment requirements for protection of organizational information and require individuals to sign an acknowledgment of these requirements, if applicable, as part of granting initial access to covered information [NIST PS-6(3)].
The Security Program / GRC team implements policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information that are consistent with the applicable requirements of subpart E.

If a health care clearinghouse is part of a larger organization, implement policies and procedures that protect the clearinghouse's ePHI from unauthorized access by the larger organization [HIPAA 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(A)].
Implement policies and procedures for granting access to ePHI, for example, through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism [HIPAA 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(B)].

Based on the entity's access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify each user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process, recording the current rights in the [Identity Provider] and the review record in the [GRC Tool] [HIPAA 164.308(a)(4)(ii)(C)].

The Security Program / GRC team, with Facilities and IT Operations, implements policies and procedures governing the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media containing ePHI into and out of a facility, and the movement of these items within the facility.
Implement policies and procedures to address the final disposition of ePHI, and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored [HIPAA 164.310(d)(2)(i)].
Implement procedures for removal of ePHI from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use [HIPAA 164.310(d)(2)(ii)].
Maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible for them, kept in the media movement log [HIPAA 164.310(d)(2)(iii)].
Create a retrievable, exact copy of ePHI, when needed, before movement of equipment, and verify the copy's retrievability before releasing the equipment [HIPAA 164.310(d)(2)(iv)].

Before permitting a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI on the organization's behalf, obtain satisfactory assurances, documented through a written contract or other arrangement in the [Contract Management System], that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the ePHI.
Require each business associate to obtain the same satisfactory assurances from its subcontractors that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI on its behalf.

Ensure business associate contracts require the business associate to: comply with the applicable requirements of the rule; ensure that any subcontractors agree to comply with those requirements by entering into a compliant contract or other arrangement; and report to the organization any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information as required by § 164.410 [HIPAA 164.314(a)(2)(i)].

Where compliance with the contract requirement is achieved through another arrangement, verify the arrangement meets the requirements of § 164.504(e)(3) and document that determination [HIPAA 164.314(a)(2)(ii)].

Apply the contract or other arrangement requirements in the same manner to the arrangement between a business associate and a subcontractor as they apply to contracts between covered entities and business associates [HIPAA 164.314(a)(2)(iii)].

For a group health plan, ensure its plan documents require the plan sponsor to implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the ePHI it creates, receives, maintains, or transmits on the plan's behalf; ensure the adequate separation required by § 164.504(f)(2)(iii) is supported by reasonable and appropriate security measures; ensure any agent to whom it provides the information agrees to implement reasonable and appropriate security measures; and require the plan sponsor to report to the group health plan any security incident of which it becomes aware — except where only permitted disclosures apply [HIPAA 164.314(b)(1) | HIPAA 164.314(b)(2)].

The Security Program / GRC team, with [Contracting Officers], establishes personnel security requirements, including security roles and responsibilities, for external providers, and documents those requirements in the contract or provider agreement in the [Contract Management System].
Require external providers to comply with the personnel security policies and procedures established by the organization.

Require external providers to notify the organization-defined personnel or roles — which may include the security manager, Contracting Officers, or Contracting Officer's Representatives via the roster of contractor personnel — of any personnel transfers or terminations of external personnel who possess organizational credentials and/or badges, or who have system privileges, within twenty-four (24) hours.
Upon receiving such notification, direct the revocation of the affected credentials, badges, and system privileges through the [Identity Provider] and [Physical Access Control System].
Monitor provider compliance with the personnel security requirements, recording monitoring results in the [GRC Tool].
Clearly document any nationality requirements for any account type within the platform; if none exist, explicitly state that none exist.

The Security Program / GRC team employs a formal sanctions process and applies appropriate sanctions against individuals and workforce members who fail to comply with established information security and privacy policies and procedures.

When a formal employee sanctions process is initiated, notify the organization-defined personnel or roles — which may include Human Resources, Managers, Supervisors, Contracting Officer's Representatives, Physical Security personnel, Information System Security Officers, or similar roles as defined in the SSPP — within twenty-four (24) hours, identifying the individual sanctioned and the reason for the sanction.

When personnel sanctions are associated with the loss, theft, or compromise of PII, take additional care to prevent further privacy incidents by not providing the PII involved in the incident to anyone without an explicit need to know; instead, provide a characterization of the type(s) of PII breached (e.g., "Full Name" rather than the individual's actual name).

The Security Program / GRC team develops, documents, and disseminates to the organization-defined personnel and roles an organization-level system and services acquisition policy addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, consistent with applicable laws, Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Develop procedures to facilitate the implementation of the acquisition policy and the associated acquisition controls, and publish both in the [Document Management System].
Designate the official who manages the development, documentation, and dissemination of the acquisition policy and procedures, and record the designation in the [GRC Tool].

Review and update the acquisition policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, including assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws (to include privacy laws), Executive Orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Designate the officials responsible for the management of system acquisition and ensure they are named in the appropriate security and privacy documents.

Actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect system and services acquisition policies, and review them at least every one (1) year to ensure the acquisition policies remain effective.

Ensure the acquisition policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and for the information on the systems, and update the Approved policy set with review dates.

The Security Program / GRC team determines the high-level information security and privacy requirements for the system or system service during mission and business process planning, and records them in the planning documentation.

Determine, document, and allocate the resources required to protect the system or system service — including the information in the system, to include PII — as part of the organizational capital planning and investment control process.
Establish a discrete line item for information security and privacy in organizational programming and budgeting documentation, and verify the line item during each budgeting cycle.

The Security Program / GRC team owns this procedure end to end: it authors and maintains the program plan, policies, strategies, and system plans; coordinates reviews; tracks approvals; and answers for the resulting evidence (the Approved policy set with review dates and the Program plan and org chart).

The senior risk-accountable official approves the organization-wide program plan, the authorizing official approves system security and privacy plans, and participants such as Human Resources, [Contracting Officers], Facilities, and system-level plan officials execute their assigned steps; exceptions to any step in this procedure are reviewed and approved by the Security Program / GRC team in consultation with the senior risk-accountable official.

analyze: This procedure provides the step-by-step operational instructions for establishing, authorizing, monitoring, and terminating remote access, wireless access, mobile device access, and third-party/external system access to Example Org systems.

Executing it ensures every remote and third-party connection path is documented, cryptographically protected, routed through managed control points, and revocable on demand, in accordance with the Example Org Information Security Standard: Remote & Third-Party Access.

This procedure is performed by the Network Security team on all Example Org remote access solutions (VPN, MPLS, wireless, mobile, and vendor/third-party connections) and applies to all users, devices, and external systems that connect to Example Org networks or systems.
It covers government furnished equipment (GFE), contractor furnished equipment (CFE), personally owned devices, vendor accounts, and external information systems.

- Network Security team membership with administrative access to the [VPN Gateway], [Firewall Management Console], [Network Access Control System], [Wireless LAN Controller], [Mobile Device Management (MDM) System], [Identity Provider], and [SIEM].
- A current Third-party access register and the approved VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
- Written authorization from the Authorizing Official (AO) or designated representative for any exception-based access (e.g., personally owned devices, portable storage on external systems).
- System Security and Privacy Plans (SSPPs) for each system supporting remote access, including documented definitions of compelling operational need.
- Executed system connection or processing agreements (per CA-3/SA-9) for each external system in scope.
- A [Ticketing System] for recording access requests, authorizations, and disconnect orders.

Network Security enumerates every type of remote access permitted to Example Org systems (e.g., VPN, MPLS, vendor logon, wireless, mobile) and records each type, its usage restrictions, configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
For each documented type, Network Security obtains authorization from the [Authorizing Official] prior to enabling any connections of that type.
Network Security records the authorization decision and date in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline and updates the baseline whenever a new remote access type is proposed.
No remote access type is enabled until steps 1–3 are complete; requests for new types are submitted via the [Ticketing System] to Network Security.
Network Security identifies all connections that cannot traverse the MPLS service network and flags them in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
For each such connection, Network Security configures the [VPN Gateway] or [Remote Access Gateway] to require callback to a pre-registered, authorized location before the session is established.
Network Security configures the callback flow to require full re-authentication of the user after the callback is completed, using the standard authentication process.
Network Security verifies callback and re-authentication behavior with a test connection for each flagged path and records the test result in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security assigns each vendor requiring logon to an application or turnkey system a unique User ID and password — never a shared account — via the [Identity Provider].
Network Security configures the vendor account so that logon is only possible through the standard authentication process, with access to the target system authorized and logged.
Network Security enables logging of all vendor session activity to the [SIEM] and records the vendor account, owning system, and authorization in the Third-party access register.

Network Security recertifies every vendor-assigned User ID every one (1) year: it reviews each account in the Third-party access register, confirms with the System Business Owner that the vendor still requires access, and disables or deletes accounts that fail recertification.
Network Security records the recertification outcome and date for each account in the Third-party access register.
Network Security reviews the latest published NIST SP 800-63 and maps its authenticator assurance requirements to the Example Org remote access authentication configuration.

Network Security configures the [Identity Provider] and [VPN Gateway] to meet the applicable SP 800-63 assurance level for each remote access type documented in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security re-checks the configuration against the latest published SP 800-63 each quarter and records the review outcome in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.

Network Security defines, in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline, the minimum secure configuration for any device — GFE, CFE, or personal — that requires network access: up-to-date system patches; current anti-virus software; a host-based intrusion detection system; automatic execution of code disabled; and the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.

Before granting network access, Network Security verifies each device against this baseline using the [Network Access Control System] posture checks; devices that fail are quarantined until remediated.
For CFE and personal devices, Network Security records the verification result and device owner in the Third-party access register.
Network Security re-verifies device compliance each quarter and revokes network access for devices that cannot meet the baseline.

Network Security reviews the latest published NIST SP 800-46 and confirms the Example Org remote access policies define: the forms of permitted remote access; the types of devices permissible for remote access; the types of access granted to remote users; and the handling of remote user account provisioning.
Network Security updates the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline to reflect any gaps found, and routes policy changes to the [Authorizing Official] for approval.
Network Security applies the provisioning rules in step 1 when creating, modifying, or deprovisioning remote user accounts via the [Identity Provider].
Network Security configures the [SIEM] to ingest session, authentication, and configuration logs from the [VPN Gateway], [Wireless LAN Controller], [MDM System], and [Identity Provider].

Network Security creates automated alerts in the [SIEM] for unauthorized remote access methods, connections from unapproved locations, and configuration drift from the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security configures the [Network Access Control System] to automatically block non-compliant remote connections.
Network Security reviews automated monitoring output each quarter and records the review in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.

Network Security configures the [VPN Gateway] and all remote access endpoints to require the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptographic mechanisms for every remote session, protecting confidentiality and integrity of information in transit.
Network Security disables any remote access protocol or cipher suite that does not meet the FIPS 140 requirement.
Network Security verifies session encryption during the quarterly configuration review and records the verified cipher configuration in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security designates the [VPN Gateway] and [Network Access Control System] as the authorized network access control points for all remote access.
Network Security configures the perimeter [Firewall Management Console] rules so that remote access traffic is only accepted at these control points and is denied at all other ingress paths.
Network Security monitors the [SIEM] for connection attempts bypassing the control points and blocks the offending source.
Network Security confirms the routing configuration each quarter as part of the VPN and remote-access configuration review.

Network Security works with each System Business Owner to define, in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP), what constitutes a compelling operational need for remote execution of privileged commands and for remote access to security-relevant information.

Network Security configures privileged remote access so that each execution is performed in a format that provides assessable evidence — commands and sessions logged to the [SIEM] with user, command, target, and timestamp.
Before granting a privileged remote access request, Network Security confirms a compelling operational need as defined in the SSPP exists and records the justification in the [Ticketing System].

Network Security documents the rationale for permitting remote execution of privileged commands in the security plan for the affected system and updates the SSPP whenever the definition of compelling operational need changes.

Network Security restricts access to remote access mechanism details — gateway addresses, configuration, ports, authentication parameters — to Network Security personnel and explicitly authorized recipients, enforced via the [Identity Provider].
Network Security stores the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline and related mechanism documentation in [Restricted Document Repository] with access controls and encryption.
Network Security reviews access permissions to this documentation each quarter and removes any unauthorized access.

Network Security configures the [VPN Gateway], [Network Access Control System], and [Identity Provider] so that any remote access session or account can be disconnected or disabled on demand, and validates that the capability operates within one (1) hour of a disconnect order.

Upon issuance of a disconnect or disable order by an organization-defined official, Network Security executes the disconnect via the [VPN Gateway] or [Identity Provider] and confirms termination within one (1) hour.

Upon issuance of an order by organization-defined officials to terminate or suspend a system-to-system network interconnection, Network Security disables the connection at the [Firewall Management Console] and confirms termination within one (1) hour.
Network Security records each disconnect or termination order, the time of issuance, and the time of confirmed termination in the [Ticketing System].
Network Security implements the organization-defined mechanism — via the [Identity Provider] and [Remote Command Gateway] — to authenticate all remote commands before execution.
Network Security rejects any remote command that fails authentication and logs the rejection to the [SIEM].
Network Security tests the remote command authentication mechanism each quarter and records the result in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.

Network Security documents, for each workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information (ePHI), the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the permitted surroundings.

Network Security records these workstation specifications in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline and enforces them through the [Network Access Control System] and physical access controls at [Workstation Locations].
Network Security reviews the workstation specifications each quarter and updates them when ePHI-accessing workstations or their surroundings change.
Network Security documents, for each type of wireless access, the configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security obtains authorization from the [Authorizing Official] for each wireless access type prior to allowing any connections of that type.
Network Security enables the wireless access type only after authorization is recorded and blocks all unauthorized wireless types at the [Wireless LAN Controller].
Network Security disables SSID broadcasting on all approved wireless access points via the [Wireless LAN Controller].

Network Security enforces the following controls on each approved wireless network: encryption protection enabled; access points placed in secure areas; access points shut down when not in use (e.g., nights, weekends); a stateful inspection firewall between the wireless network and the wired infrastructure; MAC address authentication; static IP addresses (not DHCP); personal firewalls on all wireless clients; file sharing disabled on all wireless clients; intrusion detection agents deployed on the wireless side of the firewall; and adherence to the latest published IEEE 802.11 WLAN standard.
Network Security monitors and records wireless activity via the [Wireless IDS] and reviews the records on a regular basis as defined in the applicable security/privacy plans ([Review Frequency]).
Network Security verifies each control in step 2 each quarter and records the verification in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security configures the [Wireless LAN Controller] to require authentication of both users and devices before granting wireless access to the system.
Network Security enables the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption for all communications via the wireless access device.
Network Security disables any wireless authentication or encryption configuration that does not meet these requirements and verifies compliance each quarter.
Before issuance and deployment of any system component with embedded wireless networking capabilities, Network Security determines whether the wireless capability is intended for use.
If not intended for use, Network Security disables the embedded wireless capability via the [Endpoint Management System] and records the disablement in the device's configuration record.
Network Security verifies during the quarterly configuration review that disabled wireless capabilities remain off.

Network Security identifies and explicitly authorizes, by name, the users allowed to independently configure wireless networking capabilities, and records the list in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security grants the corresponding configuration privileges in the [Wireless LAN Controller] and [Identity Provider] only to users on the authorized list.
Network Security reviews the authorized list each quarter and revokes privileges for users no longer authorized.

Network Security selects radio antennas and calibrates transmission power levels on each wireless access point to reduce the probability that signals are receivable outside organization-controlled boundaries.
Network Security performs a signal perimeter survey after each calibration and records the measured boundary in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security repeats the survey each quarter and re-calibrates any access point whose signal extends beyond the controlled boundary.

Network Security documents configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for organization-controlled mobile devices — including requirements applicable when devices are outside controlled areas — in the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline.
Network Security obtains authorization from the System Business Owner for the use of mobile devices before enrolling any device in the [MDM System].

Network Security authorizes the connection of each mobile device to organizational systems only after steps 1–2 are complete, and records the device, owner, and authorization in the Third-party access register.
Network Security configures the [MDM System] so that only organization-owned mobile devices and organization-approved software may process, access, or store Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Network Security blocks PII access from any device not enrolled as organization-owned and reviews enrolled devices each quarter to confirm ownership status.

Network Security configures each organization-controlled mobile device via the [MDM System] to protect the storage and transmission of information on the device (device passcode, transmission encryption, storage protection).
Network Security installs and enables a virus protection application on each mobile device and configures scheduled scanning.
Network Security verifies the protection configuration and scan status each quarter via the [MDM System] console and remediates non-compliant devices.
Network Security enables full-device encryption or container-based encryption on all approved mobile devices via the [MDM System].
Network Security confirms the encryption implementation uses the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.
For any mobile device that contains PII, Network Security verifies encryption of the information on the device is enabled before PII access is granted.
Network Security verifies encryption status for all enrolled devices each quarter and blocks access for devices failing verification.

Network Security either establishes organization-defined terms and conditions — identifying the controls asserted to be implemented on external systems, consistent with the trust relationships with the organizations owning, operating, or maintaining those systems, allowing authorized individuals to (1) access the system from external systems and (2) process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information using external systems — or prohibits the organization-defined prohibited types of external systems.

Network Security ensures the terms and conditions address, at a minimum: the types of applications that can be accessed from external information systems; the maximum FIPS 199 security category of information that can be processed, stored, and transmitted; how other users of the external information system will be prevented from accessing federal information; the use of VPN and stateful inspection firewall technologies; the use of and protection against the vulnerabilities of wireless technologies; the maintenance of adequate physical security controls; the use of virus and spyware protection software; and how often the security capabilities of installed software are to be updated.
Network Security records the executed terms and conditions (or the prohibition decision) in the Third-party access register and reviews them each quarter.
Network Security applies AC-20 to govern system access to and from external systems.
When data is exchanged between a CSO and an external system, Network Security ensures the respective system owners document an agreement per CA-3.

Network Security ensures the responsibilities of external system owners (per SA-9) are captured in the agreement required by CA-3, and records the agreement reference in the Third-party access register.

Before permitting any authorized individual to use an external system to access the system or to process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information, Network Security either verifies implementation of the controls on the external system as specified in the organization's security and privacy policies and plans, or confirms retention of an approved system connection or processing agreement with the organizational entity hosting the external system.
Network Security records the verification or agreement reference in the Third-party access register and denies access requests lacking either.
Network Security re-verifies each external system each quarter and suspends access for systems whose verification or agreement has lapsed.
Network Security defines the restrictions on the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices on external systems and documents them in the applicable system security and privacy plans.

Network Security permits such use only when: the use is documented within the appropriate security/privacy plans; the use is explicitly authorized, in writing, by the Authorizing Official (AO) or designated representative; any personally owned devices to which the portable storage devices are to be attached comply with organization policies and directives on use of personally owned systems and components; and security and privacy safeguards appropriate for the sensitivity of the data are employed.
Network Security enforces the restrictions via the [Endpoint Management System] device control policy and records each written AO authorization in the Third-party access register.

Network Security restricts the use of non-organizationally owned systems or system components to process, store, or transmit organizational information using the organization-defined restrictions, unless: the use of contractor-owned devices is documented within the contract and appropriate security and privacy plans and explicitly authorized, in writing, by the Authorizing Official (AO) or designated representative; the use of personally owned devices complies with organizational policies and directives on use of personally-owned systems and components; security and privacy safeguards appropriate for the sensitivity of the data are employed; and either full-device or virtual container encryption is implemented to reduce the vulnerability of sensitive information processed, stored, or transmitted by the non-organizationally owned system or component.

Network Security communicates the strong discouragement of personally owned device use to all users and enforces the restrictions above via the [Network Access Control System] and [Endpoint Management System].
Network Security records each written AO authorization for contractor-owned device use in the Third-party access register and reviews all non-organizationally owned system usage each quarter.

Before device users are provided access to PII on remote devices, Network Security requires each user to acknowledge, through a binding agreement, their responsibilities to safeguard the PII accessible from the device and their awareness of the applicable handling requirements.
Network Security collects the signed agreement via [Agreement/Attestation System] and records the acknowledgment in the Third-party access register before provisioning PII access.
Network Security blocks PII access for any remote device user without a recorded acknowledgment and re-verifies acknowledgments during the quarterly review.

The Network Security team is accountable for this procedure end to end: it executes the configuration, authorization, monitoring, recertification, and disconnect steps, and maintains the VPN and remote-access configuration baseline and the Third-party access register as evidence.

System Business Owners, the Authorizing Official (or designated representative), vendors, and external system owners participate as named in individual steps; the Authorizing Official (or designated representative) reviews and approves all exceptions, including personally owned device use, portable storage on external systems, and contractor-owned device use.
