analyze: This procedure provides the step-by-step operational instructions for Example Org's Detection & Response team to implement the Example Org Logging, Monitoring & Alerting Standard: identifying what to log, collecting and protecting those logs, detecting and alerting on suspicious activity, and maintaining the associated documentation.
Executing this procedure produces evidence of continuous logging, monitoring, and alerting coverage, including a Log source inventory and coverage report and Alert tuning and review records.

This procedure is performed by the Detection & Response team on all information systems, networks, appliances, devices, services, and applications (including databases) that generate or consume audit records, including cloud-hosted environments.
Other teams (e.g., System Owners, Privacy Officer, ISSO, Authorizing Official) participate as reviewers, approvers, or recipients of findings.
- Access to the organization's log aggregation platform ([SIEM]) with analyst and administrator privileges.
- Access to the network and host-based intrusion detection/prevention management consoles ([IDS/IPS Platform]).
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for recording tuning, review, and incident actions.
- The current System Security and Privacy Plan(s) and Privacy Impact Assessment(s) for each system in scope.
- The name of the designated audit and accountability official recorded in the System Security and Privacy Policy.
- A current risk assessment covering the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information.
- A documented legal opinion regarding system monitoring activities, or an open request with [Legal Counsel] to obtain one.
- Authorized contact rosters for incident response personnel, the ISSO, the System Owner, and the Authorizing Official.
- An approved alternate/backup log destination distinct from the primary logging infrastructure.

Draft or update the audit and accountability policy at the organization level (and, where applicable, at the mission/business process or system level), covering purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance.
Verify the policy is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, including HIPAA and ACA/ARC-AMPE requirements.
Draft or update this procedure (and any related procedures) to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated controls.
Submit both documents to the Designated Official and the Authorizing Official for approval.
Disseminate the approved policy and procedures to the personnel and roles defined in the policy, using [Document Management System], and record the dissemination date and recipients.
Confirm the written (electronic is acceptable) copies are retained per the documentation retention requirements in the "Maintain Required Documentation" section below.
Identify the official responsible for the development, documentation, and dissemination of the audit and accountability policy and procedures.
Record that official by name and role in the organization's System Security and Privacy Policy.
When the designation changes, update the System Security and Privacy Policy and re-disseminate the policy per the preceding section.
Review and update the audit and accountability policy and procedures at least every one (1) year, on the schedule tracked by the Detection & Response team in [Ticketing System].

Trigger an out-of-cycle review and update following any of the following events: assessment or audit findings, security incidents or breaches, and changes in applicable laws, regulations, or standards.

Actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect audit and accountability (assign monitoring ownership in [Ticketing System] so it runs on a continuous basis), and update the documents when changes are identified.
Record each review and update — including the trigger, changes made, and approver — as part of the Alert tuning and review records.
Review the audit and accountability policies to confirm they support privacy to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system life cycle.
Review and update the associated access control policies and procedures to limit unnecessary or inappropriate access to PII.
Document the review outcome and any changes in [Ticketing System].

Confirm that hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms are in place on every information system containing or using electronic protected health information to record and examine system activity.
Verify each mechanism forwards its records to [SIEM]; add any uncovered source to the Log source inventory and coverage report as a gap with an owner and due date.
Retain the written (electronic is acceptable) policies and procedures implementing this requirement, and a written record of any action, activity, or assessment required to be documented.
Maintain all policies, procedures, and required records of actions, activities, and assessments in written (electronic acceptable) form in [Document Management System].
Retain each document for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
Make documentation available to the persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains (via [Document Management System] access grants).

Review the documentation periodically at [Documentation Review Frequency] and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
Operate the monitoring and alerting steps in this procedure as the mechanisms to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

When a potential risk or vulnerability to the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of electronic protected health information is identified, contribute log and monitoring data to the risk assessment and validate that the assessment is accurate and thorough.

Recommend and implement security measures, through the alert and monitoring controls in this procedure, sufficient to reduce identified risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.

When a workforce member fails to comply with security policies and procedures, package the evidence from audit records and refer the case to [Human Resources] and the appropriate official for application of appropriate sanctions; record the referral in [Ticketing System].

Regularly review records of information system activity — audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports — using the review steps in the "Review and Analyze Audit Records" section.
Issue security reminders (periodic security updates) to the workforce at [Security Reminder Frequency] using [Communication Platform].
Maintain and test the procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software, coordinating with [Endpoint Security] and the malicious-code response requirements of SI-3.
Monitor log-in attempts via [SIEM] dashboards and report discrepancies identified to the ISSO via [Ticketing System].
Verify the procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords remain implemented through [Identity Provider], and report any observed discrepancy to the ISSO.
Identify the types of events each system is capable of logging in support of the audit function, based on a risk assessment of organization-defined mission/business needs.
Coordinate with other organizational entities requiring audit-related information (e.g., Privacy, Compliance, Legal, System Owners) to inform the selection criteria for events to be logged.

Specify, for each system, the subset of event types to be logged, along with the frequency of (or situation requiring) logging for each, and document that frequency or situation in the System Security and Privacy Plan.

Provide a documented rationale for why the selected event types are adequate to support after-the-fact investigation of incidents, and attach the rationale to the Log source inventory and coverage report.

Review and update the selected event types at [Event Type Review Frequency], and in any case at least every one (1) year and whenever there is a significant system modification or change in the system environment.
Record each review outcome — selected events, rationale, and approver — in the Log source inventory and coverage report.

Confirm the risk assessment includes, at minimum, the following auditable events: server events and error messages; user log-on and log-off (successful or unsuccessful); all system administration (including privileged user) activities; modification of privileges and access; start up and shut down; application modifications; application alerts and error messages; configuration changes; account creation, modification, or deletion; file access, creation, modification, or deletion; read access to sensitive information; modification to sensitive information; printing sensitive information; anomalous (e.g., non-attributable) activity; data required for privacy monitoring controls; concurrent log-on from different work stations; override of access control mechanisms; and process creation.

Confirm each system is configured to log, at minimum: user log-on and log-off (successful or unsuccessful); configuration changes; application alerts and error messages; all system administration (including privileged user) activities; modification of privileges and access; account creation, modification, or deletion; concurrent log-on from different work stations; and override of access control mechanisms.
Record the configuration verification results in the Log source inventory and coverage report and remediate any missing event type with the System Owner.
Define the events to be audited for each cloud environment.
Submit the defined cloud audit events to the Authorizing Official for acceptance and approval, and record the approval in the System Security and Privacy Plan and [Ticketing System].

Configure each log source so audit records contain information establishing: what type of event occurred; when the event occurred; where the event occurred; the source of the event; the outcome of the event; and the identity of any individuals, subjects, or objects/entities associated with the event.

Configure logging of disclosures of sensitive information, including Protected Health Information and financial information, recording the information type, date, time, receiving party, and releasing party.

Validate a sample of records from each source against these content requirements during onboarding and after any source change, and record the validation in the Log source inventory and coverage report.

Configure audit records to additionally capture: session, connection, transaction, or activity duration; for client-server transactions, the number of bytes received and sent; additional informational messages to diagnose or identify the event; characteristics that describe or identify the object or resource being acted upon; individual identities of group account users; and full text of privileged commands.
Define the audit record types containing this additional information and submit them to the System Owner for approval and acceptance; record the approval in [Ticketing System].

Identify the minimum PII elements in audit records that are relevant and necessary to accomplish the purpose of the collection, using the elements identified in the Privacy Impact Assessment as system-defined elements.
Confirm that any collection of PII requiring legal authorization is legally authorized before enabling its capture.
Document in the audit policy the justification for inclusion of PII in audit logs, and configure [SIEM] and all log sources to restrict PII in audit records to those approved elements.
Review the PII element list whenever the Privacy Impact Assessment changes, and update log source configurations accordingly.

Calculate log volume per source, including peak performance periods (e.g., open enrollment), and allocate storage capacity of at least ninety (90) days plus any additional organization-defined retention requirements ([Additional Retention Period]).
Provision the capacity in the log repository ([SIEM] / [Log Storage Platform]) and verify headroom before adding new log sources.
Re-verify allocated capacity against actual consumption whenever a new source is onboarded, and record the result in the Log source inventory and coverage report.
Configure [SIEM] to alert the system administrator and ISSO (as defined in the SSPP) in near real time upon detection of an audit logging process failure.

Upon a confirmed logging process failure, either shut down the affected system or halt processing immediately, or — for systems that do not support automatic shutdown — shut down the system within one (1) hour of the audit processing failure.

Take the configured additional action for the failure type ([Additional Failure Action], e.g., overwriting the oldest audit records, shutting down the system, or stopping audit record generation), selected by the Detection & Response analyst responding to the alert.
Record every failure, alert, and response action in [Ticketing System].
Configure the log repository to warn [Warning Recipients] within [Warning Time Period] when allocated audit log storage reaches [Storage Warning Percentage] of maximum capacity.

Define the audit failure events requiring real-time alerts ([Real-Time Alert Failure Events]) and configure [SIEM] to alert [Real-Time Alert Recipients] within [Real-Time Alert Period] when those events occur.
Include these alert configurations in the Alert tuning and review records.

Configure configurable network communications traffic volume thresholds reflecting limits on audit log storage capacity in [Network Controls], and set the enforcement action to reject, delay, or both ([Threshold Enforcement Selection]) for traffic above those thresholds.

Define the audit logging failures that invoke a shutdown response ([Shutdown-Triggering Failures]) and configure the response — full system shutdown, partial system shutdown, or degraded operational mode with limited mission/business functionality ([Shutdown Mode Selection]) — unless an alternate audit logging capability exists.
Deploy and maintain an alternate audit logging capability that implements [Alternate Logging Functionality], and verify the failover path by testing it [Alternate Logging Test Frequency].
Record threshold, shutdown, and failover configuration details in the Alert tuning and review records.

Review and analyze system audit records no less often than weekly (every seven [7] days) for indications of inappropriate or unusual activity, covering at minimum: initialization sequences; logons (successful and unsuccessful); errors; system processes; security software; applications; performance; system resource utilization; network traffic; bandwidth utilization rates; alert notifications; border defense devices; and creation of unauthorized administrator, system, and privileged application accounts.
Assess the potential impact of any identified inappropriate or unusual activity.
Report findings to [Finding Recipients] (e.g., ISSO, System Owner) via [Ticketing System].

Adjust the level of audit record review, analysis, and reporting when there is a change in risk based on law enforcement information, intelligence information, or other credible sources; document the adjustment and its justification.
Treat audit record review, analysis, and reporting as vulnerability detection: follow all applicable Vulnerability Detection and Response rules for findings produced by this step.

Investigate suspicious activity or suspected violations on the information system, report findings to appropriate officials, and take appropriate action, recording each investigation in [Ticketing System].

For cloud environments, document and accept the coordination between the service provider and the organization; in multi-tenant environments, document the capability and means for providing review, analysis, and reporting of consumer data in the System Security and Privacy Plan.
Retain each weekly review record as part of the Alert tuning and review records.

Integrate audit record review, analysis, and reporting using automated mechanisms ([SIEM] and/or [CDM Tools]) to the fullest extent possible, ensuring the mechanisms support investigation and response to suspicious activities.

Onboard audit record sources from systems, appliances, devices, services, and applications (including databases), including integrated audit records from automated information security capabilities and service tools, and verify the records in [SIEM] are searchable.

Configure [SIEM] correlation rules to analyze and correlate audit records across different repositories to gain organization-wide situational awareness, and confirm the central capability to review and analyze audit records from multiple system components.

Integrate analysis of audit records with analysis of [Integrated Analysis Sources] (e.g., vulnerability scanning information, performance data, system monitoring information); treat resulting findings as vulnerability detection subject to the Vulnerability Detection and Response rules.
Correlate audit record information with information obtained from monitoring physical access to enhance detection of suspicious, inappropriate, unusual, or malevolent activity.

Specify and document the permitted actions for each system process, role, and user associated with the review, analysis, and reporting of audit record information; configure role permissions in [SIEM] accordingly.
Perform full text analysis of logged privileged commands in a physically distinct component or subsystem, or in another system dedicated to that analysis ([Privileged Command Analysis Platform]).

Correlate nontechnical source information (e.g., HR notifications, physical access records) with audit record information to enhance organization-wide situational awareness, documenting the correlation method in the Alert tuning and review records.

Configure [SIEM] to provide audit record reduction and report generation supporting on-demand review, analysis, reporting, and after-the-fact incident investigation, without altering the original content or time ordering of audit records.
Configure search and sort capability over the organization-defined selectable event criteria and fields within audit records ([Searchable Audit Fields]).

Validate the reduction and reporting capability does not modify originals by comparing generated reports against raw records [Reduction Validation Frequency], and record the validation in the Alert tuning and review records.
Configure all audit-generating components to use internal system clocks synchronized to [Time Synchronization Service] for audit record time stamps.

Record time stamps with a granularity of [Time Measurement Granularity], either in Coordinated Universal Time, with a fixed local time offset from UTC, or including the local time offset in the stamp; in all cases they must be mappable to UTC or GMT and accurate to within one hundred (100) milliseconds.
Verify clock synchronization and accuracy across log sources [Time Sync Verification Frequency] and correct any drifting source immediately.

Configure access controls on [SIEM] and all audit logging tools to protect audit information from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion, and configure alerts to [Audit Protection Alert Recipients] (e.g., system administrator or ISSO per the SSPP) upon detection of unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of audit information.
Where the platform supports it, write audit trails to hardware-enforced, write-once media ([Write-Once Media Platform]).

Store audit records [Offload Frequency] in a repository that is part of a physically different system or system component than the system being audited, running a different operating system than the audited component.
Implement cryptographic mechanisms (e.g., hashing or signing in [SIEM] / [Log Storage Platform]) to protect the integrity of audit information and audit tools.

Restrict management of audit logging functionality to the subset of privileged users or roles defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan — preferably individuals or roles not subject to audit by that system — by configuring role assignments in [SIEM].
Enforce dual authorization, via [SIEM] workflow or [Ticketing System] approval, for movement and/or deletion of audit information ([Dual Auth Operations Selection], [Dual Auth Data Scope]).
Grant read-only access to audit information to the subset of privileged users or roles defined as [Read-Only Audit Roles].

Implement mechanisms providing irrefutable evidence that an individual (or process acting on behalf of an individual) has performed the organization-defined covered actions, which must include at minimum the addition, modification, deletion, approval, sending, or receiving of data, and — for ACA systems — eligibility and enrollment functions including applying for advance payments of the Advance Premium Tax Credit and Cost-sharing Reductions, applying for enrollment in Qualified Health Plans, completing enrollment in Qualified Health Plans, and providing related Customer Service, with covered actions defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.

Bind the identity of the information producer to the information at [Binding Strength], using signing or equivalent mechanisms, and provide authorized individuals the means to determine the identity of the producer.
Validate the producer-identity binding at [Binding Validation Frequency] and perform [Binding Error Actions] in the event of a validation error.
Maintain reviewer or releaser credentials within the established chain of custody for information reviewed or released.

Validate the binding of the information reviewer's identity to the information at transfer or release points, prior to release or transfer between [Security Domains], and perform [Reviewer Validation Error Actions] on validation failure.
Retain audit records for ninety (90) days in the searchable live tier of [SIEM].
Archive records older than ninety (90) days for ten (10) years, consistent with the records retention policy per the ACA retention rule (45 CFR §155.1210).

When records are subject to a legal investigation (e.g., Insider Threat), maintain them in place until released by the investigating authority; place a legal hold in [Ticketing System] and confirm with [Legal Counsel].
Retain audit inspection reports, including a record of corrective actions, for a minimum of three (3) years from the date the inspection was completed.

Ensure long-term records remain retrievable by converting records to newer formats as needed, retaining equipment capable of reading them, and retaining the documentation needed to interpret them; verify retrievability of archived records [Archive Retrieval Test Frequency].

Enable audit record generation for the event types identified in the auditable-event selection on at least all information system and network components where audit capability is deployed or available.

Permit the personnel or roles defined as [Event Selection Roles] to select the event types logged by specific system components, and generate records for the selected event types containing the audit record content defined in the audit record content requirements.
Compile audit records from [Compiled Components] into a system-wide (logical or physical) audit trail time-correlated to within [Correlation Tolerance].
Produce the system-wide audit trail in a standardized format (e.g., the [SIEM] normalized schema) and verify format compliance for each onboarded source.

Provide the capability for [Dynamic Logging Roles] to change logging on [Dynamic Logging Components] based on [Selectable Event Criteria] within [Dynamic Logging Time Thresholds]; document any such change in [Ticketing System].

Implement the capability to audit the parameters of user query events for data sets containing personally identifiable information, and confirm query-parameter logging is active on all PII data stores.

Operate system monitoring on a continuous basis, with monitoring objectives aligned to the organization's incident response policy and procedures (per IR-1), to detect attacks and indicators of potential attacks and to detect unauthorized local, network, and remote connections.
Identify unauthorized use of the system using the techniques and methods documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.

Invoke internal monitoring capabilities and strategically deploy monitoring devices within the system to collect essential information, and deploy at ad hoc locations to track specific types of transactions of interest.
Analyze detected events and anomalies in [SIEM]; triage each and open a ticket in [Ticketing System] for anything requiring investigation.

Adjust the level of system monitoring activity when there is a change in risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation; document each adjustment in the Alert tuning and review records.
Maintain the legal opinion regarding system monitoring activities with [Legal Counsel], and refresh it when monitoring scope changes.
Provide [Monitoring Information Outputs] to [Monitoring Information Recipients] as needed and consistent with the frequency documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.
Follow all applicable rules within the Vulnerability Detection and Response and Incident Communication Procedure guidance for all monitoring findings.

Operate a centrally managed IDS/IPS capability ([IDS/IPS Platform]) monitoring network communications on all networks and subnets, using centrally managed devices at network perimeter points (including between zones) and/or centrally managed host-based sensor agents in components where agents are available.
For zones where communications are encrypted, configure mechanisms capable of either decrypting content for analysis or analyzing content before transmission or after receipt.
Document any components that do not support host-based IDS/IPS sensors in the applicable risk assessment and System Security and Privacy Plan.
Connect and configure individual intrusion detection tools into the system-wide intrusion detection system, and ensure raw intrusion detection information remains available in an unaltered format.

Operate automated tools supporting near real-time analysis of events; verify aggregated intrusion detection information is searchable, provided in the organization-defined compliant format, sourced from all network- and host-based IDS/IPS capabilities on all networks and subnets, and that organization-directed collection rules/requests are implemented within the specified timeframe.
Integrate intrusion detection tools and mechanisms with access control and flow control mechanisms.

Configure alerts to [Compromise Alert Recipients] (documented in the SSPP) when the following indicators occur: malicious code, unauthorized export of information, signaling to an external information system, or potential intrusions; handle malicious code detections consistent with the SI-3 malicious code response.

Follow the Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules for all IDS/IPS findings, and support sharing of threat awareness information in a format meeting CMS requirements.

Determine criteria for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions for inbound and outbound communications traffic, and monitor inbound and outbound traffic on a continuous basis against those criteria.
Analyze outbound communications traffic at the external interfaces to the system and at [Interior Analysis Points] to discover anomalies and to detect covert exfiltration of information.

Analyze communications traffic and event patterns, develop profiles representing common traffic and event patterns, and use those profiles in tuning system-monitoring devices; record each tuning change in the Alert tuning and review records.
Notify [Incident Response Personnel] of detected suspicious events and take the configured least-disruptive actions upon detection; open a ticket in [Ticketing System] for each notification.

Configure automated alerting mechanisms ([SIEM] / [IDS/IPS Platform]) to alert [Activity Alert Recipients] when the following indications of inappropriate or unusual activities with security or privacy implications occur: [Alert-Triggering Activities].

Detect network services that have not been authorized or approved by the organization's authorization or approval processes, and when detected, audit and/or alert [Unauthorized Service Alert Recipients] per the configured selection ([Unauthorized Service Action]).
Test intrusion-monitoring tools and mechanisms at [Tool Testing Frequency] and record each test and result in the Alert tuning and review records.
Make provisions so that [Encrypted Communications Traffic] is visible to [Monitoring Tools] (e.g., via TLS inspection or pre/post-encryption analysis per the IDS/IPS configuration).

Correlate information from monitoring tools and mechanisms employed throughout the system, and correlate physical, cyber, and supply chain monitoring information to achieve integrated, organization-wide situational awareness.

Provide visibility into network traffic at external and key internal system interfaces (e.g., via [Network Visibility Tooling] / SPAN or TAP configuration) to optimize the effectiveness of monitoring devices.

Employ a wireless intrusion detection system ([Wireless IDS]) to identify rogue wireless devices and detect attack attempts and potential compromises or breaches, covering both external monitoring (events at system boundaries) and internal monitoring (events within the system).
Configure the intrusion detection capability to monitor wireless communications traffic as it passes from wireless to wireline networks.
Route wireless IDS alerts into [SIEM] and handle them through the same triage and notification steps as other compromise indicators.
Implement the additional monitoring defined as [Increased-Risk Monitoring] for individuals identified by [Increased-Risk Sources] as posing an increased level of risk.

Implement the additional monitoring defined as [Privileged User Monitoring] for privileged users, and the additional monitoring defined as [Probationary Monitoring] for individuals during [Probationary Period].

Deploy host-based monitoring mechanisms — specifically IDS/IPS per ARC-AMPE — at [Host-Based Monitoring Components], including but not limited to systems, appliances, devices, services, and applications.
Document any devices and appliances that do not support a host-based IDS/IPS sensor capability in the applicable information system risk assessment and System Security and Privacy Plan.
Discover, collect, and distribute indicators of compromise provided by [IOC Sources] to [IOC Recipients] on an ongoing basis, recording distribution in [Ticketing System].

The Detection & Response team is accountable for this procedure end to end: it operates the logging, monitoring, and alerting capabilities, performs reviews, produces the Log source inventory and coverage report and Alert tuning and review records, and manages handoffs to other teams.

System Owners, the ISSO, the Designated Official, the Authorizing Official, the Privacy Officer, and [Legal Counsel] participate as approvers, reviewers, or recipients as specified in individual steps; exceptions to this procedure require review and approval by the Designated Official, in coordination with the Privacy Officer where PII is affected.

analyze: Executing this procedure delivers, maintains, and evidences Example Org's security awareness and training program so that every workforce member — including management, senior executives, and contractors — receives the literacy, role-based, and privacy training required by the Workforce Security Training Standard.
It also produces the retained evidence of training delivery and awareness testing, including the Training completion report and Phishing simulation results.

The Security Awareness team performs this procedure end to end on behalf of Example Org, covering all employees, managers, senior executives, and contractors who access, use, manage, or develop organizational systems or process PII.
Participants include [Human Resources], [Identity Provider] administrators, and people managers, who act on handoffs owned by Security Awareness.
- Access to the [Learning Management System] with the ability to assign courses, view completion status, and export reports.
- Access to the [Phishing Simulation Platform] for creating and launching simulated phishing exercises.
- Access to the [Documentation Repository] where the awareness and training policy, procedures, and records are maintained.
- Access to the [Identity Provider] to verify account status and, where required, disable accounts of personnel who have not completed role-based training.
- Access to the [Human Resources System] to identify new hires, role changes, and contractor onboarding events.
- A designated [Designated Training Official] responsible for the awareness and training policy and procedures.
- An active ticketing queue in the [Ticketing System] for tracking training assignments, escalations, and remediation actions.

Security Awareness drafts or updates the organization-level security awareness and training policy so that it addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance.

Security Awareness verifies the policy is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, and that it is written at the organization level as ARC-AMPE requires.

Security Awareness stores the approved policy in the [Documentation Repository] and disseminates it to the organization-defined personnel and roles (management, [Human Resources], system owners, and all workforce members via the [Learning Management System] announcement channel).
Security Awareness records the publication date and distribution list in the [Documentation Repository] as part of the written record required for this activity.
Security Awareness documents the step-by-step procedures (this document) that facilitate implementation of the awareness and training policy and the associated awareness and training controls.
Security Awareness publishes the procedures to the [Documentation Repository] and makes them available to every person responsible for implementing them (see Step 5).
Security Awareness records the version, approval date, and dissemination actions for the procedures in the [Documentation Repository].
Example Org designates the [Designated Training Official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the awareness and training policy and procedures.
Security Awareness records the designation — the named individual, their role, and the effective date — in the [Documentation Repository].
Security Awareness updates the designation record whenever the official changes, and re-disseminates the policy and procedures under the new official's authority.

Security Awareness reviews and updates the awareness and training policy at least annually, and following [Assignment: organization-defined events] (for example, regulatory change, audit findings, or significant incidents).
Security Awareness reviews and updates the awareness and training procedures on the same cycle: at least annually and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

Security Awareness actively monitors for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect the awareness and training policies, using [Regulatory Monitoring Source], and logs each identified change in the [Ticketing System].

For each logged change, Security Awareness assesses whether the policy and procedures still support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards throughout the system life cycle and the life cycle of the information on those systems, and updates the documents accordingly.

Security Awareness additionally reviews the documentation periodically and updates it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii)].
Security Awareness records each review — date, reviewer, changes made, or a determination that no changes were needed — in the [Documentation Repository].

Security Awareness maintains all policies and procedures in written (electronic) form in the [Documentation Repository], and maintains a written (electronic permitted) record of every action, activity, or assessment required to be documented under this procedure.

Security Awareness retains each required documentation item — including the Training completion report and Phishing simulation results — for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
Security Awareness configures access to the [Documentation Repository] so that persons responsible for implementing the procedures can retrieve the documentation that pertains to their duties.
Security Awareness operates a security awareness and training program covering all members of the workforce, including management.

When [Human Resources] onboards a new user, Security Awareness assigns the security and privacy literacy training course in the [Learning Management System] as part of initial training; the audience includes managers, senior executives, and contractors.
Security Awareness requires each new user to complete the initial literacy training and tracks completion in the [Learning Management System].
Security Awareness assigns refresher literacy training to all system users at least annually thereafter and tracks completion the same way.
On completion of each training cycle, Security Awareness exports the Training completion report from the [Learning Management System] and files it in the [Documentation Repository] per Step 5.

Security Awareness provides additional literacy training when required by system changes or following [Assignment: organization-defined events], including assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Security Awareness updates literacy training and awareness content at least annually and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

After each internal or external security incident or breach, Security Awareness reviews the incident record in the [Ticketing System], extracts lessons learned, and incorporates them into the literacy training content and awareness techniques.
Security Awareness records each content update — trigger, date, and change summary — in the [Documentation Repository].

Security Awareness employs the organization-defined awareness techniques — including phishing email tests and other [Assignment: organization-defined awareness techniques] — to increase the security and privacy awareness of system users.
Security Awareness builds a simulated phishing campaign in the [Phishing Simulation Platform], targeting the user population defined for the campaign.
Security Awareness launches the campaign, monitors click and reporting behavior in the platform, and identifies users who require remedial coaching.
Security Awareness exports the Phishing simulation results from the [Phishing Simulation Platform] and files them in the [Documentation Repository] per Step 5.
Security Awareness feeds identified weaknesses from the simulation results into the training content update cycle in Step 7.
Security Awareness includes, within the information security and privacy education and awareness training, the individual's responsibilities associated with sending sensitive information in email.
Security Awareness verifies the course module covering email handling is present in the [Learning Management System] curriculum before each annual training cycle opens.
Security Awareness coordinates with [Human Resources] and system owners to identify all systems that collect, maintain, store, use, or disclose Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
For all employees and contractors who require access to those systems, Security Awareness ensures privacy training is completed before access to organizational systems and networks is granted.

Security Awareness confirms with the [Identity Provider] administrators that access provisioning is gated on recorded privacy training completion, and escalates any gap through the [Ticketing System].

Security Awareness includes practical exercises in literacy training that simulate events and incidents [NIST AT-2(1)], using the [Phishing Simulation Platform] and [Tabletop Exercise Materials] to reinforce recognition and reporting behaviors.

Security Awareness delivers literacy training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat, including how to communicate employee and management concerns about potential insider threat indicators through appropriate organizational channels in accordance with established organizational policies and procedures [NIST AT-2(2) | ARC-AMPE AT-2(2)].

Security Awareness delivers literacy training on recognizing and reporting potential and actual instances of social engineering and social mining, including how to recognize and report — through appropriate organizational and defined channels (e.g., applicable security and privacy plans) — attempts to trick an individual into revealing information or taking an action that can be used to breach, compromise, or otherwise adversely impact a system [NIST AT-2(3) | ARC-AMPE AT-2(3)].

Security Awareness delivers literacy training on recognizing suspicious communications and anomalous behavior in organizational systems using organization-defined indicators of malicious code, covering potentially suspicious email or web communications (e.g., an unexpected email, an email with strange or poor grammar, or an email from an unfamiliar sender appearing to be a known sponsor or contractor) and anomalous behaviors in systems, and how to report them through appropriate organizational and defined channels [NIST AT-2(4) | ARC-AMPE AT-2(4)].

Security Awareness delivers literacy training on the advanced persistent threat (APT), including techniques for recognizing suspicious emails, use of removable systems in non-secure settings, the potential targeting of individuals at home, and the ways APTs can infiltrate the organization (e.g., through websites, emails, advertisement pop-ups, articles, and social engineering) [NIST AT-2(5) | ARC-AMPE AT-2(5)].

Security Awareness delivers literacy training on the cyber threat environment and coordinates with [Threat Intelligence Function] to reflect current cyber threat information in system operations [NIST AT-2(6)].

Security Awareness confirms each module above is present and current in the [Learning Management System] curriculum before each annual training cycle and records the confirmation in the [Documentation Repository].

Security Awareness implements periodic security updates (security reminders) to all workforce members through [Communication Channel], on the cadence defined by the Standard's periodic reminder requirement [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(A)].
Security Awareness includes reminders covering procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(B)].
Security Awareness includes reminders covering procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(C)].
Security Awareness includes reminders covering procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords [HIPAA 164.308(a)(5)(ii)(D)].
Security Awareness retains copies of each reminder and its distribution record in the [Documentation Repository].
Security Awareness identifies, with system owners, the significant information security and privacy roles and responsibilities requiring role-based training.

Before authorizing access to the system or information or performing assigned duties, Security Awareness assigns the applicable role-based training in the [Learning Management System] to personnel in those roles and confirms completion.
Security Awareness assigns role-based refresher training at least annually thereafter.

Security Awareness assigns additional role-based training when required by system changes; when an employee enters a new position that requires additional role-specific training; and when significant information system or system environment changes occur.

Security Awareness updates role-based training content at least annually and following [Assignment: organization-defined events], including significant changes to the system or the system environment.
After each internal or external security incident or breach, Security Awareness incorporates the lessons learned into role-based training content.
Security Awareness exports role-based training completion data into the Training completion report and files it in the [Documentation Repository] per Step 5.

Security Awareness monitors role-based training completion in the [Learning Management System] and flags personnel with significant information security and privacy roles who have not completed required training within the mandated timeframes.
Security Awareness notifies the flagged individual and their manager through the [Ticketing System] that completion is required.
If the requirement remains unmet, Security Awareness requests that [Identity Provider] administrators disable the user's account until the role-based training requirement is met.

Security Awareness confirms with [Identity Provider] administrators that the account is re-enabled only after the individual has completed the required training, and records the disablement and re-enablement actions in the [Ticketing System].

Security Awareness provides the organization-defined personnel or roles with initial training — and refresher training at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] — in the employment and operation of environmental controls [NIST AT-3(1)].

Security Awareness provides the organization-defined personnel or roles with initial training — and refresher training at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] — in the employment and operation of physical security controls [NIST AT-3(2)].
Security Awareness includes practical exercises in security and privacy training that reinforce training objectives [NIST AT-3(3)].

Security Awareness provides organizational personnel — including vendors, contractors, and employees — with initial training, and refresher training at least annually thereafter, in the employment and operation of personally identifiable information processing and transparency controls [NIST AT-3(5) | ARC-AMPE AT-3(5)].

Security Awareness develops and implements a privacy education and awareness training program for all employees and individuals working on behalf of the organization involved in managing, using, and/or processing PII; this program may be integrated with the general cybersecurity training.
Security Awareness includes responsibilities associated with sending PII in email within the privacy education and awareness training.
Security Awareness ensures privacy communications and training are job-specific and commensurate with each employee's responsibilities, tailoring modules by role in the [Learning Management System].

Security Awareness ensures initial training of employees (including managers) on their privacy responsibilities is completed before permitting access to organizational information and systems, with refresher training completed every one (1) year thereafter.

Security Awareness ensures any additional or advanced training provided is commensurate with the individual's responsibilities and level of PII access, and records the tailoring decisions in the [Documentation Repository].
Security Awareness files the privacy program's completion data into the Training completion report per Step 5.

The Security Awareness team owns and executes every step of this procedure end to end, including all handoffs to [Human Resources], [Identity Provider] administrators, system owners, and people managers.

Exceptions to any step — including deferrals of training deadlines or hold-open requests for accounts flagged in Step 14 — must be reviewed and approved by [Executive Approver], with the exception record retained per Step 5.
This procedure operationalizes the **Workforce Security Training Standard**, which contains the full requirement text, the control definitions, and the rationale for each step above.

analyze: Executing this procedure develops, documents, disseminates, and maintains Example Org's incident response policy and its supporting implementation procedures, ensuring they remain compliant with applicable laws and regulations and effective against current threats.
It establishes the named ownership, review cadence, and privacy guidance integration required for the organization's incident response program.

This procedure is performed by Security Operations, which is accountable end to end for incident response policy and procedure lifecycle management, on a continuous basis across Example Org at the organization level.
It covers the incident response policy document, its implementing procedures, and the review and update activities that keep both current.
- Access to the organization's document management and publication system ([Document Management System]) for drafting, versioning, and disseminating the policy and procedures.
- A formally designated official responsible for the incident response policy and procedures, named in the appropriate security and privacy documents ([Designated IR Policy Official]).
- A named point of contact in the privacy office for PII-related incident handling guidance ([Privacy Office]).
- Access to incident tickets with timelines and the most recent tabletop exercise report for event-triggered reviews ([Incident Management System], [Exercise Records Repository]).
- Awareness of current applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines governing incident response.

Security Operations drafts the incident response policy, ensuring it explicitly addresses each required element: purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance.

Cross-check each policy element against applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines to confirm consistency, and record the sources consulted in the policy document's references section.
Submit the draft to the [Designated IR Policy Official] for review and to management for sign-off evidencing management commitment.
Publish the approved policy in the [Document Management System] as a versioned document.
Author the policy as an organization-level policy document, per the ARC-AMPE requirement, rather than scoping it to a single mission/business process or system.
Verify the policy's stated scope covers all Example Org personnel and systems subject to incident response obligations.
If any mission/business process-level or system-level supplements exist, confirm they align with and do not contradict the organization-level policy.
Security Operations develops procedures that operationalize each requirement of the incident response policy and its associated incident response controls.
Map each procedure section to the specific policy provision and control it implements so traceability between policy, procedures, and controls is explicit.
Publish the procedures alongside the policy in the [Document Management System] under version control.

Confirm the [Designated IR Policy Official] assigned to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the incident response policy and procedures is recorded by name in the appropriate security and privacy documents, as ARC-AMPE requires.
Record the designated official's name and role in the policy document's header/metadata block.

Security Operations disseminates the approved policy and procedures to all applicable personnel and roles using the [Document Management System] distribution workflow, and tracks acknowledgement of receipt.
Re-disseminate each time a new or updated version is published.
Security Operations reviews and updates the incident response policy and procedures on the organization-defined schedule ([Review Frequency]).

Trigger an out-of-cycle review following any organization-defined event, including assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines.
Record the review outcome — date, reviewer, changes made, and rationale — in the document's version history.
At least every one (1) year, Security Operations conducts a full review of the incident response policy and procedures, and updates them as needed.

Following any assessment or audit finding, security incident, or privacy incident, pull the relevant incident tickets with timelines (or audit/assessment findings) from the [Incident Management System] and the most recent tabletop exercise report, and evaluate whether the policy and procedures performed as written.
Where the review identifies gaps, Security Operations updates the policy or procedures, obtains [Designated IR Policy Official] approval, and re-disseminates per the dissemination steps above.
Retain each annual review record and its supporting artifacts (incident tickets with timelines, tabletop exercise report) as evidence of the review.

On a continuous basis, Security Operations actively monitors for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching organizational policy that affect the incident response policy, using [Legal/Regulatory Monitoring Source].
When a change is identified, log it in a change-tracking record ([Ticketing System]) and assess its impact on the incident response policy and procedures.

At least every one (1) year, review the accumulated change record and confirm the incident response policies and procedures remain effective in light of those changes, documenting the effectiveness determination in the review record.
Obtain written guidance from the [Privacy Office] on handling incidents involving Personally Identifiable Information (PII), including any support the privacy office requires during such incidents.
Incorporate that guidance directly into the incident response policy and procedures as a dedicated PII incident handling section.
Re-engage the [Privacy Office] whenever the policy or procedures are updated, to confirm the PII guidance remains accurate and complete.
Security Operations is authorized to develop, document, disseminate, review, and update the incident response policy and procedures and owns this process end to end.

The [Designated IR Policy Official] approves policy content and is named in the security and privacy documents, the [Privacy Office] provides and validates PII incident handling guidance, and exceptions to any step in this procedure require review and approval by the [Designated IR Policy Official].

analyze: This procedure gives Network Security the concrete, repeatable steps needed to authorize, configure, monitor, and terminate remote, wireless, mobile, and third-party/external-system access to Example Org systems, and to keep the resulting records current and auditable.

This procedure applies to Network Security personnel and any other Example Org staff, contractors, or third parties who configure, approve, or use remote access, wireless access, mobile devices, or external systems to connect to or exchange data with Example Org systems.
- Approved access to the [VPN/Remote Access Gateway] administrative console
- Approved access to the [Network Access Control System] used to manage authorized access control points
- Approved access to the [Wireless Access Point Management Console]
- Approved access to the [Mobile Device Management (MDM) Platform]
- Approved access to the [Identity Provider] for authentication configuration and user/device authorization records
- Approved access to the [Ticketing System] for tracking authorization requests, exceptions, and remediation
- A current, maintained Third-party access register
- A current record of VPN and remote-access configuration baselines
- Written sign-off authority identified for the Authorizing Official (AO) or designated representative
- Access to the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan for the system in scope
- Access to [Legal Counsel] for review of binding agreements involving personally owned devices or PII handling
- Access to the [Third-Party Risk Management System] or equivalent register for tracking external-party connection agreements
Network Security enumerates every remote access method in use or proposed (e.g., VPN client, remote desktop gateway) and records it in the VPN and remote-access configuration documentation.
For each method, Network Security documents usage restrictions, connection requirements, and implementation guidance in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.
Network Security submits each remote access type to the AO or designated representative for authorization via the [Ticketing System] before any connections of that type are permitted.
Network Security records the authorization decision and date in the VPN and remote-access configuration record.
Network Security reviews this authorization list [Review Frequency] and updates it when new remote access types are proposed.
Network Security configures the [VPN/Remote Access Gateway] to log all remote connection attempts, successes, and failures automatically.

Network Security configures automated alerting for anomalous remote access patterns (e.g., off-hours logins, impossible travel) within the [VPN/Remote Access Gateway] or connected [Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) System].
Network Security reviews automated monitoring output on a quarterly basis and logs the review in the [Ticketing System].
Network Security escalates any control failures found during review through the [Ticketing System] for remediation.
Network Security configures the [VPN/Remote Access Gateway] to require cryptographic protection (encryption) for the confidentiality and integrity of all remote sessions.

Network Security verifies the encryption protocol and cipher suite in use meet the applicable FIPS 140-compliant encryption standard and records this configuration in the VPN and remote-access configuration.
Network Security disables any legacy or unencrypted remote access protocols identified during configuration review.
Network Security re-verifies encryption settings whenever the [VPN/Remote Access Gateway] firmware or software is updated.
Network Security identifies and documents all authorized network access control points (e.g., VPN concentrators, gateways) in the VPN and remote-access configuration.
Network Security configures network routing and firewall rules so that all remote access traffic must pass through one of the documented access control points.
Network Security blocks direct remote access paths that bypass these control points.
Network Security reviews access control point configuration quarterly to confirm no unauthorized paths have been introduced.

Network Security identifies which privileged commands and security-relevant information may be accessed remotely and documents the [Approved Remote Access Needs] in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.
Before granting such access, Network Security requires the requestor to submit justification through the [Ticketing System], describing the compelling operational need.
Network Security or the AO approves or denies the request and records the rationale in the System Security and Privacy Plan.

Network Security configures the [VPN/Remote Access Gateway] or privileged access tooling to log privileged remote command execution in a format that provides assessable evidence (e.g., session recording, command logging).
Network Security retains these logs alongside the VPN and remote-access configuration record.

Network Security restricts access to remote access configuration files, connection strings, and topology diagrams to authorized Network Security personnel only, enforced through the [Identity Provider] role assignments.
Network Security stores remote access mechanism documentation (VPN and remote-access configuration) in a system with access controls and audit logging.
Network Security reviews access permissions to this documentation quarterly and removes access for personnel who no longer require it.
Network Security configures the [VPN/Remote Access Gateway] with the administrative capability to disconnect or disable any remote access session or account on demand.

Upon receipt of a disconnect order from an authorized official (via the [Ticketing System] or direct notification), Network Security disables or terminates the specified remote access within one (1) hour.
For system-to-system interconnections, Network Security terminates or suspends the connection within one (1) hour of the order being issued.
Network Security logs the disconnection action, the time of the order, and the time of completion in the [Ticketing System] and updates the VPN and remote-access configuration record accordingly.
Network Security identifies the [Remote Commands Requiring Authentication] that require authentication prior to execution.
Network Security implements the [Authentication Mechanism for Remote Commands] (e.g., signed command tokens, multi-factor challenge) on the systems that accept those commands.
Network Security tests the authentication mechanism during configuration changes to confirm unauthenticated remote commands are rejected.
Network Security documents the mechanism and covered commands in the VPN and remote-access configuration.

Network Security, in coordination with the applicable facilities/compliance function, documents the proper functions permitted on workstations or workstation classes that can access electronic protected health information (ePHI).
Network Security documents the manner in which those functions must be performed (e.g., screen-lock timeout, prohibited peripherals).
Network Security documents the required physical attributes of the surroundings for such workstations (e.g., screen positioning away from public view, physical access restrictions).
Network Security distributes these workstation-use requirements to system owners and verifies implementation during quarterly access reviews.

Network Security enumerates each type of wireless access in use or proposed and documents configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.
Network Security submits each wireless access type to the AO for authorization via the [Ticketing System] before deployment.
Network Security records the authorization in the VPN and remote-access configuration (or equivalent wireless configuration record).
Network Security reviews authorized wireless access types quarterly.
Network Security configures the [Wireless Access Point Management Console] to require authentication of both users and devices before granting wireless network access.
Network Security configures wireless encryption using the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standard.
Network Security verifies encryption and authentication settings during configuration audits and records findings in the [Ticketing System].
Network Security remediates any access point found using non-compliant authentication or encryption settings before returning it to service.
Network Security identifies system components with embedded wireless networking capability during procurement or provisioning intake.
Network Security disables embedded wireless capability on any component not intended to use wireless prior to issuance or deployment.
Network Security records the disablement action in the asset/configuration record.
Network Security verifies wireless capability remains disabled during periodic configuration checks.
Network Security identifies users who require the ability to independently configure wireless networking capabilities.
Network Security submits these users for explicit authorization via the [Ticketing System], approved by the AO or designated representative.
Network Security grants the corresponding configuration privilege through the [Identity Provider] only after authorization is recorded.
Network Security reviews the list of authorized users quarterly and revokes privileges no longer needed.
Network Security selects radio antennas and transmission power settings for each wireless access point to minimize signal propagation outside organization-controlled boundaries.
Network Security tests signal strength at the perimeter of organization-controlled areas after installation or reconfiguration.
Network Security adjusts antenna type or power calibration if signal is detected beyond the controlled boundary.
Network Security documents the calibration settings in the wireless configuration record.

Network Security documents configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for organization-controlled mobile devices, including use outside controlled areas, in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.
Network Security submits mobile device connection types for AO authorization via the [Ticketing System] before allowing connections.
Network Security enrolls authorized mobile devices in the [Mobile Device Management (MDM) Platform] and applies the documented configuration.
Network Security records authorized mobile device types and configurations in the asset/configuration record.
Network Security identifies facilities containing systems that process, store, or transmit classified information.
Network Security prohibits unclassified mobile devices in those facilities unless the AO specifically permits use.

For permitted exceptions, Network Security configures the [Mobile Device Management (MDM) Platform] to prevent connection of unclassified mobile devices to classified systems, and requires AO written approval before connecting to unclassified systems.
Network Security disables internal and external modems and wireless interfaces on permitted unclassified mobile devices via the [Mobile Device Management (MDM) Platform].
Network Security coordinates with designated security officials to conduct random reviews/inspections of unclassified mobile devices and their stored information.
If classified information is discovered on an unclassified device, Network Security follows the organization's incident handling policy and logs the event in the [Ticketing System].
Network Security restricts connection of classified mobile devices to classified systems according to the organization-defined security policy governing those systems.

Network Security configures full-device encryption or container-based encryption on the [Mobile Devices Subject to Encryption Requirement] using the [Mobile Device Management (MDM) Platform], applying the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standard.
Network Security verifies that any mobile device storing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) has encryption enabled before allowing it to connect.
Network Security records encryption status per device in the [Mobile Device Management (MDM) Platform] and reconciles it against the asset/configuration record quarterly.
Network Security remediates any device found without required encryption before permitting further access.
Network Security identifies external systems that authorized individuals may use to access Example Org systems or to process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information.

Network Security establishes and documents the [Assignment: Organization-Defined Terms and Conditions] and/or the required controls to be implemented on each external system, consistent with the trust relationship established with the owning organization.
Network Security records these terms in the Third-party access register.
Network Security identifies and documents the [Prohibited External System Types] that are not permitted to connect under any circumstances.

Network Security cross-references entries in the Third-party access register against related CA-3 interconnection agreements and SA-9 external-provider responsibility records to keep the three control areas (AC-20, CA-3, SA-9) consistent and non-duplicative.
Before permitting use of an external system, Network Security verifies that the controls required by organizational security and privacy policies/plans are implemented on that external system, or
Network Security retains an approved system connection or processing agreement with the entity hosting the external system.
Network Security records the verification result or the retained agreement in the Third-party access register.
Network Security re-verifies controls or agreement validity [Review Frequency] and updates the register accordingly.
Network Security documents the [Portable Storage Device Restrictions] for organization-controlled portable storage devices used on external systems in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.

Network Security prohibits such use unless: the use is documented in the security/privacy plan; the AO or designated representative has authorized it in writing; any personally owned device to which the storage device is attached complies with organizational policy on personally owned systems; and appropriate safeguards commensurate with data sensitivity are applied.
Network Security records each approved exception in the Third-party access register, including the written AO authorization.
Network Security reviews approved exceptions quarterly to confirm continued compliance.

Network Security documents the [Assignment: Organization-Defined Restrictions] applicable to non-organizationally owned systems or components used to process, store, or transmit organizational information.
For contractor-owned devices, Network Security confirms the device is documented in the contract and applicable security/privacy plans and has written AO authorization before granting access.

For personally owned devices, Network Security confirms compliance with organizational policy on personally owned systems, notes that such use is strongly discouraged, and applies appropriate safeguards for the sensitivity of the data.
Network Security requires full-device or virtual container encryption on any non-organizationally owned system or component before granting access.

Prior to granting access to PII on remote devices, Network Security obtains the device user's signed acknowledgment of a binding agreement covering their responsibility to safeguard accessible PII and their agreement to the organization's ability to manage that PII on the device, including confiscation in consultation with [Legal Counsel] if necessary.
Network Security records each authorized device and its safeguards in the Third-party access register.
Network Security identifies the [Network-Accessible Storage Device Types] prohibited from use in external systems.
Network Security configures network access control points to block connections from the prohibited device types where technically feasible.
Network Security documents the prohibition in the Third-party access register and communicates it to third parties as part of onboarding.
Network Security investigates and remediates any detected violation through the [Ticketing System].

Network Security determines whether organization-controlled portable storage devices are prohibited outright on external systems for the system in scope (as distinct from the restricted-use case in Step 20).
Where prohibited, Network Security configures technical controls (e.g., device control policies) to block use of such devices on external systems.
Network Security documents the prohibition in the Third-party access register.
Network Security audits compliance with this prohibition quarterly.

Network Security, in coordination with the content-owning business unit, designates individuals authorized to post information to publicly accessible systems and records these designations in the [Ticketing System].
Network Security ensures designated individuals are trained to recognize and exclude nonpublic information before posting.
Network Security reviews proposed content prior to posting on the publicly accessible system to confirm no nonpublic information is included.
Network Security reviews existing content on the publicly accessible system for nonpublic information no less often than every fourteen (14) days (bi-weekly).
If nonpublic information is discovered, Network Security removes it immediately and logs the removal action, including discovery date and remediation date, in the [Ticketing System].

Network Security owns this procedure end to end: its personnel perform, configure, and verify each step above, and Network Security is accountable for the accuracy of the VPN and remote-access configuration and the Third-party access register.
Exceptions, prohibited-use waivers, and privileged/remote-command approvals require sign-off from the Authorizing Official (AO) or designated representative before Network Security implements them.
This procedure operationalizes the **Remote & Third-Party Access Standard**, which defines the full requirement text, rationale, and control objectives referenced above.
