analyze: Executing this procedure delivers, tracks, and continuously improves Example Org's security and privacy awareness, literacy, and role-based training programs, and maintains the supporting policy, screening, and documentation practices that keep workforce training compliant with applicable frameworks.

The Security Awareness team performs this procedure for all workforce members — employees, management, senior executives, and contractors — who access, use, manage, or develop Example Org systems, and for the personnel screening and position designation activities that gate access to those systems.
- Access to the [Learning Management System] with administrative rights for the Security Awareness team
- Access to the [Identity Provider] for account status checks and training-based access enforcement
- Access to the [HR System] for workforce rosters, position data, and onboarding/termination events
- Access to the [Ticketing System] for tracking training assignments, exceptions, and remediation
- A designated awareness and training official, named in organizational security and privacy documentation
- The current, approved organization-level security and privacy awareness and training policy
- Access to the [Background Check Vendor] or equivalent screening channel
- Current position descriptions and position risk designations from the [HR System]

Security Awareness develops and documents the organization-level security and privacy awareness and training policy, covering purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and verifies it is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Security Awareness develops and documents supporting procedures that facilitate implementation of the awareness and training policy and its associated controls (this document is one such procedure).
Security Awareness disseminates the policy and procedures to applicable personnel and roles via [Learning Management System] announcements and the organization's document repository.

Security Awareness confirms the designated official responsible for development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures is named in the appropriate security and privacy documents; if the designation changes, update those documents.

Security Awareness reviews and updates the policy and procedures at least every one (1) year, and additionally following assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines.

Security Awareness actively monitors for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect awareness and training policies, and verifies the policy and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards throughout the system life cycle.

Security Awareness maintains the policy, procedures, and all required documentation in written (electronic) form, retains HIPAA-required documentation for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect (whichever is later), makes it available to persons responsible for implementing it, and reviews and updates it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.

Security Awareness enrolls every new system user — including managers, senior executives, and contractors — in security and privacy literacy training in the [Learning Management System] as part of initial onboarding.
Security Awareness schedules annual refresher literacy training for all users and tracks enrollment through the [Learning Management System].

When triggered by system changes, assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, or changes to applicable laws, directives, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines, Security Awareness issues supplemental literacy training covering the triggering event.
Security Awareness ensures the training program addresses each individual's responsibilities associated with sending sensitive information in email.

Security Awareness coordinates with [HR System] administrators to confirm that employees and contractors who work on systems collecting, maintaining, storing, using, or disclosing PII complete privacy training before access to organizational systems and networks is granted.
Security Awareness updates literacy training and awareness content at least once every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.
Security Awareness incorporates lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into literacy training content and awareness techniques.
Security Awareness configures phishing email tests and other practical exercises that simulate events and incidents in the [Phishing Simulation Platform].
Security Awareness executes the simulations against the workforce population and records delivery, click, and reporting metrics.
Security Awareness retains the Phishing simulation results as evidence of this activity.
Security Awareness assigns remediation or targeted follow-up training in the [Learning Management System] to users who fail simulations, and tracks completion through the [Ticketing System].
Security Awareness includes, in literacy training, content on recognizing potential indicators of insider threat.

Security Awareness ensures the training explains how to communicate employee and management concerns regarding potential insider threat indicators through appropriate organizational channels in accordance with established organizational policies and procedures.
Security Awareness includes, in literacy training, content on recognizing potential and actual instances of social engineering and social mining.

Security Awareness ensures the training covers how to recognize and report — through appropriate organizational and defined channels (e.g., applicable security and privacy plans) — attempts to trick an individual into revealing information or taking an action that could breach, compromise, or adversely impact a system.

Security Awareness includes, in literacy training, content on recognizing suspicious communications and anomalous behavior in organizational systems, using the organization-defined indicators of malicious code.

Security Awareness ensures the training covers how to recognize and report — through appropriate organizational and defined channels — potentially suspicious email or web communications (e.g., unexpected emails, emails with strange or poor grammar, or emails from an unfamiliar sender appearing to be from a known sponsor or contractor) and anomalous behaviors in systems.
Security Awareness issues periodic security updates (security reminders) to workforce members covering current threats and required behaviors.
Security Awareness includes in training and reminders the procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software, coordinating content with [Security Operations].
Security Awareness includes in training and reminders the procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.
Security Awareness includes in training and reminders the procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords.

Security Awareness includes, in literacy training, content on the advanced persistent threat, covering techniques for recognizing suspicious emails, use of removable systems in non-secure settings, the potential targeting of individuals at home, and the various ways APTs can infiltrate the organization (e.g., through websites, emails, advertisement pop-ups, articles, and social engineering).
Security Awareness includes, in literacy training, content on the current cyber threat environment.
Security Awareness coordinates with [Security Operations] to reflect current cyber threat information in system operations.
Security Awareness identifies personnel with significant information security and privacy roles and responsibilities, using position risk designations (see the position designation procedure below).

Security Awareness delivers role-based training to those personnel before they are authorized access to the system or information or perform assigned duties, and at least every one (1) year thereafter.

Security Awareness delivers role-based training when required by system changes, when an employee enters a new position requiring additional role-specific training, and following significant changes to the system or the system environment.

Security Awareness monitors role-based training completion in the [Learning Management System]; when personnel have not completed required role-based training within [Training Completion Deadline], Security Awareness notifies [Identity Provider] administrators to disable their user accounts until the role-based training requirement is met.
Security Awareness updates role-based training content at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events or significant changes to the system or system environment.
Security Awareness incorporates lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into role-based training.
Security Awareness identifies the personnel or roles who operate or depend on environmental controls, in coordination with [Facilities].
Security Awareness delivers initial training, and recurring training annually, in the employment and operation of environmental controls to those personnel.
Security Awareness identifies the personnel or roles who operate or depend on physical security controls, in coordination with [Facilities].
Security Awareness delivers initial training, and recurring training annually, in the employment and operation of physical security controls to those personnel.

Security Awareness builds practical exercises into security and privacy role-based training that reinforce the training objectives (e.g., hands-on scenarios, tabletop exercises, or simulated incidents delivered via the [Learning Management System]).

Security Awareness delivers initial training, and refresher training at least every one (1) year, to organizational personnel — including vendors, contractors, and employees — in the employment and operation of personally identifiable information processing and transparency controls.

Security Awareness maintains a privacy education and awareness training program for all employees and individuals working on behalf of the organization who are involved in managing, using, and/or processing PII, and includes responsibilities associated with sending PII in email.
Security Awareness ensures privacy communications and training are job-specific and commensurate with each employee's responsibilities.

Security Awareness coordinates with [HR System] administrators to confirm initial privacy training is completed before permitting access to organizational information and systems, with annual refresher training thereafter.
Security Awareness delivers additional or advanced training commensurate with increased responsibilities or changes in duties.
Security Awareness includes acceptable rules of behavior and the consequences of not following them in both initial and refresher training.
Security Awareness ensures training addresses the rules for telework and other authorized remote access programs.

Security Awareness documents and monitors all information security and privacy training activities in the [Learning Management System], including security and privacy awareness training and specific role-based security and privacy training.
Security Awareness generates the Training completion report from the [Learning Management System] and retains it as evidence of program execution.
Security Awareness retains individual training records for a minimum of 5 years after completion of a specific training course.
Security Awareness, in coordination with [HR System] owners and the security and privacy officers, assigns a risk designation to all organizational positions.

Security Awareness establishes screening criteria for individuals filling positions, including explicit information security role appointment requirements (e.g., training and security clearances), and factors whether the workforce member will work with PII into the screening criteria.
Security Awareness reviews and updates position risk designations at least every one (1) year, and whenever a position's duties are changed, revised, or realigned.
Security Awareness verifies that all individuals with significant security responsibilities possess, at a minimum, a background investigation.

Security Awareness coordinates with [HR System] owners to screen individuals prior to authorizing access to the system, and implements procedures to determine that a workforce member's access to electronic protected health information is appropriate.

Security Awareness rescreens individuals in accordance with the organizational Personnel Security Policy, [Rescreening Frequency], and anytime an individual changes position, consistent with the position risk designation for the new position.

Security Awareness ensures background investigations are conducted in a manner commensurate with organizational Personnel Security policy and guidance prior to employment; for prospective and existing employees accessing ACA-sensitive information or PII, Security Awareness confirms personnel suitability based on a valid need-to-know (which cannot be assumed from position or title) and favorable background check results, with the background check including, at a minimum, contacting provided references and the local law enforcement agency or agencies.

Security Awareness verifies that employees and contractors are not permitted access to information systems until they have been vetted in accordance with organizational policy and have signed the appropriate access agreements.

Security Awareness implements procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with electronic protected health information or in locations where it might be accessed.

Security Awareness coordinates with [Identity Provider] administrators to implement procedures for terminating access to electronic protected health information when employment or other arrangement with a workforce member ends, or as required by clearance determinations.

Security Awareness implements procedures to ensure all workforce members have appropriate access to electronic protected health information and to prevent workforce members without such access from obtaining it.

For systems processing, storing, or transmitting classified information, Security Awareness verifies that accessing individuals are cleared and indoctrinated to the highest classification level of the information to which they have access on the system.

For classified information types requiring formal indoctrination, Security Awareness verifies that accessing individuals are formally indoctrinated for all relevant types of information to which they have access on the system.

Security Awareness ensures individuals accessing information requiring special protective measures have valid access authorizations demonstrated by assigned official government duties and satisfy the organization-defined additional personnel screening criteria.
Security Awareness verifies that individuals accessing a system processing, storing, or transmitting organization-defined information types meet the organization-defined citizenship requirements.

Security Awareness consults with the organization's security and privacy officers to incorporate security and privacy roles and responsibilities — including role-based training requirements — into organizational position descriptions maintained in the [HR System].
Security Awareness reviews affected position descriptions whenever role-based training requirements change and submits updates to [HR System] owners.

The Security Awareness team is authorized to perform all steps in this procedure and is accountable for the process end to end, including handoffs to [HR System] owners, [Identity Provider] administrators, [Security Operations], and [Facilities].

Exceptions to training deadlines, screening requirements, or record retention must be reviewed and approved by the designated awareness and training official, with decisions documented in the [Ticketing System].
This procedure operationalizes the **Workforce Security Training Standard**, which contains the full requirement text and the rationale for each control implemented above.

analyze: This procedure provides the Network Security team with the operational steps required to enforce, monitor, and maintain information flow controls at Example Org's network boundary and internal segmentation points, as required by the Information Security Standard: Network & Boundary Protection.
Executing it produces the Firewall and segmentation rule review and the External attack-surface scan as evidence of continuous compliance.

This procedure is performed by the Network Security team on all network boundary and internal flow-control enforcement points (firewalls, segmentation controls, cross-domain transfer mechanisms, and interconnection gateways) at Example Org, on a continuous basis.
It applies to all information flows within the system and between connected systems.
- Administrative access to the [Firewall Management Console] and the [Segmentation Management Platform]
- Administrative access to the [Cross-Domain Solution] and [Data Diode] management interfaces where deployed
- Access to the current System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP) in the [SSPP Repository]
- Approved change tickets raised in the [Ticketing System] for any rule or filter modification

- The organization-defined information flow control policies, security and privacy attributes, and policy filters recorded in the SSPP (all `[Assignment: ...]` values below must be resolved there before enforcement)
- Access to the [External Attack-Surface Scanner] and the [Flow Monitoring / SIEM Platform]
- Network Security team approval for rule changes; Authorizing Official involvement for interconnection decisions
Confirm the information flow control policies defined in the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined information flow control policies]`) are current before making any flow-control change.

Open the [Firewall Management Console] and verify that every allow rule maps to an approved authorization recorded in the [Ticketing System]; deny-by-default must be the baseline posture on all boundary and segmentation enforcement points.
Reject or remove any rule that cannot be traced to an approved authorization; document the removal in the change ticket.
On a continuous basis, monitor flow logs in the [Flow Monitoring / SIEM Platform] for traffic that does not match an authorized flow definition and block it at the enforcement point.
Record the results of each verification as part of the Firewall and segmentation rule review evidence.
Verify the SSPP names the authority to order immediate termination and/or suspension of any interconnection; if it does not, escalate to the Authorizing Official to have it defined and recorded.
When an interconnection is assessed as presenting an unacceptable level of risk to the enterprise and/or mission, notify the Authorizing Official and the system owner immediately.

The Authorizing Official makes the risk-informed decision to terminate or suspend the interconnection, in consultation with the system owner; record the decision and its rationale in the [Ticketing System].

On the Authorizing Official's order, the Network Security team disables the interconnection at the [Firewall Management Console] or disconnects it at the [Interconnection Gateway], and confirms the flow is no longer passing.
Retain the decision record and the enforcement confirmation as evidence.

Confirm the security and privacy attributes (`[Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy attributes]`) and the information, source, and destination objects they attach to (`[Assignment: organization-defined information, source, and destination objects]`) are defined in the SSPP.

Configure the [Segmentation Management Platform] and [Firewall Management Console] rules to evaluate those attributes when making flow control decisions, per the SSPP's information flow control policies.
Test each attribute-based rule with representative allowed and denied flows and record the results in the change ticket.
Identify the protected processing domains defined in the SSPP for the systems in scope.
Configure the [Segmentation Management Platform] so that flow control decisions between processing domains are enforced at the domain boundary, per the SSPP's information flow control policies.
Verify that no flow path exists between protected processing domains that bypasses the configured boundary controls, using flow logs from the [Flow Monitoring / SIEM Platform].
Confirm which information flow control policies the SSPP requires to be enforced dynamically (`[Assignment: organization-defined information flow control policies]`).

Configure the [Flow Monitoring / SIEM Platform] and the enforcement points it integrates with (e.g., [Firewall Management Console], [Segmentation Management Platform]) so that flow decisions are evaluated at the time of the flow, not only from static rules.
Validate dynamic enforcement by simulating a flow that should be permitted under one condition and denied under another, and confirm the enforcement point responds correctly.

Determine from the SSPP which method(s) Example Org uses to prevent encrypted information from bypassing flow control mechanisms: `[Selection (one or more): decrypting the information; blocking the flow of the encrypted information; terminating communications sessions attempting to pass encrypted information; [Assignment: organization-defined procedure or method]]`.

Configure the [Inspection/Proxy Gateway] or [Firewall Management Console] to apply the selected method(s) at every boundary enforcement point where encrypted traffic could otherwise bypass inspection.
Verify the configuration by attempting to pass encrypted traffic that would violate a flow control policy, and confirm it is decrypted and inspected, blocked, or its session terminated as selected.
Record the test outcome in the change ticket and retain it with the Firewall and segmentation rule review evidence.
Identify the limitations on embedding data types within other data types defined in the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined limitations]`).
Configure the [Content Inspection Gateway] or [Cross-Domain Solution] filters to detect and block or strip data structures that embed prohibited data types within other data types.
Test the filter with a sample payload containing a prohibited embedding and confirm it is handled per the SSPP policy.
Confirm the metadata used for flow control decisions is defined in the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined metadata]`).
Configure the enforcement points ([Segmentation Management Platform], [Content Inspection Gateway]) to read and evaluate that metadata as a basis for permitting or denying flows.
Verify that flows carrying incorrect or missing required metadata are denied, using a controlled test transfer.
Identify the information flows the SSPP requires to be one-way.
Deploy or verify a [Data Diode] (hardware-based flow control mechanism) on each one-way flow path; do not implement one-way flows with software-only controls.
Verify the hardware configuration permits flow in only the required direction by attempting a transfer in the prohibited direction and confirming it fails.
Include the diode configuration in the Firewall and segmentation rule review evidence.

Confirm the security or privacy policy filters (`[Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters]`) and the information flows they apply to (`[Assignment: organization-defined information flows]`) are defined in the SSPP.

Configure the filters on the appropriate enforcement points ([Firewall Management Console], [Content Inspection Gateway], [Cross-Domain Solution]) as the basis for flow control decisions on those flows.

Configure the failure action for each filter per the SSPP: `[Selection (one or more): block; strip; modify; quarantine]` data after a filter processing failure, in accordance with `[Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy]`.
Test the failure path by forcing a filter processing failure and confirming the selected action is taken.

Identify the information flows and the conditions under which human review is required, per the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined information flows]`, `[Assignment: organization-defined conditions]`).
Configure the [Cross-Domain Solution] or [Content Inspection Gateway] to route flows meeting those conditions to a review queue rather than transferring them automatically.

Assign Network Security personnel to review queued items against the applicable flow control policy; approve and release, or deny and return, each item with the decision recorded in the [Ticketing System].

Verify that privileged administrator accounts on the [Firewall Management Console], [Content Inspection Gateway], and [Cross-Domain Solution] have the capability to enable and disable security or privacy policy filters under the conditions defined in the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined conditions]`).
Verify those administrators can configure the filters to support different security or privacy policies as defined in the SSPP.

Restrict these capabilities to privileged administrator roles only, and log every enable, disable, and configuration change to the [Flow Monitoring / SIEM Platform] for review by the Network Security team.
Confirm the data type identifiers used to validate data essential for flow decisions are defined in the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined data type identifiers]`).
Configure the [Cross-Domain Solution] to validate incoming and outgoing transfers against those identifiers before releasing information between different security domains.
Test with a transfer carrying an unrecognized or mismatched data type identifier and confirm the transfer is rejected.
Confirm the policy-relevant subcomponents are defined in the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined policy-relevant subcomponents]`).
Configure the [Cross-Domain Solution] to decompose information transferred between different security domains into those subcomponents before submission to the policy enforcement mechanisms.
Verify each subcomponent is individually evaluated by the policy enforcement mechanism and that no transfer occurs as an un-decomposed whole.
Confirm the security or privacy policy filters requiring fully enumerated formats are defined in the SSPP.
Configure the [Cross-Domain Solution] filters to restrict data structure and content to the enumerated formats, rejecting anything outside them.
Test with a transfer using a non-enumerated format or unexpected content and confirm it is rejected.

Confirm the definition of unsanctioned information and the governing security or privacy policy in the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined unsanctioned information]`, `[Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy]`).
Configure the [Cross-Domain Solution] or [Content Inspection Gateway] to examine all information transferred between different security domains for the presence of unsanctioned information.
Prohibit the transfer of any information found to contain unsanctioned content, per the SSPP policy, and record the blocked transfer in the [Ticketing System].
Determine from the SSPP the basis for endpoint identification: `[Selection (one or more): organization, system, application, service, individual]`.

Configure the boundary enforcement points ([Firewall Management Console], [Cross-Domain Solution], [Interconnection Gateway]) to uniquely identify and authenticate both the source and the destination of every information transfer on that basis.
Verify that transfers from unauthenticated or unidentified endpoints are denied, using a controlled test from an endpoint without valid credentials.
Confirm the security or privacy policy filters that apply to metadata are defined in the SSPP.
Configure the [Cross-Domain Solution] to run those filters against the metadata accompanying transfers between different security domains, not only the payload content.
Test with a transfer whose metadata violates a filter and confirm the transfer is blocked or the metadata is sanitized per the SSPP.

Confirm which solutions and approved configurations the SSPP defines for controlling the flow of the designated information across security domains (`[Assignment: organization-defined solutions in approved configurations]`, `[Assignment: organization-defined information]`).

Verify each deployed [Cross-Domain Solution] or [Data Diode] matches its approved configuration before placing it in the flow path; if it deviates, take it out of service and raise a change ticket in the [Ticketing System].
Route the designated information flows only through solutions in approved configurations; deny flows attempting to cross domains by any other path.

Confirm the required separations and the mechanisms and/or techniques to accomplish them are defined in the SSPP (`[Assignment: organization-defined required separations]`, `[Assignment: organization-defined mechanisms and/or techniques]`).

Implement the required separations in the [Segmentation Management Platform] (logical separation, e.g., VLANs, subnets, security zones) or via physical separation (e.g., [Data Diode], dedicated hardware) as the SSPP specifies.

Verify no traffic path exists between flows that the SSPP requires to be separated, using flow logs from the [Flow Monitoring / SIEM Platform], and record the verification in the Firewall and segmentation rule review evidence.
Confirm the security domains and access patterns the SSPP defines for single-device multi-domain access.

Configure the [Multi-Domain Access Solution] so that a single device can reach computing platforms, applications, or data residing in multiple different security domains while information flow between those domains is prevented.
Verify the isolation by attempting to move information from one domain to another through the single-device session and confirming the transfer is blocked.

On a continuous basis, the Network Security team performs the Firewall and segmentation rule review: verify every rule on the boundary and segmentation enforcement points against current approved authorizations, remove stale or unauthorized rules, and retain the review output as evidence.

On a continuous basis, run the [External Attack-Surface Scanner] against the external boundary, review findings for exposed services or flows not covered by an approved authorization, and remediate or raise a change ticket in the [Ticketing System] for each finding.
Retain the External attack-surface scan output alongside the Firewall and segmentation rule review as the standing evidence artifacts for this procedure.

The Network Security team is accountable for this procedure end to end: it executes every step, performs the continuous Firewall and segmentation rule review and External attack-surface scan, and coordinates with system owners, privileged administrators, and the Authorizing Official as individual steps require.

The Authorizing Official approves interconnection termination and suspension decisions, and the Authorizing Official (in consultation with Network Security) reviews and approves any exception to the flow control policies defined in the SSPP.
Information Security Standard: Network & Boundary Protection

analyze: This procedure operationalizes the organization's information security program governance activities so that program plans, policies, risk management strategy, and system-level security artifacts are developed, approved, disseminated, and kept current.
Executing this procedure produces an approved policy set with documented review dates and a maintained program plan and organizational chart.

This procedure applies to the Security Program / GRC team, which performs and owns each step below, and to all organization-wide policies, the information security program plan, system security and privacy plans/architectures, personnel security processes, acquisition security requirements, and physical/facility security controls across Example Org's systems and facilities.
Other teams (HR, Facilities, Contracts, system owners) participate in specific steps as noted but do not own the process.
- Access to the organization's [Document Management System] where policies, plans, and architectures are stored and version-controlled
- Access to [Identity Provider] to verify workforce roles, provisioning status, and account attributes referenced in access agreements and rules of behavior
- Access to [Ticketing System] to log, route, and track remediation, sanctions notifications, and external provider notifications
- Access to [Contract Management System] for business associate agreements, access agreements, and external provider contracts
- Access to [Physical Access Control System] for facility/workstation control records
- Written designation or confirmation of the senior accountable official (e.g., CISO/SAISO) authorized to approve the program plan and policies
- Current enterprise architecture documentation and system inventory
- [Access Request System] for recording workforce clearance, authorization, and termination actions

Security Program / GRC drafts or updates the organization-wide information security program plan in the [Document Management System], covering: program requirements overview, security program management and common controls (in place and planned), roles/responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance.
Circulate the draft to entities with security responsibilities for coordination comments; incorporate feedback.
Route the finalized plan to the senior accountable official for approval and signature.
Record the approval date and next scheduled review date in the plan header; retain this as part of the "Approved policy set with review dates" evidence artifact.

Restrict edit and view permissions on the plan in the [Document Management System] to authorized Security Program / GRC personnel and approvers to protect it from unauthorized disclosure or modification.

Review and update the plan annually and immediately following any [organization-defined triggering event, e.g., major reorganization or significant security incident]; log each review in the plan's revision history.

Security Program / GRC confirms or formally designates a senior official (SAISO/SISO) with documented mission, resources, and authority to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain the organization-wide security program.
Document the appointment, scope of authority, and reporting line in the organizational chart maintained in the [Document Management System].
Publish the updated org chart as part of the "Program plan and org chart" evidence artifact.
Update the designation record whenever the appointee or scope of authority changes.

Security Program / GRC drafts a comprehensive, organization-wide risk management strategy addressing security risk to operations, assets, and individuals, and privacy risk from authorized PII processing.
Obtain input from system owners and mission/business process owners on operational risk factors.
Submit the strategy to the senior accountable official for approval.
Disseminate the approved strategy to system owners and require its consistent application in risk assessments and authorization decisions.

Review and update the strategy annually or immediately upon significant organizational change (e.g., merger, new business line, major system change); record the review date in the [Document Management System].

Security Program / GRC drafts the planning policy and implementing procedures, addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance, aligned to applicable laws/regulations.
Designate a Security Program / GRC lead as the official responsible for developing, documenting, and disseminating the policy and procedures.
Disseminate the approved policy and procedures to [organization-defined personnel or roles, e.g., all system owners and IT staff] via the [Document Management System].
Document any change to the policy or procedures and implement it in accordance with applicable requirements before it takes effect.
Review and update the policy and procedures annually and following any [organization-defined triggering event]; record the review date as part of the approved policy set evidence artifact.

For each system, the system owner, with Security Program / GRC support, drafts a security and privacy plan consistent with the enterprise architecture, describing: constituent components, operational/mission context, individuals fulfilling system roles, information types processed/stored/transmitted, security categorization with rationale, threats of concern, privacy risk assessment results (for systems processing PII), operational environment and system dependencies/connections, security and privacy requirements overview, applicable control baseline/overlay, controls in place or planned with tailoring rationale, and risk determinations tied to architecture/design decisions.
Identify security- and privacy-related activities requiring coordination with [organization-defined individuals or groups] and document the coordination points in the plan.
Submit the completed plan to the authorizing official or designated representative for review and approval prior to implementation.
Distribute approved copies and communicate subsequent changes to [organization-defined personnel, roles, or stakeholders] via the [Document Management System].
Review the plan annually or following significant system/environment changes; update it to reflect changes or issues identified during implementation or assessments.
Restrict access to the plan in the [Document Management System] to authorized personnel to protect it from unauthorized disclosure or modification.
Security Program / GRC maintains all required policies, procedures, and records of required actions/activities/assessments in written (including electronic) form in the [Document Management System].
Retain each document for 6 years from its creation date or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later; configure retention rules in the [Document Management System] accordingly.
Grant access to the documentation to personnel responsible for implementing the procedures it describes.
Review documentation periodically and update it in response to environmental or operational changes affecting ePHI security; record the review date in the document metadata.
Security Program / GRC develops and maintains policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.
Conduct a thorough risk analysis of potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of ePHI; document findings in the [Document Management System].

Based on the risk analysis, implement security measures sufficient to reduce identified risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level; log implemented measures against each identified risk.

Establish a recurring procedure for reviewing information system activity records — audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports — and document each review in the [Ticketing System] or [Document Management System].

Security Program / GRC, with Facilities, develops policies and procedures limiting physical access to electronic information systems and the facilities housing them while ensuring authorized personnel retain access.
Establish and document a contingency access procedure enabling facility access to support data restoration under disaster recovery and emergency mode operations plans.
Implement safeguards to protect the facility and equipment from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft, recorded in the [Physical Access Control System].
Implement access control and validation procedures based on role or function, including visitor control processes and controls over access to software used for testing/revision.
Document all security-related repairs and modifications to physical components of a facility in a maintenance log retained in the [Document Management System].

Security Program / GRC, with Legal/Contracts, reviews group health plan documents to confirm they require the plan sponsor to reasonably and appropriately safeguard ePHI created, received, maintained, or transmitted on the plan's behalf (unless disclosure is limited to summary health information, enrollment/disenrollment data, or is otherwise authorized).
Amend plan documents, where needed, to require the plan sponsor to implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards.
Confirm reasonable and appropriate security measures support adequate separation between the plan sponsor and the group health plan.

Obtain written agreement from any agent receiving the ePHI on the sponsor's behalf that it will implement reasonable and appropriate security measures and report security incidents to the group health plan; retain the agreement in the [Contract Management System].

Security Program / GRC drafts rules of behavior describing responsibilities and expected behavior for information and system usage, security, and privacy, including restrictions on: use of social media/social networking/external sites, posting organizational information on public websites, and using organization-provided identifiers/authentication secrets to create external accounts.
Publish the rules in the [Document Management System] and provide them to every individual prior to granting system access.

Obtain a documented acknowledgment (electronic or signed) from each individual confirming they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules, via [Identity Provider] or [Document Management System] workflow, before authorizing access.
Review and update the rules annually.
Require individuals who acknowledged a prior version to re-acknowledge whenever the rules are revised or updated; track outstanding re-acknowledgments in the [Ticketing System].

Security Program / GRC develops policies and procedures specifying the proper functions to be performed on workstations or classes of workstations that access ePHI, the manner in which those functions are performed, and the required physical attributes of the workstation's surroundings.
Disseminate the workstation use policy to workforce members whose workstations can access ePHI.
Periodically confirm workstation placement and use align with the documented policy during facility or workstation reviews; log findings in the [Document Management System].

Security Program / GRC, with system owners, develops a security and privacy architecture for each system describing the requirements and approach for protecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability, and for minimizing privacy risk in PII processing.
Document how the architecture integrates into and supports the enterprise architecture, and describe assumptions about and dependencies on external systems and services.
Store the architecture document in the [Document Management System] and cross-reference it in the system's security and privacy plan.

Review and update the architecture annually or following a significant change, reflecting enterprise architecture changes; propagate resulting changes into the system's security/privacy plan, CONOPS, criticality analysis, organizational procedures, and upcoming procurements/acquisitions.
Security Program / GRC, together with the system owner, determines and documents the applicable control baseline for the system based on its security categorization.
Record the selected baseline in the system's security and privacy plan and retain the selection rationale in the [Document Management System].

Security Program / GRC, with the system owner, tailors the selected control baseline using approved tailoring actions, informed by mission/business functions, operating environment, and known threats/vulnerabilities.
Confirm that no control included in the ARC-AMPE baseline is removed or reduced, and that AC-2(8) is not added to the baseline.
Document the risk-informed rationale for any added controls, confirming they do not conflict with or create less stringent standards than the baseline.
Record the final tailored baseline and rationale in the system's security and privacy plan.
Security Program / GRC drafts the personnel security policy and implementing procedures, addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance.
Designate a Security Program / GRC lead as the official responsible for developing, documenting, and disseminating the policy and procedures.
Disseminate the approved policy and procedures to [organization-defined personnel or roles].
Review and update the policy and procedures annually and following any [organization-defined triggering event]; record the review as part of the approved policy set evidence artifact.
Security Program / GRC, with HR, implements policies and procedures ensuring workforce members have appropriate access to ePHI and preventing access by those who do not need it.
Implement authorization and/or supervision procedures for workforce members who work with ePHI or in locations where ePHI might be accessed, recorded via [Access Request System].
Implement a workforce clearance procedure to determine the appropriate level of access for each workforce member before granting access.

Implement termination procedures to revoke system and facility access via [Identity Provider] and [Physical Access Control System] when employment or another arrangement ends, or as otherwise determined necessary.
Security Program / GRC develops and documents access agreements (e.g., nondisclosure, acceptable use) for organizational systems, stored in the [Contract Management System].
Verify that each individual requiring access signs the appropriate access agreement, via [Identity Provider] or e-signature workflow, prior to being granted access.
Review and update access agreements as part of the system security authorization or when a contract is renewed or extended, but at minimum annually.
Require individuals to re-sign agreements when updated or annually, whichever occurs first; track outstanding re-signatures in the [Ticketing System].
Security Program / GRC implements policies and procedures for authorizing access to ePHI consistent with applicable requirements.
Where a health care clearinghouse function exists within a larger organization, implement isolating controls to protect ePHI from unauthorized access by the larger organization.
Implement access authorization procedures for workstations, transactions, programs, or processes, recorded via [Access Request System].

Implement procedures to establish, document, review, and modify each user's right of access based on the organization's access authorization policies; log each review in the [Document Management System].

Security Program / GRC, with Facilities/IT Operations, implements policies and procedures governing receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media containing ePHI into and out of a facility, and movement within the facility.
Document final disposition procedures for the information and/or the media on which it is stored.
Implement procedures to remove ePHI from media before its reuse.
Maintain a record of hardware/media movements and the person responsible, logged in the [Ticketing System] or [Document Management System].
Before moving equipment, create a retrievable, exact copy of the ePHI when needed and verify the copy's integrity.

Security Program / GRC, with Legal/Contracts, confirms satisfactory assurances are obtained — via a written contract or other arrangement — before permitting a business associate (or subcontractor) to create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI on the organization's behalf.

Ensure each contract requires the business associate to comply with applicable requirements, requires its subcontractors to agree by contract to the same requirements, and requires the business associate to report security incidents, including breaches of unsecured PHI, to the covered entity.
Where an alternative arrangement substitutes for a contract, document how it satisfies the applicable requirements.
Apply the same contractual requirements to agreements between a business associate and its subcontractors.
Store all executed agreements in the [Contract Management System] and track renewal/review dates.
Security Program / GRC establishes personnel security requirements, including security roles and responsibilities, for external providers, and documents them in the [Contract Management System].
Require external providers, by contract, to comply with the organization's personnel security policies and procedures.

Require external providers to notify [organization-defined personnel or roles] of personnel transfers or terminations involving external personnel who hold organizational credentials/badges or system privileges within 24 hours.
Monitor external provider compliance with these personnel security requirements on an ongoing basis, logging findings in the [Ticketing System].

Require CSPs to clearly document any nationality requirements applicable to any account type on their platform, or explicitly state that none exist; retain this documentation in the [Document Management System].

Security Program / GRC, with HR, employs a formal sanctions process for individuals (including workforce members) who fail to comply with established information security and privacy policies and procedures.
Apply appropriate sanctions against noncompliant individuals in accordance with the documented process.

Notify [organization-defined personnel or roles] within 24 hours whenever a formal sanctions process is initiated, identifying the individual sanctioned and the reason for the sanction; log the notification in the [Ticketing System].

Security Program / GRC drafts the system and services acquisition policy and implementing procedures, addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance.
Designate a Security Program / GRC lead as the official responsible for developing, documenting, and disseminating the policy and procedures.
Disseminate the approved policy and procedures to [organization-defined personnel or roles].
Review and update the policy and procedures annually and following any [organization-defined triggering event]; record the review as part of the approved policy set evidence artifact.

During mission and business process planning, Security Program / GRC works with system owners to determine the high-level information security and privacy requirements for the system or system service being acquired.
Determine, document, and allocate the resources required to protect the system or service as part of the organizational capital planning and investment control process.
Establish a discrete line item for information security and privacy in the organization's programming and budgeting documentation; retain the budget documentation in the [Document Management System].

The Security Program / GRC team is the sole authorized owner and executor of this procedure, including drafting, disseminating, and reviewing all plans, policies, and agreements described above; other teams (HR, Facilities, Legal/Contracts, IT Operations, system owners) participate in individual steps at Security Program / GRC's direction.
The senior accountable official (e.g., CISO/SAISO) approves the program plan, policies, and any exceptions to this procedure.

This procedure implements the requirements defined in the **Example Org Information Security Program Governance Standard**, which contains the authoritative rationale and full requirement text for each control referenced above.
