analyze: **Document Owner:** IAM Engineering **Applies to:** All Example Org information systems, users, devices, and processes that authenticate to organizational systems **Process cadence:** Continuous
This Standard defines the mandatory requirements for authentication and credential management at Example Org.

It governs invalid logon handling, session control, system use notification, identification and authentication of users and devices, authenticator management, authentication feedback, cryptographic module authentication, non-organizational user authentication, and re-authentication.
IAM Engineering is accountable for this process end to end, including implementation, review, and evidence production.

- **IAM Engineering** owns this Standard and the authentication and credential management process it defines, including configuration of authentication controls, review of authentication policy settings, and production of the MFA enrolment report and the Authentication policy configuration export.
- **System administrators** participate in account lockout release and authenticator lifecycle actions as specified below.
- **Help desk support** shall require user identification for any transaction with information security and privacy implications.
The organization shall enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period].
The limit shall be five (5) consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a fifteen (15) minute time period.

When the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded, the organization shall automatically take one or more of the following: lock the account or node for [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; lock the account or node until released by an administrator; delay the next logon prompt per [Assignment: organization-defined delay algorithm]; notify the system administrator; or take another [Assignment: organization-defined action].
[NIST AC-7 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

When the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded, the organization shall automatically lock the account or node for a minimum of thirty (30) minutes, lock it until released by an administrator, delay the next logon prompt consistent with a delay algorithm, notify the system administrator, or take other action as determined by the organization.

The organization shall purge or wipe information from [Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices], based on [Assignment: organization-defined purging or wiping requirements and techniques], after [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive unsuccessful device logon attempts.
Mobile devices shall be configured to purge or wipe information after ten (10) consecutive unsuccessful logon attempts.
The organization shall limit the number of unsuccessful biometric logon attempts to [Assignment: organization-defined number].

After the organization-defined number of consecutive invalid logon attempts is exceeded, the organization shall allow the use of [Assignment: organization-defined authentication factors] different from the primary authentication factors, and shall enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts through use of those alternative factors by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period].
IAM Engineering shall monitor lockout enforcement through the [Identity Provider] on a continuous basis.

The organization shall display [Assignment: organization-defined system use notification] to users before granting access to the system, providing privacy and security notices consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
[NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

The system use notification shall state that: system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; unauthorized use is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.
[NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]
The system use notification shall state that users are accessing a U.S. Government system.
The system use notification shall state that users are accessing a system that contains U.S. Government information.
The organization shall retain the notification message or banner on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit actions to log on to or further access the system.
[NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

For publicly accessible systems, the organization shall: display system use information under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions] before granting further access; display references, if any, to monitoring, recording, or auditing consistent with privacy accommodations for such systems that generally prohibit those activities; and include a description of the authorized uses of the system.
[NIST AC-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]
The organization shall limit the number of concurrent sessions for each [Assignment: organization-defined account and/or account types] to [Assignment: organization-defined number].

The number of concurrent sessions for each account and/or account type shall be limited to one (1) session; any requirement for more than one concurrent session must be expressly required for the performance of job duties and documented in the applicable security and privacy plan.

The organization shall prevent further access to the system by initiating a device lock after [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of inactivity and/or requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended.

Further access to the system shall be prevented by initiating a device lock after fifteen (15) minutes of inactivity (covering both remote and internal access connections) and by requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended.
The device lock shall be retained until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures.
[NIST AC-11 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]
The organization shall conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image.

The organization shall implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information.
The organization shall automatically terminate a user session after [Assignment: organization-defined conditions or trigger events].
[NIST AC-12 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall provide a logout capability for user-initiated communications sessions whenever authentication is used to gain access to [Assignment: organization-defined information resources]; for ARC-AMPE, the information resources must be defined in the applicable security and privacy plans.

The organization shall display an explicit logout message to users indicating the termination of authenticated communications sessions; for ARC-AMPE, an organization-defined standard logout message must be documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (e.g., "Your session has been terminated").

The organization shall display an explicit message to users indicating that the session will end in [Assignment: organization-defined time]; for ARC-AMPE, the time until end of session must be specified in the applicable security and privacy plans.
The organization shall implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity.

The organization shall implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4).
The organization shall assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
The organization shall establish (and implement as needed) procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency.
The organization shall implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information.
The organization shall implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed.

The organization shall develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] an identification and authentication policy (addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines) and procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated controls.
[NIST IA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the identification and authentication policy and procedures.
[NIST IA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall review and update the current identification and authentication policy and procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

The identification and authentication policy and procedures shall be reviewed and updated at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events (such as assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines).
IAM Engineering shall perform the reviews required by 7.3 and 7.4 and shall retain the resulting Authentication policy configuration export as evidence of the configured state.

The organization shall maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule in written (which may be electronic) form, and shall maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required to be documented.
Required documentation shall be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
Documentation shall be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.
Documentation shall be reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the electronic protected health information.
The organization shall uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and associate that unique identification with processes acting on behalf of those users.
[NIST IA-2 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite, and shall require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for organizational users; help desk support requires user identification for any transaction with information security and privacy implications.
The organization shall implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts.
[NIST IA-2(1) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]
Multi-factor authentication must be phishing-resistant, in accordance with current CISA guidance.
The organization shall implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts.
[NIST IA-2(2) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]
For non-privileged accounts, multi-factor authentication is required for all non-consumer account types; while MFA is not currently mandated for consumer accounts, it is strongly recommended.
IAM Engineering shall produce the MFA enrolment report on a continuous basis as evidence of multi-factor authentication enrolment under 8.3 through 8.6.
When shared accounts or authenticators are employed, the organization shall require users to be individually authenticated before granting access to the shared accounts or resources.
[NIST IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]

For multi-factor authentication to local, network, and remote access to privileged and non-privileged accounts, one of the factors must be provided by a device separate from the system gaining access, and that device must meet [Assignment: organization-defined strength of mechanism requirements].

For multi-factor authentication to local, network, and remote access to privileged and non-privileged accounts, one of the factors must be provided by a device separate from the system gaining access, and that device must meet the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography.
The organization shall implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
[NIST IA-2(8) Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]
The organization shall provide a single sign-on capability for [Assignment: organization-defined system accounts and services].
The organization shall accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials.

The organization shall implement the following out-of-band authentication mechanisms under \[Assignment: organization-defined conditions\]: [Assignment: organization-defined out-of-band authentication].

The organization shall uniquely identify and authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a [Selection (one or more): local; remote; network] connection.

The organization shall uniquely identify and authenticate devices that require authentication mechanisms before establishing a local, remote, or network connection, using at minimum shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access; the specific devices and/or device types approved for identification and authentication management must be defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.

The organization shall authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a [Selection (one or more): local; remote; network] connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically based.

Where addresses are allocated dynamically, the organization shall standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined lease information and lease duration], and shall audit lease information when assigned to a device.
The organization shall handle device identification and authentication based on attestation by [Assignment: organization-defined configuration management process].

The organization shall manage system authenticators by: verifying, as part of initial authenticator distribution, the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator; establishing initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization; ensuring authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use; establishing and implementing administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution, for lost, compromised, or damaged authenticators, and for revoking authenticators; changing default authenticators prior to first use; protecting authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification; requiring individuals to take, and having devices implement, specific controls to protect authenticators; and changing authenticators for group or role accounts when membership to those accounts changes.
[NIST IA-5 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
The organization shall change or refresh authenticators [Assignment: organization-defined time period by authenticator type] or when [Assignment: organization-defined events] occur.

Authenticators shall be changed or refreshed immediately when they are no longer valid due to known or suspected compromise, and immediately upon system installation (e.g., default or vendor-supplied passwords).

Authenticators must be compliant with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL, AAL, and FAL level 1 for Certification Class B, level 2 for Certification Class C, and level 3 for Certification Class D.

The organization shall encrypt authentication assertions when passed through third parties, such as a browser (e.g., a SAML assertion encrypted using XML-Encryption, or an OpenID Connect ID Token encrypted using JSON Web Encryption).

The organization shall comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B for authenticator management; Organizational System/User Account passwords shall be paired with multi-factor authentication (strongly recommended for Organizational ACA Consumer Account passwords), and it is strongly recommended to enforce a policy requiring Organizational System/User Account passwords be changed or refreshed at least once every six (6) months.

The organization shall maintain a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords and shall update the list [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly.

The organization shall maintain a list of commonly used, expected, or compromised passwords and shall update it using a frequency defined in applicable security/privacy plans, not to exceed one (1) year, and when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly.
When users create or update passwords, the organization shall verify that the passwords are not found on the list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Passwords shall be transmitted only over cryptographically-protected channels.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Passwords shall be stored using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
The organization shall require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
The organization shall allow user selection of long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
The organization shall employ automated tools to assist the user in selecting strong password authenticators.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
The organization shall enforce password composition and complexity rules of [Assignment: organization-defined composition and complexity rules].

Password composition and complexity shall comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B, with a minimum of eight (8) characters for ACA Consumer Accounts and all other accounts, and a minimum of twelve (12) characters for Administrator/Privileged Accounts; dictionary words must not be used as passwords, use of passphrases is strongly recommended, temporary passwords should trigger an immediate change to a permanent password, and mobile devices may be excluded from the complexity requirement depending on organizational risk tolerance.

For public key-based authentication, the organization shall enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key, and shall map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group; and when PKI is used, the organization shall validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status information, and shall implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation.
The organization shall require developers and installers of system components to provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation.
The organization shall protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information to which use of the authenticator permits access.
[NIST IA-5(6) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory]
The organization shall ensure that unencrypted static authenticators are not embedded in applications or other forms of static storage.
The organization shall implement [Assignment: organization-defined security controls] to manage the risk of compromise due to individuals having accounts on multiple systems.
The organization shall prohibit the use of cached authenticators after [Assignment: organization-defined time period].
The organization shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined password managers] to generate and manage passwords, and shall protect the passwords using [Assignment: organization-defined controls].
The organization shall use the following external organizations to federate credentials: [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations].
The organization shall bind identities and authenticators dynamically using the following rules: [Assignment: organization-defined binding rules].
For biometric-based authentication, the organization shall employ mechanisms that satisfy [Assignment: organization-defined biometric quality requirements].

For PKI-based authentication, the organization shall employ an organization-wide methodology for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms, including networks, operating systems, browsers, and applications.
The organization shall use only General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management.

The organization shall require that the issuance of [Assignment: organization-defined types of and/or specific authenticators] be conducted [Selection: in person; by a trusted external party] before [Assignment: organization-defined registration authority] with authorization by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
The organization shall employ presentation attack detection mechanisms for biometric-based authentication.
The organization shall obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation and use by unauthorized individuals.
[NIST IA-6 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-6 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines for such authentication.
[NIST IA-7 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]
Information systems containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) must use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.
The organization shall uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users or processes acting on behalf of non-organizational users.
[NIST IA-8 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

The organization shall employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL-2/AAL-2, shall require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for non-organizational users, and shall require user identification for help desk support transactions with information security and privacy implications.
The organization shall accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials from other federal agencies.
The organization shall accept only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant, and shall document and maintain a list of accepted external authenticators.
[NIST IA-8(2) Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

External credentials must be certified as compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite by an approved accreditation authority, must meet or exceed those guidelines, and the organization must use General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management.
The organization shall conform to [Assignment: organization-defined identity management profiles] for identity management.

analyze: This standard establishes requirements for managing information exchange agreements, business associate relationships, external service providers, and supply chain risks for Acme Health systems and information assets.

This standard applies to all personnel, contractors, and third parties involved in the exchange of information, provision of external services, or participation in the supply chain for Acme Health systems.

Acme Health must approve and manage the exchange of information between systems using interconnection security agreements, information exchange security agreements, memoranda of understanding or agreement, service level agreements, user agreements, non-disclosure agreements, or other organization-defined agreement types.
Acme Health must have appropriate information exchange agreements approved and in place prior to any information sharing.

Acme Health must document in each exchange agreement the interface characteristics, security and privacy requirements, controls, responsibilities for each system, and the impact level of the information communicated.
Acme Health must review and update information exchange agreements [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].
Acme Health must review and update information exchange agreements at least every one (1) year.

Acme Health must update interconnection agreements following significant changes to the system, organizations, or the nature of electronic information sharing that could impact the validity or security postures of the agreement.

Acme Health must enter into memoranda of understanding, memoranda of agreement, letters of intent, computer matching agreements, information exchange agreements, or similar agreements with parties that specifically describe the Personally Identifiable Information covered and enumerate the purposes for which the PII may be used.
Acme Health must ensure any PII sharing is compatible with the purpose for which it was collected, and obtain additional notice and consent from individuals before sharing for incompatible purposes.

Acme Health must grant the Authorizing Official or other senior leadership the authority to order immediate termination or suspension of any interconnection that presents an unacceptable level of risk.

Acme Health must verify that individuals or systems transferring data between interconnecting systems have the requisite authorizations (i.e., write permissions or privileges) prior to accepting such data.

Acme Health must identify transitive (downstream) information exchanges with other systems through the systems identified in information exchange agreements, and take measures to ensure that transitive information exchanges cease when the controls on identified transitive systems cannot be verified or validated.

Acme Health must permit business associates to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information only if the covered entity obtains satisfactory assurances that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information.

Acme Health must permit business associates to use subcontractors to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information only if the business associate obtains satisfactory assurances that the subcontractor will appropriately safeguard the information.
Acme Health must document satisfactory assurances from business associates through a written contract or other arrangement that meets the applicable requirements of § 164.314(a).

Acme Health must ensure business associate contracts provide that the business associate will comply with applicable security requirements, ensure subcontractors comply with applicable requirements, and report any security incident including breaches of unsecured protected health information.
Acme Health must apply the same contract requirements to business associate-subcontractor arrangements as apply to covered entity-business associate arrangements.

For group health plans, Acme Health must ensure plan documents provide that the plan sponsor will reasonably and appropriately safeguard electronic protected health information, implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards, ensure adequate separation with security measures, ensure agents implement security measures, and report security incidents.
Acme Health must require providers of external system services to comply with organizational security and privacy requirements and employ [Assignment: organization-defined controls].
Acme Health must base organization-defined controls for external service providers on the ARC-AMPE security and privacy controls or equivalent.

Acme Health must ensure contracts and other acquisition-related documents provide enforceable means to ensure privacy and security controls are implemented for Personally Identifiable Information shared with or disclosed to recipients outside the organization.
Acme Health must include in service contracts or agreements language requiring the provider to be subject to U.S. Federal laws and regulations protecting PII.

Acme Health must include in service contracts or agreements language requiring adherence to the security and privacy policies and standards set by the organization consistent with 45 CFR §155.260(b), and define security and privacy roles and responsibilities.
Acme Health must define and document organizational oversight and user roles and responsibilities with regard to external system services.
Acme Health must employ [Assignment: organization-defined processes, methods, and techniques] to monitor control compliance by external service providers on an ongoing basis.

Acme Health must conduct an organizational assessment of risk prior to the acquisition or outsourcing of information security services, and verify that the acquisition or outsourcing of dedicated information security services is approved by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].

Acme Health must require providers of [Assignment: organization-defined external system services] to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and other services required for the use of such services.

Acme Health must require providers of all external systems where federal customer data is processed or stored to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and other services required for the use of such services.

Acme Health must establish, document, and maintain trust relationships with external service providers based on [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy requirements, properties, factors, or conditions defining acceptable trust relationships].

Acme Health must take [Assignment: organization-defined actions] to verify that the interests of [Assignment: organization-defined external service providers] are consistent with and reflect organizational interests.

Acme Health must restrict the location of [Selection (one or more): information processing; information or data; system services] to [Assignment: organization-defined locations] based on [Assignment: organization-defined requirements or conditions].
For Certification Classes C and D, Acme Health must restrict the location of information processing, information or data, AND system services for all federal customer data.
For Certification Class D, Acme Health must restrict the location of information processing and data to the U.S./U.S. Territories or geographic locations where there is U.S. jurisdiction.

Acme Health must process and store Personally Identifiable Information of the system within the continental U.S., Hawaii, or U.S. Territories, and weigh the risk if support, development, and information technology services are off-shored.
For ACA Administering Entities, Acme Health must notify CMS at least sixty (60) days prior to commitment of outsourcing information system services outside of the U.S.
Acme Health must ensure the safeguards afforded to sensitive information are no less than the safeguards mandated by state regulation, federal law, Executive Order, or other authoritative direction.
Acme Health must maintain exclusive control of cryptographic keys for encrypted material stored or transmitted through an external system.
Acme Health must provide the capability to check the integrity of information while it resides in the external system.
Acme Health must restrict the geographic location of information processing and data storage to facilities located within the legal jurisdictional boundary of the United States.
For organizations that process Federal Tax Information, Acme Health must adhere to IRS Publication 1075.
Acme Health must notify CMS at least sixty (60) days prior to transmitting data into an external information service environment per the requirements in the Change Notification guidance.

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] a supply chain risk management policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the supply chain risk management policy and associated controls.
Acme Health must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the supply chain risk management policy and procedures.
Acme Health must review and update the supply chain risk management policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].
Acme Health must review and update the supply chain risk management policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.
Acme Health must review and update supply chain risk management procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].
Acme Health must review and update supply chain risk management procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.
Acme Health must actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect supply chain risk management policies.
Acme Health must ensure supply chain risk management policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards throughout the system's life cycle.

Acme Health must develop a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with the research and development, design, manufacturing, acquisition, delivery, integration, operations and maintenance, and disposal of [Assignment: organization-defined systems, system components, or system services].

Acme Health must include in the supply chain risk management plan an expression of supply chain risk tolerance, acceptable risk mitigation strategies or controls, a process for consistently evaluating and monitoring supply chain risk, approaches for implementing and communicating the plan, a description and justification for risk mitigation measures taken, and associated roles and responsibilities.

Acme Health must address in the supply chain risk management plan requirements for developing trustworthy, secure, privacy-protective, and resilient system components and systems, including the application of security design principles implemented as part of life cycle-based systems security engineering processes.

Acme Health must address in the supply chain risk management plan the managing, implementing, and monitoring of supply chain risk management controls identified as applicable and any added tailored controls based on the organization's risk assessment of its system development life cycle management process.
Acme Health must review and update the supply chain risk management plan [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] or as required to address threat, organizational, or environmental changes.
Acme Health must review and update the supply chain risk management plan at least every one (1) year or as required to address threat, organizational, or environmental changes.
Acme Health must protect the supply chain risk management plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

Acme Health must establish a supply chain risk management team consisting of [Assignment: organization-defined personnel, roles and responsibilities] to lead and support [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain risk management activities].
[NIST 800-53 SR-2(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SR-2(1)]

Acme Health must ensure the supply chain risk management team consists of organizational personnel with diverse roles and responsibilities including risk executive, information technology, contracting, information security, privacy, mission or business, legal, supply chain and logistics, acquisition, business continuity, and other relevant functions, with collective awareness of acquisition processes, legal practices, vulnerabilities, threats, attack vectors, and technical aspects and dependencies of systems.
Acme Health must consult NIST publications including NIST SP 800-161 and NISTIR 8276 for guidance on supply chain risk management activities.

Acme Health must assess and review the supply chain-related risks associated with suppliers or contractors and the system, system component, or system service they provide [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

Acme Health must employ [Selection (one or more): organizational analysis; independent third-party analysis; organizational testing; independent third-party testing] of [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain elements, processes, and actors] associated with the system, system component, or system service.

Acme Health must establish agreements and procedures with entities involved in the supply chain for the [Selection (one or more): notification of supply chain compromises; [Assignment: organization-defined results of assessments or audits]].

Acme Health must establish agreements and procedures with entities involved in the supply chain for the notification of supply chain compromises, results of assessments or audits, and organization information.
Acme Health must follow the FedRAMP Incident Evaluation and Communication rules when establishing notification agreements for supply chain entities.
Acme Health must ensure notifications of supply chain incidents are consistent with organizational incident handling and incident reporting processes.
Acme Health must maintain policies and procedures implemented to comply with HIPAA Security Rule requirements in written (which may be electronic) form.
Acme Health must maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required by the HIPAA Security Rule to be documented.
Acme Health must retain documentation required by HIPAA Security Rule for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
Acme Health must make documentation available to persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.
Acme Health must review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.

This Standard establishes the requirements governing remote access to Example Org systems, wireless access, mobile device use, external system use, and the publication of information to publicly accessible systems.

It applies to all Example Org personnel, contractors, and third parties who access Example Org systems from locations, networks, or devices outside Example Org's direct control, and to all systems that permit such access.
Network Security is accountable for this process end to end, including authorizations, monitoring, evidence production, and handoffs to other participating teams.
Network Security must establish and document usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed.
These restrictions and requirements must be reflected in the VPN and remote-access configuration.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17 AE Mandatory]
Each type of remote access to the system must be authorized prior to allowing such connections.
Network Security is responsible for granting this authorization.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17 AE Mandatory]
Callback capability with re-authentication must be required to verify connections from authorized locations when the MPLS service network cannot be used.

For remote access, including teleworking, Example Org must follow the latest published NIST SP 800-46 guidelines via policies and procedures that define: forms of permitted remote access; types of devices permissible for remote access; types of access granted to remote users; and handling of remote user account provisioning.
Network Security must maintain these policies and procedures.
The rationale for remote access must be documented in the security plan for the system.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17(4) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17(4) AE Mandatory]

For application and turnkey systems requiring vendor logon, Network Security must assign the vendor a User ID and password, require entry through the standard authentication process, authorize and log such access, and recertify vendor User IDs at least every one (1) year.
All vendor User IDs and their authorization and recertification status must be recorded in the Third-party access register.
Network Security must maintain the Third-party access register as the authoritative record of all third-party access covered by this Standard and must review it quarterly.

Network Security must ensure all computers and devices requiring network access (government-furnished, contractor-furnished, or personal) are securely configured with, at minimum: up-to-date system patches; current anti-virus software; a host-based intrusion detection system; functionality providing automatic execution of code disabled; and the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.

Implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information.
Automated mechanisms must be employed to monitor and control remote access methods.
Network Security is responsible for operating these mechanisms.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17(1) AE Mandatory]
Cryptographic mechanisms must be implemented to protect the confidentiality and integrity of remote access sessions.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17(2) AE Mandatory]
Remote accesses must be routed through authorized and managed network access control points.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17(3) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17(3) AE Mandatory]
Information about remote access mechanisms must be protected from unauthorized use and disclosure.

The execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access must be authorized only in a format that provides assessable evidence and only for [Assignment: organization-defined needs].

The execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access must be authorized only in a format that provides assessable evidence and only for compelling operational needs, and Example Org must define what constitutes a compelling operational need in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP).
Example Org must provide the capability to disconnect or disable remote access to the system within [Assignment: organization-defined time period].

Example Org must provide the capability to disconnect or disable remote access to the system within one (1) hour, and terminate or suspend network connections (i.e., a system-to-system interconnection) within one (1) hour upon issuance of an order by organization-defined officials.
Example Org must implement [Assignment: organization-defined mechanisms] to authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined remote commands].
Network Security must establish configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of wireless access.
[NIST 800-53 AC-18 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-18 AE Mandatory]
Each type of wireless access to the system must be authorized prior to allowing such connections.
[NIST 800-53 AC-18 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-18 AE Mandatory]

If wireless access is explicitly approved, Network Security must: disable wireless device service set identifier (SSID) broadcasting; enable encryption protection; place access points in secure areas; shut down access points when not in use (e.g., nights, weekends); implement a stateful inspection firewall between the wireless network and the wired infrastructure; utilize Media Access Control (MAC) address authentication; utilize static IP addresses rather than DHCP; utilize personal firewalls on all wireless clients; disable file sharing on all wireless clients; deploy intrusion detection agents on the wireless side of the firewall; monitor and record wireless activity with records reviewed on a regular basis (as defined in applicable security/privacy plans); and adhere to the latest published IEEE 802.11 WLAN standard.

Wireless access to the system must be protected using authentication of users and devices and encryption, and all communications via the wireless access device must be encrypted using the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.
[NIST 800-53 AC-18(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-18(1) AE Mandatory]
Wireless networking capabilities embedded within system components must be disabled, when not intended for use, prior to issuance and deployment.
[NIST 800-53 AC-18(3) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-18(3) AE Mandatory]
Users allowed to independently configure wireless networking capabilities must be identified and explicitly authorized.

Radio antennas must be selected and transmission power levels calibrated to reduce the probability that signals from wireless access points can be received outside of organization-controlled boundaries.

Network Security must establish configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for organization-controlled mobile devices, to include when such devices are outside of controlled areas.
[NIST 800-53 AC-19 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-19 AE Mandatory]
The connection of mobile devices to organizational systems must be authorized; the system Business Owner must authorize the use of mobile devices.
[NIST 800-53 AC-19 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-19 AE Mandatory]
Only organization-owned mobile devices and software can be used to process, access, and store Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Mobile devices must be configured to protect the storage and transmission of information on the device, and scanning of the device using a virus protection application must be implemented.

Full-device encryption or container-based encryption using the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards must be employed to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on approved mobile devices, and information on all mobile devices that contain PII must be encrypted.
[NIST 800-53 AC-19(5) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-19(5) AE Mandatory]

The use of unclassified mobile devices is prohibited in facilities containing systems processing, storing, or transmitting classified information unless specifically permitted by the authorizing official.

For individuals so permitted: connection of unclassified mobile devices to classified systems is prohibited; authorizing official approval is required for connection of unclassified mobile devices to unclassified systems; use of internal or external modems or wireless interfaces within the unclassified mobile devices is prohibited; and unclassified mobile devices and their stored information must be subject to random reviews and inspections by [Assignment: organization-defined security officials], following the incident handling policy if classified information is found.
The connection of classified mobile devices to classified systems must be restricted in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined security policies].

Example Org must establish organization-defined terms and conditions and identify organization-defined controls asserted to be implemented on external systems, consistent with the trust relationships established with other organizations owning, operating, and/or maintaining external systems, allowing authorized individuals to: access the system from external systems; and process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information using external systems; or prohibit the use of organization-defined prohibited types of external systems.
[NIST 800-53 AC-20 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP AC-20 | ARC-AMPE AC-20 AE Mandatory]

The defined terms and conditions for external system use must address, at a minimum: the types of applications that can be accessed from external information systems; the maximum FIPS 199 security category of information that can be processed, stored, and transmitted; how other users of the external information system will be prevented from accessing federal information; the use of VPN and stateful inspection firewall technologies; the use of and protection against the vulnerabilities of wireless technologies; the maintenance of adequate physical security controls; the use of virus and spyware protection software; and how often the security capabilities of installed software are to be updated.

The interrelated controls must be differentiated as follows: AC-20 describes system access to and from external systems; CA-3 describes documentation of an agreement between the respective system owners when data is exchanged between the CSO and an external system; and SA-9 describes the responsibilities of external system owners, typically captured in the agreement required by CA-3.

Authorized individuals may use an external system to access the system or to process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information only after: verification of the implementation of controls on the external system as specified in the organization's security and privacy policies and security and privacy plans; or retention of approved system connection or processing agreements with the organizational entity hosting the external system.
[NIST 800-53 AC-20(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-20(1) AE Mandatory]

The use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems must be restricted using organization-defined restrictions, and such use is permitted only when: the use is documented within appropriate security/privacy plans; the use is explicitly authorized, in writing, by the Authorizing Official (AO) or designated representative; personally owned devices to which the devices are to be attached comply with organization policies and directives on use of personally owned systems and components; and security and privacy safeguards appropriate for the sensitivity of the data are employed.
[NIST 800-53 AC-20(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-20(2) AE Mandatory]

The use of non-organizationally owned systems or system components to process, store, or transmit organization information must be restricted unless: contractor-owned device use is documented within the contract and appropriate security and privacy plans and explicitly authorized, in writing, by the AO or designated representative; personally owned device use complies with organizational policies and directives on use of personally owned systems and components; security and privacy safeguards appropriate for the sensitivity of the data are employed; and either full-device or virtual container encryption is implemented to reduce the vulnerability of sensitive information processed, stored, or transmitted by such systems or components.

The use of personally owned devices must be strongly discouraged, and prior to providing access to PII on remote devices, device users must acknowledge through a binding agreement their responsibilities to safeguard the PII accessible from the device and their awareness of and agreement to the organization's capabilities to manage the organization's PII on the device, including confiscation, in consultation with the organization's counsel if necessary to remove the PII.
The use of [Assignment: organization-defined network-accessible storage devices] in external systems is prohibited.
The use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems is prohibited.
Individuals authorized to make information publicly accessible must be designated.
[NIST 800-53 AC-22 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-22 AE Mandatory]
Authorized individuals must be trained to ensure that publicly accessible information does not contain nonpublic information.
[NIST 800-53 AC-22 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-22 AE Mandatory]
The proposed content of information must be reviewed prior to posting onto the publicly accessible system to ensure that nonpublic information is not included.
[NIST 800-53 AC-22 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-22 AE Mandatory]
The content on the publicly accessible system must be reviewed for nonpublic information at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and such information must be removed, if discovered.
The content on the publicly accessible system must be reviewed for nonpublic information bi-weekly (no less often than every fourteen [14] days) and such information must be removed, if discovered.
Network Security must retain the VPN and remote-access configuration and the Third-party access register as the evidence of compliance with this Standard.

Network Security must review the VPN and remote-access configuration and the Third-party access register quarterly to confirm that all remote and third-party access remains authorized, documented, and consistent with the requirements of this Standard.

Network Security is accountable for the outcomes of this process end to end, including coordination with participating teams (including system Business Owners and the Authorizing Official) on the authorization decisions described in this Standard.

analyze: This Standard defines the authentication and credential management requirements that Example Org must implement to control access to its systems, applications, and information, including electronic protected health information (ePHI) where applicable.
IAM Engineering is accountable for the end-to-end implementation, operation, monitoring, and audit of this process.
Other teams that participate in individual steps (e.g., help desk staff, System Owners) do so as participants; IAM Engineering owns the process and all handoffs between participants.

This Standard applies on a continuous basis to all in-scope systems, accounts, and users — organizational and non-organizational, local, network, and remote — unless a specific requirement below states otherwise.

- IAM Engineering must develop, document, and disseminate an identification and authentication policy (addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance, and consistent with applicable laws/regulations) and associated procedures, to defined personnel or roles.
IAM Engineering must designate an official responsible for managing the development, documentation, and dissemination of this policy and its procedures.

This policy and its procedures must be reviewed and updated at least annually and following defined events (e.g., audit findings, incidents, legal/regulatory changes), with organization-level personnel/roles defined in the organizational SSPP.

- Policies and procedures implemented to comply with applicable requirements must be maintained in written (which may be electronic) form, and any required action, activity, or assessment must be documented in writing.

This documentation must be retained for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later; made available to persons responsible for implementing the related procedures; and reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting security.

- Organizational users (and processes acting on their behalf) must be uniquely identified and authenticated via the [Identity Provider] before access is granted; this applies to all local, network, and remote access except for explicitly documented exceptions involving authorized group authenticators.

Identity proofing and authentication processes must comply with the latest NIST SP 800-63 suite, use system/network authenticators and unique identifiers, and identify users for any help desk transaction with security/privacy implications.
This requirement also satisfies verification that a person or entity seeking access to health information is the one claimed.
[NIST IA-2 | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(d)]
- A unique name and/or number must be assigned to identify and track each user's identity.
- Technical policies and procedures must restrict access to electronic protected health information systems to only those persons or software programs granted access rights.
- Single sign-on capability must be provided via the [Identity Provider] for [SSO-Eligible System Accounts and Services].
- Personal Identity Verification (PIV)-compliant credentials must be accepted and electronically verified.
- [Out-of-Band Authentication Conditions] must trigger use of defined out-of-band authentication mechanisms.
- When shared accounts or authenticators are used, users must be individually authenticated via the [Identity Provider] before being granted access to the shared account or resource.
[NIST IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]
- Multi-factor authentication must be implemented via the [Identity Provider] for access to privileged accounts.

This MFA must be phishing-resistant per current CISA guidance and must use two or more different factor types (something you know/have/are), applied regardless of local, network, or remote access type, appropriate to risk level.
[NIST IA-2(1) | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]
- Multi-factor authentication must be implemented via the [Identity Provider] for access to non-privileged accounts.
This MFA must be phishing-resistant per current CISA guidance.
MFA for consumer accounts is strongly recommended but not currently mandated; MFA is required for all other non-privileged account types.
[NIST IA-2(2) | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]

- MFA for accessing privileged and non-privileged accounts must include a factor provided by a device separate from the system being accessed; that separate device must meet the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography standard.
This applies to local, network, and remote access for both privileged and non-privileged accounts.
[NIST IA-2(6) | FedRAMP IA-2(6) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(6) AE Mandatory]
- Replay-resistant authentication mechanisms must be implemented via the [Identity Provider] for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
[NIST IA-2(8) | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]

- Organizational system/user account passwords must be paired with MFA consistent with the privileged/non-privileged MFA requirements above; pairing consumer account passwords with MFA is strongly recommended.
Authenticator management must comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B.

- IAM Engineering must manage authenticators by: verifying the identity of the individual/group/role/service/device receiving the authenticator as part of initial distribution; establishing initial authenticator content; ensuring authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use; establishing and implementing administrative procedures for initial distribution, lost/compromised/damaged authenticators, and revocation; changing default authenticators prior to first use; protecting authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification; requiring individuals/devices to implement specific protective controls; and changing authenticators for group/role accounts when membership changes.
[NIST IA-5 | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
- Authenticators must be changed or refreshed on a defined schedule or upon defined trigger events.
Authenticators must be changed immediately upon known or suspected compromise, or immediately upon system installation (e.g., default/vendor-supplied passwords).
Changing system/user account passwords at least every six months is strongly recommended.
[NIST IA-5(f) | FedRAMP IA-5(f) | ARC-AMPE IA-5(f) AE Mandatory]
- Authenticators must comply with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines at a specified IAL/AAL/FAL level (Level 1 for Certification Class B, Level 2 for Class C, Level 3 for Class D).
Authentication assertions passed through third parties (e.g., browsers) must be encrypted (e.g., via XML-Encryption for SAML or JWE for OpenID Connect ID Tokens).
- Developers and installers of system components must provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation.
- Authenticators must be protected commensurate with the security category of the information their use permits access to.
[NIST IA-5(6) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory]
- Unencrypted static authenticators must not be embedded in applications or other forms of static storage.
- [Multi-System Account Risk Controls] must be implemented to manage the risk of compromise arising from individuals holding accounts on multiple systems.
- Credentials must be federated via the [Identity Provider] with [Approved Federation Partners].
- Identities and authenticators must be bound dynamically according to [Identity-Authenticator Binding Rules].
- Use of cached authenticators must be prohibited after [Cached Authenticator Time Limit].
- An organization-wide methodology must be employed for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms (networks, operating systems, browsers, applications).
- Only GSA-approved products and services must be used for identity, credential, and access management.

- Issuance of [Authenticator Types Requiring In-Person Issuance] must be conducted in person or by a trusted external party before [Registration Authority], with authorization by [Authorizing Personnel/Roles].
- Organizations must employ [Password Manager] to generate and manage passwords and protect those passwords using [Password Manager Protection Controls].
- For password-based authentication, IAM Engineering must:
- maintain and update at least annually (or immediately when compromise is suspected) a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords;
- verify new/updated passwords via the [Identity Provider] against that list;
- transmit passwords only over cryptographically-protected channels;
- store passwords using an approved salted key derivation function (preferably a keyed hash), with salting recommended to mitigate brute-force attacks;
- require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery;
- allow user selection of long passwords/passphrases including spaces and all printable characters, with passphrases strongly recommended and dictionary words prohibited;
- employ automated tools within the [Identity Provider] to assist users in selecting strong passwords; and

- enforce composition and complexity rules complying with the latest NIST SP 800-63B, with minimum password lengths of 8 characters for ACA consumer accounts and all other accounts, and 12 characters for administrator/privileged accounts.
- Temporary password lifetime restrictions do not apply but must trigger an immediate change to a permanent password.
Mobile devices may be excluded from complexity requirements based on organizational risk tolerance.

- For public key-based authentication, IAM Engineering must enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key, map the authenticated identity to the individual's or group's account, and, when PKI is used, validate certificates via a certification path to an accepted trust anchor (including checking certificate status) and implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation.
- The number of unsuccessful biometric logon attempts must be limited to [Biometric Logon Attempt Limit].
- Biometric-based authentication mechanisms must satisfy [Biometric Quality Requirements].
- Presentation attack detection mechanisms must be employed for biometric-based authentication.
- Devices (or defined types of devices) must be uniquely identified and authenticated before establishing a local, remote, or network connection.

At minimum, this must use shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access, with the specific list of approved device types documented in the applicable SSPP.
[NIST IA-3 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]
- Devices must be authenticated using cryptographically based bidirectional authentication before establishing a local, remote, or network connection.

- Where addresses are allocated dynamically, dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration must be standardized per [Dynamic Address Allocation Lease Requirements], and lease information must be audited when assigned to a device.
- Device identification and authentication may be handled based on attestation via a defined configuration management process.
- Non-organizational users (or processes acting on their behalf) must be uniquely identified and authenticated via the [Identity Provider].

Identity proofing and authentication processes must comply with the latest NIST SP 800-63-3 Digital Identity Guidelines at IAL-2/AAL-2, use system/network authenticators and unique identifiers, and identify users for help desk transactions with security/privacy implications.
- Personal Identity Verification (PIV)-compliant credentials from other federal agencies must be accepted and electronically verified.
- Only NIST-compliant external authenticators must be accepted, and a documented list of accepted external authenticators must be maintained.

External credentials must be certified compliant with the latest NIST SP 800-63 suite by an approved accreditation authority, must meet or exceed that guidance, and only GSA-approved products/services must be used for identity, credential, and access management.
- Organizations must conform to [Identity Management Profiles], defined using identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest NIST SP 800-63 suite.
- Federated or PKI credentials meeting a defined policy (PIV-I) must be accepted and verified.
- [Disassociation Measures] must be implemented to disassociate user attributes or identifier assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties.

- Feedback of authentication information during the authentication process must be obscured by the [Identity Provider] to protect it from possible exploitation and use by unauthorized individuals (e.g., displaying asterisks for typed passwords or limiting display time).
- Mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module must meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines.
Information systems containing PII must use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.
- A mechanism must be implemented to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information (addressable requirement).

- The [Identity Provider] must prevent further access by initiating a device lock after 15 minutes of inactivity (including remote and internal connections), or by requiring the user to manually initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended, and must retain the lock until the user reestablishes access via established identification and authentication procedures.
Device locks must conceal previously visible display information behind a publicly viewable image.
[NIST AC-11 Moderate/High | NIST AC-11(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]

- Organizations must implement policies and procedures specifying the proper functions, manner of performance, and physical attributes of workstations or workstation classes that can access electronic protected health information.

- User sessions must be automatically terminated by the [Identity Provider] when defined conditions or trigger events occur (e.g., periods of inactivity, incident response, time-of-day restrictions); these conditions/events must be defined in the applicable security and privacy plan.
[NIST AC-12 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory]

- A logout capability must be provided via the [Identity Provider] for user-initiated communications sessions whenever authentication is used to access defined information resources; those information resources must be defined in the applicable security and privacy plan.

- An explicit logout message must be displayed to users indicating termination of an authenticated communications session; a documented standard logout message must be specified in the SSPP (e.g., "Your session has been terminated").

- An explicit warning message must be displayed to users indicating that their session will end after a defined period of time; that time period must be specified in the applicable security and privacy plan.
- Electronic sessions must be automatically terminated by the [Identity Provider] after a predetermined period of inactivity (addressable requirement).

- The [Identity Provider] must limit consecutive invalid logon attempts to 5 attempts within a 15-minute period and automatically respond when that limit is exceeded (e.g., locking the account/node for a minimum of 30 minutes or until administrator release via the [Ticketing System], delaying the next logon prompt, notifying an administrator, or taking another defined action).
Automatically unlocking an account after a set time is generally not permitted, though exceptions may be allowed based on operational need.
- Mobile devices must be configured to purge or wipe information after 10 consecutive unsuccessful device logon attempts, using defined purging/wiping requirements and techniques.

- Organizations may allow use of alternate authentication factors different from the primary factors after the defined number of consecutive invalid logon attempts is exceeded, and must enforce a limit on consecutive invalid attempts using those alternate factors within [Alternate Factor Time Period].
- IAM Engineering must continuously monitor authentication attempts across in-scope systems for consecutive invalid logon activity as part of this process.

- Before granting access, systems must display a system use notification/banner via the [Identity Provider] providing privacy and security notices consistent with applicable laws, regulations, and policies, stating that: (1) users are accessing a U.S. Government system or a system containing U.S. Government information; (2) system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; (3) unauthorized use is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and (4) use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.
The notification must remain on screen until the user acknowledges the conditions and takes explicit action to log on or continue access.

For publicly accessible systems, the notification must be displayed under defined conditions before further access is granted, include any references to monitoring/recording/auditing consistent with privacy accommodations, and describe the system's authorized uses.

- The System Owner determines which parts of the environment require system use notification and how/how often compliance is verified; if not verified via configuration baseline checks, a documented agreement must specify how verification results are provided and their periodicity.

- The [Identity Provider] must limit the number of concurrent sessions allowed for each account and/or account type to one (1) concurrent session per account/account type; any requirement for more than one session must be documented in the applicable security and privacy plan.
[NIST AC-10 High | ARC-AMPE AC-10 AE Mandatory]
- Procedures must be established (and implemented as needed) for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency.

- Users must be required to re-authenticate via the [Identity Provider] when defined circumstances or situations occur (e.g., role, authenticator, or credential changes; system security category changes; execution of privileged functions; after [Re-authentication Time Period]; or periodically).
These circumstances must be defined in the applicable security and privacy plans, using the same example triggers, with re-authentication after a fixed time period required at a minimum.

- **IAM Engineering** owns this Standard end to end: it is accountable for implementing, operating, monitoring, and auditing all requirements in this document, for maintaining associated procedures, and for handoffs to participating teams.
- **System Owners** determine which parts of their environment require system use notification and the method and periodicity of verifying compliance, per Section 13.
- **Help desk staff** must positively identify users for any help desk transaction with security/privacy implications, per Section 3 and Section 9.
- **Developers and installers of system components** must provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation, per Section 5.

IAM Engineering must generate and retain, on a continuous basis, the following evidence of compliance with this Standard: - **MFA enrolment report** — evidencing enrollment status and factor types for privileged and non-privileged accounts against the requirements in Section 4. - **Authentication policy configuration export** — evidencing the current configuration of the [Identity Provider] against the identification, authentication, session management, lockout, and notification requirements in Sections 3, 5, 6, 11, 12, 13, and 14.

Documentation supporting this Standard, including the above evidence, must be retained for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later, made available to persons responsible for implementing the related procedures, and reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting security.
