Dual authorization must be enforced for [Selection (one or more): movement; deletion] of [Assignment: organization-defined audit information].
Read-only access to audit information must be authorized to [Assignment: organization-defined subset of privileged users or roles].
Example Org must provide irrefutable evidence that an individual (or process acting on behalf of an individual) has performed [Assignment: organization-defined actions].
This evidence must cover at least actions including the addition, modification, deletion, approval, sending, or receiving of data.

Covered actions must include organization-defined actions to be covered by non-repudiation, which must include ACA eligibility and enrollment functions including, but not limited to, applying for advance payments of the Advance Premium Tax Credit and Cost-sharing Reductions; applying for enrollment in Qualified Health Plans; completing enrollment in Qualified Health Plans; and providing related Customer Service, with the covered actions defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.

The identity of the information producer must be bound with the information to [Assignment: organization-defined strength of binding], and the means for authorized individuals to determine the identity of the producer of the information must be provided.

The binding of the information producer identity to the information must be validated at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency], and [Assignment: organization-defined actions] must be performed in the event of a validation error.
Reviewer or releaser credentials must be maintained within the established chain of custody for information reviewed or released.

The binding of the information reviewer identity to the information must be validated at the transfer or release points prior to release or transfer between [Assignment: organization-defined security domains], and [Assignment: organization-defined actions] must be performed in the event of a validation error.

Audit records must be retained for [Assignment: organization-defined time period] to provide support for after-the-fact investigations of incidents and to meet regulatory and organizational information retention requirements.

Audit records must be retained for ninety (90) days and archived for ten (10) years consistent with records retention policy (per the ACA retention rule, 45 CFR §155.1210); when subject to a legal investigation (e.g., Insider Threat), audit records must be maintained until released by the investigating authority; and audit inspection reports, including a record of corrective actions, must be retained for a minimum of three (3) years from the date the inspection was completed.

Example Org must employ [Assignment: organization-defined measures] to ensure that long-term audit records generated by the system can be retrieved; ARC-AMPE measures include converting records to newer formats, retaining equipment capable of reading the records, and retaining the necessary documentation to help personnel understand how to interpret the records.
Example Org must provide audit record generation capability for the event types the system is capable of auditing as defined in Section 5.1 on [Assignment: organization-defined system components].

Audit record generation capability must be provided for the event types the system is capable of auditing as defined in Section 5.1 on at least all information system and network components where audit capability is deployed/available.
Detection & Response must maintain a Log source inventory and coverage report identifying all log sources and confirming generation coverage across components.
[Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] must be allowed to select the event types that are to be logged by specific components of the system.
Audit records for the event types defined in Section 5.2 must be generated that include the audit record content defined in Section 6.1.

Audit records from [Assignment: organization-defined system components] must be compiled into a system-wide (logical or physical) audit trail that is time-correlated to within [Assignment: organization-defined level of tolerance].
A system-wide (logical or physical) audit trail composed of audit records in a standardized format must be produced.

The capability must be provided and implemented for [Assignment: organization-defined individuals or roles] to change the logging to be performed on [Assignment: organization-defined system components] based on [Assignment: organization-defined selectable event criteria] within [Assignment: organization-defined time thresholds].
The capability for auditing the parameters of user query events for data sets containing personally identifiable information must be provided and implemented.

Example Org must monitor the system to detect: (1) attacks and indicators of potential attacks in accordance with the following monitoring objectives: [Assignment: organization-defined monitoring objectives] (per ARC-AMPE, the organization's incident response policy and procedures, per IR-1); and (2) unauthorized local, network, and remote connections.
Unauthorized use of the system must be identified through [Assignment: organization-defined techniques and methods], documented per ARC-AMPE in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.

Internal monitoring capabilities must be invoked or monitoring devices deployed strategically within the system to collect organization-determined essential information, and at ad hoc locations within the system to track specific types of transactions of interest to the organization.
Detected events and anomalies must be analyzed by Detection & Response.
Detection & Response must adjust the level of system monitoring activity when there is a change in risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, or the Nation.
Alert tuning and review records must be produced as evidence of this activity.
A legal opinion regarding system monitoring activities must be obtained.

[Assignment: organization-defined system monitoring information] must be provided to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] \[Selection (one or more): as needed; [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]\]; ARC-AMPE specifies as needed and consistent with the organization-defined frequency documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.

A centrally managed IDS/IPS capability must be implemented to monitor network communications on all networks and subnets, using centrally managed IDS/IPS devices at network perimeter points (including between zones) and/or centrally managed host-based IDS/IPS sensor agents in information technology components for which such agents are available; where communications are encrypted within a zone, mechanisms capable of either decrypting content for analysis or analyzing content before transmission/after receipt must be used; components that do not support host-based IDS/IPS sensors must be documented in the applicable risk assessment and SSPP; support for sharing of threat awareness information in a format that meets CMS requirements must be provided; and unauthorized remote connections must be monitored for continuously in real time, taking appropriate action if an unauthorized connection is discovered.
All applicable rules within the Vulnerability Detection and Response and Incident Communication Procedure guidance must be followed.

Individual intrusion detection tools must be connected and configured into a system-wide intrusion detection system; ARC-AMPE requires that raw intrusion detection information be available in an unaltered format; FedRAMP requires following the Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules.
[NIST SI-4(1) | FedRAMP SI-4(1) | ARC-AMPE SI-4(1) AE Mandatory]

Automated tools and mechanisms must be employed to support near real-time analysis of events; ARC-AMPE requires that aggregated intrusion detection information be searchable, provided in a format compliant with organization-defined requirements, sourced from all network- and host-based IDS/IPS capabilities on all networks and subnets, with organization-directed collection rules/requests implemented within the timeframe specified, and that raw intrusion detection information be available in an unaltered format; FedRAMP requires following the Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules.
[NIST SI-4(2) Moderate, High | FedRAMP SI-4(2) | ARC-AMPE SI-4(2) AE Mandatory]
Automated tools and mechanisms must be employed to integrate intrusion detection tools and mechanisms into access control and flow control mechanisms.

Criteria for unusual or unauthorized activities or conditions for inbound and outbound communications traffic must be determined, and inbound and outbound communications traffic must be monitored [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] for those activities or conditions; ARC-AMPE specifies continuous monitoring; FedRAMP requires following the Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules.
[NIST SI-4(4) Moderate, High | FedRAMP SI-4(4) | ARC-AMPE SI-4(4) AE Mandatory]

[Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] must be alerted when the following system-generated indications of compromise or potential compromise occur: [Assignment: organization-defined compromise indicators]; ARC-AMPE specifies malicious code, unauthorized export of information, signaling to an external information system, or potential intrusions, with the alerted personnel documented in the SSPP and the malicious code response consistent with SI-3; FedRAMP requires following the Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules.
[NIST SI-4(5) Moderate, High | FedRAMP SI-4(5) | ARC-AMPE SI-4(5) AE Mandatory]

[Assignment: organization-defined incident response personnel] must be notified of detected suspicious events, and [Assignment: organization-defined least-disruptive actions] must be taken upon detection.
Intrusion-monitoring tools and mechanisms must be tested [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].
Provisions must be made so that [Assignment: organization-defined encrypted communications traffic] is visible to [Assignment: organization-defined system monitoring tools and mechanisms].
Outbound communications traffic must be analyzed at the external interfaces to the system and selected [Assignment: organization-defined interior points] to discover anomalies.

[Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] must be alerted using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms] when the following indications of inappropriate or unusual activities with security or privacy implications occur: [Assignment: organization-defined activities that trigger alerts].

Communications traffic and event patterns for the system must be analyzed, profiles representing common traffic and event patterns must be developed, and those profiles must be used in tuning system-monitoring devices.
Outbound communications traffic must be analyzed at external interfaces to the system and at [Assignment: organization-defined interior points] to detect covert exfiltration of information.

A wireless intrusion detection system must be employed to identify rogue wireless devices and to detect attack attempts and potential compromises or breaches to the system, including both external monitoring (events at system boundaries) and internal monitoring (events within the system).
[NIST SI-4(14) High | ARC-AMPE SI-4(14) AE Mandatory]
An intrusion detection system must be employed to monitor wireless communications traffic as the traffic passes from wireless to wireline networks.
Information from monitoring tools and mechanisms employed throughout the system must be correlated.
Information from monitoring physical, cyber, and supply chain activities must be correlated to achieve integrated, organization-wide situational awareness.

[Assignment: organization-defined additional monitoring] must be implemented of individuals who have been identified by [Assignment: organization-defined sources] as posing an increased level of risk.
[Assignment: organization-defined additional monitoring] must be implemented of privileged users.
[Assignment: organization-defined additional monitoring] must be implemented of individuals during [Assignment: organization-defined probationary period].

Network services that have not been authorized or approved by [Assignment: organization-defined authorization or approval processes] must be detected, and \[Selection (one or more): audit; alert [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]\] must occur when detected.

Host-based monitoring mechanisms — specifically IDS/IPS per ARC-AMPE — must be implemented at [Assignment: organization-defined system components] (per ARC-AMPE, including, but not limited to, systems, appliances, devices, services, and applications), documenting devices and appliances that do not support a host-based IDS/IPS sensor capability in the applicable information system risk assessment and SSPP.
Indicators of compromise provided by [Assignment: organization-defined sources] must be discovered, collected, and distributed to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
Visibility into network traffic at external and key internal system interfaces must be provided to optimize the effectiveness of monitoring devices.
Periodic security updates (security reminders) must be implemented.
Procedures must be implemented for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software.
Procedures must be implemented for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.
Procedures must be implemented for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords.
This process is expected to produce and retain, at minimum, the following evidence artifacts, owned by Detection & Response:

| Artifact | Description | Referenced Sections | | ---------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | | Log source inventory and coverage report | Inventory of all log sources and confirmation of audit record generation coverage | Section 15.1, Section 5 | | Alert tuning and review records | Records of alert tuning decisions and monitoring adjustments | Section 16.2, Section 9 |
All documentation produced under this Standard is subject to the written-form and retention requirements in Section 4.2.

analyze: This Standard establishes mandatory requirements for remote access, wireless access, mobile device use, external system connections, workstation use, and publicly accessible information at Acme Health.
This Standard applies to all systems, personnel, contractors, and third parties requiring or providing such access to Acme Health information and systems.
Acme Health shall establish and document usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall authorize each type of remote access to the system prior to allowing such connections.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall employ automated mechanisms to monitor and control remote access methods.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17(1) AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality and integrity of remote access sessions.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17(2) AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall route remote accesses through authorized and managed network access control points.
[NIST 800-53 AC-17(3) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-17(3) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health shall authorize the execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access only in a format that provides assessable evidence and for [Assignment: organization-defined needs], and document the rationale for remote access in the security plan for the system.

Acme Health shall authorize the execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access only in a format that provides assessable evidence and for compelling operational needs, and document the rationale for remote access in the security plan for the system.
Acme Health shall protect information about remote access mechanisms from unauthorized use and disclosure.
Acme Health shall provide the capability to disconnect or disable remote access to the system within [Assignment: organization-defined time period].
Acme Health shall provide the capability to disconnect or disable remote access to the system within one (1) hour.
Acme Health shall implement [Assignment: organization-defined mechanisms] to authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined remote commands].
Acme Health shall require callback capability with re-authentication to verify connections from authorized locations when the Multi-Protocol Label Switching (MPLS) service network cannot be used.

For application systems and turnkey systems that require the vendor to log on, Acme Health shall assign the vendor a User ID and password and have them enter the network through the standard authentication process, with access authorized and logged; Acme Health shall recertify User IDs assigned to vendors within every one (1) year.
For remote access solutions (e.g., e-authentication), Acme Health shall refer to the latest published NIST SP 800-63.

Acme Health shall ensure that all computers and devices, whether government furnished equipment (GFE), contractor furnished equipment (CFE), or personal, that require any network access to an organization network or system are securely configured and meet, as a minimum, the following security requirements: up-to-date system patches; current anti-virus software; host-based intrusion detection system; functionality that provides the capability for automatic execution of code disabled; and employs the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.

For organizations supporting remote access (including teleworking), Acme Health shall ensure the latest published NIST SP 800-46 guidelines are followed by establishing policies and procedures that define: forms of permitted remote access; types of devices permissible for remote access; types of access granted to remote users; and handling of remote user account provisioning.
Acme Health shall establish configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of wireless access.
[NIST 800-53 AC-18 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-18 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall authorize each type of wireless access to the system prior to allowing such connections.
[NIST 800-53 AC-18 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-18 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall protect wireless access to the system using authentication of [Selection (one or more): users; devices] and encryption.
Acme Health shall protect wireless access to the system using authentication of users, devices, and encryption.
Acme Health shall ensure all communications via the wireless access device are encrypted using the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.
Acme Health shall disable, when not intended for use, wireless networking capabilities embedded within system components prior to issuance and deployment.
[NIST 800-53 AC-18(3) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-18(3) AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall identify and explicitly authorize users allowed to independently configure wireless networking capabilities.

Acme Health shall select radio antennas and calibrate transmission power levels to reduce the probability that signals from wireless access points can be received outside of organization-controlled boundaries.

If wireless access is explicitly approved, Acme Health shall disable wireless device service set identifier broadcasting and implement the following wireless restrictions and access controls: encryption protection is enabled; access points are placed in secure areas; access points are shut down when not in use (i.e., nights, weekends); a stateful inspection firewall is implemented between the wireless network and the wired infrastructure; Media Access Control (MAC) address authentication is utilized; static IP addresses, not Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol (DHCP), is utilized; personal firewalls are utilized on all wireless clients; file sharing is disabled on all wireless clients; intrusion detection agents are deployed on the wireless side of the firewall; wireless activity is monitored and recorded, and the records are reviewed on a regular basis (defined in applicable security/privacy plans); and adheres to the latest published IEEE 802.11 Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) standard.

Acme Health shall establish configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for organization-controlled mobile devices, to include when such devices are outside of controlled areas.
[NIST 800-53 AC-19 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-19 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall authorize the connection of mobile devices to organizational systems.
[NIST 800-53 AC-19 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-19 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall obtain authorization from the system Business Owner for the use of mobile devices.

Acme Health shall prohibit the use of unclassified mobile devices in facilities containing systems processing, storing, or transmitting classified information unless specifically permitted by the authorizing official, and enforce restrictions including: connection of unclassified mobile devices to classified systems is prohibited; connection of unclassified mobile devices to unclassified systems requires approval from the authorizing official; use of internal or external modems or wireless interfaces within the unclassified mobile devices is prohibited; and unclassified mobile devices and the information stored on those devices are subject to random reviews and inspections by [Assignment: organization-defined security officials], and if classified information is found, the incident handling policy is followed.
Acme Health shall restrict the connection of classified mobile devices to classified systems in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined security policies].

Acme Health shall employ [Selection: full-device encryption; container-based encryption] to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on [Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices].

Acme Health shall employ full device encryption or container encryption using the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards to protect the confidentiality and integrity of information on approved mobile devices.
Acme Health shall encrypt information on all mobile devices that contain Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Acme Health shall use only organization-owned mobile devices and software to process, access, and store Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Acme Health shall ensure mobile devices are configured to protect the storage and transmission of information on the device and implement scanning of the device using a virus protection application.

Acme Health shall either [Selection (one or more): establish [Assignment: organization-defined terms and conditions]; identify [Assignment: organization-defined controls asserted]], consistent with the trust relationships established with other organizations owning, operating, and/or maintaining external systems, allowing authorized individuals to: (1) access the system from external systems; and (2) process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information using external systems; or prohibit the use of [Assignment: organization-defined prohibited types of external systems].
[NIST 800-53 AC-20 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP AC-20]

Acme Health shall establish organization-defined terms and conditions and identify organization-defined controls asserted to be implemented on external systems, consistent with the trust relationships established with other organizations owning, operating, and/or maintaining external systems, allowing authorized individuals to: (1) access the system from external systems; and (2) process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information using external systems; or prohibit the use of organizationally defined types of external systems.

Acme Health shall ensure that terms and conditions address, at a minimum: the types of applications that can be accessed from external information systems; the maximum FIPS 199 security category of information that can be processed, stored, and transmitted; how other users of the external information system will be prevented from accessing federal information; the use of Virtual Private Network (VPN) and stateful inspection firewall technologies; the use of and protection against the vulnerabilities of wireless technologies; the maintenance of adequate physical security controls; the use of virus and spyware protection software; and how often the security capabilities of installed software are to be updated.

Acme Health shall permit authorized individuals to use an external system to access the system or to process, store, or transmit organization-controlled information only after: (a) verification of the implementation of controls on the external system as specified in the organization's security and privacy policies and security and privacy plans; or (b) retention of approved system connection or processing agreements with the organizational entity hosting the external system.
[NIST 800-53 AC-20(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-20(1) AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall restrict the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems using [Assignment: organization-defined restrictions].
Acme Health shall restrict the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems using organization-defined restrictions.

Acme Health shall restrict the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems unless: the use is documented within appropriate security/privacy plans; the use is explicitly authorized, in writing, by the Authorizing Official (AO) or his/her designated representative; personally owned devices to which organization-controlled portable storage devices are to be attached comply with organization policies and directives on use of personally owned systems and components; and security and privacy safeguards are employed that are appropriate for the sensitivity of the data.

Acme Health shall restrict the use of non-organizationally owned systems or system components to process, store, or transmit organizational information using [Assignment: organization-defined restrictions].

Acme Health shall restrict the use of non-organizationally owned systems or system components to process, store, or transmit organization information unless: (a) the use of contractor-owned devices are: (1) documented within the contract and appropriate security and privacy plans; and (2) explicitly authorized, in writing, by the Authorizing Official (AO) or his/her designated representative; and (b) the use of personally owned devices must comply with organizational policies and directives on use of personally-owned systems and components; and (c) security and privacy safeguards are employed that are appropriate for the sensitivity of the data; and (d) implements either full-device or virtual container encryption to reduce the vulnerability to sensitive information processed, stored, or transmitted by non-organizationally owned systems or system components (devices).

Acme Health shall, prior to being provided access to Personally Identifiable Information (PII) on remote devices, require device users to acknowledge through a binding agreement their responsibilities to safeguard the PII accessible from the device and that they are aware of and agree to the organization's capabilities to manage the organization's PII on the device, including confiscation, in consultation with the organization's counsel, if necessary to remove the PII.
Acme Health shall prohibit the use of [Assignment: organization-defined network-accessible storage devices] in external systems.
Acme Health shall prohibit the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems.

Acme Health shall differentiate the interrelated controls of AC-20, CA-3, and SA-9 as follows: AC-20 describes system access to and from external systems; CA-3 describes documentation of an agreement between the respective system owners when data is exchanged between the CSO and an external system; SA-9 describes the responsibilities of external system owners, which would typically be captured in the agreement required by CA-3.

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information.
Acme Health shall designate individuals authorized to make information publicly accessible.
[NIST 800-53 AC-22 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-22 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall train authorized individuals to ensure that publicly accessible information does not contain nonpublic information.
[NIST 800-53 AC-22 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-22 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall review the proposed content of information prior to posting onto the publicly accessible system to ensure that nonpublic information is not included.
[NIST 800-53 AC-22 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-22 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall review the content on the publicly accessible system for nonpublic information [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and remove such information, if discovered.
Acme Health shall review the content on the publicly accessible system for nonpublic information bi-weekly (no less often than fourteen [14] days) and remove such information, if discovered.

Acme Health shall recognize that a system of records maintaining Personally Identifiable Information (PII) that is not approved for release under the Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) is nonpublic information, and when agencies consider sharing or posting PII, they must do so in a way that fully protects individual privacy.

analyze: This Standard establishes the requirements for identity lifecycle management, account management, access enforcement, and periodic access review at Example Org.

It defines the controls that IAM Engineering must implement, operate, and evidence in order to ensure that access to Example Org systems and to electronic protected health information (ePHI) is granted, maintained, reviewed, and revoked in a controlled and auditable manner.

This Standard applies to all Example Org information systems, accounts (including privileged, non-privileged, shared, group, temporary, and emergency accounts), and to all personnel, contractors, and non-organizational users who are granted logical or physical access to those systems.
It applies to systems that create, receive, maintain, or transmit ePHI, and to all identity and access data held in the [Identity Provider].

IAM Engineering owns the identity lifecycle and access review process end to end, including account provisioning, deprovisioning, privileged access administration, periodic access certification, and the retention of associated evidence.
IAM Engineering is accountable for the outcomes of this process and for coordinating handoffs with HR, supervisors/sponsors, incident response, and other participating teams described below.
Other teams (e.g., HR, supervisors, application owners) participate in individual steps of the process but do not own it.

- Example Org must develop, document, and disseminate an access control policy (addressing purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines) and associated procedures to personnel or roles defined by the organization; designate an official to manage development, documentation, and dissemination of this policy and procedures; and review and update the policy and procedures on an organization-defined frequency (at least every 1 year for AE Mandatory) and following organization-defined events (e.g., assessment/audit findings, security or privacy incidents, or changes in applicable laws/regulations/policies).

- IAM Engineering must implement policies and procedures ensuring workforce members have appropriate access to electronic PHI and preventing those without authorized access from obtaining it, including procedures for authorization and/or supervision of workforce members, a workforce clearance procedure to determine appropriateness of access, and termination procedures to remove access when employment or the arrangement ends.

- IAM Engineering must implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic PHI consistent with applicable requirements, including access authorization procedures for granting access (e.g., to workstations, transactions, programs, or processes) and procedures to establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access based on those authorization policies; if a health care clearinghouse is part of a larger organization, it must implement policies and procedures protecting its electronic PHI from unauthorized access by the larger organization.

- IAM Engineering must define and document the types of accounts allowed and specifically prohibited for use within the system, assign account managers, require organization-defined prerequisites and criteria for group and role membership, specify authorized users, group/role membership, and access authorizations (and any additional organization-defined attributes) for each account, require approvals by organization-defined personnel or roles for account creation requests, create/enable/modify/disable/remove accounts per organization-defined policy and criteria, monitor account use, authorize access based on valid access authorization, intended system usage, and other organization-defined attributes, and align account management processes with personnel termination and transfer processes.

- IAM Engineering must notify account managers and organization-defined personnel or roles within an organization-defined time period (24 hours for AE Mandatory) when accounts are no longer required, within an organization-defined time period (8 hours for AE Mandatory) when users are terminated or transferred, and within an organization-defined time period (8 hours for AE Mandatory) when system usage or need-to-know changes for an individual.

- IAM Engineering must review accounts for compliance with account management requirements on an organization-defined frequency (at least every 90 days for all systems for AE Mandatory), and must establish and implement a process for changing shared or group account authenticators, if deployed, when individuals are removed from the group.
- IAM Engineering must support management of system accounts using automated mechanisms.
[NIST AC-2(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(1) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must automatically remove or disable temporary and emergency accounts after an organization-defined time period (no more than 96 hours from last use for AE Mandatory).
[NIST AC-2(2) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(2) AE Mandatory]

- IAM Engineering must disable accounts (non-consumer accounts within 24 hours for AE Mandatory) that have expired, are no longer associated with a user or individual, are in violation of organizational policy, or have been inactive for an organization-defined time period (60 days for AE Mandatory).
[NIST AC-2(3) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(3) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must automatically audit account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions.
[NIST AC-2(4) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(4) AE Mandatory]

- Example Org must require that users log out when an organization-defined time period of expected inactivity is reached or when a described condition occurs (exceeding 24 hours for AE Mandatory, implemented as a user-policy requirement rather than an automated control).
[NIST AC-2(5) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(5) AE Mandatory]

- IAM Engineering must establish and administer privileged user accounts in accordance with a role-based (or, per NIST, optionally attribute-based) access scheme, monitor privileged role or attribute assignments and changes to roles or attributes, and revoke access when privileged role or attribute assignments are no longer appropriate; for AE Mandatory, this extends to application-specific privileged accounts, and administrator groups, root accounts, and other system-related accounts must be inspected on demand and at least every 14 days, with application-related privileged roles inspected every 30 days.

- IAM Engineering must only permit the use of shared and group accounts that meet organization-defined conditions (for AE Mandatory: a documented, AO-approved business need in advance, and a system security plan describing account use with compensating processes for unique attribution of account user activities).

- IAM Engineering must monitor system accounts for atypical usage and report atypical usage to organization-defined personnel or roles (and, for AE Mandatory, to applicable incident response teams if necessary).
[NIST AC-2(12) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(12) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must disable accounts of individuals within an organization-defined time period (1 hour for AE Mandatory) of discovery that the individual poses a significant risk.
[NIST AC-2(13) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-2(13) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.

- Example Org must enforce the revocation of access authorizations resulting from changes to the security attributes of subjects and objects based on organization-defined rules (including rules governing the timing of revocations, per AE Mandatory).

- Example Org must release information outside the system only if the receiving system, component, or external organization provides organization-defined controls (or, for AE Mandatory, information security and privacy safeguards commensurate with those implemented by the organization), and organization-defined controls are used to validate the appropriateness of the information designated for release.

- Example Org must provide organization-defined mechanisms to enable individuals to have access to organization-defined elements of their personally identifiable information (for AE Mandatory, PII/PHI elements defined in applicable security/privacy plans).

- Example Org must implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems maintaining electronic PHI to allow access only to persons or software programs granted access rights, including assigning a unique name and/or number to identify and track each user's identity, establishing (and implementing as needed) emergency access procedures, implementing automatic logoff after a predetermined period of inactivity, and implementing a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic PHI.
- Example Org must implement procedures to verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic PHI is the one claimed.
- IAM Engineering must identify and document organization-defined duties of individuals requiring separation, and define system access authorizations to support separation of duties.
[NIST AC-5 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-5 AE Mandatory]

- Example Org must employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses for users (or processes acting on behalf of users) that are necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.
[NIST AC-6 Moderate/High | FedRAMP AC-6 | ARC-AMPE AC-6 AE Mandatory]

- IAM Engineering must authorize access to organization-defined security functions (deployed in hardware, software, and firmware) and organization-defined security-relevant information (for FedRAMP: all functions not publicly accessible and all security-relevant information not publicly available; for AE Mandatory: including setting/modifying audit logs and auditing behavior, boundary protection rules, access authorizations, authentication parameters, and system configurations/parameters).
[NIST AC-6(1) Moderate/High | FedRAMP AC-6(1) | ARC-AMPE AC-6(1) AE Mandatory]

- Example Org must require that users of accounts or roles with access to organization-defined security functions or security-relevant information (for FedRAMP: all security functions) use non-privileged accounts or roles when accessing nonsecurity functions.
[NIST AC-6(2) Moderate/High | FedRAMP AC-6(2) | ARC-AMPE AC-6(2) AE Mandatory]
- IAM Engineering must restrict privileged accounts on the system to organization-defined personnel or roles.
[NIST AC-6(5) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(5) AE Mandatory]

- IAM Engineering must review the privileges assigned to organization-defined roles and classes (all users with privileges, at least every 90 days, for AE Mandatory) to validate the need for such privileges, and reassign or remove privileges as necessary to correctly reflect organizational mission and business needs.
[NIST AC-6(7) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(7) AE Mandatory]

- Example Org must prevent organization-defined software (for FedRAMP: any software except software explicitly documented) from executing at higher privilege levels than the users executing the software.
- Example Org must log the execution of privileged functions.
[NIST AC-6(9) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(9) AE Mandatory]
- Example Org must prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.
[NIST AC-6(10) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(10) AE Mandatory]

- Example Org must identify organization-defined user actions that can be performed on the system without identification or authentication, consistent with organizational mission and business functions, and document and provide supporting rationale in the system security plan for user actions not requiring identification or authentication.

- IAM Engineering must manage system identifiers by receiving authorization from organization-defined personnel or roles to assign an individual, group, role, service, or device identifier; selecting an identifier that identifies the individual, group, role, service, or device; assigning the identifier to the intended individual, group, role, service, or device; and preventing reuse of identifiers for an organization-defined time period (2 years for AE Mandatory, including removal of previous identifier-based access authorizations before reuse).
[NIST IA-4 | FedRAMP IA-4 | ARC-AMPE IA-4 AE Mandatory]

- IAM Engineering must manage individual identifiers by uniquely identifying each individual according to organization-defined characteristics identifying individual status (for FedRAMP: contractors and foreign nationals; for AE Mandatory: characteristics such as contractors, foreign nationals, or non-organizational users, as defined in applicable security/privacy plans).
[NIST IA-4(4) Moderate/High | FedRAMP IA-4(4) | ARC-AMPE IA-4(4) AE Mandatory]

- IAM Engineering must identity-proof users who require accounts for logical access to systems based on appropriate identity assurance level requirements specified in applicable standards and guidelines, resolve user identities to a unique individual, and collect, validate, and verify identity evidence (for AE Mandatory, this applies to all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts, and users must be proofed to Identity Assurance Level 2 (IAL-2) or higher per NIST SP 800-63, or via the Federal Data Services Hub Remote Identity Proofing Service for ACA Consumer Accounts).
[NIST IA-12 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-12 AE Mandatory]

- IAM Engineering must require that the registration process to receive an account for logical access include supervisor or sponsor authorization (for AE Mandatory, required for all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts).

- IAM Engineering must require that evidence of individual identification be presented to the registration authority (for AE Mandatory, required for all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts).
[NIST IA-12(2) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-12(2) AE Mandatory]

- IAM Engineering must require that presented identity evidence be validated and verified through organization-defined (or organization-approved, for AE Mandatory, and CMS-agreement-compliant) methods of validation and verification, applying to all accounts including non-privileged/consumer accounts for AE Mandatory.
[NIST IA-12(3) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE IA-12(3) AE Mandatory]

- Upon termination of individual employment, IAM Engineering must disable system access within an organization-defined time period (the same day as termination for AE Mandatory), terminate or revoke any authenticators and credentials associated with the individual, conduct exit interviews covering organization-defined information security topics (including non-disclosure of information security and privacy information for AE Mandatory), retrieve all security-related organizational system-related property, and retain access to organizational information and systems formerly controlled by the terminated individual.

- When individuals are reassigned or transferred to other positions within the organization, IAM Engineering must review and confirm ongoing operational need for current logical and physical access authorizations to systems and facilities, initiate organization-defined transfer or reassignment actions within an organization-defined time period following the formal transfer action (for AE Mandatory, ensuring all no-longer-required system accesses are removed or disabled within 24 hours), modify access authorization as needed to correspond with changes in operational need, and notify organization-defined personnel or roles within an organization-defined time period (24 hours for AE Mandatory).

- Example Org must implement policies and procedures specifying the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic PHI.

- IAM Engineering must maintain access-related policies and procedures, and records of required actions, activities, or assessments, in written (which may be electronic) form; retain such documentation for 6 years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later; make it available to those responsible for implementing the procedures; and review and update it periodically in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic PHI.
IAM Engineering must conduct the identity lifecycle and access review process described in this Standard on a quarterly basis.

Each quarterly cycle must, at a minimum, satisfy the account-review and privileged-access-review floors set out in Sections 5 and 7 above (e.g., the at-least-every-90-days review requirement under [NIST AC-2 | ARC-AMPE AC-2 AE Mandatory] and [NIST AC-6(7) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(7) AE Mandatory]).
[NIST AC-6(7) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE AC-6(7) AE Mandatory]
For each quarterly cycle, IAM Engineering must produce and retain the following evidence, consistent with the retention requirements in Section 11:

| Evidence Artifact | Source / System | Purpose | | ----------------------------------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Identity provider user export | [Identity Provider] | Establishes the authoritative list of active accounts and associated attributes for the review cycle. | | HR active-employee roster | HR system of record | Establishes the authoritative list of currently employed/engaged individuals, used to reconcile against active accounts and identify accounts requiring disablement per Sections 5 and 9. | | Access review tickets with sign-off | [Ticketing System] | Records the review decision, approver, and remediation action for each account or privilege identified during the review, providing the auditable trail of account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions described in Section 5. |

IAM Engineering must reconcile the identity provider user export against the HR active-employee roster during each quarterly cycle, open an access review ticket in the [Ticketing System] for any discrepancy (including accounts of individuals no longer on the HR roster, dormant accounts, or privileged accounts lacking a validated business need), and obtain documented sign-off in the [Ticketing System] before closing each ticket.
These sign-off records constitute the evidence of compliance with the account review, privileged access review, and access authorization modification requirements referenced throughout this Standard.

analyze: This Standard defines the mandatory requirements for authentication, credential management, session control, and system use notification across Example Org information systems.

It applies to all organizational users, processes acting on behalf of users, non-organizational users, and devices that connect to Example Org systems, and to all personnel and teams that implement, operate, or audit these capabilities.
IAM Engineering is accountable for this process end to end, including implementation, operation, review, and evidence production.
Other teams participate in individual steps as identified below.
- **IAM Engineering** owns this Standard and the authentication and credential management process end to end.
IAM Engineering implements, configures, monitors, reviews, and produces the evidence artifacts defined in Section 15.

- **System Owners** determine the elements of the environment that require System Use Notification control, determine how notification compliance will be verified, and provide the periodicity of the check (Section 4.4).
- **Help desk and support personnel** must require user identification for any support transaction that has information security and privacy implications (Section 8.4).
- **Developers and installers of system components** must provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation (Section 10.10).
Example Org must enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period].
ARC-AMPE defines this as five (5) consecutive invalid attempts within a fifteen (15) minute period.
[NIST AC-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

When the maximum number of unsuccessful logon attempts is exceeded, Example Org must automatically take one or more of the following actions: lock the account or node for an organization-defined time period (ARC-AMPE: a minimum of thirty (30) minutes); lock the account or node until released by an administrator; delay the next logon prompt per an organization-defined delay algorithm; notify the system administrator; or take another organization-defined action.
[NIST AC-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-7 AE Mandatory]

Example Org must purge or wipe information from [Assignment: organization-defined mobile devices] based on [Assignment: organization-defined purging or wiping requirements and techniques] after [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive, unsuccessful device logon attempts.
ARC-AMPE sets this at ten (10) consecutive unsuccessful attempts.
Example Org must limit the number of unsuccessful biometric logon attempts to [Assignment: organization-defined number].

Example Org must allow the use of [Assignment: organization-defined authentication factors] different from the primary authentication factors after the organization-defined number of consecutive invalid logon attempts has been exceeded, and must enforce a limit of [Assignment: organization-defined number] consecutive invalid logon attempts through use of the alternative factors by a user during a [Assignment: organization-defined time period].

Example Org must display an organization-defined system use notification message or banner to users before granting access to the system that provides privacy and security notices consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, and states that: - users are accessing a U.S. Government system (ARC-AMPE wording: a system that contains U.S. Government information); - system usage may be monitored, recorded, and subject to audit; - unauthorized use of the system is prohibited and subject to criminal and civil penalties; and - use of the system indicates consent to monitoring and recording.
[NIST AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]
The notification message or banner must be retained on the screen until users acknowledge the usage conditions and take explicit actions to log on to or further access the system.
[NIST AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

For publicly accessible systems, Example Org must display system use information under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions] before granting further access; must display references, if any, to monitoring, recording, or auditing consistent with the privacy accommodations for such systems (which generally prohibit those activities); and must include a description of the authorized uses of the system.
[NIST AC-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-8 AE Mandatory]

The System Owner determines the elements of the environment that require the System Use Notification control, determines how notification compliance will be verified, and provides the periodicity of the check.
If verification is not performed as part of a configuration baseline check, a documented agreement covers how verification results are provided and the verification periodicity.
Example Org must limit the number of concurrent sessions for each [Assignment: organization-defined account and/or account types] to [Assignment: organization-defined number].
Concurrent sessions must be limited for each account and/or account type to one (1) session.
A session is an encounter between an end-user interface device (e.g., computer, terminal, process) and an application, including a network logon.
Any requirement for more than one (1) concurrent session must be expressly required for the performance of job duties and documented in the applicable security and privacy plan.

Example Org must prevent further access to the system by initiating a device lock after a period of inactivity (NIST: [Assignment: organization-defined time period]; ARC-AMPE: fifteen (15) minutes, with inactivity including both remote and internal access connections) and/or by requiring the user to initiate a device lock before leaving the system unattended.
ARC-AMPE requires both the timed lock and the user-initiated lock.
[NIST AC-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]
The device lock must be retained until the user reestablishes access using established identification and authentication procedures.
[NIST AC-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-11 AE Mandatory]
Example Org must conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image.

Example Org must automatically terminate a user session after [Assignment: organization-defined conditions or trigger events] (e.g., periods of user inactivity, targeted responses to certain types of incidents, or time-of-day restrictions on system use), including electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity.
[NIST AC-12 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-12 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(iii) Addressable]
Example Org must provide a logout capability for user-initiated communications sessions whenever authentication is used to gain access to [Assignment: organization-defined information resources].
ARC-AMPE defines information resources as those defined in the applicable security and privacy plans.
Example Org must display an explicit logout message to users indicating the termination of authenticated communications sessions.
ARC-AMPE requires an organization-defined standard logout message documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (e.g., "Your session has been terminated").
Example Org must display an explicit message to users indicating that the session will end in [Assignment: organization-defined time].
ARC-AMPE requires that the organization-defined time until end of session be specified in the applicable security and privacy plans.

Example Org must implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information.

Example Org must implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4).
Example Org must establish (and implement as needed) procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency.
Example Org must implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information.

IAM Engineering must develop, document, and disseminate to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] an identification and authentication policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, together with procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated controls, maintained in written (which may be electronic) form.
[NIST IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.316(b)(1)(i)]
Example Org must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the identification and authentication policy and procedures.
[NIST IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory]

IAM Engineering must review and update the current identification and authentication policy and procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

ARC-AMPE requires review at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, such as assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, or changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Example Org must also review periodically and update as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
[NIST IA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-1 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(iii) Required]
Documentation required under these requirements must be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
Documentation must be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

Example Org must uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users and processes acting on their behalf, including assigning a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity, and must verify that a person or entity seeking access to electronic protected health information is the one claimed.
[NIST IA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2 | ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.312(a)(2)(i) Required | HIPAA 164.312(d)]

Example Org must employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite, and must require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for organizational users.
Example Org must require user identification for any help desk support transaction that has information security and privacy implications.
[ARC-AMPE IA-2 AE Mandatory | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]
Multi-factor authentication must be phishing-resistant, in accordance with current CISA guidance.

Example Org must implement multi-factor authentication for access to privileged accounts, using two or more different factors (something you know, something you have, or something you are) appropriate for the level of risk.
[NIST IA-2(1) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(1) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(1) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must implement multi-factor authentication for access to non-privileged accounts.
ARC-AMPE requires MFA for all non-privileged account types, and strongly recommends (but does not currently mandate) it for consumer accounts.
[NIST IA-2(2) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(2) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(2) AE Mandatory]
When shared accounts or authenticators are employed, Example Org must require users to be individually authenticated before granting access to the shared accounts or resources.
[NIST IA-2(5) High | ARC-AMPE IA-2(5) AE Mandatory]

Example Org must implement multi-factor authentication for local, network, and remote access to privileged and non-privileged accounts such that (a) one of the factors is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access, and (b) the device meets [Assignment: organization-defined strength of mechanism requirements].
ARC-AMPE requires that the device meets the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography.
[NIST IA-2(6) | FedRAMP IA-2(6) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(6) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for access to privileged and non-privileged accounts.
[NIST IA-2(8) Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-2(8) | ARC-AMPE IA-2(8) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must provide a single sign-on capability for [Assignment: organization-defined system accounts and services].
Example Org must accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials.
Example Org must implement [Assignment: organization-defined out-of-band authentication] mechanisms under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions].
Example Org must uniquely identify and authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a local, remote, or network connection.

ARC-AMPE requires, at a minimum, authentication mechanisms using shared information (MAC or IP address) and access control lists to control remote network access, with the specific devices and/or device types approved for identification and authentication management defined in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan.
[NIST IA-3 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-3 AE Mandatory]

Example Org must authenticate [Assignment: organization-defined devices and/or types of devices] before establishing a local, remote, or network connection using bidirectional authentication that is cryptographically based.

Where addresses are allocated dynamically, Example Org must standardize dynamic address allocation lease information and lease duration assigned to devices in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined lease information and lease duration], and must audit lease information when assigned to a device.
Example Org must handle device identification and authentication based on attestation by [Assignment: organization-defined configuration management process].

IAM Engineering must manage system authenticators by verifying, as part of initial authenticator distribution, the identity of the individual, group, role, service, or device receiving the authenticator, and by establishing initial authenticator content for any authenticators issued by the organization.
[NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
Example Org must ensure that authenticators have sufficient strength of mechanism for their intended use.
[NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
IAM Engineering must establish and implement administrative procedures for initial authenticator distribution, for lost or compromised or damaged authenticators, and for revoking authenticators.
[NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
Default authenticators must be changed prior to first use.
[NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
Authenticators must be changed or refreshed [Assignment: organization-defined time period by authenticator type] or when [Assignment: organization-defined events] occur.

ARC-AMPE requires immediate change when authenticators are no longer valid due to known or suspected compromise, and immediate change upon system installation (e.g., default or vendor-supplied passwords), and strongly recommends changing organizational System/User Account passwords at least once every six (6) months.
[NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]

Example Org must protect authenticator content from unauthorized disclosure and modification, and must require individuals to take, and have devices implement, specific controls to protect authenticators (e.g., maintaining possession, not sharing authenticators, and immediately reporting lost, stolen, or compromised authenticators).
[NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
Authenticators for group or role accounts must be changed when membership to those accounts changes.
[NIST IA-5 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP IA-5 | ARC-AMPE IA-5 AE Mandatory]
Example Org must comply with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B for authenticator management.
Organizational System/User Account passwords must be paired with multi-factor authentication (MFA) solutions, and MFA is strongly recommended for ACA Consumer Account passwords.

Authenticators must be compliant with the most recent NIST Digital Identity Guidelines IAL, AAL, and FAL levels appropriate to the certification class: Class B requires level 1, Class C requires level 2, and Class D requires level 3.
Example Org must require developers and installers of system components to provide unique authenticators or change default authenticators prior to delivery and installation.
Example Org must protect authenticators commensurate with the security category of the information to which use of the authenticator permits access.
[NIST IA-5(6) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(6) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must ensure that unencrypted static authenticators are not embedded in applications or other forms of static storage.
Example Org must implement [Assignment: organization-defined security controls] to manage the risk of compromise due to individuals having accounts on multiple systems.
Example Org must use [Assignment: organization-defined external organizations] to federate credentials.
Example Org must bind identities and authenticators dynamically using [Assignment: organization-defined binding rules].
For biometric-based authentication, Example Org must employ mechanisms that satisfy [Assignment: organization-defined biometric quality requirements].
Example Org must prohibit the use of cached authenticators after [Assignment: organization-defined time period].

For PKI-based authentication, Example Org must employ an organization-wide methodology for managing the content of PKI trust stores installed across all platforms, including networks, operating systems, browsers, and applications.
Example Org must use only General Services Administration-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management.

Example Org must require that the issuance of [Assignment: organization-defined types of and/or specific authenticators] be conducted [Selection: in person; by a trusted external party] before [Assignment: organization-defined registration authority] with authorization by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
Example Org must employ presentation attack detection mechanisms for biometric-based authentication.
Example Org must employ [Assignment: organization-defined password managers] to generate and manage passwords, and must protect the passwords using [Assignment: organization-defined controls].
IAM Engineering must maintain a list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords and must update the list [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

ARC-AMPE requires a frequency defined in applicable security/privacy plans, not to exceed one (1) year, and requires updates when organizational passwords are suspected to have been compromised directly or indirectly.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
When users create or update passwords, Example Org must verify that the passwords are not found on the list of commonly-used, expected, or compromised passwords.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Passwords must be transmitted only over cryptographically protected channels.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Passwords must be stored using an approved salted key derivation function, preferably using a keyed hash.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must require immediate selection of a new password upon account recovery.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must allow user selection of long passwords and passphrases, including spaces and all printable characters.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must employ automated tools to assist the user in selecting strong password authenticators.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must enforce [Assignment: organization-defined composition and complexity rules] for passwords.

ARC-AMPE requires compliance with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B, with a minimum of eight (8) characters for ACA Consumer Accounts, a minimum of twelve (12) characters for Administrator/Privileged Accounts, and a minimum of eight (8) characters for all other accounts.
[NIST IA-5(1) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
For public key-based authentication, Example Org must enforce authorized access to the corresponding private key, and must map the authenticated identity to the account of the individual or group.

When public key infrastructure (PKI) is used, Example Org must validate certificates by constructing and verifying a certification path to an accepted trust anchor, including checking certificate status information, and must implement a local cache of revocation data to support path discovery and validation.

Example Org must encrypt authentication assertions when passed through third parties, such as a browser (e.g., a SAML assertion encrypted using XML-Encryption, or an OpenID Connect ID Token encrypted using JSON Web Encryption).
Example Org must obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect the information from possible exploitation and use by unauthorized individuals.
[NIST IA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-6 AE Mandatory]

Example Org must implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet the requirements of applicable laws, executive orders, directives, policies, regulations, standards, and guidelines for such authentication.
[NIST IA-7 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-7 AE Mandatory]
Example Org must use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards for information systems containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Example Org must uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users or processes acting on behalf of non-organizational users.
[NIST IA-8 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8 AE Mandatory]

Example Org must employ effective identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite (ARC-AMPE: compliant with NIST SP 800-63-3 IAL-2/AAL-2), and must require the use of system and/or network authenticators and unique user identifiers for non-organizational users.
Example Org must accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification-compliant credentials from other federal agencies.
Example Org must accept only external authenticators that are NIST-compliant, and must document and maintain a list of accepted external authenticators.

ARC-AMPE additionally requires that external credentials be certified as compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines by an approved accreditation authority, meet or exceed those guidelines, and that the organization use GSA-approved products and services for identity, credential, and access management.
[NIST IA-8(2) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(2) AE Mandatory]

Example Org must conform to [Assignment: organization-defined identity management profiles], defined using identity proofing and authentication processes compliant with the latest published NIST SP 800-63 Digital Identity Guidelines document suite.
[NIST IA-8(4) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-8(4) AE Mandatory]
Example Org must accept and verify federated or PKI credentials that meet [Assignment: organization-defined policy].

Example Org must implement [Assignment: organization-defined measures] to disassociate user attributes or identifier assertion relationships among individuals, credential service providers, and relying parties.

Example Org must require users to re-authenticate when [Assignment: organization-defined circumstances or situations] occur, such as when authenticators, roles, or credentials change, when security categories of systems change, when execution of privileged functions occurs, or after a fixed time period.
ARC-AMPE requires that circumstances requiring re-authentication be defined in the applicable security/privacy plans, including at a minimum after a fixed time period.
[NIST IA-11 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE IA-11 AE Mandatory]
