This Standard establishes the requirements for governing Example Org's information security program, including the development, maintenance, approval, dissemination, and protection of the organization-wide information security program plan, the risk management strategy, planning policies and procedures, system security and privacy plans, and the documentation required by the HIPAA Security Rule.
The Security Program / GRC team is accountable for this process end to end, including all reviews, updates, approvals coordination, dissemination, and evidence retention described in this Standard.
Other teams participate in individual steps as identified, but the Security Program / GRC team owns the process and its handoffs.
This Standard applies to all organizational systems, all organizational entities, and all personnel or roles involved in information security planning and program governance at Example Org.
Example Org must appoint a senior information security officer with the mission and resources to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain an organization-wide information security program.

Example Org must identify the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by the HIPAA Security Rule for the covered entity or business associate.
Example Org must designate an organization-defined official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the planning policy and procedures.
The Security Program / GRC team shall record the designated official and ensure the designation is reflected in the Program plan and org chart.

Example Org must designate officials to be responsible for the development of system information security program plans, and must name these officials in the appropriate security and privacy documents.

Example Org must designate officials to be responsible for the management of planning controls for systems, must name these officials in the appropriate security and privacy documents, and must ensure planning policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and the information on that system.
The Security Program / GRC team shall maintain the record of these designations as part of the Program plan and org chart.

The Security Program / GRC team shall develop and disseminate an organization-wide information security program plan that: Provides an overview of the security program requirements and describes the program management controls and common controls in place or planned for meeting them; Identifies and assigns roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; Reflects coordination among the organizational entities responsible for information security; and Is approved by a senior official with responsibility and accountability for the risk being incurred to organizational operations (including mission, functions, image, and reputation), organizational assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
The approved program plan constitutes the "Program plan and org chart" evidence artifact and must be retained by the Security Program / GRC team with its review dates.

The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the organization-wide information security program plan at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, which include: - System architectural or design changes; - Organization-wide assessment or audit findings; - Security or privacy incidents or breaches; and - Changes to applicable laws (including privacy laws), executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
The organization-wide information security program plan must be protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification.
The Security Program / GRC team shall store and control access to the plan in the [Document Management System] such that disclosure and modification are restricted to authorized personnel.

Common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems must be documented in an appendix to the organization-wide information security program plan, unless they are described in a separate system security plan.
The plan must indicate which separate security plans contain descriptions of common controls.
The Security Program / GRC team shall maintain this appendix and the cross-references to separate security plans.

The Security Program / GRC team shall actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect information security program plans, and shall review the plans at least every one (1) year to ensure they remain effective.
The plans must support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and the information on that system.

The Security Program / GRC team shall develop a comprehensive strategy to manage security risk to organizational operations and assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation associated with the operation and use of organizational systems, and privacy risk to individuals resulting from the authorized processing of personally identifiable information.
The risk management strategy must be implemented consistently across the organization.
The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the risk management strategy at least every one (1) year or as required, to address organizational changes.

The Security Program / GRC team shall develop, document, and disseminate to organization-defined personnel or roles an organization-level planning policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
The Security Program / GRC team shall also develop procedures to facilitate implementation of the planning policy and associated planning controls.

The planning policy, together with the other approved policies governed by this Standard, forms part of the "Approved policy set with review dates" evidence artifact maintained by the Security Program / GRC team.

The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the planning policy and the planning procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, which include: - Assessment or audit findings; - Security or privacy incidents; and - Changes to applicable laws (including privacy laws), executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

Security and privacy plans must be developed for the system that: Are consistent with the organization's enterprise architecture; Explicitly define the constituent system components; Describe the operational context in terms of mission and business processes; Identify the individuals that fulfill system roles and responsibilities; Identify the information types processed, stored, and transmitted; Provide the security categorization with supporting rationale; Describe specific threats of concern; Provide the results of a privacy risk assessment for systems processing PII; Describe the operational environment and any dependencies on or connections to other systems or components; Provide an overview of the security and privacy requirements; Identify any relevant control baselines or overlays; Describe the controls in place or planned, including rationale for tailoring decisions; Include risk determinations for security and privacy architecture and design decisions; and Include security- and privacy-related activities requiring planning and coordination with organization-defined individuals or groups.
The System Security and Privacy Plan must be consistent with the ARC-AMPE SSPP template.
The system security and privacy plans must be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to plan implementation.
The Security Program / GRC team shall coordinate the approval and record it.
Copies of the system security and privacy plans must be distributed, and subsequent changes to the plans must be communicated, to organization-defined personnel, roles, or stakeholders.
The Security Program / GRC team shall perform and record this distribution and change communication.

The system security and privacy plans must be reviewed at least every one (1) year or following significant changes, and must be updated to address changes to the system and environment of operation or problems identified during plan implementation or control assessments.
The system security and privacy plans must be protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification.
The Security Program / GRC team shall store and control access to the plans in the [Document Management System] such that disclosure and modification are restricted to authorized personnel.
Example Org must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

Example Org must conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the covered entity or business associate.
Example Org must implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and [Assignment: complete requirement text — source requirement truncated in input].
Example Org must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule standards, implementation specifications, and other requirements.
Any changes to these policies and procedures must be documented and implemented in accordance with the Rule.

Example Org must maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule in written (which may be electronic) form, and must maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required by the Rule to be documented.
HIPAA Security Rule documentation must be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
The Security Program / GRC team shall manage retention of this documentation in the [Document Management System].
HIPAA Security Rule documentation must be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

HIPAA Security Rule documentation must be reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
The Security Program / GRC team shall perform and record this review.

The Security Program / GRC team shall retain, as evidence of compliance with this Standard: - The approved policy set with review dates, comprising the planning policy and the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule; and - The Program plan and org chart, comprising the approved organization-wide information security program plan and the recorded role designations required by Section 2.

analyze: This Standard establishes requirements for the governance, risk management, and oversight of Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems at Acme Health.
This Standard applies to all AI systems developed, deployed, evaluated, or used by the organization throughout their lifecycle.
Acme Health must establish and maintain policies, processes, procedures, and practices related to the mapping, measuring, and managing of AI risks.
These policies, processes, procedures, and practices must be transparent and implemented effectively.
The organization must implement processes, procedures, and practices to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization's risk tolerance.
The risk management process and its outcomes must be established through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.
Legal and regulatory requirements involving AI must be understood, managed, and documented.
The characteristics of trustworthy AI must be integrated into organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.
Acme Health must plan for ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes.
Organizational roles and responsibilities must be clearly defined, including determining the frequency of periodic review.
Mechanisms must be in place to inventory AI systems and be resourced according to organizational risk priorities.
Processes and procedures must be in place for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organization's trustworthiness.
Accountability structures must be in place so that the appropriate teams and individuals are empowered, responsible, and trained for mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks.
Roles and responsibilities and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks must be documented and clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.

The organization's personnel and partners must receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements.
Executive leadership of the organization must take responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment.
Workforce diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility processes must be prioritized in the mapping, measuring, and managing of AI risks throughout the lifecycle.

Decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle must be informed by a diverse team (e.g., diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and backgrounds).
Policies and procedures must be in place to define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.
Organizational teams must be committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk.

Organizational policies and practices must be in place to foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative impacts.
Organizational teams must document the risks and potential impacts of the AI technology they design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use, and communicate about the impacts more broadly.
Organizational practices must be in place to enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.
Processes must be in place for robust engagement with relevant AI actors.

Organizational policies and practices must be in place to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system regarding the potential individual and societal impacts related to AI risks.
Mechanisms must be established to enable the team that developed or deployed AI systems to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation.

Acme Health shall review and update the current system and communications protection procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.

Acme Health shall review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the electronic protected health information.

Acme Health shall enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between connected systems based on [Assignment: organization-defined information flow control policies].

Acme Health shall use [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy attributes] associated with [Assignment: organization-defined information, source, and destination objects] to enforce [Assignment: organization-defined information flow control policies] as a basis for flow control decisions.
Acme Health shall use protected processing domains to enforce [Assignment: organization-defined information flow control policies] as a basis for flow control decisions.
Acme Health shall enforce [Assignment: organization-defined information flow control policies] dynamically.

Acme Health shall prevent encrypted information from bypassing [Assignment: organization-defined information flow control mechanisms] by [Selection (one or more): decrypting the information; blocking the flow of the encrypted information; terminating communications sessions attempting to pass encrypted information; [Assignment: organization-defined procedure or method]].
Acme Health shall enforce [Assignment: organization-defined limitations] on embedding data types within other data types.
Acme Health shall enforce information flow control based on [Assignment: organization-defined metadata].
Acme Health shall enforce one-way information flows through hardware-based flow control mechanisms.

Acme Health shall enforce the use of human reviews for [Assignment: organization-defined information flows] under the following conditions: [Assignment: organization-defined conditions].

Acme Health shall provide the capability for privileged administrators to enable and disable [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] under the following conditions: [Assignment: organization-defined conditions].

Acme Health shall provide the capability for privileged administrators to configure [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] to support different security or privacy policies.

- Decompose information into [Assignment: organization-defined policy-relevant subcomponents] for submission to policy enforcement mechanisms.
- Implement [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] requiring fully enumerated formats that restrict data structure and content.

- Implement [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] on metadata.
- Modify non-releasable information by implementing [Assignment: organization-defined modification action].
- Parse incoming data into an internal normalized format and regenerate the data to be consistent with its intended specification.

- Sanitize data to minimize [Selection (one or more): delivery of malicious content, command and control of malicious code, malicious code augmentation, and steganography-encoded data; spillage of sensitive information] in accordance with [Assignment: organization-defined policy].

- Implement content filtering solutions that provide redundant and independent filtering mechanisms for each data type.
- Implement a linear content filter pipeline that is enforced with discretionary and mandatory access controls.

- Ensure content filtering mechanisms successfully complete execution without errors and that content filtering actions occur in the correct order and comply with [Assignment: organization-defined policy].
- Implement content filtering mechanisms using multiple processes.
- Prevent the transfer of failed content to the receiving domain.

Acme Health shall uniquely identify and authenticate source and destination points by [Selection (one or more): organization, system, application, service, individual] for information transfer.
Acme Health shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined solutions in approved configurations] to control the flow of [Assignment: organization-defined information] across security domains.

Acme Health shall separate information flows logically or physically using [Assignment: organization-defined mechanisms and/or techniques] to accomplish [Assignment: organization-defined required separations].

Acme Health shall provide access from a single device to computing platforms, applications, or data residing in multiple different security domains, while preventing information flow between the different security domains.

Acme Health shall define in the System Security and Privacy Plan the authority to order the immediate termination and/or suspension of any interconnection, with the Authorizing Official making risk-informed decisions in consultation with the system owner if an interconnection presents an unacceptable level of risk.

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to ensure that all members of the workforce have appropriate access to electronic protected health information and to prevent those workforce members who do not have access from obtaining access to electronic protected health information.
Acme Health shall implement procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with electronic protected health information or in locations where it might be accessed.
Acme Health shall implement procedures to determine that the access of a workforce member to electronic protected health information is appropriate.

Acme Health shall implement procedures for terminating access to electronic protected health information when the employment of, or other arrangement with, a workforce member ends or as required by determinations made regarding appropriateness of access.
Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information that are consistent with applicable requirements.

If a health care clearinghouse is part of a larger organization, the clearinghouse must implement policies and procedures that protect the electronic protected health information of the clearinghouse from unauthorized access by the larger organization.

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures for granting access to electronic protected health information, for example, through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism.

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures that, based upon the covered entity's or business associate's access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures that specify the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are to be performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of a specific workstation or class of workstation that can access electronic protected health information.
Acme Health shall authorize internal connections of [Assignment: organization-defined system components] to the system.
Acme Health shall authorize internal connections of organization-defined system components or classes of components to the system.
Acme Health shall document, for each internal connection, the interface characteristics, security and privacy requirements, and the nature of the information communicated.

Acme Health shall terminate internal system connections after [Assignment: organization-defined conditions].

Acme Health shall terminate internal system connections after issuance of an order by the organization's Chief Information Officer (CIO), Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), or senior privacy official and when such internal system connections no longer support the organization's missions or business functions.
Acme Health shall review [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] the continued need for each internal connection.
Acme Health shall review at least every one (1) year the continued need for each internal connection.
Acme Health shall perform security and privacy compliance checks on constituent system components prior to the establishment of the internal connection.
Acme Health shall separate user functionality, including user interface services, from system management functionality.
Acme Health shall prevent the presentation of system management functionality at interfaces to non-privileged users.
Acme Health shall withhold system administration options until users establish sessions with administrator privileges, rather than using grey-out options to eliminate accessibility.
Acme Health shall store state information from applications and software separately.
Acme Health shall isolate security functions from nonsecurity functions.
Acme Health shall employ hardware separation mechanisms to implement security function isolation.
Acme Health shall isolate security functions enforcing access and information flow control from nonsecurity functions and from other security functions.
Acme Health shall minimize the number of nonsecurity functions included within the isolation boundary containing security functions.
Acme Health shall implement security functions as largely independent modules that maximize internal cohesiveness within modules and minimize coupling between modules.

Acme Health shall prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.

Acme Health shall [Selection: protect against; limit] the effects of the following types of denial-of-service events: [Assignment: organization-defined types of denial-of-service events].

Acme Health shall employ the following controls to achieve the denial-of-service objective: [Assignment: organization-defined controls by type of denial-of-service event].

Acme Health shall restrict the ability of individuals to launch the following denial-of-service attacks against other systems: [Assignment: organization-defined denial-of-service attacks].
Acme Health shall manage capacity, bandwidth, or other redundancy to limit the effects of information flooding denial-of-service attacks.
Acme Health shall employ the following monitoring tools to detect indicators of denial-of-service attacks against, or launched from, the system: [Assignment: organization-defined monitoring tools].
Acme Health shall employ organization-defined monitoring tools to detect indicators of denial-of-service attacks against, or launched from, the system.

Acme Health shall monitor the following system resources to determine if sufficient resources exist to prevent effective denial-of-service attacks: [Assignment: organization-defined system resources].
Acme Health shall monitor organization-defined system resources to determine if sufficient resources exist to prevent effective denial-of-service attacks.
Acme Health shall monitor and control communications at the external managed interfaces to the system and at key internal managed interfaces within the system.

Acme Health shall implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are [Selection: physically; logically] separated from internal organizational networks.
[NIST 800-53 SC-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP SC-7]
Acme Health shall implement subnetworks for publicly accessible system components that are logically separated from internal organizational networks.

Acme Health shall ensure logical separation between publicly accessible components and internal networks prevents traversal without inspection and authorization, such that traffic may not flow unrestricted from publicly accessible components to internal networks.

Acme Health shall connect to external networks or systems only through managed interfaces consisting of boundary protection devices arranged in accordance with an organizational security and privacy architecture.
[NIST 800-53 SC-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP SC-7 | ARC-AMPE SC-7]
Acme Health shall ensure that access to all proxies is denied, except for those hosts, ports, and services that are explicitly required.

Acme Health shall utilize stateful inspection/application firewall hardware and software, using firewalls from at least two (2) or more different vendors at the various levels within the network to reduce the possibility of compromising the entire network.

If Acme Health has an outward-facing web or email presence to the public internet, Acme Health shall implement and support a technical capability to detect malware in web traffic traversing the organization's boundary by monitoring assets without the need to deploy software agents, dynamically generating actionable malware intelligence, detecting and stopping web-based and email attacks, and sending alert data to the organization's Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) system as applicable.
Acme Health shall ensure aggregated boundary protection device information is searchable.
Acme Health shall limit the number of external network connections to the system.
Acme Health shall implement a managed interface for each external telecommunication service.
Acme Health shall establish a traffic flow policy for each managed interface.
Acme Health shall protect the confidentiality and integrity of the information being transmitted across each interface.

Acme Health shall publish information to enable remote networks to detect unauthorized control plane traffic from internal networks.
Acme Health shall filter unauthorized control plane traffic from external networks.

Acme Health shall detect and deny outgoing communications traffic posing a threat to external systems.
Acme Health shall audit the identity of internal users associated with denied communications.
Acme Health shall prevent the exfiltration of information.
Acme Health shall conduct exfiltration tests [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].
Acme Health shall only allow incoming communications from [Assignment: organization-defined authorized sources] to be routed to [Assignment: organization-defined authorized destinations].
Acme Health shall implement [Assignment: organization-defined host-based boundary protection mechanisms] at [Assignment: organization-defined system components].

Acme Health shall isolate [Assignment: organization-defined information security tools, mechanisms, and support components] from other internal system components by implementing physically separate subnetworks with managed interfaces to other components of the system.
Acme Health shall protect against unauthorized physical connections at [Assignment: organization-defined managed interfaces].
Acme Health shall route networked, privileged accesses through a dedicated, managed interface for purposes of access control and auditing.
Acme Health shall prevent the discovery of specific system components that represent a managed interface.
Acme Health shall enforce adherence to protocol formats.
Acme Health shall prevent systems from entering unsecure states in the event of an operational failure of a boundary protection device.

Acme Health shall block inbound and outbound communications traffic between [Assignment: organization-defined communication clients] that are independently configured by end users and external service providers.
Acme Health shall provide the capability to dynamically isolate [Assignment: organization-defined system components] from other system components.

Acme Health shall implement separate network addresses to connect to systems in different security domains.
Acme Health shall disable feedback to senders on protocol format validation failure.
Acme Health shall apply the following processing rules to data elements of personally identifiable information: [Assignment: organization-defined processing rules].

Acme Health shall monitor for permitted processing at the external interfaces to the system and at key internal boundaries within the system.
Acme Health shall document each processing exception.
Acme Health shall review and remove exceptions that are no longer supported.

Acme Health shall prohibit the direct connection of [Assignment: organization-defined unclassified national security system] to an external network without the use of [Assignment: organization-defined boundary protection device].
Acme Health shall prohibit the direct connection of a classified national security system to an external network without the use of [Assignment: organization-defined boundary protection device].

Acme Health shall prohibit the direct connection of [Assignment: organization-defined system] to a public network.

Acme Health shall implement physically or logically separate subnetworks to isolate organization-defined critical system components and functions.

Acme Health shall maintain the [Selection (one or more): confidentiality; integrity] of information during preparation for transmission and during reception.
Acme Health shall maintain the confidentiality and integrity of information during preparation for transmission and during reception.

Acme Health shall implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that electronic protected health information has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.

Acme Health shall implement security measures to ensure that electronically transmitted electronic protected health information is not improperly modified without detection until disposed of.
Acme Health shall implement a mechanism to encrypt electronic protected health information whenever deemed appropriate.
Acme Health shall terminate the network connection associated with a communications session at the end of the session or after [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of inactivity.

Acme Health shall prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices and applications with the following exceptions: [Assignment: organization-defined exceptions where remote activation is to be allowed].

Acme Health shall provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.

Acme Health shall provide [Selection (one or more): physical; logical] disconnect of collaborative computing devices in a manner that supports ease of use.

Acme Health shall provide an explicit indication of current participants in [Assignment: organization-defined online meetings and teleconferences].

Acme Health shall only allow the use of [Assignment: organization-defined certificated authorities] for verification of the establishment of protected sessions.

Acme Health shall provide additional data origin authentication and integrity verification artifacts along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns in response to external name/address resolution queries.

Acme Health shall provide data origin and integrity protection artifacts for internal name/address resolution queries.
Acme Health shall request and perform data origin authentication and data integrity verification on the name/address resolution responses the system receives from authoritative sources.

Acme Health shall ensure the systems that collectively provide name/address resolution service for an organization are fault-tolerant and implement internal and external role separation.

Acme Health shall fail to a [Assignment: organization-defined known system state] for the following failures on the indicated components while preserving [Assignment: organization-defined system state information] in failure: [Assignment: organization-defined types of system failures on system components].
Acme Health shall maintain a separate execution domain for each executing system process.

Acme Health shall implement hardware separation mechanisms to facilitate process isolation.
Acme Health shall maintain a separate execution domain for each thread in [Assignment: organization-defined multi-threaded processing].

analyze: **Standard ID:** SEC-STD-BCP-001 **Owning Team:** Site Reliability Engineering **Applies To:** All personnel, systems, and processes within the scope of Example Org's contingency, backup, and recovery operations

This Standard establishes Example Org's requirements for contingency planning, emergency mode operations, contingency training, contingency plan testing, alternate site and telecommunications arrangements, system backup, and system recovery and reconstitution.
Site Reliability Engineering is accountable for this process end to end, including all handoffs described herein.

- Example Org shall develop, document, and disseminate to applicable personnel and roles a contingency planning policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall develop and document procedures to facilitate the implementation of the contingency planning policy and the associated contingency planning controls, and shall disseminate them to applicable personnel and roles.

- Example Org designates the Site Reliability Engineering team lead as the official responsible for managing the development, documentation, and dissemination of the contingency planning policy and procedures.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall review and update the contingency planning policy and the associated procedures at least annually and following organization-defined events (such as assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines).

- Example Org shall maintain contingency-related policies, procedures, and required records of actions, activities, or assessments in written (which may be electronic) form, shall retain them for 6 years from the date of creation or the date they were last in effect (whichever is later), shall make them available to the persons responsible for implementing the procedures they pertain to, and shall review them periodically and update as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall develop a contingency plan for the system that:
- identifies essential mission and business functions and associated contingency requirements;
- provides recovery objectives, restoration priorities, and metrics;
- addresses contingency roles, responsibilities, and assigned individuals with contact information;
- addresses maintaining essential mission and business functions despite a system disruption, compromise, or failure;
- addresses eventual full system restoration without deterioration of the originally planned and implemented controls;
- addresses the sharing of contingency information; and
- is reviewed and approved by organization-defined personnel or roles.
[NIST CP-2 | FedRAMP CP-2 | ARC-AMPE CP-2 AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall distribute copies of the contingency plan to organization-defined key contingency personnel (identified by name and/or by role) and organizational elements.
[NIST CP-2 | FedRAMP CP-2 | ARC-AMPE CP-2 AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall coordinate contingency planning activities with incident handling activities.
[NIST CP-2 | FedRAMP CP-2 | ARC-AMPE CP-2 AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall review the contingency plan for the system at least annually.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall update the contingency plan to address changes to the organization, system, or environment of operation and problems encountered during contingency plan implementation, execution, or testing, and shall communicate contingency plan changes to organization-defined key contingency personnel and organizational elements.
[NIST CP-2 | FedRAMP CP-2 | ARC-AMPE CP-2 AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall incorporate lessons learned from contingency plan testing, training, or actual contingency activities into contingency testing and training.
[NIST CP-2 | FedRAMP CP-2 | ARC-AMPE CP-2 AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall protect the contingency plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.
[NIST CP-2 | FedRAMP CP-2 | ARC-AMPE CP-2 AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall coordinate contingency plan development with organizational elements responsible for related plans (for example, Business Continuity Plans, Disaster Recovery Plans, Continuity of Operations Plans, Crisis Communications Plans, Critical Infrastructure Plans, Cyber Incident Response Plans, Insider Threat Implementation Plans, and Occupant Emergency Plans), including providing the system contingency plan to organization-defined personnel or roles (for example, the COOP Program Office).
[NIST CP-2(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-2(1) AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall coordinate the contingency plan with the contingency plans of external service providers to ensure that contingency requirements can be satisfied.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall conduct capacity planning so that necessary capacity for information processing, telecommunications, and environmental support exists during contingency operations.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall plan for the resumption of all or essential mission and business functions within the time period defined in the service provider and organization Service Level Agreements of contingency plan activation.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall plan for the resumption of essential mission and business functions within the Business Owner-approved Maximum Tolerable Downtime (MTD) of contingency plan activation; shall calculate the MTD (consistent with the mission/business Continuity of Operations Plan) and recovery time objectives (RTO), with the RTO not exceeding the MTD; shall determine, with the designated authority who can activate the contingency plan, when to activate it based on maintaining continuity of critical mission/business processes; shall ensure resumption meets mission/business COOP requirements for the system; and shall document the results in the mission/business Contingency Plan.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall plan for the continuance of all or essential mission and business functions with minimal or no loss of operational continuity, sustaining that continuity until full system restoration at primary processing and/or storage sites.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall plan for the transfer of all or essential mission and business functions to alternate processing and/or storage sites with minimal or no loss of operational continuity, sustaining that continuity through system restoration to primary processing and/or storage sites.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall identify critical system assets supporting all or essential mission and business functions — including hardware, software, firmware, information, data, applications, communications, and people — shall maintain an active inventory of those critical assets in the Information System Contingency Plan, and shall assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components.
[NIST CP-2(8) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-2(8) AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(E)]

- Example Org shall establish (and implement as needed) policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (for example, fire, vandalism, system failure, and natural disaster) that damages systems containing electronic protected health information, including procedures to restore any loss of data.

- Example Org shall establish (and implement as needed) procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for the protection of the security of electronic protected health information while operating in emergency mode.
- Example Org shall establish (and implement as needed) procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency.

- Example Org shall establish (and implement as needed) procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operations plan in the event of an emergency.
- Site Reliability Engineering is accountable for maintaining these procedures and for their execution during emergency operations.

- Example Org shall provide contingency training to system users consistent with their assigned roles and responsibilities within thirty (30) days of assuming a contingency role or responsibility, when required by system changes, and every one (1) year thereafter.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall review and update contingency training content at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall incorporate simulated events into contingency training to facilitate effective response by personnel in crisis situations.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall employ mechanisms used in operations to provide a more thorough and realistic contingency training environment.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall test the contingency plan for the system at least within every one (1) year using organization-defined tests — including the latest published NIST SP 800-34, NIST SP 800-84, and any organization-defined functional tests or exercises — to determine the effectiveness of the plan and the readiness to execute it.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall review the contingency plan test results and initiate corrective actions if needed.
- Example Org shall implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall produce an after-action report from contingency plan tests to improve existing processes, procedures, and policies; shall make contingency plan test results available to the Business Owner; and shall include in tests and exercises an evaluation of the capability to meet privacy requirements in a contingency scenario, along with corrective measures to address any privacy risks identified.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall coordinate contingency plan testing with organizational elements responsible for related plans (for example, COOP, BCP, CIP, DRP, ISCP, CIRP, and OEP).
[NIST CP-4(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-4(1) AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall test the contingency plan at the alternate processing site both to familiarize contingency personnel with the facility and available resources and to evaluate the capabilities of the alternate processing site to support contingency operations.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall test the contingency plan using organization-defined automated mechanisms.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall include a full recovery and reconstitution of the system to a known state as part of contingency plan testing.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall employ organization-defined mechanisms against an organization-defined system or system component to disrupt and adversely affect the system or system component (self-challenge).
- Each contingency plan test shall produce Restore test results documenting the outcome of the test.
Site Reliability Engineering shall review the Restore test results quarterly and shall record any corrective actions arising from them.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall establish an alternate storage site, including necessary agreements (for example, Service Level Agreements) to permit the storage and retrieval of system backup information, and shall ensure that the alternate storage site provides controls equivalent to those of the primary site.
[NIST CP-6 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-6 AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall identify an alternate storage site that is sufficiently separated from the primary storage site to reduce susceptibility to the same threats, with the sufficient degree of separation (minimum safe distance) determined based on the types of threats of concern to the operation.
[NIST CP-6(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-6(1) AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall configure the alternate storage site to facilitate recovery operations in accordance with recovery time and recovery point objectives.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall identify potential accessibility problems to the alternate storage site in the event of an area-wide disruption or disaster, shall outline explicit mitigation actions to remediate those risks (for example, duplicating backup information at other geographically diverse alternate storage sites or planning for physical access to retrieve backup information if electronic accessibility is disrupted), and shall document those mitigation actions in the ISCP.
[NIST CP-6(3) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-6(3) AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall establish an alternate processing site, including necessary agreements to permit the transfer and resumption of organization-defined system operations for essential mission and business functions within an organization-defined time period (consistent with the recovery time and recovery point objectives specified in the applicable system contingency plan, ISCP, or COOP) when primary processing capabilities are unavailable; shall make the required equipment and supplies available at that site or put contracts in place to support delivery within the organization-defined time period for transfer and resumption; and shall provide controls at the alternate processing site equivalent to those at the primary site.
[NIST CP-7 Moderate, High | FedRAMP CP-7 | ARC-AMPE CP-7 AE Mandatory]

- When an alternate processing site is used, Site Reliability Engineering shall implement administrative, physical, and technical controls to protect Personally Identifiable Information in accordance with the identified privacy risks.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall identify an alternate processing site that is sufficiently separated from the primary processing site to reduce susceptibility to the same threats, with the sufficient degree of separation determined by the organization based on the types of threats of concern (noting that for hostile cyber attacks the degree of separation between sites is less relevant).
[NIST CP-7(1) Moderate, High | FedRAMP CP-7(1) | ARC-AMPE CP-7(1) AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall identify potential accessibility problems to the alternate processing site in the event of an area-wide disruption or disaster, shall outline explicit mitigation actions to remediate those risks (for example, duplicating backup information at other geographically diverse alternate storage sites or planning for physical access to retrieve backup information if electronic accessibility is disrupted), and shall document those remediation actions in the ISCP.
[NIST CP-7(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-7(2) AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall develop alternate processing site agreements (for example, Service Level Agreements) that contain priority-of-service provisions in accordance with availability requirements (including recovery time objectives as specified in the ISCP).
[NIST CP-7(3) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-7(3) AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall prepare the alternate processing site so that it can serve as the operational site supporting essential mission and business functions.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall plan and prepare for circumstances that preclude returning to the primary processing site.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall establish alternate telecommunications services, including necessary agreements, to permit the resumption of organization-defined system operations for essential mission and business functions within the organization-defined resumption time (for example, as specified by system Recovery Time Objectives and business function Maximum Tolerable Downtime in the applicable contingency plan, ISCP, Business Impact Analysis, or COOP) when primary telecommunications capabilities are unavailable at either the primary or alternate processing or storage sites.
[NIST CP-8 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-8 AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall develop primary and alternate telecommunications service agreements that contain priority-of-service provisions in accordance with availability requirements (including recovery time objectives as specified in the ISCP, documented in the ISCP remediation/mitigation strategy), and shall request Telecommunications Service Priority for all telecommunications services used for national security emergency preparedness if the primary and/or alternate telecommunications services are provided by a common carrier.
[NIST CP-8(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-8(1) AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall obtain alternate telecommunications services to reduce the likelihood of sharing a single point of failure with primary telecommunications services, and shall document the remediation/mitigation strategy in the ISCP.
[NIST CP-8(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-8(2) AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall obtain alternate telecommunications services from providers that are separated from primary service providers to reduce susceptibility to the same threats.

- Example Org shall require primary and alternate telecommunications service providers to have contingency plans; Site Reliability Engineering shall review provider contingency plans to ensure they meet organizational contingency requirements and shall obtain evidence of contingency testing and training by providers at the organization-defined frequency.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall test alternate telecommunication services at the organization-defined frequency.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall conduct backups of user-level information contained in organization-defined system components, system-level information contained in the system, and system documentation (including security- and privacy-related documentation), at the organization-defined frequency — for ARC-AMPE, consistent with daily incremental backups and weekly full backups while maintaining three (3) generations of backups, at least one of which is available online (a full backup and all related incremental backups) — and shall create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information.
[NIST CP-9 | ARC-AMPE CP-9 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(A)]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of backup information.

- Example Org shall create a retrievable, exact copy of electronic protected health information when needed before movement of equipment, and shall ensure that a current, retrievable copy of Personally Identifiable Information is available before movement of information system equipment.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall test backup information to verify media reliability and information integrity at the organization-defined frequency — at least every six (6) months for ARC-AMPE — including, for example, decrypting and transporting a random sample of backup files from the alternate storage or backup site and comparing the information to the same information at the primary processing site.
[NIST CP-9(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-9(1) AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall use a sample of backup information in the restoration of selected system functions as part of contingency plan testing.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall store backup copies of organization-defined critical system software and other security-related information in a separate facility or in a fire-rated container that is not collocated with the operational system.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall transfer system backup information to the alternate storage site within an organization-defined time period and transfer rate consistent with the recovery time and recovery point objectives.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall conduct system backup by maintaining a redundant secondary system that is not collocated with the primary system and that can be activated without loss of information or disruption to operations.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall enforce dual authorization for the deletion or destruction of organization-defined backup information.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of organization-defined backup information (all backup files for ARC-AMPE), including encryption of backups at the storage location using the methodology referenced for encrypting Personally Identifiable Information, and mechanisms such as digital signatures and cryptographic hashes to protect backup integrity.
[NIST CP-9(8) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-9(8) AE Mandatory]
- Site Reliability Engineering shall monitor backup job execution through the [Backup System] and shall produce a Backup job success report documenting the outcome of each backup cycle.
Site Reliability Engineering shall review the Backup job success report quarterly and shall record any corrective actions arising from failed or incomplete backup jobs.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall provide for the recovery and reconstitution of the system to a known state within the organization-defined time period consistent with recovery time and recovery point objectives (as defined in the service provider and organization Service Level Agreements, and as specified in the contingency plan or COOP) after a disruption, compromise, or failure.
[NIST CP-10 | FedRAMP CP-10 | ARC-AMPE CP-10 AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall perform secure system recovery and reconstitution in a trusted, secure, and verifiable manner, including resetting all system parameters, reinstalling patches, reestablishing configuration settings, reinstalling application and system software, and fully testing the system.

- Site Reliability Engineering shall implement transaction recovery for systems that are transaction-based (for example, database management systems and transaction processing systems), using mechanisms such as transaction rollback and transaction journaling.
[NIST CP-10(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-10(2) AE Mandatory]

- Site Reliability Engineering shall provide the capability to restore system components within the organization-defined restoration time periods (consistent with the restoration time periods defined in the service provider and organization Service Level Agreements) from configuration-controlled and integrity-protected information representing a known, operational state for the components.
- Site Reliability Engineering shall protect system components used for recovery and reconstitution.

| Activity | Accountable Party | | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------- | | Contingency planning policy and procedure development, dissemination, review, and update | Site Reliability Engineering | | Information System Contingency Plan development, maintenance, testing, and execution | Site Reliability Engineering | | Emergency mode operations procedures | Site Reliability Engineering | | Contingency training delivery and content maintenance | Site Reliability Engineering | | Backup execution, verification, and monitoring | Site Reliability Engineering | | System recovery and reconstitution | Site Reliability Engineering | | Business Owner approval of Maximum Tolerable Downtime and receipt of test results | Business Owner |

Site Reliability Engineering shall maintain the following records as evidence of compliance with this Standard: - **Restore test results** — produced from each contingency plan test and restore verification activity.
[NIST CP-4 | ARC-AMPE CP-4 AE Mandatory | NIST CP-9(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CP-9(1) AE Mandatory]
- **Backup job success report** — produced by the [Backup System] for each backup cycle and reviewed by Site Reliability Engineering quarterly.

All records under this Standard, including contingency-related policies, procedures, and records of actions, activities, or assessments, shall be maintained in written (which may be electronic) form and retained for 6 years from the date of creation or the date they were last in effect, whichever is later.

Acme Health must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards, implementation specifications, or other requirements of this subpart, taking into account those factors specified in § 164.306(b)(2)(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv).

Acme Health must maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with this subpart in written (which may be electronic) form, and maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required by this subpart to be documented.
Acme Health must retain the documentation required by paragraph (b)(1) of this section for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
Acme Health must make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.
Acme Health must review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the electronic protected health information.
Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

Acme Health must conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the covered entity or business associate.
Acme Health must implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level to comply with § 164.306(a).
Acme Health must apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures of the covered entity or business associate.
Acme Health must implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.
Acme Health must implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information that are consistent with the applicable requirements of subpart E of this part.

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures for granting access to electronic protected health information, for example, through access to a workstation, transaction, program, process, or other mechanism.

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures that, based upon the covered entity's or the business associate's access authorization policies, establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process.

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to its electronic information systems and the facility or facilities in which they are housed, while ensuring that properly authorized access is allowed.

Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operations plan in the event of an emergency.
Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.

Acme Health must implement procedures to control and validate a person's access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control, and control of access to software programs for testing and revision.

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility which are related to security (for example, hardware, walls, doors, and locks).
Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to address the final disposition of electronic protected health information, and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored.
Acme Health must implement procedures for removal of electronic protected health information from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use.
Acme Health must maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible therefore.

Acme Health must implement policies and procedures that govern the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media that contain electronic protected health information into and out of a facility, and the movement of these items within the facility.
Acme Health must create a retrievable, exact copy of electronic protected health information, when needed, before movement of equipment.

Acme Health must ensure that plan documents for group health plans provide that the plan sponsor will reasonably and appropriately safeguard electronic protected health information created, received, maintained, or transmitted to or by the plan sponsor on behalf of the group health plan.

Acme Health must amend the plan documents of the group health plan to incorporate provisions requiring the plan sponsor to implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards that reasonably and appropriately protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the electronic protected health information that it creates, receives, maintains, or transmits on behalf of the group health plan.

Acme Health must ensure that business associate contracts provide that the business associate will comply with the applicable requirements of this subpart, ensure that any subcontractors that create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on behalf of the business associate agree to comply with the applicable requirements of this subpart by entering into a contract or other arrangement that complies with this section, and report to the covered entity any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information as required by § 164.410.
