analyze: This standard establishes requirements for the acquisition, development, and management of information systems, system components, and services at Acme Health.

These requirements apply to all systems that store, process, or transmit organizational data, including systems containing Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and Protected Health Information (PHI).
Acme Health shall acquire, develop, and manage systems using a formally defined and documented system development life cycle (SDLC) that incorporates information security and privacy considerations.
Acme Health shall define and document information security and privacy roles and responsibilities throughout the system development life cycle.
Acme Health shall identify individuals having information security and privacy roles and responsibilities.
Acme Health shall integrate the organizational information security and privacy risk management process into system development life cycle activities.

Acme Health shall ensure the security and privacy offices have an opportunity to ensure requirements to protect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) are appropriately considered throughout the system development life cycle.
Acme Health shall protect system preproduction environments commensurate with risk throughout the system development life cycle for the system, system component, or system service.
Acme Health shall approve, document, and control the use of live data in preproduction environments for the system, system component, or system service.

Acme Health shall protect preproduction environments for the system, system component, or system service at the same impact or classification level as any live data in use within the preproduction environments.
If Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is used in the test environment, Acme Health shall apply the same controls required for systems containing PII to the test environment.
Acme Health shall use synthetic PII information to the maximum extent practicable when testing system functionality.
Acme Health shall limit the creation, collection, use, and/or disclosure of PII only to the extent necessary to accomplish a specified and authorized purpose(s).
Acme Health shall obtain approval from the senior official for privacy for the use of PII in testing, training, and research, with preference for using synthetic or de-identified data.
Acme Health shall use non-production data when executing test scripts or in a test environment that is configured to comply with the security controls as though it were a production environment.

Acme Health shall connect all systems supporting development and pre-production testing to an isolated network separated from production systems, with network traffic permitted only to facilitate system testing and restricted by source and destination access control lists as well as ports and protocols.
Acme Health shall plan for and implement a technology refresh schedule for the system throughout the system development life cycle.

Acme Health shall include the following requirements, descriptions, and criteria, explicitly or by reference, in the acquisition contract for the system, system component, or system service: security and privacy functional requirements; strength of mechanism requirements; security and privacy assurance requirements; controls needed to satisfy the security and privacy requirements; security and privacy documentation requirements; requirements for protecting security and privacy documentation; description of the system development environment and environment in which the system is intended to operate; allocation of responsibility or identification of parties responsible for information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management; and acceptance criteria.
Acme Health shall include standardized contract language in acquisition contracts.

In each contract and Statement of Work (SOW) that requires development or access to systems that contain Personally Identifiable Information (PII), Acme Health shall include language requiring adherence to the security and privacy policies and standards set by the organization, define security and privacy roles and responsibilities, and receive approval from the system owner.

When acquiring information systems, components, or services used to store, process, or transmit PII, Acme Health shall ensure the acquisition contract includes: a list of security and privacy controls necessary to ensure protection of PII; privacy requirements, including privacy training and awareness, and rules of behavior; and privacy functional requirements.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to provide a description of the functional properties of the controls to be implemented.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to provide design and implementation information for the controls that includes: [Selection (one or more): security-relevant external system interfaces; high-level design; low-level design; source code or hardware schematics; [Assignment: organization-defined design and implementation information]] at [Assignment: organization-defined level of detail].

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to provide design and implementation information for the controls that includes security-relevant external system interfaces, high-level design documentation, and source code or hardware schematics at organization-defined level of detail to prove the control implementation.

Functional properties of security controls describe the functionality visible at the interfaces of the controls and specifically exclude functionality and data structures internal to the operation of the controls.

Acme Health shall require the developer to use [Assignment: organization-defined systems engineering methods]; [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined system security engineering methods]; [Assignment: organization-defined privacy engineering methods]]; and [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined software development methods]; [Assignment: organization-defined testing, evaluation, assessment, verification, and validation methods]; [Assignment: organization-defined quality control processes]].

Acme Health shall deliver the system, component, or service with [Assignment: organization-defined security configurations] implemented and use the configurations as the default for any subsequent system, component, or service reinstallation or upgrade.

Acme Health shall employ only government off-the-shelf or commercial off-the-shelf information assurance and information assurance-enabled information technology products that compose an NSA-approved solution to protect classified information when the networks used to transmit the information are at a lower classification level than the information being transmitted, and ensure that these products have been evaluated and/or validated by NSA or in accordance with NSA-approved procedures.

Acme Health shall limit the use of commercially provided information assurance and information assurance-enabled information technology products to those products that have been successfully evaluated against a National Information Assurance partnership (NIAP)-approved Protection Profile for a specific technology type, if such a profile exists.

If no NIAP-approved Protection Profile exists for a specific technology type but a commercially provided information technology product relies on cryptographic functionality to enforce its security policy, Acme Health shall require that the cryptographic module is FIPS-validated or NSA-approved.
Acme Health shall employ only information technology products on the FIPS 201-approved products list for Personal Identity Verification (PIV) capability implemented within organizational systems.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to produce a plan for continuous monitoring of control effectiveness that is consistent with the continuous monitoring program of the organization.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services intended for organizational use.

Acme Health shall include [Assignment: organization-defined Privacy Act requirements] in the acquisition contract for the operation of a system of records on behalf of an organization to accomplish an organizational mission or function.

Acme Health shall include organizational data ownership requirements in the acquisition contract and require all data to be removed from the contractor's system and returned to the organization within [Assignment: organization-defined time frame].

Acme Health shall permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on the covered entity's behalf only if the covered entity obtains satisfactory assurances, documented through a written contract, that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information.
[HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(b)(1) | HIPAA Security Rule 164.308(b)(3) | HIPAA Security Rule 164.314(a)(1)]

Acme Health shall ensure the business associate contract requires the business associate to: comply with the applicable requirements of this subpart; ensure that any subcontractors that create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on behalf of the business associate agree to comply with the applicable requirements by entering into a contract that complies with this section; and report to the covered entity any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information.
Acme Health shall apply the same contract requirements to business associate contracts with subcontractors as apply to contracts between a covered entity and business associate.

Acme Health shall obtain or develop administrator documentation for the system, system component, or system service that describes: secure configuration, installation, and operation of the system, component, or service; effective use and maintenance of security and privacy functions and mechanisms; and known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative or privileged functions.

Acme Health shall obtain or develop user documentation for the system, system component, or system service that describes: user-accessible security and privacy functions and mechanisms and how to effectively use those functions and mechanisms; methods for user interaction, which enables individuals to use the system, component, or service in a more secure manner and protect individual privacy; and user responsibilities in maintaining the security of the system, component, or service and privacy of individuals.

Acme Health shall document attempts to obtain system, system component, or system service documentation when such documentation is either unavailable or nonexistent and take [Assignment: organization-defined actions] in response.
Acme Health shall distribute documentation to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
Acme Health shall follow the FedRAMP Secure Configuration Guide rules.
Acme Health shall develop system documentation to describe the system and to specify the purpose, technical operation, access, maintenance, and required training for administrators and users.
Acme Health shall maintain an updated list of related system operations and security documentation.
Upon changes in system functions or processes, Acme Health shall update relevant system documentation and ensure these documents include date and version numbers.

Acme Health shall evaluate and protect documentation based on whether it is in alignment with the risk management strategy or essential for the effective implementation or operation of security controls.

Acme Health shall apply [Assignment: organization-defined systems security and privacy engineering principles] in the specification, design, development, implementation, and modification of the system and system components.
Acme Health shall implement the security design principle of least privilege in [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].
Acme Health shall implement the principle of least privilege consistent with the principle of least privilege as discussed in AC-6.
Acme Health shall implement the security design principle of trusted communications channels in [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].
Acme Health shall restrict access to the communication channel and employ end-to-end protections for data transmitted over the communication channel.
Acme Health shall implement the security design principle of accountability and traceability in [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].

Acme Health shall trace security-relevant actions (i.e., subject-object interactions) to the entity on whose behalf the action is being taken and create a trustworthy infrastructure that can record details about actions that affect system security.
Acme Health shall implement the security design principle of secure defaults in [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].
Acme Health shall implement the security design principle of secure system modification in [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].
Acme Health shall accompany all system changes with a Security Impact Analysis (SIA) and a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA).
Acme Health shall implement the security design principle of sufficient documentation in [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].
Acme Health shall implement the privacy principle of minimization using [Assignment: organization-defined processes].
Acme Health shall drive processes used to implement minimization by business needs and coordinate with the senior privacy officer, consistent with PM-25, PT-2, and SI-12.
Acme Health shall require the developer to perform configuration management during system, component, or service [Selection (one or more): design; development; implementation; operation; disposal].
Acme Health shall document, manage, and control the integrity of changes to [Assignment: organization-defined configuration items].
Acme Health shall implement only organization-approved changes to the system, component, or service.
Acme Health shall document approved changes to the system, component, or service and the potential security and privacy impacts of such changes.
Acme Health shall track security flaws and flaw resolution within the system, component, or service and report findings to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel].
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to enable integrity verification of software and firmware components.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to enable integrity verification of hardware components.
Acme Health shall provide an alternate configuration management process using organizational personnel in the absence of a dedicated developer configuration management team.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to employ tools for comparing newly generated versions of security-relevant hardware descriptions, source code, and object code with previous versions.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to maintain the integrity of the mapping between the master build data describing the current version of security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware and the on-site master copy of the data for the current version.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to execute procedures for ensuring that security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware updates distributed to the organization are exactly as specified by the master copies.
Acme Health shall include [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy representatives] in the [Assignment: organization-defined configuration change management and control process].
Acme Health shall require the developer to develop and implement a plan for ongoing security and privacy control assessments.

Acme Health shall require the developer to perform [Selection (one or more): unit; integration; system; regression] testing/evaluation [Assignment: organization-defined frequency to conduct] at [Assignment: organization-defined depth and coverage].
Acme Health shall require the developer to produce evidence of the execution of the assessment plan and the results of the testing and evaluation.
Acme Health shall require the developer to implement a verifiable flaw remediation process.
Acme Health shall require the developer to correct flaws identified during testing and evaluation.
Acme Health shall not make security-relevant modifications of the information systems after the assessment.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to employ static code analysis tools to identify common flaws and document the results of the analysis.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to employ dynamic code analysis tools to identify common flaws and document the results of the analysis.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to employ interactive application security testing tools to identify flaws and document the results.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to perform threat modeling and vulnerability analyses during development and subsequent testing and evaluation that: uses [Assignment: organization-defined information]; employs [Assignment: organization-defined tools and methods]; conducts the modeling and analyses at [Assignment: organization-defined breadth and depth of modeling and analyses]; and produces evidence that meets [Assignment: organization-defined acceptance criteria].

Acme Health shall require an independent agent satisfying [Assignment: organization-defined independence criteria] to verify the correct implementation of the developer security and privacy assessment plans and the evidence produced during testing and evaluation, and verify that the independent agent is provided with sufficient information to complete the verification process or granted the authority to obtain such information.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to perform a manual code review of [Assignment: organization-defined specific code] using [Assignment: organization-defined processes, procedures, and/or techniques].
Acme Health shall require the developer to perform penetration testing at [Assignment: organization-defined breadth and depth of testing] under [Assignment: organization-defined constraints].
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to perform attack surface reviews.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to verify that the scope of testing and evaluation provides complete coverage of the required controls at [Assignment: organization-defined breadth and depth of testing and evaluation].

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to follow a documented development process that: explicitly addresses security and privacy requirements; identifies the standards and tools used in the development process; documents the specific tool options and tool configurations used in the development process; and documents, manages, and ensures the integrity of changes to the process and/or tools used in development.

Acme Health shall review the development process, standards, tools, tool options, and tool configurations [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] to determine if the process, standards, tools, tool options and tool configurations selected and employed can satisfy [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy requirements].

Acme Health shall review the development process, standards, tools, tool options, and tool configurations at least every one (1) year or as needed to determine if the process, standards, tools, and tool options/configurations selected and employed can satisfy organization-defined security and privacy requirements.

Acme Health shall ensure organization-defined security and privacy requirements include all applicable System Acquisition (SA) and Configuration Management (CM) security controls and are based on the ARC-AMPE security and privacy controls or their equivalent.

When documenting a development process, Acme Health shall consider how to reduce risk to the organization's system architecture and design through efforts such as attack surface reduction, layered defenses, or applying secure software development practices.

Acme Health shall define quality metrics at the beginning of the development process and provide evidence of meeting the quality metrics [Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; [Assignment: organization-defined program review]; upon delivery].
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to select and employ security and privacy tracking tools for use during the development process.

Acme Health shall perform criticality analysis at [Assignment: organization-defined decision points] in the system development life cycle at [Assignment: organization-defined breadth and depth of criticality analysis].
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to reduce attack surfaces to [Assignment: organization-defined thresholds].
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to implement an explicit process to continuously improve the development process.

Acme Health shall perform an automated vulnerability analysis using [Assignment: organization-defined tools]; determine the exploitation potential for discovered vulnerabilities; determine potential risk mitigations for delivered vulnerabilities; and deliver the outputs of the tools and results of the analysis to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to use threat modeling and vulnerability analyses from similar systems, components, or services to inform the current development process.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to provide, implement, and test an incident response plan.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system or system component to archive the system or component to be released or delivered together with the corresponding evidence supporting the final security and privacy review.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system or system component to minimize the use of personally identifiable information in development and test environments.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system or system component to minimize the use of personally identifiable information in development and test environments.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to provide [Assignment: organization-defined training] on the correct use and operation of the implemented security and privacy functions, controls, and/or mechanisms.

Acme Health shall require the developer to produce a design specification and security and privacy architecture that: is consistent with the organization's security and privacy architecture that is an integral part the organization's enterprise architecture; accurately and completely describes the required security and privacy functionality, and the allocation of controls among physical and logical components; and expresses how individual security and privacy functions, mechanisms, and services work together to provide required security and privacy capabilities and a unified approach to protection.

Acme Health shall produce, as an integral part of the development process, a formal policy model describing [Assignment: organization-defined elements of organizational security and privacy policy] to be enforced, and prove that the formal policy model is internally consistent and sufficient to enforce the defined elements of the organizational security and privacy policy when implemented.
Acme Health shall define security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware, and provide a rationale that the definition for security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware is complete.

Acme Health shall produce, as an integral part of the development process, a formal top-level specification that specifies the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware in terms of exceptions, error messages, and effects; show via proof to the extent feasible with additional informal demonstration as necessary that the formal top-level specification is consistent with the formal policy model; show via informal demonstration that the formal top-level specification completely covers the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware; show that the formal top-level specification is an accurate description of the implemented security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware; and describe the security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware mechanisms not addressed in the formal top-level specification but strictly internal to the security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware.

Acme Health shall produce, as an integral part of the development process, an informal descriptive top-level specification that specifies the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware in terms of exceptions, error messages, and effects; show via [Selection: informal demonstration, convincing argument with formal methods as feasible] that the descriptive top-level specification is consistent with the formal policy model; show via informal demonstration that the descriptive top-level specification completely covers the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware; show that the descriptive top-level specification is an accurate description of the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware; and describe the security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware mechanisms not addressed in the descriptive top-level specification but strictly internal to the security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware.

Acme Health shall design and structure the security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to use a complete, conceptually simple protection mechanism with precisely defined semantics, and internally structure the security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware with specific regard for this mechanism.
Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to facilitate testing.

Acme Health shall require the developer of the system, system component, or system service to structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to facilitate controlling access with least privilege.
Acme Health shall design [Assignment: organization-defined critical systems] with coordinated behavior to implement [Assignment: organization-defined capabilities].
Acme Health shall use different designs for [Assignment: organization-defined critical systems] to satisfy a common set of requirements or to provide equivalent functionality.

Acme Health shall require that the developer of systems, system components, or system services has appropriate access authorizations as determined by [Assignment: organization-defined official government duties].

Acme Health shall require that the developer of systems, system components, or system services has appropriate access authorizations as determined by the assigned Authorizing Official (AO) or Designee.
Acme Health shall require that the developer satisfies [Assignment: organization-defined additional personnel screening criteria].
Acme Health shall require that the developer satisfies personnel screening criteria consistent with PS-3.
Acme Health shall replace system components when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor, or manufacturer.

Acme Health shall provide [Selection (one or more): in-house support; [Assignment: organization-defined support from external providers]] for alternative sources for continued support for unsupported components.
Acme Health shall provide justification and document the approval for the continued use of unsupported system components required to satisfy mission/business needs.

Acme Health shall document the justification and approval for the continued use of unsupported system components required to satisfy mission/business needs in a risk acceptance form and ensure the related Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) finding is updated.
Acme Health shall establish plans to mitigate or remove the unsupported system, application, operating system, or software once identified.
Acme Health shall upgrade, retire, or stop the use of the element or component before end of life or the vendor discontinues product support.
Acme Health shall have in place a governance process to review unsupported system components and make a risk-based decision on its continued use when removal is not feasible.
Acme Health shall check the validity of [Assignment: organization-defined information inputs].

Acme Health shall check the validity of defined information inputs for accuracy, completeness, and validity to ensure that inputs match the specific definitions for format and content.

When Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is entered, Acme Health shall use validation techniques to support data quality measures and provide the capability to limit or exclude entering PII within a field.

Acme Health shall provide a manual override capability for input validation of [Assignment: organization-defined information inputs]; restrict the use of the manual override capability to only [Assignment: organization-defined authorized individuals]; and audit the use of the manual override capability.
Acme Health shall review and resolve input validation errors within [Assignment: organization-defined time period].
Acme Health shall verify that the system behaves in a predictable and documented manner when invalid inputs are received.
Acme Health shall account for timing interactions among system components in determining appropriate responses for invalid inputs.
Acme Health shall restrict the use of information inputs to [Assignment: organization-defined trusted sources] and/or [Assignment: organization-defined formats].
Acme Health shall prevent untrusted data injections.
Acme Health shall generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited.
Acme Health shall reveal error messages only to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].

Acme Health shall establish a process or processes to identify and address weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes of [Assignment: organization-defined system or system component] in coordination with [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain personnel].

Acme Health shall document the selected and implemented supply chain processes and controls in [Selection (one or more): security and privacy plans; supply chain risk management plan; [Assignment: organization-defined document]].

Acme Health shall document and maintain the supply chain custody, including replacement devices, to ensure the integrity of the devices before being introduced to the boundary.

Acme Health shall select organization-defined supply chain controls that are not limited to those defined in ARC-AMPE; select other NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supply chain controls as appropriate for the organization.
Acme Health shall employ a diverse set of sources for [Assignment: organization-defined system components and services].
Acme Health shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined controls] to limit harm from potential adversaries identifying and targeting the organizational supply chain.
Acme Health shall ensure that the controls included in the contracts of prime contractors are also included in the contracts of subcontractors.

Acme Health shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined strategies, tools, and methods] acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks.
Acme Health shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined controls] to ensure an adequate supply of [Assignment: organization-defined critical system components].
Acme Health shall assess the system, system component, or system service prior to selection, acceptance, modification, or update.
Acme Health shall implement a tamper protection program for the system, system component, or system service.
Acme Health shall employ anti-tamper technologies, tools, and techniques throughout the system development life cycle.

analyze: This Standard establishes Acme Health's requirements for treating identified AI risks and for responding to, recovering from, and communicating AI-related incidents and errors.
It applies to all Acme Health personnel and systems involved in the development, deployment, operation, monitoring, and decommissioning of AI systems.

The **AI Risk / Incident Response** team is accountable for this process end to end, including all handoffs between risk treatment, monitoring, incident response, and recovery activities described in this document.

| Activity | Accountable Team | Participants | | --- | --- | --- | | AI risk prioritization and treatment decisions | AI Risk / Incident Response | Relevant AI actors, system owners | | High-priority risk response planning | AI Risk / Incident Response | Relevant AI actors, system owners | | Residual risk documentation and disclosure | AI Risk / Incident Response | Downstream acquirers, end users | | Post-deployment monitoring and decommissioning | AI Risk / Incident Response | System owners, relevant AI actors | | Incident tracking, response, recovery, and communication | AI Risk / Incident Response | Affected communities, relevant AI actors |
Acme Health must ensure that AI risks identified through assessments and other analytical output from the MAP and MEASURE functions are prioritized, responded to, and managed.

The AI Risk / Incident Response team shall make a determination as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives, and whether its development or deployment should proceed.
Treatment of documented AI risks must be prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods.

The AI Risk / Incident Response team shall ensure that responses to AI risks deemed high priority, as identified by the MAP function, are developed, planned, and documented; risk response options can include mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.
Negative residual risks (the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users must be documented.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Manage 1.1, considering trustworthiness characteristics when evaluating AI systems' negative risks and benefits [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.1 Action 1], utilizing TEVV outputs from the MAP and MEASURE functions when considering risk treatment [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.1 Action 2], regularly tracking and monitoring negative risks and benefits throughout the AI system lifecycle, including in post-deployment monitoring [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.1 Action 3], regularly assessing and documenting system performance relative to trustworthiness characteristics and tradeoffs between negative risks and opportunities [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.1 Action 4], and evaluating tradeoffs in connection with real-world use cases and impacts and as enumerated in MAP function outcomes [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.1 Action 5].

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Manage 1.2, assigning risk management resources relative to established risk tolerance so that AI systems with lower risk tolerances receive greater oversight, mitigation, and management resources [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.2 Action 1], documenting AI risk tolerance determination practices and resource decisions [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.2 Action 2], and regularly reviewing risk tolerances and re-calibrating, as needed, in accordance with information from AI system monitoring and assessment [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.2 Action 3].

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Manage 1.3, observing regulatory and established organizational, sector, discipline, or professional standards and requirements for applying risk tolerances within the organization [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.3 Action 1], documenting procedures for acting on AI system risks related to trustworthiness characteristics [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.3 Action 2], prioritizing risks involving physical safety, legal liabilities, regulatory compliance, and negative impacts on individuals, groups, or society [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.3 Action 3], identifying risk response plans and resources and organizational teams for carrying out response functions [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.3 Action 4], and storing risk management and system documentation in an organized, secure repository that is accessible by relevant AI actors and appropriate personnel [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.3 Action 5].

Acme Health adopts NIST's suggested repository action as its own requirement: the AI Risk / Incident Response team shall store AI risk management and system documentation in an organized, secure [Document Repository] that is accessible by relevant AI actors and appropriate personnel.

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Manage 1.4, documenting residual risks within risk response plans, denoting risks that have been accepted, transferred, or subject to minimal mitigation [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.4 Action 1], establishing procedures for disclosing residual risks to relevant downstream AI actors [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.4 Action 2], and informing relevant downstream AI actors of requirements for safe operation, known limitations, and suggested warning labels as identified in MAP 3.4 [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 1.4 Action 3].
Acme Health must ensure that strategies to maximize AI benefits and minimize negative impacts are planned, prepared, implemented, and documented, informed by input from relevant AI actors.
Resources required to manage AI risks must be taken into account — along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods — to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts.
Mechanisms must be in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Manage 2.1, planning and implementing risk management practices in accordance with established organizational risk tolerances [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.1 Action 1], verifying that risk management teams are resourced to carry out their functions, including establishing processes for considering methods that are not automated, semi-automated, or other procedural alternatives for AI functions, enhancing AI system transparency mechanisms for AI teams, enabling exploration of AI system limitations by AI teams, and identifying, assessing, and cataloging past failed designs and negative impacts or outcomes to avoid known failure modes [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.1 Action 2], identifying resource allocation approaches for managing risks in systems deemed high-risk, that self-update (adaptive, online, reinforcement self-supervised learning or similar), that are trained without access to ground truth (unsupervised, semi-supervised learning or similar), or with high uncertainty or where risk management is insufficient [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.1 Action 3], regularly seeking and integrating external expertise and perspectives to supplement organizational diversity (e.g., demographic, disciplinary), equity, inclusion, and accessibility where internal capacity is lacking [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.1 Action 4], enabling and encouraging regular, open communication and feedback among AI actors and internal or external stakeholders related to system design or deployment decisions [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.1 Action 5], and preparing and documenting plans for continuous monitoring and feedback mechanisms [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.1 Action 6].

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Manage 2.2, establishing risk controls considering trustworthiness characteristics, including data management, quality, and privacy controls (e.g., minimization, rectification or deletion requests) as part of organizational data governance policies; machine learning and end-point security countermeasures (e.g., robust models, differential privacy, authentication, throttling); business rules that augment, limit, or restrict AI system outputs within certain contexts; utilization of domain expertise related to the deployment context for continuous improvement and TEVV across the AI lifecycle; development and regular tracking of human-AI teaming configurations; model assessment and test, evaluation, validation, and verification (TEVV) protocols; use of standardized documentation and transparency mechanisms; software quality assurance practices across the AI lifecycle; and mechanisms to explore system limitations and avoid past failed designs or deployments [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.2 Action 1], establishing mechanisms to capture feedback from system end users and potentially impacted groups while the system is in deployment, including feedback about how changes in system deployment (e.g., introducing new technology, decommissioning algorithms and models, adapting the system, model, or algorithm) may create negative impacts that are not visible along the AI lifecycle [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.2 Action 2], reviewing insurance policies, warranties, or contracts for legal or oversight requirements for risk transfer procedures [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.2 Action 3], and documenting risk tolerance decisions and risk acceptance procedures [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.2 Action 4].
Procedures must be followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.
The AI Risk / Incident Response team owns these procedures and directs the response and recovery effort.

NIST suggests, among its 7 actions for Manage 2.3, maintaining protocols, resources, and metrics for continual monitoring of AI systems' performance, trustworthiness, and alignment with contextual norms and values [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.3 Action 1], establishing and regularly reviewing treatment and response plans for incidents, negative impacts, or outcomes [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.3 Action 2], establishing and maintaining procedures to regularly monitor system components for drift, decontextualization, or other AI system behavior factors [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.3 Action 3], establishing and maintaining procedures for capturing feedback about negative impacts [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.3 Action 4], verifying contingency processes to handle any negative impacts associated with mission-critical AI systems and to deactivate systems [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.3 Action 5], enabling preventive and post-hoc exploration of AI system limitations by relevant AI actor groups [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.3 Action 6], and decommissioning systems that exceed risk tolerances [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.3 Action 7].

Mechanisms must be in place and applied, and responsibilities must be assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.
The AI Risk / Incident Response team is responsible for these mechanisms and assigns the associated responsibilities.

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Manage 2.4, regularly reviewing established procedures for AI system bypass actions, including plans for redundant or backup systems to ensure continuity of operational and/or business functionality [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.4 Action 1], regularly reviewing and identifying system incident thresholds for activating bypass or deactivation responses [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.4 Action 2], applying change management processes to understand the upstream and downstream consequences of bypassing or deactivating an AI system or AI system components [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.4 Action 3], applying protocols, resources, and metrics for decisions to supersede, bypass, or deactivate AI systems or AI system components [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.4 Action 4], preserving materials for forensic, regulatory, and legal review [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.4 Action 5], conducting internal root cause analysis and process reviews of bypass or deactivation events [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.4 Action 6], decommissioning and preserving system components that cannot be updated to meet criteria for redeployment [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.4 Action 7], and establishing criteria for redeploying updated system components, in consideration of trustworthiness characteristics [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 2.4 Action 8].

Acme Health adopts NIST's suggested preservation action as its own requirement: the AI Risk / Incident Response team shall preserve materials from bypass, deactivation, and incident events for forensic, regulatory, and legal review.
Risk treatments for identified and measured AI risks — including response and recovery and communication plans — must be documented and monitored regularly.
The AI Risk / Incident Response team owns this documentation and monitoring.

Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans must be implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.

NIST suggests, among its 9 actions for Manage 4.1, establishing and maintaining procedures to monitor AI system performance for risks and negative and positive impacts associated with trustworthiness characteristics [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 1], performing post-deployment TEVV tasks to evaluate AI system validity and reliability, bias and fairness, privacy, and security and resilience [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 2], evaluating AI system trustworthiness in conditions similar to the deployment context of use, and prior to deployment [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 3], establishing and implementing red-teaming exercises at a prescribed cadence and evaluating their efficacy [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 4], establishing procedures for tracking dataset modifications such as data deletion or rectification requests [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 5], establishing mechanisms for regular communication and feedback between relevant AI actors and internal or external stakeholders to capture information about system performance, trustworthiness, and impact [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 6], sharing information about errors, near-misses, and attack patterns with incident databases, other organizations with similar systems, and system users and stakeholders [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 7], responding to and documenting detected or reported negative impacts or issues in AI system performance and trustworthiness [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 8], and decommissioning systems that exceed established risk tolerances [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.1 Action 9].
Measurable activities for continual improvement must be integrated into AI system updates and include regular engagement with interested parties, including relevant AI actors.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Manage 4.2, integrating trustworthiness characteristics into protocols and metrics used for continual improvement [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.2 Action 1], establishing processes for evaluating and integrating feedback into AI system improvements [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.2 Action 2], assessing and evaluating the alignment of proposed improvements with relevant regulatory and legal frameworks [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.2 Action 3], assessing and evaluating the alignment of proposed improvements connected to the values and norms within the context of use [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.2 Action 4], and documenting the basis for decisions made relative to tradeoffs between trustworthiness characteristics, system risks, and system opportunities [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.2 Action 5].

Incidents and errors must be communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities, and processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors must be followed and documented.
The AI Risk / Incident Response team owns these communication, tracking, response, and recovery processes end to end.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Manage 4.3, establishing procedures to regularly share information about errors, incidents, and negative impacts with relevant stakeholders, operators, practitioners and users, and impacted parties [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.3 Action 1], maintaining a database of reported errors, near-misses, incidents, and negative impacts including date reported, number of reports, assessment of impact and severity, and responses [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.3 Action 2], maintaining a database of system changes, reason for change, and details of how the change was made, tested, and deployed [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.3 Action 3], maintaining version history information and metadata to enable continuous improvement processes [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.3 Action 4], and verifying that relevant AI actors responsible for identifying complex or emergent risks are properly resourced and empowered [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 4.3 Action 5].

Acme Health adopts NIST's suggested database actions as its own requirements: the AI Risk / Incident Response team shall maintain a database of reported errors, near-misses, incidents, and negative impacts — including date reported, number of reports, assessment of impact and severity, and responses — in the [Ticketing System], and shall maintain a database of system changes, the reason for change, and details of how the change was made, tested, and deployed in the [Ticketing System].

analyze: This Standard defines the requirements that Example Org must satisfy for the secure acquisition, development, and management of systems, system components, and system services.

It applies to all systems, system components, and system services developed, acquired, operated, modified, and disposed of by Example Org, and to all developers, integrators, and contractors performing development work on behalf of Example Org.
Application Security is accountable for this process end to end, including its execution, its handoffs to other teams, and the evidence it produces.
Evidence artifacts expected from this process include SAST/DAST results per release and dependency and supply-chain scan output.

Example Org must acquire, develop, and manage the system using a formally defined and documented system development life cycle process that incorporates information security and privacy considerations.
Information security and privacy roles and responsibilities throughout the system development life cycle must be defined and documented.
The individuals holding information security and privacy roles and responsibilities must be identified.
The organizational information security and privacy risk management process must be integrated into system development life cycle activities.

The security and privacy offices must be provided an opportunity to ensure that requirements for protecting Personally Identifiable Information (PII) are appropriately considered throughout the system development life cycle.
Application Security must coordinate this opportunity as part of its ownership of the lifecycle process.
System preproduction environments must be protected commensurate with risk throughout the system development life cycle for the system, system component, or system service.
The use of live data in preproduction environments for the system, system component, or system service must be approved, documented, and controlled.
Application Security owns the approval and control of this use.
Preproduction environments must be protected at the same impact or classification level as any live data in use within those environments.

If PII is used in a test environment, the same controls required for systems containing PII must be applied to that test environment, and synthetic PII must be used to the maximum extent practicable when testing system functionality.
The creation, collection, use, and/or disclosure of PII must be limited only to the extent necessary to accomplish a specified and authorized purpose.
Approval from the senior official for privacy must be obtained for the use of PII in testing, training, and research; the use of synthetic or de-identified data is preferred for these purposes.
A technology refresh schedule for the system must be planned for and implemented throughout the system development life cycle.
Application Security owns the planning and implementation of this schedule.

The acquisition contract for the system, system component, or system service must include, explicitly or by reference and using organization-defined standardized contract language, the following: security and privacy functional requirements; strength of mechanism requirements; security and privacy assurance requirements; controls needed to satisfy security and privacy requirements; security and privacy documentation requirements; requirements for protecting security and privacy documentation; a description of the system development environment and the intended operating environment; allocation of responsibility (or identification of parties responsible) for information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management; and acceptance criteria.

Each contract and Statement of Work requiring development of, or access to, systems containing PII must include language requiring adherence to the organization's security and privacy policies and standards (consistent with 45 CFR § 155.260(b)), must define security and privacy roles and responsibilities, and must receive approval from the system owner.

When acquiring systems, components, or services used to store, process, or transmit PII, the acquisition contract must include, in consultation with the privacy office: a list of security and privacy controls necessary to protect PII (e.g., how data is stored, handled, and accessed within the service provider environment) and, if appropriate, enforcement of applicable privacy requirements; privacy requirements including privacy training and awareness and rules of behavior; and privacy functional requirements specific to privacy.
The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to provide a description of the functional properties of the security and privacy controls to be implemented.
[NIST 800-53 SA-4(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-4(1) AE Mandatory]

The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to provide design and implementation information for the controls — including security-relevant external system interfaces, high-level design documentation, and source code or hardware schematics — at [Assignment: organization-defined level of detail] to prove control implementation.
[NIST 800-53 SA-4(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-4(2) AE Mandatory]

Functional properties of security controls describe functionality (security capabilities, functions, or mechanisms) visible at the interfaces of the controls and specifically exclude functionality and data structures internal to the operation of the controls.

The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to use [Assignment: organization-defined systems engineering methods]; \[Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined system security engineering methods]; [Assignment: organization-defined privacy engineering methods]\]; and \[Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined software development methods]; [Assignment: organization-defined testing, evaluation, assessment, verification, and validation methods]; [Assignment: organization-defined quality control processes]\].

The system, component, or service must be delivered with [Assignment: organization-defined security configurations] implemented, and those configurations must be used as the default for any subsequent reinstallation or upgrade.

Only government off-the-shelf or commercial off-the-shelf information assurance (and information assurance-enabled) IT products that compose an NSA-approved solution must be employed to protect classified information when the transmitting networks are at a lower classification level than the information, and such products must have been evaluated and/or validated by NSA or in accordance with NSA-approved procedures.

Commercially provided information assurance (and information assurance-enabled) IT products must be limited to those successfully evaluated against a NIAP-approved Protection Profile for the specific technology type, if such a profile exists; if no such profile exists but the product relies on cryptographic functionality to enforce its security policy, the cryptographic module must be FIPS-validated or NSA-approved.

The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to produce a plan for continuous monitoring of control effectiveness that is consistent with the organization's continuous monitoring program.
The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services intended for organizational use.
[NIST 800-53 SA-4(9) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-4(9) AE Mandatory]
Only information technology products on the FIPS 201-approved products list must be employed for Personal Identity Verification (PIV) capability implemented within organizational systems.
[Assignment: organization-defined Privacy Act requirements] must be included in the acquisition contract for the operation of a system of records on behalf of the organization.

Organizational data ownership requirements must be included in the acquisition contract, and the contract must require all data to be removed from the contractor's system and returned to the organization within [Assignment: organization-defined time frame].

A covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on its behalf only if the covered entity obtains satisfactory assurances (in accordance with § 164.314(a)) that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information; a business associate may permit a subcontractor to do the same only if the business associate obtains equivalent satisfactory assurances from the subcontractor.

The satisfactory assurances obtained from a business associate (or subcontractor) must be documented through a written contract or other arrangement that meets the applicable requirements of § 164.314(a).

Business associate contracts must require the business associate to comply with the applicable requirements of the Security Rule; to ensure that any subcontractors creating, receiving, maintaining, or transmitting electronic protected health information on its behalf agree to comply with those requirements by entering into a compliant contract or other arrangement; and to report to the covered entity any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information as required by § 164.410.

The same contract requirements that apply between a covered entity and a business associate apply in the same manner to the contract or other arrangement between a business associate and its subcontractor.

Administrator documentation for the system, system component, or system service must be obtained or developed describing: secure configuration, installation, and operation; effective use and maintenance of security and privacy functions and mechanisms; and known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative or privileged functions.

User documentation for the system, system component, or system service must be obtained or developed describing: user-accessible security and privacy functions and mechanisms and how to use them effectively; methods for user interaction that enable more secure use of the system and protection of individual privacy; and user responsibilities for maintaining system security and individual privacy.
[NIST 800-53 SA-5 | FedRAMP SA-5 | ARC-AMPE SA-5 AE Mandatory]
Attempts to obtain system, component, or service documentation when it is unavailable or nonexistent must be documented, and [Assignment: organization-defined actions] must be taken in response.
[NIST 800-53 SA-5 | FedRAMP SA-5 | ARC-AMPE SA-5 AE Mandatory]
System documentation must be distributed to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
[NIST 800-53 SA-5 | FedRAMP SA-5 | ARC-AMPE SA-5 AE Mandatory]
System documentation must be developed that describes the system and specifies the purpose, technical operation, access, maintenance, and required training for administrators and users.
An updated list of related system operations and security documentation must be maintained.
Relevant system documentation must be updated upon changes in system functions or processes, and the documents must include date and version numbers.

System documentation must be evaluated and protected based on whether it is aligned with the risk management strategy or is essential for the effective implementation or operation of security controls.
The FedRAMP Secure Configuration Guide rules for system documentation must be followed.

[Assignment: organization-defined systems security and privacy engineering principles] must be applied in the specification, design, development, implementation, and modification of the system and system components.
The security design principles listed below must be implemented in [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components].
