The security design principle of least privilege must be implemented consistently with the principle of least privilege as discussed in AC-6 and reflected across all aspects of secure system design.

The security design principle of trusted communications channels must be implemented including restricting access to the communication channel and employing end-to-end protections for data transmitted over it.

The security design principle of accountability and traceability must be implemented enabling tracing of security-relevant actions (subject-object interactions) to the entity on whose behalf the action is taken, supported by a trustworthy infrastructure that records details of actions affecting system security.
The security design principle of secure system modification must be implemented with all system changes accompanied by a Security Impact Analysis (SIA) and a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA).
Application Security owns the review of these analyses.

The privacy principle of minimization must be implemented using [Assignment: organization-defined processes], with those processes driven by business needs, coordinated with the senior privacy officer, and implemented consistently with PM-25, PT-2, and SI-12.

The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to perform configuration management during design, development, implementation, operation, and disposal of the system, component, or service.
[NIST 800-53 SA-10 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-10 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to document, manage, and control the integrity of changes to [Assignment: organization-defined configuration items].
[NIST 800-53 SA-10 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-10 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to implement only organization-approved changes to the system, component, or service.
[NIST 800-53 SA-10 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-10 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to document approved changes to the system, component, or service and the potential security and privacy impacts of those changes.
[NIST 800-53 SA-10 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-10 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to track security flaws and flaw resolution within the system, component, or service and report findings to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
[NIST 800-53 SA-10 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-10 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to enable integrity verification of software and firmware components.
An alternate configuration management process using organizational personnel must be provided in the absence of a dedicated developer configuration management team.
Application Security owns this alternate process.
The developer must be required to enable integrity verification of hardware components.
The developer must be required to employ tools for comparing newly generated versions of security-relevant hardware descriptions, source code, and object code with previous versions.

The developer must be required to maintain the integrity of the mapping between the master build data describing the current version of security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware and the on-site master copy of that data.

The developer must be required to execute procedures ensuring that security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware updates distributed to the organization are exactly as specified by the master copies.
[Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy representatives] must be required to be included in the [Assignment: organization-defined configuration change management and control process].

The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required, at all post-design stages of the system development life cycle, to develop and implement a plan for ongoing security and privacy control assessments.
[NIST 800-53 SA-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-11 AE Mandatory]

The developer must be required to perform unit, integration, system, and regression testing/evaluation at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency to conduct] and at [Assignment: organization-defined depth and coverage].
[NIST 800-53 SA-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-11 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to produce evidence of the execution of the assessment plan and the results of the testing and evaluation.
[NIST 800-53 SA-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-11 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to implement a verifiable flaw remediation process.
[NIST 800-53 SA-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-11 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to correct flaws identified during testing and evaluation.
[NIST 800-53 SA-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-11 AE Mandatory]
No security-relevant modifications may be made to the information systems after the assessment.
Non-production data must be used when executing test scripts, or a test environment configured to comply with the security controls as though it were a production environment must be used.

All systems supporting development and pre-production testing must be connected to an isolated network separated from production systems, permitting network traffic into and out of that environment only to facilitate system testing and restricting it by source and destination access control lists as well as ports and protocols.
The developer must be required to employ static code analysis tools to identify common flaws and document the results of the analysis.
The results per release are recorded and retained as SAST/DAST results per release.

The developer must be required to perform threat modeling and vulnerability analyses during development and subsequent testing and evaluation that use [Assignment: organization-defined information] (contextual information such as impact, environment of operations, known or assumed threats, and acceptable risk levels), employ [Assignment: organization-defined tools and methods], conduct the modeling and analyses at [Assignment: organization-defined breadth and depth], and produce evidence meeting [Assignment: organization-defined acceptance criteria].

An independent agent satisfying [Assignment: organization-defined independence criteria] must be required to verify the correct implementation of the developer security and privacy assessment plans and the evidence produced during testing and evaluation, and it must be verified that the independent agent is provided with sufficient information to complete the verification or granted the authority to obtain it.
The developer must be required to perform a manual code review of [Assignment: organization-defined specific code] using [Assignment: organization-defined processes, procedures, and/or techniques].
The developer must be required to perform penetration testing at [Assignment: organization-defined breadth and depth of testing] and under [Assignment: organization-defined constraints].
The developer must be required to perform attack surface reviews.

The developer must be required to verify that the scope of testing and evaluation provides complete coverage of the required controls at [Assignment: organization-defined breadth and depth of testing and evaluation].
The developer must be required to employ dynamic code analysis tools to identify common flaws and document the results of the analysis.
The results per release are recorded and retained as SAST/DAST results per release.
The developer must be required to employ interactive application security testing tools to identify flaws and document the results.

The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to follow a documented development process that explicitly addresses security and privacy requirements; identifies the standards and tools used in the development process; documents the specific tool options and tool configurations used; and documents, manages, and ensures the integrity of changes to the process and/or tools used in development.
[NIST 800-53 SA-15 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-15 AE Mandatory]

The development process, standards, tools, tool options, and tool configurations must be reviewed at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] (at least annually, or as needed, per ARC-AMPE) to determine whether they can satisfy the [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy requirements].
[NIST 800-53 SA-15 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SA-15 AE Mandatory]

The developer must be required to define quality metrics at the beginning of the development process and provide evidence of meeting them \[Selection (one or more): [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; [Assignment: organization-defined program review]; upon delivery\].
The developer must be required to select and employ security and privacy tracking tools for use during the development process.

Criticality analysis must be performed at [Assignment: organization-defined decision points] in the system development life cycle and at [Assignment: organization-defined breadth and depth of criticality analysis].
The developer must be required to reduce attack surfaces to [Assignment: organization-defined thresholds].
The developer must be required to implement an explicit process to continuously improve the development process.

The developer must be required to perform an automated vulnerability analysis using [Assignment: organization-defined tools]; determine the exploitation potential for discovered vulnerabilities; determine potential risk mitigations for delivered vulnerabilities; and deliver the tool outputs and analysis results to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
The tool outputs per release are recorded and retained as dependency and supply-chain scan output.
The developer must be required to use threat modeling and vulnerability analyses from similar systems, components, or services to inform the current development process.
The developer must be required to provide, implement, and test an incident response plan.
The developer must be required to archive the system or component to be released or delivered together with the corresponding evidence supporting the final security and privacy review.
The developer of the system or system component must be required to minimize the use of personally identifiable information in development and test environments.
[NIST 800-53 SA-15(12) | NIST 800-53 SA-15(13) | ARC-AMPE SA-15(12) AE Mandatory]

The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to provide [Assignment: organization-defined training] on the correct use and operation of the implemented security and privacy functions, controls, and/or mechanisms.

The developer of the system, system component, or system service must be required to produce a design specification and security and privacy architecture that is consistent with the organization's security and privacy architecture (an integral part of the enterprise architecture); accurately and completely describes the required security and privacy functionality and the allocation of controls among physical and logical components; and expresses how individual security and privacy functions, mechanisms, and services work together to provide the required capabilities and a unified approach to protection.
Application Security reviews this specification and architecture.
[NIST 800-53 SA-17 High | ARC-AMPE SA-17 AE Mandatory]

The developer must be required to produce, as an integral part of the development process, a formal policy model describing [Assignment: organization-defined elements of organizational security and privacy policy] to be enforced, and prove that the model is internally consistent and sufficient to enforce those elements when implemented.
The developer must be required to define security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware and provide a rationale that the definition is complete.

The developer must be required to produce, as an integral part of the development process, a formal top-level specification of the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware; demonstrate (to the extent feasible via proof, supplemented by informal demonstration) its consistency with the formal policy model and its complete coverage of those interfaces; show it accurately describes the implemented security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware; and describe internal mechanisms not addressed in the specification.

The developer must be required to produce, as an integral part of the development process, an informal descriptive top-level specification of the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware; demonstrate via [Selection: informal demonstration, convincing argument with formal methods as feasible] its consistency with the formal policy model and via informal demonstration its complete coverage of those interfaces; show it accurately describes those interfaces; and describe internal mechanisms not addressed in the specification.

The developer must be required to design and structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware around a complete, conceptually simple protection mechanism with precisely defined semantics, and to internally structure them with specific regard for that mechanism.
The developer must be required to structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to facilitate testing.
The developer must be required to structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to facilitate controlling access with least privilege.
[Assignment: organization-defined critical systems] must be designed with coordinated behavior to implement [Assignment: organization-defined capabilities].
Different designs must be used for [Assignment: organization-defined critical systems] to satisfy a common set of requirements or provide equivalent functionality.

The developer of systems, system components, or system services must be required to have appropriate access authorizations as determined by assigned [Assignment: organization-defined official government duties] / the assigned Authorizing Official or designee.
[NIST 800-53 SA-21 High | ARC-AMPE SA-21 AE Mandatory]
The developer must be required to satisfy personnel screening criteria — [Assignment: organization-defined additional personnel screening criteria] per NIST, consistent with PS-3 per ARC-AMPE.
[NIST 800-53 SA-21 High | ARC-AMPE SA-21 AE Mandatory]
System components must be replaced when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor, or manufacturer.

Where replacement is not done, alternative sources for continued support for unsupported components must be provided \[Selection (one or more): in-house support; [Assignment: organization-defined support from external providers]\].

Alternatively (per ARC-AMPE), continued use of unsupported system components required to satisfy mission/business needs must be justified and approved, with the justification and approval recorded in a risk acceptance form and the related Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) finding updated.
Application Security owns this justification and approval.

Plans must be established to mitigate or remove the unsupported system, application, operating system, or software once identified, and the element or component must be upgraded, retired, or stopped from use before end of life or vendor discontinuation of product support.
Where removal of unsupported components is not feasible, a governance process must be maintained to review them and make a risk-based decision on their continued use.
Application Security owns this governance process.

The validity of [Assignment: organization-defined information inputs] — per ARC-AMPE, all inputs to web/application servers, database servers, and any system or application input that might receive a crafted exploit aimed at executing code or causing a buffer overflow — must be checked for accuracy, completeness, and validity (character set, length, numerical range, and acceptable values) to ensure inputs match the specified definitions for format and content.
[NIST 800-53 SI-10 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SI-10 AE Mandatory]

When PII is entered, validation techniques that support data quality must be used (e.g., ensuring the PII entered is the expected type and format), the capability must be provided to limit or exclude entering PII within a field that should not contain it (e.g., recognizing a restricted format such as a Social Security Number), and reasonable steps must be taken to ensure PII is complete, accurate, and up to date as required by laws and regulations.

A manual override capability for input validation of [Assignment: organization-defined information inputs] must be provided, its use restricted to [Assignment: organization-defined authorized individuals], and its use audited.
Input validation errors must be reviewed and resolved within [Assignment: organization-defined time period].
It must be verified that the system behaves in a predictable and documented manner when invalid inputs are received.
Timing interactions among system components must be accounted for in determining appropriate responses for invalid inputs.
The use of information inputs must be restricted to [Assignment: organization-defined trusted sources] and/or [Assignment: organization-defined formats].
Untrusted data injections must be prevented.

Error messages must be generated that provide the information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited (e.g., user name/password combinations, password-reset validation attributes, PII, biometric or authenticator data, sensitive financial records, or content related to internal security functions such as private encryption keys, allow/deny-list rules, and object permission settings).
[NIST 800-53 SI-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SI-11 AE Mandatory]

Error messages must be revealed only to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] — per ARC-AMPE, personnel or roles documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP), i.e., authorized individuals with a need for the information in the performance of their duties.
[NIST 800-53 SI-11 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SI-11 AE Mandatory]

A process or processes must be established to identify and address weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes of [Assignment: organization-defined system or system component], in coordination with [Assignment: organization-defined supply chain personnel].
[NIST 800-53 SR-3 | FedRAMP SR-3 | ARC-AMPE SR-3 AE Mandatory]

[Assignment: organization-defined supply chain controls] must be employed to protect against supply chain risks to the system, system component, or system service and to limit the harm or consequences from supply chain-related events; these controls are not limited to those defined in ARC-AMPE and may include other NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supply chain controls as appropriate.
[NIST 800-53 SR-3 | FedRAMP SR-3 | ARC-AMPE SR-3 AE Mandatory]

The selected and implemented supply chain processes and controls must be documented in \[Selection (one or more): security and privacy plans; supply chain risk management plan; [Assignment: organization-defined document]\].
[NIST 800-53 SR-3 | FedRAMP SR-3 | ARC-AMPE SR-3 AE Mandatory]
The Cloud Service Operator must document and maintain supply chain custody — including replacement devices — to ensure the integrity of devices before they are introduced to the boundary.
A diverse set of sources must be employed for [Assignment: organization-defined system components and services].
[Assignment: organization-defined controls] must be employed to limit harm from potential adversaries identifying and targeting the organizational supply chain.
The controls included in the contracts of prime contractors must also be included in the contracts of subcontractors.
[Assignment: organization-defined acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods] must be employed to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks.
[Assignment: organization-defined controls] must be employed to ensure an adequate supply of [Assignment: organization-defined critical system components].
The system, system component, or system service must be assessed prior to selection, acceptance, modification, or update.
A tamper protection program must be implemented for the system, system component, or system service.
Anti-tamper technologies, tools, and techniques must be employed throughout the system development life cycle.

[Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components] must be inspected for tampering \[Selection (one or more): at random; at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; upon [Assignment: organization-defined indications of need for inspection]\].
Anti-counterfeit policy and procedures must be developed and implemented that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components from entering the system.

Counterfeit system components must be reported to \[Selection (one or more): source of counterfeit component; [Assignment: organization-defined external reporting organizations]; [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]\].
[Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] must be trained to detect counterfeit system components (including hardware, software, and firmware).
Configuration control must be maintained over [Assignment: organization-defined system components] awaiting service or repair and serviced or repaired components awaiting return to service.
Counterfeit system components must be scanned for at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

[Assignment: organization-defined data, documentation, tools, or system components] must be disposed of using [Assignment: organization-defined techniques and methods] — per ARC-AMPE, in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88, Guidelines for Media Sanitization, with techniques consistent with MP-6 Media Sanitization.
This Standard's lifecycle process operates on a continuous basis.
Application Security owns the continuous execution of the process, its handoffs to participating teams, and its outcomes.

The process must produce and retain the following evidence artifacts: SAST/DAST results per release (generated per Sections 9.9 and 9.16) and dependency and supply-chain scan output (generated per Section 10.8).
Application Security is accountable for the production and retention of these artifacts.

analyze: This Standard establishes requirements for measuring, monitoring, and documenting risks associated with Acme Health's artificial intelligence (AI) systems throughout their lifecycle.

This Standard ensures that AI systems deployed by Acme Health are evaluated for trustworthiness, safety, security, fairness, and other characteristics critical to healthcare operations and patient safety.

This Standard applies to all AI systems developed, deployed, or operated by Acme Health, including: - AI models used in clinical decision support - AI systems processing protected health information - AI applications supporting administrative or operational functions - Third-party AI systems integrated into Acme Health operations
This Standard applies to all personnel involved in the development, deployment, evaluation, or management of AI systems.
Acme Health must select approaches and metrics for measuring AI risks for implementation, starting with the most significant AI risks.
Risks or trustworthiness characteristics that will not or cannot be measured must be documented.
The appropriateness of AI metrics and effectiveness of existing controls must be regularly assessed and updated, including reports of errors and potential impacts on affected communities.
Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the system and/or independent assessors must be involved in regular assessments and updates.

Domain experts, users, AI actors external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, and affected communities must be consulted in support of assessments as necessary per organizational risk tolerance.
Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV must be documented.
Evaluations involving human subjects must meet applicable requirements (including human subject protection) and must be representative of the relevant population.
AI system performance or assurance criteria must be measured qualitatively or quantitatively and demonstrated for conditions similar to deployment setting(s).
The functionality and behavior of the AI system and its components must be monitored when in production.
The AI system to be deployed must be demonstrated to be valid and reliable.
Limitations of the generalizability beyond the conditions under which the technology was developed must be documented.

The AI system must be evaluated regularly for safety risks, demonstrated to be safe with residual negative risk not exceeding the risk tolerance, and able to fail safely, particularly if made to operate beyond its knowledge limits.
Safety metrics must reflect system reliability and robustness, real-time monitoring, and response times for AI system failures.
AI system security and resilience must be evaluated and documented.
Risks associated with transparency and accountability must be examined and documented.
The AI model must be explained, validated, and documented.
AI system output must be interpreted within its context to inform responsible use and governance.
Privacy risk of the AI system must be examined and documented.
Fairness and bias must be evaluated and results must be documented.
Environmental impact and sustainability of AI model training and management activities must be assessed and documented.
Effectiveness of the employed TEVV metrics and processes in the measure function must be evaluated and documented.

Approaches, personnel, and documentation must be in place to regularly identify and track existing, unanticipated, and emergent AI risks based on factors such as intended and actual performance in deployed contexts.
Risk tracking approaches must be considered for settings where AI risks are difficult to assess using currently available measurement techniques or where metrics are not yet available.
Feedback processes for end users and impacted communities to report problems and appeal system outcomes must be established and integrated into AI system evaluation metrics.
Measurement approaches for identifying AI risks must be connected to deployment context(s) and informed through consultation with domain experts and other end users.

Measurement results regarding AI system trustworthiness in deployment context(s) and across the AI lifecycle must be informed by input from domain experts and relevant AI actors to validate whether the system is performing consistently as intended.

Measurable performance improvements or declines based on consultations with relevant AI actors, including affected communities, and field data about context-relevant risks and trustworthiness characteristics must be identified and documented.
AI system owners must ensure that all measurement, monitoring, and documentation requirements in this Standard are implemented for AI systems under their responsibility.
The Information Security function must verify compliance with this Standard through [Review Frequency] audits and assessments.
Clinical and domain experts must participate in the evaluation, validation, and ongoing assessment of AI systems within their areas of expertise as required by this Standard.
Acme Health must establish processes to engage affected communities, end users, and patients in providing feedback on AI system performance and impacts as required by this Standard.

All documentation required by this Standard must be: - Maintained in [Document Management System] - Accessible to authorized personnel responsible for AI system governance, audit, and compliance - Retained for [Retention Period] - Updated when changes occur to AI systems, measurement approaches, or risk assessments

Failure to comply with this Standard may result in: - Suspension of AI system deployment or operation - Disciplinary action in accordance with Acme Health policies - Regulatory or legal consequences where applicable

This Standard must be reviewed [Review Frequency] and updated as necessary to reflect changes in: - Regulatory requirements - AI technology and measurement capabilities - Organizational risk tolerance - Lessons learned from AI system incidents or performance issues

analyze: This Standard establishes the requirements governing the maintenance, repair, and replacement of Example Org information systems and their components, including maintenance performed locally, off site, and remotely (nonlocally).

It defines the policy framework, maintenance controls, tool management requirements, personnel authorization requirements, and documentation obligations that Infrastructure Security shall implement and audit against.
[NIST 800-53 MA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-1 AE Mandatory]

This Standard applies to all Example Org information systems and system components subject to maintenance, repair, or replacement, to all maintenance tools used on those systems, to all personnel and external organizations performing maintenance activities, and to the facilities housing electronic information systems and electronic protected health information (ePHI).
The System Maintenance process operates on a **continuous** basis and is owned end to end by **Infrastructure Security**.

- **Infrastructure Security** owns the System Maintenance process end to end, including scheduling, approval, monitoring, recordkeeping, review, and evidence production for all maintenance activities.
- Infrastructure Security shall designate a **Maintenance Policy Official** to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the maintenance policy and procedures required by Section 4.
[NIST 800-53 MA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-1 AE Mandatory]

- Personnel or roles designated by Infrastructure Security shall perform the explicit approval functions identified in this Standard (e.g., approval of off-site removal, approval of nonlocal maintenance sessions).
- Supervisory and escorting personnel shall meet the authorization, training, and technical competence requirements of Section 8.
[NIST 800-53 MA-5 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP MA-5 | ARC-AMPE MA-5 AE Mandatory]
- All workforce members are subject to the ePHI access requirements of Sections 8 and 10.

Infrastructure Security shall develop, document, and disseminate to applicable personnel or roles a maintenance policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
Infrastructure Security shall develop and maintain procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and the associated maintenance controls.
[NIST 800-53 MA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-1 AE Mandatory]
The Maintenance Policy Official designated by Infrastructure Security shall manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the maintenance policy and procedures.
[NIST 800-53 MA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-1 AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall review and update the maintenance policy and the maintenance procedures at [Review Frequency] and following organization-defined events (such as assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines).
ARC-AMPE requires this review at least every one (1) year.
[NIST 800-53 MA-1 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-1 AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with this Standard in written (which may be electronic) form, and shall maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required to be documented under this Standard.

Infrastructure Security shall schedule, document, and review records of maintenance, repair, and replacement on system components in accordance with manufacturer or vendor specifications and/or organizational requirements.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-2 AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall approve and monitor all maintenance activities, whether performed on site or remotely and whether the system or components are serviced on site or removed to another location.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-2 AE Mandatory]

Personnel or roles designated by Infrastructure Security shall explicitly approve removal of the system or system components from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-2 AE Mandatory]
Infrastructure Security shall sanitize equipment to remove information from associated media prior to removal from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement.
ARC-AMPE requires removal of all organizational information using sanitization methods per the latest published NIST SP 800-88.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-2 AE Mandatory]
Infrastructure Security shall check all potentially impacted controls to verify they are still functioning properly following maintenance, repair, or replacement actions.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-2 AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall include the following maintenance-related information in organizational maintenance records (maintenance records with authorization): date and time, description of maintenance performed, names of individuals performing it, escort name, and components removed or replaced.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-2 AE Mandatory]
All repairs and modifications to system components on systems where Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is stored or accessed shall be documented.

Infrastructure Security shall implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to security-related physical components of a facility (for example, hardware, walls, doors, and locks).

Infrastructure Security shall schedule, conduct, and document maintenance, repair, and replacement actions for the system using [Automated Maintenance Mechanism], and shall produce up-to-date, accurate, and complete records of all such actions requested, scheduled, in process, and completed.
Infrastructure Security shall approve, control, and monitor the use of system maintenance tools, and shall review previously approved maintenance tools at [Tool Review Frequency].
ARC-AMPE requires this review at least every one (1) year.
[NIST 800-53 MA-3 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-3 AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall check all maintenance tools with the capability of retaining information to ensure information is not saved on the tool and that the tool is appropriately sanitized, using approved sanitization methods from the latest published NIST SP 800-88.
Infrastructure Security shall inspect the maintenance tools used by maintenance personnel for improper or unauthorized modifications.
[NIST 800-53 MA-3(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-3(1) AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall check media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used in the system; if malware or unauthorized changes are discovered, the discovery shall be treated consistent with organizational policies and procedures for incident handling.
[NIST 800-53 MA-3(2) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-3(2) AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall prevent the removal of maintenance equipment containing organizational information by verifying there is no organizational information on the equipment, sanitizing or destroying the equipment, retaining the equipment within the facility, or obtaining an exemption from personnel or roles designated by Infrastructure Security explicitly authorizing removal.
Infrastructure Security shall check all such tools with information-retention capability to ensure no information is saved and shall sanitize them per the latest published NIST SP 800-88.
[NIST 800-53 MA-3(3) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-3(3) AE Mandatory]
The use of maintenance tools shall be restricted to authorized personnel only.

Infrastructure Security shall monitor the use of maintenance tools that execute with increased privilege, including monitoring to detect unauthorized access to information and assets that would otherwise be inaccessible to individuals as a result of increased system privileges.

Infrastructure Security shall inspect maintenance tools to ensure the latest software updates and patches are installed, and shall, to the extent possible, install updates and patches on organizational systems to minimize vulnerabilities, with minimal impact to organizational systems.

Infrastructure Security shall approve and monitor nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic activities, and shall allow the use of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic tools only as consistent with organizational policy and documented in the security plan for the system.
[NIST 800-53 MA-4 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-4 AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall employ strong authentication in the establishment of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions, in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B. If password-based authentication is used during remote maintenance, the passwords shall be changed following each remote maintenance service.
[NIST 800-53 MA-4 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-4 AE Mandatory]
Infrastructure Security shall maintain records for nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic activities (remote maintenance session logs).
[NIST 800-53 MA-4 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-4 AE Mandatory]
Session and network connections shall be terminated when nonlocal maintenance is completed.
[NIST 800-53 MA-4 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-4 AE Mandatory]
Infrastructure Security shall sanitize media used during remote nonlocal maintenance in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88.

Infrastructure Security shall log organization-defined audit events (as defined in the organization's formal audit policy; see AU-2) for nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions, and shall review the audit records of those sessions to detect anomalous behavior.

Infrastructure Security shall require that nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic services be performed from a system implementing a security capability comparable to the system being serviced, or shall remove the component to be serviced prior to nonlocal maintenance, sanitize it for organizational information, and after service inspect and sanitize it for potentially malicious software before reconnecting it.

Infrastructure Security shall protect nonlocal maintenance sessions by employing [Replay-Resistant Authenticators] and by separating the maintenance sessions from other network sessions with the system using physically or logically separated communications paths.

Each nonlocal maintenance session shall require approval by personnel or roles designated by Infrastructure Security, and personnel and roles designated by Infrastructure Security shall be notified of the date and time of planned nonlocal maintenance.

Infrastructure Security shall implement organization-defined cryptographic mechanisms ([Cryptographic Mechanisms]) to protect the integrity and confidentiality of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic communications.
Infrastructure Security shall verify session and network connection termination after the completion of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions.

Infrastructure Security shall ensure all workforce members have appropriate access to electronic protected health information and shall prevent workforce members without such access from obtaining it.

Infrastructure Security shall establish a process for maintenance personnel authorization and shall maintain a list of authorized maintenance organizations or personnel, including procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with electronic protected health information or in locations where it might be accessed.
[NIST 800-53 MA-5 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP MA-5 | ARC-AMPE MA-5 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(A) Addressable]

Infrastructure Security shall verify that non-escorted personnel performing maintenance on the system possess the required access authorizations (and security credentials), and shall implement procedures to determine that a workforce member's access to electronic protected health information is appropriate.
[NIST 800-53 MA-5 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP MA-5 | ARC-AMPE MA-5 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.308(a)(3)(ii)(B) Addressable]

Infrastructure Security shall designate organizational personnel with required access authorizations and technical competence to supervise the maintenance activities of personnel who do not possess the required access authorizations.
Infrastructure Security shall ensure supervisors are trained on supervisory and escorting responsibilities, and shall follow organization-established visitor logging and escort security protocols.
[NIST 800-53 MA-5 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP MA-5 | ARC-AMPE MA-5 AE Mandatory]
Infrastructure Security shall clearly document nationality requirements (or lack thereof) for maintenance personnel where applicable.

Infrastructure Security shall implement procedures for terminating access to electronic protected health information when a workforce member's employment or other arrangement ends, or as required by clearance determinations.

Infrastructure Security shall implement procedures for the use of maintenance personnel who lack appropriate security clearances or are not U.S. citizens, under which such personnel are escorted and supervised during maintenance and diagnostic activities by approved organizational personnel who are fully cleared, have appropriate access authorizations, and are technically qualified.
Prior to such maintenance, all volatile information storage components shall be sanitized and all nonvolatile storage media shall be removed or physically disconnected and secured.

Where a component cannot be sanitized, removed, or disconnected, Infrastructure Security shall develop and implement organization-defined alternate controls (identified in the System Security and Privacy Plan).
[NIST 800-53 MA-5(1) High | FedRAMP MA-5(1) | ARC-AMPE MA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

Infrastructure Security shall verify that personnel performing maintenance and diagnostic activities on a system processing, storing, or transmitting classified information possess security clearances and formal access approvals for at least the highest classification level and for compartments of information on the system.
Infrastructure Security shall verify that personnel performing maintenance and diagnostic activities on a system processing, storing, or transmitting classified information are U.S. citizens.

Foreign nationals with appropriate security clearances may be used to conduct maintenance on classified systems only when the systems are jointly owned and operated by the United States and foreign allied governments, or owned and operated solely by foreign allied governments, with approvals, consents, and operational conditions fully documented within Memoranda of Agreements.

Infrastructure Security shall ensure that non-escorted personnel performing maintenance activities not directly associated with the system but in its physical proximity have required access authorizations.
Infrastructure Security shall obtain maintenance support and/or spare parts for organization-defined system components within [Maintenance Support Time Period] of failure.
ARC-AMPE requires obtaining them within the applicable Recovery Time Objective (RTO) specified in the system Contingency Plan, consistent with the RTOs defined in CP-7(3) and CP-8.
[NIST 800-53 MA-6 Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE MA-6 AE Mandatory]
Infrastructure Security shall perform preventive maintenance on organization-defined system components at [Preventive Maintenance Interval].
ARC-AMPE specifies intervals based on the applicable Recovery Time Objective (RTO) in the system Contingency Plan, consistent with CP-7(3) and CP-8.
Infrastructure Security shall perform predictive maintenance on organization-defined system components at [Predictive Maintenance Interval].
Infrastructure Security shall transfer predictive maintenance data to a maintenance management system using [Automated Maintenance Mechanism].

Infrastructure Security shall implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and the facilities in which they are housed, while ensuring properly authorized access is allowed.

Infrastructure Security shall establish (and implement as needed) procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operations plan in the event of an emergency.
Infrastructure Security shall implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.

Infrastructure Security shall implement procedures to control and validate a person's access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control, and control of access to software programs for testing and revision.
Documentation maintained under this Standard shall be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.
Required documentation shall be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
Documentation shall be reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
Infrastructure Security shall produce and retain, as evidence of conformance with this Standard:

| Artifact | Produced Under | Retention | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Maintenance records with authorization (including date and time, description of work, names of individuals performing it, escort name, and components removed or replaced) | Sections 5.1, 5.6, 5.7 | 6 years from creation or from date last in effect, whichever is later [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) Required] | | Remote maintenance session logs (nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic activity records) | Sections 7.3, 7.6, 7.11 | 6 years from creation or from date last in effect, whichever is later [HIPAA 164.316(b)(2)(i) Required] |
Infrastructure Security is accountable for the completeness, accuracy, and availability of these artifacts on a continuous basis.

analyze: **Standard Owner:** AI Risk / Product **Applies to:** All personnel who develop, procure, deploy, operate, or oversee AI systems at Acme Health
This standard defines the requirements for establishing the context, categorization, capability assessment, and impact assessment of every AI system used at Acme Health.
The documentation produced under this standard constitutes the AI system inventory record for each system.
AI Risk / Product is accountable for this process end to end, including the performance of each step, the review of its outputs, and the handoffs between participating teams.
- **AI Risk / Product** owns this standard, performs and reviews the documentation activities it requires, and answers for the outcome of each assessment.

- Participating teams (including development, operations, legal, and clinical or business units that engage with a given AI system) contribute to individual steps at AI Risk / Product's direction, but ownership of the process and its handoffs remains with AI Risk / Product.

AI Risk / Product must establish and document the context for each AI system, including its intended purposes and potentially beneficial uses, the context-specific laws, norms, and expectations that apply, and the prospective settings in which it will be deployed.
[NIST AI RMF Map 1, NIST AI RMF Map 1.1]
AI Risk / Product must document the specific set or types of users of the AI system along with their expectations.

AI Risk / Product must document assumptions and related limitations about the AI system's purposes, uses, and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle, along with related TEVV and system metrics.

AI Risk / Product must ensure that the interdisciplinary AI actors, competencies, skills, and capacities used to establish context reflect demographic diversity and broad domain and user experience expertise, must document their participation, and must prioritize opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration.
AI Risk / Product must understand and document the organization's mission and relevant goals for AI technology.
AI Risk / Product must clearly define the business value or context of business use for each AI system; for existing AI systems, AI Risk / Product must re-evaluate it.
AI Risk / Product must determine and document the organization's risk tolerances for AI.

AI Risk / Product must elicit system requirements (e.g., "the system shall respect the privacy of its users") from relevant AI actors and ensure they are understood by those actors, and must take socio-technical implications into account in design decisions to address AI risks.

NIST suggests, among its 13 actions for Map 1.1, maintaining awareness of industry, technical, and applicable legal standards; examining the trustworthiness of the AI system design and considering non-AI solutions; identifying whether non-AI or non-technology alternatives would lead to more trustworthy outcomes; determining and delineating the expected and acceptable AI system context of use, including social norms, impacted individuals, groups, and communities, potential positive and negative impacts, and the operational environment; performing context analysis related to time frame, safety concerns, geographic area, physical environment, ecosystems, social environment, and cultural norms within the intended setting; identifying human-AI interaction and roles, such as whether the application will support or replace human decision making; and planning for risks related to human-AI configurations by documenting requirements, roles, and responsibilities for human oversight of deployed systems.

[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.1 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.1 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.1 Action 9 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.1 Action 10 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.1 Action 12 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.1 Action 13]

NIST suggests, among its 2 actions for Map 1.2, establishing interdisciplinary teams that reflect a wide range of skills, competencies, and capabilities, verifying that team membership includes demographic diversity, broad domain expertise, and lived experiences, and documenting team composition; and creating and empowering interdisciplinary expert teams to capture and engage the interdependencies of deployed AI systems and related concepts from disciplines outside of AI practice such as law, sociology, psychology, anthropology, public policy, systems design, and engineering.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.2 Action 2]

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Map 1.3, reviewing the documented system purpose from a socio-technical perspective and in consideration of societal values; determining possible misalignment between societal values and stated organizational principles and code of ethics; flagging latent incentives that may contribute to negative impacts; and evaluating AI system purpose in consideration of potential risks, societal values, and stated organizational principles.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.3 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.3 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.3 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.3 Action 5]

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Map 1.4, documenting the business value or context of business use; reconciling documented concerns about the system's purpose within the business context of use against the organization's stated values, mission statements, social responsibility commitments, and AI principles; and reconsidering the design, implementation strategy, or deployment of AI systems whose potential impacts do not reflect institutional values.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.4 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.4 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.4 Action 3]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Map 1.5, utilizing existing regulations and guidelines for risk criteria, tolerance, and response; establishing risk tolerance levels for AI systems and allocating appropriate oversight resources to each level; establishing risk criteria in consideration of different sources of risk (e.g., financial, operational, safety and wellbeing, business, reputational, and model risks) and different levels of risk (e.g., from negligible to critical); identifying the maximum allowable risk tolerance above which the system will not be deployed or will need to be prematurely decommissioned; articulating and analyzing tradeoffs across trustworthiness characteristics and documenting them with traceable actions; and reviewing uses of AI systems for "off-label" purposes, especially in settings deemed high-risk.

[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.5 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.5 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.5 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.5 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.5 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.5 Action 6]

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Map 1.6, proactively incorporating trustworthy characteristics into system requirements; including potentially impacted groups, communities, and external entities (e.g., civil society organizations, research institutes, local community groups, and trade associations) in the formulation of priorities, definitions, and outcomes during impact assessment activities; conducting qualitative interviews with end users to regularly evaluate expectations and design plans related to human-AI configurations and tasks; and conducting user research to understand the individuals, groups, and communities that will be impacted by the AI, their values and context, and the role of systemic and historical biases, integrating learnings into decisions about data selection and representation.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.6 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.6 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.6 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 1.6 Action 8]

AI Risk / Product must categorize each AI system, and must define the specific tasks it will support and the methods used to implement those tasks (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders).
[NIST AI RMF Map 2, NIST AI RMF Map 2.1]

AI Risk / Product must document information about the AI system's knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans, providing sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors in making decisions and taking subsequent actions.

AI Risk / Product must identify and document scientific integrity and TEVV considerations, including those related to experimental design, data collection and selection (e.g., availability, representativeness, suitability), system trustworthiness, and construct validation.
NIST suggests, among its 1 action for Map 2.1, defining and documenting the AI system's existing and potential learning tasks along with known assumptions and limitations.

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Map 2.2, documenting settings, environments, and conditions that are outside the AI system's intended use; planning and testing human-AI configurations under close to real-world conditions and documenting the results; documenting dependencies on upstream data and other AI systems, including whether the specified system is an upstream dependency for another AI system or other data; and documenting connections the AI system or data will have to external networks (including the internet), financial markets, and critical infrastructure that have potential for negative externalities.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 2.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 2.2 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 2.2 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 2.2 Action 6]

NIST suggests, among its 16 actions for Map 2.3, documenting assumptions made and techniques used in data selection, curation, preparation, and analysis, including identification of constructs and proxy targets and development of indices that operationalize inherently unobservable concepts; documenting known limitations, risk mitigation efforts associated with, and methods used for, training data collection, selection, labeling, cleaning, and analysis; establishing and documenting practices to check for capabilities in excess of those planned for, such as emergent properties, and to revisit prior risk management steps in light of any new capabilities; and establishing processes to test and verify that design assumptions about the set of deployment contexts continue to be accurate and sufficiently complete.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 2.3 Action 8 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 2.3 Action 12 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 2.3 Action 13 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 2.3 Action 14]
AI Risk / Product must understand the AI system's capabilities, targeted usage, goals, and expected benefits and costs in comparison with appropriate benchmarks.

AI Risk / Product must examine and document the potential benefits of the AI system's intended functionality and performance, as well as the potential costs — including non-monetary costs — resulting from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality and trustworthiness, with costs considered in connection with organizational risk tolerance.
[NIST AI RMF Map 3.1 | NIST AI RMF Map 3.2]
AI Risk / Product must specify and document the targeted application scope of the AI system based on its capability, established context, and categorization.

AI Risk / Product must define, assess, and document processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness, including relevant technical standards and certifications.
AI Risk / Product must define, assess, and document processes for human oversight of the AI system in accordance with organizational policies from the govern function.

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Map 3.1, considering performance against human baseline metrics or other standard benchmarks, and incorporating feedback from end users and potentially impacted individuals and communities about perceived system benefits.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.1 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.1 Action 6]

NIST suggests, among its 2 actions for Map 3.2, performing context analysis to map potential negative impacts arising from not integrating trustworthiness characteristics — engaging, where negative impacts are not direct or obvious, with stakeholders external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system and with potentially impacted communities to examine and document who could be harmed, what could be harmed, when harm could arise, and how harm could arise — and identifying and implementing procedures for regularly evaluating the qualitative and quantitative costs of internal and external AI system failures to inform go/no-go deployment decisions throughout the AI system lifecycle.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.2 Action 2]

NIST suggests, among its 2 actions for Map 3.3, considering narrowing contexts for system deployment, including factors related to how outcomes may directly or indirectly affect users, groups, communities, and the environment, the length of time the system is deployed in between re-trainings, the geographical regions in which the system operates, dynamics related to community standards or likelihood of system misuse or abuses, and how AI system features and capabilities can be utilized within other applications or in place of other existing processes; and engaging AI actors from legal and procurement functions when specifying target application scope.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.3 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.3 Action 2]

NIST suggests, among its 10 actions for Map 3.4, defining and developing training materials for proposed end users, practitioners, and operators about AI system use and known limitations; defining and developing certification procedures for operating AI systems within defined contexts of use, including information about what exceeds operational boundaries; and verifying that AI system output is interpretable and unambiguous for downstream decision-making tasks.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.4 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.4 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.4 Action 7]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Map 3.5, identifying and documenting AI systems' features and capabilities that require human oversight in relation to operational and societal contexts, trustworthy characteristics, and risks identified in the Map function; defining and developing training materials for relevant AI actors about AI system performance, context of use, known limitations and negative impacts, and suggested warning labels; and evaluating AI system oversight practices for validity and reliability, retesting and course correcting when oversight practices undergo extensive updates or adaptations.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.5 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.5 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 3.5 Action 5]

AI Risk / Product must identify and document the potential positive and negative impacts of the AI system's uses on individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet, including the likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful), drawing on expected use, past uses of AI systems in similar contexts, public incident reports, feedback from parties external to the team that developed or deployed the system, or other data.
[NIST AI RMF Map 1.1 | NIST AI RMF Map 5, NIST AI RMF Map 5.1]
AI Risk / Product must characterize the impacts of the AI system on individuals, groups, communities, organizations, and society.

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Map 5.1, establishing assessment scales for measuring AI systems' impact — which may be qualitative, such as red-amber-green (RAG), or may entail simulations or econometric approaches — documented and applied uniformly across the organization's AI portfolio; identifying and documenting the likelihood and magnitude of system benefits and negative impacts in relation to trustworthiness characteristics; and establishing processes for red teaming to identify and connect system limitations to AI lifecycle stage(s) and potential downstream impacts.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 5.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 5.1 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 5.1 Action 4]

AI Risk / Product must establish and document practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and for integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts.

NIST suggests, among its 7 actions for Map 5.2, establishing and documenting stakeholder engagement processes at the earliest stages of system formulation to identify potential impacts from the AI system on individuals, groups, communities, organizations, and society; incorporating quantitative, qualitative, and mixed methods in the assessment and documentation of potential impacts; identifying a team, internal or external, that is independent of AI design and development functions to assess AI system benefits and positive and negative impacts and their likelihood and magnitude; and evaluating and documenting stakeholder feedback to assess potential impacts for actionable insights regarding trustworthiness characteristics and changes in design approaches and principles.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 5.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 5.2 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 5.2 Action 5 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 5.2 Action 6]

AI Risk / Product is accountable for verifying that the documentation required by this standard exists and is current for every AI system in scope, and for answering for the outcome of each context establishment, categorization, capability assessment, and impact assessment performed under this standard.
Findings of non-compliance with this standard must be recorded and tracked by AI Risk / Product through [Ticketing System] to resolution.

This standard establishes the requirements for malicious code protection, security function verification, spam protection, memory protection, media use restrictions, and mobile code controls on Example Org systems.
Endpoint Engineering owns this standard end to end and is accountable for its implementation, operation, review, and the evidence it produces.
The controls described in this document must be operated on a continuous basis.

Where a requirement below specifies a value or parameter that Example Org has not yet decided, the value remains an open assignment shown in square brackets (e.g., `[Organization-Defined Frequency]`).
Endpoint Engineering must not treat such a placeholder as satisfied until the value is formally defined.

Where a tool or system must be named to fulfill a control and Example Org has not designated a product, the role is written in square brackets (e.g., `[Endpoint Protection Platform]`, `[Email Security Gateway]`) and is substituted once a product is designated.

- Endpoint Engineering must implement signature-based and/or non-signature-based malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points (e.g., firewalls, remote access servers, workstations, email servers, web servers, proxy servers, notebook computers, and mobile devices) to detect and eradicate malicious code. `[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High]`
[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High]

- Endpoint Engineering must implement both signature-based and non-signature-based malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code. `[ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]`
- Endpoint Engineering must produce and retain an EDR deployment coverage report demonstrating the deployment of these mechanisms across in-scope entry and exit points.

- Malicious code protection mechanisms must be automatically updated as new releases are available, in accordance with organizational configuration management policies and procedures. `[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High | ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High | ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]
- Malicious code protection mechanisms must be updated only when directed by a privileged user. `[NIST SI-3(4)]`

[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High]
- For systems in ARC-AMPE scope, the periodic scan frequency must be at least every week. `[ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]`

- Malicious code protection mechanisms must be configured to perform real-time scans of files from external sources at endpoints and at network entry and exit points as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed, in accordance with organizational policy. `[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High | ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High | ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]

- Malicious code protection mechanisms must be configured to block malicious code, quarantine malicious code, or take an organization-defined action upon detection. `[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High]` `[Organization-Defined Action]`
[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High]
- For systems in ARC-AMPE scope, malicious code protection mechanisms must be configured to both block and quarantine malicious code upon detection. `[ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]`

- Malicious code protection mechanisms must send an alert to organization-defined personnel or roles in response to malicious code detection. `[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High]` `[Organization-Defined Personnel or Roles]`
[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High]

- For systems in ARC-AMPE scope, alerts must be sent to the administrator or organization-defined security personnel in near real time in response to malicious code detection. `[ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]`

- Endpoint Engineering must address the receipt of false positives during malicious code detection and eradication and the resulting potential impact on system availability. `[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High | ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST SI-3 Low | NIST SI-3 Moderate | NIST SI-3 High | ARC-AMPE SI-3 AE Mandatory]

- Endpoint Engineering must test malicious code protection mechanisms at an organization-defined frequency by introducing known benign code into the system, and must verify that detection of the code and the associated incident reporting occur. `[NIST SI-3(6)]` `[Organization-Defined Frequency]`

- Endpoint Engineering must detect organization-defined unauthorized operating system commands through the kernel application programming interface on organization-defined system hardware components, and upon detection, issue a warning, audit the command execution, and/or prevent execution of the command. `[NIST SI-3(8)]` `[Organization-Defined Unauthorized OS Commands]` `[Organization-Defined System Hardware Components]`

- Endpoint Engineering must employ organization-defined tools and techniques to analyze the characteristics and behavior of malicious code, and must incorporate the results into organizational incident response and flaw remediation processes. `[NIST SI-3(10)]` `[Organization-Defined Tools and Techniques]`

- Endpoint Engineering must verify the correct operation of organization-defined security and privacy functions. `[NIST SI-6 High | ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]` `[Organization-Defined Security and Privacy Functions]`
[NIST SI-6 High | ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]

- Verification must be performed upon organization-defined system transitional states, upon command by a user with appropriate privilege, and/or at an organization-defined frequency. `[NIST SI-6 High]` `[Organization-Defined Transitional States]` `[Organization-Defined Frequency]`

- For systems in ARC-AMPE scope, verification must be performed upon system startup and/or restart, upon command by a user with appropriate privileges, or at least monthly. `[ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]`
- Endpoint Engineering must alert organization-defined personnel or roles to failed security and privacy verification tests. `[NIST SI-6 High]` `[Organization-Defined Personnel or Roles]`
- For systems in ARC-AMPE scope, alerts must be sent to at least the system/security administrator on failed security and privacy verification tests. `[ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]`

- When anomalies are discovered during verification, Endpoint Engineering must shut the system down, restart the system, or perform organization-defined alternative action(s); for ARC-AMPE, any alternative action must be documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP). `[NIST SI-6 High | ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]` `[Organization-Defined Alternative Actions]`
[NIST SI-6 High | ARC-AMPE SI-6 AE Mandatory]
- Endpoint Engineering must implement automated mechanisms to support the management of distributed security and privacy function testing. `[NIST SI-6(2)]`
- Endpoint Engineering must report the results of security and privacy function verification to organization-defined personnel or roles. `[NIST SI-6(3)]` `[Organization-Defined Personnel or Roles]`

- Endpoint Engineering must employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and act on unsolicited messages. `[NIST SI-8 Moderate | NIST SI-8 High | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST SI-8 Moderate | NIST SI-8 High | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 AE Mandatory]

- Spam protection mechanisms must be updated when new releases are available, in accordance with organizational configuration management policies and procedures. `[NIST SI-8 Moderate | NIST SI-8 High | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST SI-8 Moderate | NIST SI-8 High | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 AE Mandatory]
- Spam protection mechanisms must be automatically updated at an organization-defined frequency. `[NIST SI-8(2) Moderate | NIST SI-8(2) High]` `[Organization-Defined Frequency]`
- For systems in ARC-AMPE scope, spam protection mechanisms must be automatically updated at least every week. `[ARC-AMPE SI-8(2) AE Mandatory]`
- Endpoint Engineering must implement spam protection mechanisms with a learning capability to more effectively identify legitimate communications traffic. `[NIST SI-8(3)]`

- When email is sent on behalf of the government as part of the business offering, Endpoint Engineering must implement Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance (DMARC) on the sending domain for outgoing messages as described in DHS Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 18-01, must confirm that the DMARC policy is set to reject and that the rua parameter includes reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov, must document DMARC compliance in the SI-08 control implementation solution description, and must list the FROM: domain(s) used when sending email on behalf of the government. `[FedRAMP SI-8]`

- Endpoint Engineering must implement organization-defined controls to protect system memory from unauthorized code execution. `[NIST SI-16 Moderate | NIST SI-16 High]` `[Organization-Defined Controls]`

- System memory must be protected from unauthorized code execution using safeguards such as data execution prevention and address space layout randomization, including at minimum the related controls within the control set. `[ARC-AMPE SI-16 AE Mandatory]`

- Endpoint Engineering must restrict or prohibit the use of organization-defined types of system media on organization-defined systems or system components, using organization-defined controls. `[NIST MP-7 Low | NIST MP-7 Moderate | NIST MP-7 High]` `[Organization-Defined Media Types]` `[Organization-Defined Systems]` `[Organization-Defined Controls]`
[NIST MP-7 Low | NIST MP-7 Moderate | NIST MP-7 High]
- Endpoint Engineering must maintain the resulting Removable media policy configuration as the record of these restrictions.

- The use of personally owned media (e.g., flash drives, external hard disk drives, and other portable storage and media devices) must be prohibited on organization-defined systems and networks, using organization-defined security safeguards. `[ARC-AMPE MP-7 AE Mandatory]` `[Organization-Defined Systems and Networks]` `[Organization-Defined Security Safeguards]`

- The use of portable storage devices in organizational systems must be prohibited when such devices have no identifiable owner. `[NIST MP-7 Low | NIST MP-7 Moderate | NIST MP-7 High | ARC-AMPE MP-7 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST MP-7 Low | NIST MP-7 Moderate | NIST MP-7 High | ARC-AMPE MP-7 AE Mandatory]
- The use of sanitization-resistant media in organizational systems must be prohibited. `[NIST MP-7(2)]`
- Endpoint Engineering must define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies. `[NIST SC-18 Moderate | NIST SC-18 High | ARC-AMPE SC-18 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST SC-18 Moderate | NIST SC-18 High | ARC-AMPE SC-18 AE Mandatory]
- The use of mobile code within the system must be authorized, monitored, and controlled. `[NIST SC-18 Moderate | NIST SC-18 High | ARC-AMPE SC-18 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST SC-18 Moderate | NIST SC-18 High | ARC-AMPE SC-18 AE Mandatory]

- The organization-defined acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies must be documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP). `[ARC-AMPE SC-18 AE Mandatory]`

- Endpoint Engineering must identify organization-defined unacceptable mobile code and take organization-defined corrective actions. `[NIST SC-18(1)]` `[Organization-Defined Unacceptable Mobile Code]` `[Organization-Defined Corrective Actions]`

- Endpoint Engineering must verify that the acquisition, development, and use of mobile code to be deployed in the system meets organization-defined mobile code requirements. `[NIST SC-18(2)]` `[Organization-Defined Mobile Code Requirements]`
- The download and execution of organization-defined unacceptable mobile code must be prevented. `[NIST SC-18(3)]` `[Organization-Defined Unacceptable Mobile Code]`

- The automatic execution of mobile code in organization-defined software applications must be prevented, and organization-defined actions must be enforced prior to executing the code. `[NIST SC-18(4)]` `[Organization-Defined Software Applications]` `[Organization-Defined Actions]`
- Execution of permitted mobile code must be allowed only in confined virtual machine environments. `[NIST SC-18(5)]`
Endpoint Engineering is accountable for the continuous operation of every control in this standard, including the handoffs between detection, alerting, verification, and response steps defined above.

The following artifacts constitute the minimum evidence set for this standard and must be produced and retained under Endpoint Engineering ownership: 1. **EDR deployment coverage report** — demonstrating malicious code protection coverage at system entry and exit points (Section 2). 1. **Removable media policy configuration** — demonstrating the media use restrictions defined in Section 6.
Failure to produce or maintain these artifacts constitutes noncompliance with this standard.

analyze: This Standard establishes the requirements for protecting Example Org's facilities, electronic information systems, and the equipment therein from unauthorized physical access, tampering, theft, and environmental hazards.

It applies to all Example Org facilities that house electronic information systems, to all personnel and visitors granted physical access to those facilities, and to all physical and environmental protection documentation created or maintained under this Standard.
Facilities / Physical Security is accountable for this process end to end, including its execution, review, evidence production, and handoffs to other participating teams.

Facilities / Physical Security must develop, document, and disseminate to applicable personnel or roles an organization-level physical and environmental protection policy that: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; and Is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
