analyze: **Document Owner:** Security Program / GRC **Applies To:** All personnel and systems within the Example Org security boundary **Review Cadence:** Annual

This Standard establishes the requirements for risk assessment, security categorization, risk response, control assessment, authorization, continuous monitoring, and penetration testing at Example Org.
It is issued and maintained by the Security Program / GRC team, which is accountable for this process end to end.
It applies to all systems that process, store, or transmit organizational data, including electronic protected health information (ePHI) where HIPAA applies.

- Example Org shall develop, document, and disseminate to organization-defined personnel or roles an organization-level risk assessment policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
The policy shall be maintained at the organization level. `[NIST RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]
- Example Org shall develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate implementation of the risk assessment policy and the associated risk assessment controls. `[NIST RA-1 | ARC-AMPE RA-1]`
- The Security Program / GRC team shall designate an organization-defined official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the risk assessment policy and procedures.
These officials shall be named in the appropriate security and privacy documents. `[NIST RA-1 | ARC-AMPE RA-1]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the risk assessment policy and the procedures following organization-defined events (including assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines) at least every one (1) year. `[NIST RA-1 | ARC-AMPE RA-1]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect risk assessment policies, and shall review at least every one (1) year to ensure the organization and mission/business/system risk assessment policies remain effective. `[ARC-AMPE RA-1]`

- Risk assessment policies and procedures shall support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and for the information on that system. `[ARC-AMPE RA-1]`

- Example Org shall develop, document, and disseminate to organization-defined personnel and roles an organization-level assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
The policy shall be maintained at the organization level. `[NIST CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

- Example Org shall develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate implementation of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and the associated controls. `[NIST CA-1 | ARC-AMPE CA-1]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall designate an organization-defined official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures.
These officials shall be named in the appropriate security and privacy documents. `[NIST CA-1 | ARC-AMPE CA-1]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and the procedures following organization-defined events (including assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines) at least every one (1) year. `[NIST CA-1 | ARC-AMPE CA-1]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect assessment, authorization, and monitoring policies, and shall review at least every one (1) year to ensure the organization and mission/business/system policies remain effective. `[ARC-AMPE CA-1]`

- Assessment, authorization, and monitoring policies and procedures shall support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and for the information on that system. `[ARC-AMPE CA-1]`
- Example Org shall implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(i)]`
- Example Org shall implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards, implementation specifications, and other requirements of the HIPAA Security Rule.
Policies and procedures may be changed at any time, provided the changes are documented and implemented in accordance with the Rule. `[HIPAA 164.316(a)]`

- Example Org shall identify the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the policies and procedures required by the HIPAA Security Rule; this official shall be named in the appropriate security documentation. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(2)]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall categorize each system and the information it processes, stores, and transmits; shall document the security categorization results, including supporting rationale, in the security plan for the system; and shall verify that the authorizing official or the authorizing official's designated representative reviews and approves the security categorization decision. `[NIST RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]
- The senior official for privacy, or their designee, shall be involved when conducting the security categorization process. `[ARC-AMPE RA-2]`
- The Security Program / GRC team shall conduct an impact-level prioritization of organizational systems to obtain additional granularity on system impact levels. `[NIST RA-2(1)]`

- Example Org shall conduct an accurate and thorough assessment (risk analysis) of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the covered entity or business associate. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall conduct a risk assessment that identifies threats to and vulnerabilities in the system; determines the likelihood and magnitude of harm from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of the system, the information it processes, stores, or transmits, and any related information; and determines the likelihood and impact of adverse effects on individuals arising from the processing of personally identifiable information. `[NIST RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall implement a risk assessment process executed annually, integrating risk assessment results and risk management decisions from the organization and mission or business process perspectives with system-level risk assessments. `[NIST RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall document risk assessment results in security and privacy plans, a risk assessment report, the Risk Register, and/or an organization-defined document. `[NIST RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3]`
- Risk assessment results shall be reviewed at least every one (1) year or when a significant change occurs. `[NIST RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3]`

- The risk assessment shall be updated at least every three (3) years at a minimum (for internal, organization-specific authorizations), before issuing a new internal organization-specific authorization, or upon significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact the security or privacy state of the system. `[NIST RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3]`
- Risk assessment results shall be disseminated to organization-defined personnel or roles. `[NIST RA-3 | ARC-AMPE RA-3]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall document and implement a privacy risk management process that assesses privacy risk to individuals resulting from the collection, sharing, storing, transmitting, use, and disposal of personally identifiable information. `[ARC-AMPE RA-3]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall assess supply chain risks associated with [Assignment: organization-defined systems, system components, and system services], and shall update the supply chain risk assessment [Assignment: organization-defined frequency], when there are significant changes to the relevant supply chain, or when changes to the system, environments of operation, or other conditions may necessitate a change in the supply chain. `[NIST RA-3(1) Low, Moderate, High]`

- Example Org shall use all-source intelligence to assist in the analysis of risk, including publicly available or open-source information, to inform engineering, acquisition, and risk management decisions, including analysis of intentional and unintentional vulnerabilities from development, manufacturing, delivery processes, people, and the environment. `[NIST RA-3(2) | ARC-AMPE RA-3(2) AE Mandatory]`
- Example Org shall determine the current cyber threat environment on an ongoing basis using [Assignment: organization-defined means]. `[NIST RA-3(3)]`

- Example Org shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined advanced automation and analytics capabilities] to predict and identify risks to [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components]. `[NIST RA-3(4)]`
- Example Org shall implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B)]`

- Example Org shall apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures of the covered entity or business associate. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(C)]`

- Example Org shall implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(D)]`

- Example Org shall establish and implement, as needed, policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (for example, fire, vandalism, system failure, and natural disaster) that damages systems containing electronic protected health information. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(i)]`
- Example Org shall establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information (data backup plan). `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(A)]`
- Example Org shall establish and implement, as needed, procedures to restore any loss of data (disaster recovery plan). `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(B)]`

- Example Org shall establish and implement, as needed, procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of electronic protected health information while operating in emergency mode. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(C)]`
- Example Org shall implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans (addressable). `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(D)]`
- Example Org shall assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components (addressable). `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(7)(ii)(E)]`
- Example Org shall respond to findings from security and privacy assessments, monitoring, and audits in accordance with organizational risk tolerance.

Response options include mitigating risk, accepting risk with appropriate justification, sharing or transferring risk, or avoiding risk. `[NIST RA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP RA-7 | ARC-AMPE RA-7 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST RA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP RA-7 | ARC-AMPE RA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Example Org shall follow the FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules when responding to findings. `[FedRAMP RA-7]`
- Risk acceptance shall be discussed with CMS prior to actual acceptance to ensure CMS agrees with the approach and mitigations.
Risk-accepted findings shall be documented and tracked in the Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) with full detail captured in the risk acceptance form. `[ARC-AMPE RA-7]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for [Assignment: organization-defined systems, system components, or system services] at organization-defined decision points in the system development life cycle. `[NIST RA-9 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-9 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST RA-9 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-9 AE Mandatory]
- All system components within the CMS Authority to Connect (ATC)/Request to Connect (RTC) boundary shall be treated as critical. `[ARC-AMPE RA-9]`

- Example Org shall perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation, based initially upon the standards implemented under the HIPAA Security Rule and subsequently in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information, that establishes the extent to which the covered entity's or business associate's security policies and procedures meet the requirements of the Rule. `[HIPAA 164.308(a)(8)]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall select the appropriate assessor or assessment team for the type of assessment to be conducted. `[NIST CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop a control assessment plan describing the scope of the assessment, including the controls and control enhancements under assessment, the assessment procedures to be used to determine control effectiveness, and the assessment environment, assessment team, and assessment roles and responsibilities. `[NIST CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2]`
- The control assessment plan shall be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to conducting the assessment. `[NIST CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2]`

- The controls in the system and its environment of operation shall be assessed at [Assignment: organization-defined assessment frequency] (ARC-AMPE: as specified in the supplemental control requirements and guidance) to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting established security and privacy requirements. `[NIST CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2]`
- The Security Program / GRC team shall produce a control assessment report that documents the results of the assessment. `[NIST CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2]`

- The results of the control assessment shall be provided to [Assignment: organization-defined individuals or roles], which FedRAMP defines to include FedRAMP and agency customers; per ARC-AMPE, results shall be provided to the Business Owner responsible for the system and the personnel responsible for reviewing assessment documentation, in writing, within thirty (30) days after completion. `[NIST CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2]`

- An independent assessment of all security and privacy controls shall be completed before the Authorizing Official issues authority to operate for any newly implemented or significantly changed system. `[ARC-AMPE CA-2]`

- A complete independent assessment of all security and privacy controls shall be conducted over a three (3) year period, either via a full controls assessment at the end of the Authority to Connect lifespan (final ATC package delivered no less than ninety (90) days prior to expiration), via independent assessments of the annually required controls designated by CMS so all controls are assessed within the three-year period (final ATC package delivered no less than ninety (90) days prior to expiration), or per CMS guidance on required documentation and testing for each significant system change. `[ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]`

- Relevant security and privacy documentation shall be updated to reflect any changes to the system within thirty (30) days of the changes or within thirty (30) days of the control assessment results, and CMS shall be notified within thirty (30) days whenever updates are made to system security and privacy authorization artifacts or when significant role changes occur. `[ARC-AMPE CA-2]`

- Independent assessors or assessment teams shall be employed to conduct control assessments; per ARC-AMPE, assessments shall follow the CMS Framework for Independent Assessment of Security and Privacy Controls provided for the program. `[NIST CA-2(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-2(1) AE Mandatory]`
[NIST CA-2(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

- As part of control assessments, at [Assignment: organization-defined specialized assessment frequency] on an [Selection: announced; unannounced] basis, Example Org shall conduct \[Selection (one or more): in-depth monitoring; security instrumentation; automated security test cases; vulnerability scanning; malicious user testing; insider threat assessment; performance and load testing; data leakage or data loss assessment; [Assignment: organization-defined other forms of assessment]\]. `[NIST CA-2(2) High]`

- The results of control assessments performed by [Assignment: organization-defined external organization(s)] on [Assignment: organization-defined system] shall be leveraged when the assessment meets [Assignment: organization-defined requirements] (FedRAMP defines the external organization as any FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service). `[NIST CA-2(3) | FedRAMP CA-2(3)]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop a plan of action and milestones (POA&M) for the system to document planned remediation actions to correct weaknesses or deficiencies noted during control assessments and to reduce or eliminate known vulnerabilities in the system. `[NIST CA-5 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST CA-5 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]

- The existing POA&M shall be updated at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] (ARC-AMPE: in accordance with the frequency documented in the organization's Information Security Continuous Monitoring strategy) based on findings from control assessments, independent audits or reviews, and continuous monitoring activities. `[NIST CA-5 | ARC-AMPE CA-5]`

- The POA&M shall be established and maintained throughout the system life cycle starting with development, including scheduled completion dates, milestones with dates, appropriate risk levels, and weakness descriptions with as much detail as possible.

All findings shall be included, whether self-discovered or identified through assessments or testing (e.g., security control assessments, penetration tests, automated configuration and vulnerability scans).
The POA&M shall follow the CMS Standard for POA&M Management and Reporting and the CMS-provided template, and entries shall be remediated consistent with SI-2. `[ARC-AMPE CA-5]`
- A fully updated and accurate POA&M shall be delivered to CMS quarterly on 31 January, 30 April, 31 July, and 31 October. `[ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]`
- The accuracy, currency, and availability of the plan of action and milestones for the system shall be ensured using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. `[NIST CA-5(1)]`

- Example Org shall assign a senior official as the authorizing official for the system and a senior official as the authorizing official for common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems. `[NIST CA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST CA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]

- Before commencing operations, the authorizing official for the system shall accept the use of common controls inherited by the system and shall authorize the system to operate; the authorizing official for common controls shall authorize the use of those controls for inheritance by organizational systems. `[NIST CA-6 | ARC-AMPE CA-6]`
- Each authorization decision shall be recorded in the Authorization Decision Record, maintained by the Security Program / GRC team.

- Authorizations shall be updated at least every three (3) years (Direct Enrollment Technology Providers must update at least every one (1) year), when significant security breaches occur, whenever there is a significant change to the system or its operating environment, and prior to expiration of the current authorization. `[NIST CA-6 | ARC-AMPE CA-6]`

- CMS shall be notified of significant or major changes to architecture, security and privacy posture, or other items that could cause degradation or unexpected results in security and privacy monitoring, detection, response, and mitigation activities prior to making the change. `[ARC-AMPE CA-6]`
- Example Org shall employ a joint authorization process for the system that includes multiple authorizing officials from the same organization conducting the authorization. `[NIST CA-6(1)]`

- Example Org shall employ a joint authorization process for the system that includes multiple authorizing officials with at least one authorizing official from an organization external to the organization conducting the authorization. `[NIST CA-6(2)]`

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop a system-level continuous monitoring strategy (ARC-AMPE: developed by the CIO and CISO, with the organization as the responsible implementation agent) and shall implement continuous monitoring in accordance with the organization-level continuous monitoring strategy. `[ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory; NIST CA-7; FedRAMP CA-7]`
[ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory; NIST CA-7; FedRAMP CA-7]

- [Assignment: organization-defined system-level metrics] shall be established to be monitored (ARC-AMPE: based on organization security and privacy goals and in accordance with the organization's ISCM strategy). `[NIST CA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7]`
[NIST CA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7]

- [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] shall be established for monitoring and [Assignment: organization-defined frequencies] for assessment of control effectiveness; per ARC-AMPE, monitoring shall include at least once-a-month scans of operating systems, databases, and web applications, and assessment of control effectiveness shall occur no less than at least every one (1) year. `[NIST CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7]`
- Ongoing control assessments shall be conducted in accordance with the continuous monitoring strategy. `[NIST CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7]`
- Ongoing monitoring of system and organization-defined metrics shall be conducted in accordance with the continuous monitoring strategy. `[NIST CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7]`
- Information generated by control assessments and monitoring shall be correlated and analyzed. `[NIST CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7]`
- Response actions shall be taken to address results of the analysis of control assessment and monitoring information. `[NIST CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7]`

- The security and privacy status of the system shall be reported to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency]; per ARC-AMPE, reporting shall occur at least every thirty (30) days (monthly). `[NIST CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7]`
- Continuous monitoring records shall be maintained until released by the investigating authority when subject to a legal investigation (e.g., of an insider threat).

Systems, appliances, devices, and applications (including databases) shall be monitored, and oversight of information security and privacy, including Security Information and Event Management (SIEM) as applicable, shall be provided for each system. `[ARC-AMPE CA-7]`

- Example Org shall follow the FedRAMP Continuous Collaborative Monitoring, Significant Change Notification, Vulnerability Detection and Response, and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules. `[FedRAMP CA-7]`

- Independent assessors or assessment teams shall be employed to monitor the controls in the system on an ongoing basis; per ARC-AMPE, monitoring shall follow the CMS Framework for Independent Assessment of Security and Privacy Controls provided for the program. `[NIST CA-7(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-7(1) AE Mandatory]`
[NIST CA-7(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-7(1) AE Mandatory]

- Trend analyses shall be employed to determine if control implementations, the frequency of continuous monitoring activities, and the types of activities used in the continuous monitoring process need to be modified based on empirical data. `[NIST CA-7(3) | FedRAMP CA-7(3)]`

- Risk monitoring shall be included as an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy, covering effectiveness monitoring, compliance monitoring, and change monitoring; per ARC-AMPE, the continuous monitoring strategy shall document the processes and guidance for what is considered effectiveness, compliance, and change monitoring as part of a holistic risk monitoring strategy. `[NIST CA-7(4) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-7(4) AE Mandatory]`
[NIST CA-7(4) Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-7(4) AE Mandatory]

- Example Org shall employ [Assignment: organization-defined actions] to validate that policies are established and implemented controls are operating in a consistent manner. `[NIST CA-7(5) | FedRAMP CA-7(5)]`
- The accuracy, currency, and availability of monitoring results for the system shall be ensured using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]. `[NIST CA-7(6) | FedRAMP CA-7(6)]`

- Example Org shall conduct penetration testing at [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] on [Assignment: organization-defined systems or system components]; per ARC-AMPE, testing shall be conducted at least every one (1) year to maintain authorization. `[NIST CA-8 High | FedRAMP CA-8 | ARC-AMPE CA-8 AE Mandatory]`
[NIST CA-8 High | FedRAMP CA-8 | ARC-AMPE CA-8 AE Mandatory]

This standard establishes the requirements under which Example Org approves, manages, monitors, and terminates the exchange of information with other systems and with third parties, including business associates, external system service providers, and supply chain entities.
It applies to all Example Org systems and to all internal and external parties that create, receive, maintain, or transmit information on Example Org's behalf.
Third-Party Risk owns this process end to end, including approval of exchange agreements, vendor security reviews, ongoing monitoring, and termination decisions and their handoffs to other teams.

Third-Party Risk must approve and manage the exchange of information between the system and other systems using interconnection security agreements, information exchange security agreements, memoranda of understanding or agreement, service level agreements, user agreements, non-disclosure agreements, or other organization-defined types of exchange agreement.
The appropriate information exchange agreements must be approved and in place prior to any information sharing.

As part of each exchange agreement, Third-Party Risk must document the interface characteristics, security and privacy requirements, controls, and responsibilities for each system, and the impact level of the information communicated.

Third-Party Risk must enter into memoranda of understanding, memoranda of agreement, letters of intent, computer matching agreements, information exchange agreements, or similar agreements with parties (internal and external) that specifically describe the Personally Identifiable Information (PII) covered and enumerate the purposes for which the PII may be used.
Third-Party Risk must review and update information exchange agreements annually.
[NIST 800-53 CA-3 — organization-defined frequency: annual | ARC-AMPE CA-3]

At a minimum, information exchange agreements must be reviewed and updated at least every one (1) year, and also following significant changes to the system, organizations, or the nature of the electronic sharing of information that could impact the validity or security posture of the agreement.
PII must be shared only in ways compatible with the purpose for which it was collected.

Any subsequent sharing that is not compatible with the original purpose may not occur until additional notice is provided to the individual, their consent is obtained, and relevant documents are updated or published.

The Authorizing Official or other senior leadership is authorized to order the immediate termination and/or suspension of any interconnection that, in their judgment and informed by senior cybersecurity or privacy officials, presents an unacceptable level of risk to the organization.

Example Org must verify that individuals or systems transferring data between interconnecting systems have the requisite authorizations (i.e., write permissions or privileges) prior to accepting such data.
Third-Party Risk must identify transitive (downstream) information exchanges with other systems through the systems identified in the information exchange inventory maintained under Section 2.
Third-Party Risk must take measures to ensure that transitive (downstream) information exchanges cease when the controls on identified transitive (downstream) systems cannot be verified or validated.

analyze: This Standard establishes requirements for the documentation, governance, and oversight of artificial intelligence (AI) systems deployed or developed by Acme Health.
This Standard applies to all AI systems used in healthcare operations, patient care support, administrative functions, and research activities.

The organization shall document the following for each AI system: - Intended purposes and potentially beneficial uses [NIST AI RMF Map 1.1] - Context-specific laws, norms, and expectations applicable to the AI system [NIST AI RMF Map 1.1] - Prospective deployment settings [NIST AI RMF Map 1.1] - The specific tasks and methods used to implement the tasks that the AI system will support (e.g., classifiers, generative models, recommenders) [NIST AI RMF Map 2.1]

The organization shall: - Document the organization's mission and relevant goals for AI technology [NIST AI RMF Map 1.3] - Clearly define the business value or context of business use for new AI systems or re-evaluate the business value for existing AI systems [NIST AI RMF Map 1.4]
Targeted application scope shall be specified and documented based on the system's capability, established context, and AI system categorization.
Specific users and their expectations shall be documented.

The organization shall document: - Interdisciplinary AI actors with competencies, skills, and capacities for establishing context who reflect demographic diversity and broad domain and user experience expertise [NIST AI RMF Map 1.2] - The participation of these interdisciplinary AI actors [NIST AI RMF Map 1.2]
Opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration shall be prioritized.
Potential positive and negative impacts to individuals, communities, organizations, society, and the planet shall be documented.
Potential benefits of intended AI system functionality and performance shall be examined and documented.

Potential costs, including non-monetary costs, which result from expected or realized AI errors or system functionality and trustworthiness shall be examined and documented in connection to organizational risk tolerance.

Likelihood and magnitude of each identified impact (both potentially beneficial and harmful) based on expected use, past uses of AI systems in similar contexts, public incident reports, feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system, or other data shall be identified and documented.
Practices and personnel for supporting regular engagement with relevant AI actors and integrating feedback about positive, negative, and unanticipated impacts shall be in place and documented.
System requirements shall be elicited from and understood by relevant AI actors.
Design decisions shall take socio-technical implications into account to address AI risks.

Information about the AI system's knowledge limits and how system output may be utilized and overseen by humans shall be documented with sufficient information to assist relevant AI actors in decision-making and subsequent actions.
Assumptions and limitations about AI system purposes, uses, and risks across the development or product AI lifecycle shall be documented.
Organizational risk tolerances shall be determined and documented.
Related TEVV and system metrics shall be documented.

Scientific integrity and TEVV considerations shall be identified and documented, including those related to: - Experimental design - Data collection and selection (e.g., availability, representativeness, suitability) - System trustworthiness - Construct validation [NIST AI RMF Map 2.3]
Processes for operator and practitioner proficiency with AI system performance and trustworthiness, and relevant technical standards and certifications, shall be defined, assessed, and documented.
Processes for human oversight shall be defined, assessed, and documented in accordance with organizational policies from the govern function.

The Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or designee shall be responsible for: - Ensuring compliance with this Standard across all AI systems - Reviewing and approving AI system documentation - Coordinating with relevant stakeholders to maintain current documentation

AI system owners and project leads shall be responsible for: - Creating and maintaining required documentation for their AI systems - Ensuring interdisciplinary team participation - Conducting impact assessments and updating them based on ongoing monitoring
The organization shall review this Standard [Review Frequency] to ensure continued alignment with applicable laws, regulations, and organizational risk management objectives.

analyze: **Standard ID:** STD-AIGOV-001 **Owner (end to end):** AI Risk / GRC **Applies to:** All Acme Health personnel, teams, and partners who design, develop, deploy, evaluate, procure, use, oversee, or decommission AI systems. **Audience:** Acme Health security, IT, risk, compliance, and engineering staff who implement and audit against this document.
This Standard establishes Acme Health's requirements for governing and accounting for artificial intelligence (AI) systems across their lifecycle.
AI Risk / GRC is accountable for this process end to end, including its handoffs to other participating teams.

Other teams (e.g., Legal, Compliance, Engineering, Clinical Operations, Executive Leadership) participate in individual steps as specified below, but AI Risk / GRC owns the process and answers for its outcome.
AI Risk / GRC shall ensure that legal and regulatory requirements involving AI are understood, managed, and documented.

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Govern 1.1, maintaining awareness of the applicable legal and regulatory considerations and requirements specific to industry, sector, and business purpose, as well as the application context of the deployed AI system (Action 1); aligning risk management efforts with applicable legal standards (Action 2); and maintaining policies for training and re-training organizational staff about necessary legal or regulatory considerations that may impact AI-related design, development, and deployment activities (Action 3).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.1 Action 1 | Govern 1.1 Action 2 | Govern 1.1 Action 3]
AI Risk / GRC shall ensure that the characteristics of trustworthy AI are integrated into Acme Health's organizational policies, processes, procedures, and practices.

NIST suggests, among its 15 actions for Govern 1.2, defining key terms and concepts related to AI systems and the scope of their purposes and intended uses (Action 1); connecting AI governance to existing organizational governance and risk controls (Action 2); aligning to broader data governance policies and practices, particularly the use of sensitive or otherwise risky data (Action 3); detailing standards for experimental design, data quality, and model training (Action 4); outlining and documenting risk mapping and measurement processes and standards (Action 5); detailing model testing and validation processes (Action 6); detailing review processes for legal and risk functions (Action 7); establishing the frequency of and detail for monitoring, auditing, and review processes (Action 8); outlining change management requirements (Action 9); outlining processes for internal and external stakeholder engagement (Action 10); establishing whistleblower policies to facilitate reporting of serious AI system concerns (Action 11); detailing and testing incident response plans (Action 12); verifying that formal AI risk management policies align to existing legal standards and industry best practices and norms (Action 13); establishing AI risk management policies that broadly align to AI system trustworthy characteristics (Action 14); and verifying that formal AI risk management policies include currently deployed and third-party AI systems (Action 15).

[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.2 Action 1 | Govern 1.2 Action 2 | Govern 1.2 Action 3 | Govern 1.2 Action 4 | Govern 1.2 Action 5 | Govern 1.2 Action 6 | Govern 1.2 Action 7 | Govern 1.2 Action 8 | Govern 1.2 Action 9 | Govern 1.2 Action 10 | Govern 1.2 Action 11 | Govern 1.2 Action 12 | Govern 1.2 Action 13 | Govern 1.2 Action 14 | Govern 1.2 Action 15]
AI Risk / GRC shall maintain processes, procedures, and practices to determine the needed level of risk management activities based on the organization's risk tolerance.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 1.3, establishing policies to define mechanisms for measuring or understanding an AI system's potential impacts, for example via regular impact assessments at key stages in the AI lifecycle connected to system impacts and frequency of system updates (Action 1); establishing policies to define mechanisms for measuring or understanding the likelihood of an AI system's impacts and their magnitude at key stages in the AI lifecycle (Action 2); establishing policies that define assessment scales for measuring potential AI system impact, which may be qualitative such as red-amber-green (RAG) or may entail simulations or econometric approaches (Action 3); establishing policies for assigning an overall risk measurement approach for an AI system or its important components, for example via multiplication or combination of a mapped risk's impact and likelihood (Action 4); and establishing policies to assign systems to uniform risk scales that are valid across the organization's AI portfolio, acknowledging that risk tolerance and risk levels may change over the lifecycle of an AI system (Action 5).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.3 Action 1 | Govern 1.3 Action 2 | Govern 1.3 Action 3 | Govern 1.3 Action 4 | Govern 1.3 Action 5]
AI Risk / GRC shall establish the risk management process and its outcomes through transparent policies, procedures, and other controls based on organizational risk priorities.

NIST suggests, among its 7 actions for Govern 1.4, establishing and regularly reviewing documentation policies addressing information such as AI actor contact information, business justification, scope and usages, expected and potential risks and impacts, assumptions and limitations, description and characterization of training data, algorithmic methodology, evaluated alternative approaches, description of output data, testing and validation results, down- and up-stream dependencies, plans for deployment, monitoring, and change management, and stakeholder engagement plans (Action 1); verifying that documentation policies for AI systems are standardized across the organization and remain current (Action 2); establishing policies for a model documentation inventory system and regularly reviewing its completeness, usability, and efficacy (Action 3); establishing mechanisms to regularly review the efficacy of risk management processes (Action 4); identifying AI actors responsible for evaluating efficacy of risk management processes and approaches and for course-correction based on results (Action 5); establishing policies and processes regarding public disclosure of the use of AI and risk management material such as impact assessments, audits, model documentation, and validation and testing results (Action 6); and documenting and reviewing the use and efficacy of different types of transparency tools and following industry standards at the time a model is in use (Action 7).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.4 Action 1 | Govern 1.4 Action 2 | Govern 1.4 Action 3 | Govern 1.4 Action 4 | Govern 1.4 Action 5 | Govern 1.4 Action 6 | Govern 1.4 Action 7]

AI Risk / GRC shall plan ongoing monitoring and periodic review of the risk management process and its outcomes, shall clearly define organizational roles and responsibilities for those activities, and shall determine the frequency of periodic review ([Review Frequency]).

NIST suggests, among its 7 actions for Govern 1.5, establishing policies to allocate appropriate resources and capacity for assessing impacts of AI systems on individuals, communities, and society (Action 1); establishing policies and procedures for monitoring and addressing AI system performance and trustworthiness, including bias and security problems, across the lifecycle of the system (Action 2); establishing policies for AI system incident response, or confirming that existing incident response policies apply to AI systems (Action 3); establishing policies to define organizational functions and personnel responsible for AI system monitoring and incident response activities (Action 4); establishing mechanisms to enable the sharing of feedback from impacted individuals or communities about negative impacts from AI systems (Action 5); establishing mechanisms to provide recourse for impacted individuals or communities to contest problematic AI system outcomes (Action 6); and establishing opt-out mechanisms (Action 7).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.5 Action 1 | Govern 1.5 Action 2 | Govern 1.5 Action 3 | Govern 1.5 Action 4 | Govern 1.5 Action 5 | Govern 1.5 Action 6 | Govern 1.5 Action 7]
AI Risk / GRC shall maintain mechanisms to inventory AI systems, and shall resource those mechanisms according to organizational risk priorities.

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Govern 1.6, establishing policies that define the creation and maintenance of AI system inventories (Action 1); establishing policies that define a specific individual or team that is responsible for maintaining the inventory (Action 2); establishing policies that define which models or systems are inventoried, with preference to inventorying all models or systems or, minimally, high risk models or systems, or systems deployed in high-stakes settings (Action 3); and establishing policies that define model or system attributes to be inventoried, for example documentation, links to source code, incident response plans, data dictionaries, and AI actor contact information (Action 4).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.6 Action 1 | Govern 1.6 Action 2 | Govern 1.6 Action 3 | Govern 1.6 Action 4]

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain processes and procedures for decommissioning and phasing out AI systems safely and in a manner that does not increase risks or decrease the organization's trustworthiness.

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Govern 1.7, establishing policies for decommissioning AI systems that typically address user and community concerns and reputational risks, business continuity and financial risks, up- and downstream system dependencies, regulatory requirements such as data retention, potential future legal, regulatory, security, or forensic investigations, and migration to the replacement system if appropriate (Action 1); establishing policies that delineate where and for how long decommissioned systems, models, and related artifacts are stored (Action 2); establishing practices to track accountability and consider how decommission and other adaptations or changes in system deployment contribute to downstream impacts for individuals, groups, and communities (Action 3); and establishing policies that address ancillary data or artifacts that must be preserved for fulsome understanding or execution of the decommissioned AI system, for example predictions, explanations, intermediate input feature representations, and usernames and passwords (Action 4).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 1.7 Action 1 | Govern 1.7 Action 2 | Govern 1.7 Action 3 | Govern 1.7 Action 4]

AI Risk / GRC shall document roles, responsibilities, and lines of communication related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks, and shall ensure they are clear to individuals and teams throughout the organization.

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Govern 2.1, establishing policies that define the AI risk management roles and responsibilities for positions directly and indirectly related to AI systems, including but not limited to boards of directors or advisory committees, senior management, AI audit functions, product management, project management, AI design, AI development, human-AI interaction, AI testing and evaluation, AI acquisition and procurement, impact assessment functions, and oversight functions (Action 1); establishing policies that promote regular communication among AI actors participating in AI risk management efforts (Action 2); establishing policies that separate management of AI system development functions from AI system testing functions to enable independent course-correction of AI systems (Action 3); establishing policies to identify, increase the transparency of, and prevent conflicts of interest in AI risk management efforts (Action 4); establishing policies to counteract confirmation bias and market incentives that may hinder AI risk management efforts (Action 5); and establishing policies that incentivize AI actors to collaborate with existing legal, oversight, compliance, or enterprise risk functions in their AI risk management activities (Action 6).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 2.1 Action 1 | Govern 2.1 Action 2 | Govern 2.1 Action 3 | Govern 2.1 Action 4 | Govern 2.1 Action 5 | Govern 2.1 Action 6]

AI Risk / GRC shall ensure that the organization's personnel and partners receive AI risk management training to enable them to perform their duties and responsibilities consistent with related policies, procedures, and agreements.

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Govern 2.2, establishing policies for personnel addressing ongoing education about applicable laws and regulations for AI systems, potential negative impacts that may arise from AI systems, organizational AI policies, and trustworthy AI characteristics (Action 1); ensuring that trainings are suitable across AI actor sub-groups, for AI actors carrying out technical tasks such as developers and operators as compared to AI actors in oversight roles such as legal, compliance, and audit (Action 2); ensuring that trainings comprehensively address technical and socio-technical aspects of AI risk management (Action 3); verifying that organizational AI policies include mechanisms for internal AI personnel to acknowledge and commit to their roles and responsibilities (Action 4); verifying that organizational policies address change management and include mechanisms to communicate and acknowledge substantial AI system changes (Action 5); and defining paths along internal and external chains of accountability to escalate risk concerns (Action 6).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 2.2 Action 1 | Govern 2.2 Action 2 | Govern 2.2 Action 3 | Govern 2.2 Action 4 | Govern 2.2 Action 5 | Govern 2.2 Action 6]
Acme Health executive leadership shall take responsibility for decisions about risks associated with AI system development and deployment.

NIST suggests, among its 2 actions for Govern 2.3, that organizational management declare risk tolerances for developing or using AI systems, support AI risk management efforts and play an active role in such efforts, integrate a risk and harm prevention mindset throughout the AI lifecycle as part of organizational culture, support competent risk management executives, and delegate the power, resources, and authorization to perform risk management to each appropriate level throughout the management chain (Action 1); and that organizations establish board committees for AI risk management and oversight functions and integrate those functions within the organization's broader enterprise risk management approaches (Action 2).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 2.3 Action 1 | Govern 2.3 Action 2]

AI Risk / GRC shall ensure that decision-making related to mapping, measuring, and managing AI risks throughout the lifecycle is informed by a diverse team, including diversity of demographics, disciplines, experience, expertise, and backgrounds.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 3.1, defining policies and hiring practices at the outset that promote interdisciplinary roles, competencies, skills, and capacity for AI efforts (Action 1); defining policies and hiring practices that lead to demographic and domain expertise diversity, empowering staff with necessary resources and support, and facilitating the contribution of staff feedback and concerns without fear of reprisal (Action 2); establishing policies that facilitate inclusivity and the integration of new insights into existing practice (Action 3); seeking external expertise to supplement organizational diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility where internal expertise is lacking (Action 4); and establishing policies that incentivize AI actors to collaborate with existing nondiscrimination, accessibility and accommodation, and human resource functions, employee resource groups (ERGs), and diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) initiatives (Action 5).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 3.1 Action 1 | Govern 3.1 Action 2 | Govern 3.1 Action 3 | Govern 3.1 Action 4 | Govern 3.1 Action 5]
AI Risk / GRC shall maintain policies and procedures that define and differentiate roles and responsibilities for human-AI configurations and oversight of AI systems.

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Govern 3.2, establishing policies and procedures that define and differentiate the various human roles and responsibilities when using, interacting with, or monitoring AI systems (Action 1); establishing procedures for capturing and tracking risk information related to human-AI configurations and associated outcomes (Action 2); establishing policies for the development of proficiency standards for AI actors carrying out system operation tasks and system oversight tasks (Action 3); establishing specified risk management training protocols for AI actors carrying out system operation tasks and system oversight tasks (Action 4); establishing policies and procedures regarding AI actor roles and responsibilities for human oversight of deployed systems (Action 5); establishing policies and procedures defining human-AI configurations, meaning configurations where AI systems are explicitly designated and treated as team members in primarily human teams, in relation to organizational risk tolerances and associated documentation (Action 6); establishing policies to enhance the explanation, interpretation, and overall transparency of AI systems (Action 7); and establishing policies for managing risks regarding known difficulties in human-AI configurations, human-AI teaming, and AI system user experience and user interactions (UI/UX) (Action 8).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 3.2 Action 1 | Govern 3.2 Action 2 | Govern 3.2 Action 3 | Govern 3.2 Action 4 | Govern 3.2 Action 5 | Govern 3.2 Action 6 | Govern 3.2 Action 7 | Govern 3.2 Action 8]

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain organizational policies and practices that foster a critical thinking and safety-first mindset in the design, development, deployment, and uses of AI systems to minimize potential negative impacts.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 4.1, establishing policies that require inclusion of oversight functions — legal, compliance, and risk management — from the outset of the system design process (Action 1); establishing policies that promote effective challenge of AI system design, implementation, and deployment decisions via mechanisms such as the three lines of defense, model audits, or red-teaming, to minimize workplace risks such as groupthink (Action 2); establishing policies that incentivize safety-first mindset and general critical thinking and review at an organizational and procedural level (Action 3); establishing whistleblower protections for insiders who report on perceived serious problems with AI systems (Action 4); and establishing policies to integrate a harm and risk prevention mindset throughout the AI lifecycle (Action 5).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 4.1 Action 1 | Govern 4.1 Action 2 | Govern 4.1 Action 3 | Govern 4.1 Action 4 | Govern 4.1 Action 5]

Organizational teams that design, develop, deploy, evaluate, and use AI technology shall document the risks and potential impacts of that technology, and shall communicate about those impacts more broadly; AI Risk / GRC owns and accounts for this documentation and communication process end to end.

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Govern 4.2, establishing impact assessment policies and processes for AI systems used by the organization (Action 1); aligning organizational impact assessment activities with relevant regulatory or legal requirements (Action 2); verifying that impact assessment activities are appropriate to evaluate the potential negative impact of a system and how quickly a system changes, and that assessments are applied on a regular basis (Action 3); and utilizing impact assessments to inform broader evaluations of AI system risk (Action 4).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 4.2 Action 1 | Govern 4.2 Action 2 | Govern 4.2 Action 3 | Govern 4.2 Action 4]
AI Risk / GRC shall maintain organizational practices that enable AI testing, identification of incidents, and information sharing.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 4.3, establishing policies and procedures to facilitate and equip AI system testing (Action 1); establishing organizational commitment to identifying AI system limitations and sharing of insights about limitations within appropriate AI actor groups (Action 2); establishing policies for reporting and documenting incident response (Action 3); establishing policies and processes regarding public disclosure of incidents and information sharing (Action 4); and establishing guidelines for incident handling related to AI system risks and performance (Action 5).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 4.3 Action 1 | Govern 4.3 Action 2 | Govern 4.3 Action 3 | Govern 4.3 Action 4 | Govern 4.3 Action 5]

AI Risk / GRC shall maintain organizational policies and practices to collect, consider, prioritize, and integrate feedback from those external to the team that developed or deployed the AI system regarding the potential individual and societal impacts related to AI risks.

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Govern 5.1, establishing AI risk management policies that explicitly address mechanisms for collecting, evaluating, and incorporating stakeholder and user feedback that could include recourse mechanisms for faulty AI system outputs, bug bounties, human-centered design, user-interaction and experience research, and participatory stakeholder engagement with individuals and communities that may experience negative impacts (Action 1); verifying that stakeholder feedback is considered and addressed, including environmental concerns and across the entire population of intended users, including historically excluded populations, people with disabilities, older people, and those with limited access to the internet and other basic technologies (Action 2); and clarifying the organization's principles as they apply to AI systems, considering those which have been proposed publicly, to inform external stakeholders of the organization's values, and considering publishing or adopting AI principles (Action 3).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 5.1 Action 1 | Govern 5.1 Action 2 | Govern 5.1 Action 3]

AI Risk / GRC shall establish mechanisms that enable the team that developed or deployed AI systems to regularly incorporate adjudicated feedback from relevant AI actors into system design and implementation.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Govern 5.2, explicitly acknowledging that AI systems and the use of AI present inherent costs and risks along with potential benefits (Action 1); defining reasonable risk tolerances for AI systems informed by laws, regulation, best practices, or industry standards (Action 2); establishing policies that ensure all relevant AI actors are provided with meaningful opportunities to provide feedback on system design and implementation (Action 3); establishing policies that define how to assign AI systems to established risk tolerance levels by combining system impact assessments with the likelihood that an impact occurs, often entailing some combination of econometric evaluations of impacts and impact likelihoods, red-amber-green (RAG) scales for impact severity and likelihood, policies for allocating risk management resources along established risk tolerance levels with higher-risk systems receiving more risk management resources and oversight, and policies for approval, conditional approval, and disapproval of the design, implementation, and deployment of AI systems (Action 4); and establishing policies facilitating the early decommissioning of AI systems that surpass an organization's ability to reasonably mitigate risks (Action 5).
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 5.2 Action 1 | Govern 5.2 Action 2 | Govern 5.2 Action 3 | Govern 5.2 Action 4 | Govern 5.2 Action 5]
Compliance with this Standard is audited by AI Risk / GRC, which owns this process end to end and answers for its outcome.
Deviations shall be reported to AI Risk / GRC and tracked to resolution.

The "NIST suggests" statements in this document reflect NIST's voluntary suggested actions from the NIST AI RMF Playbook and are not requirements of Acme Health; the tagged requirement statements in Sections 2 through 18 are binding on the personnel and teams to whom they are addressed.

analyze: This standard establishes Acme Health's requirements for identifying, assessing, and managing the risks and benefits that third-party software, data, models, and other supply chain elements introduce into the organization's AI systems.
It applies to all third-party AI technologies, third-party data, and third-party components incorporated into AI systems developed, procured, or operated by Acme Health.

The **Vendor Risk / AI Risk** team is accountable for this process end to end, including performance of the steps defined in this document, review of their outputs, and answerability for their outcomes.
Other teams (e.g., Procurement, Legal, IT, Security Engineering) participate in individual steps as identified below.
Acme Health must maintain policies and procedures that address the AI risks and benefits arising from third-party software, data, and other supply chain issues.
The Vendor Risk / AI Risk team must maintain and enforce these policies and procedures.

Acme Health must maintain policies, procedures, and documented mapping approaches that address AI risks associated with third-party entities, including the risk of infringement of a third party's intellectual property or other rights.
These approaches must be followed and documented.
[NIST AI RMF Govern 6.1 | NIST AI RMF Map 4.1]
The Vendor Risk / AI Risk team owns the development, application, and documentation of these mapping approaches.

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Govern 6.1, collaboratively establishing policies that address third-party AI systems and data [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 6.1 Action 1]; establishing policies related to transparency into third-party system functions — including knowledge about training data, training and inference algorithms, and assumptions and limitations — thorough testing of third-party AI systems, and requirements for clear and complete instructions for third-party system usage [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 6.1 Action 2]; evaluating policies for third-party technology [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 6.1 Action 3]; and establishing policies that address the supply chain, the full product lifecycle, and associated processes, including legal, ethical, and other issues concerning the procurement and use of third-party software or hardware systems and data [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 6.1 Action 4].
Acme Health must map the risks and benefits of all components of the AI system, including third-party software and data.
The Vendor Risk / AI Risk team performs and maintains this mapping.

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Map 4.1, reviewing audit reports, testing results, product roadmaps, warranties, terms of service, end user license agreements, contracts, and other documentation related to third-party entities to assist in value assessment and risk management activities [NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 4.1 Action 1]; reviewing third-party software release schedules and software change management plans (hotfixes, patches, updates, and forward- and backward-compatibility guarantees) for irregularities that may contribute to AI system risks [NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 4.1 Action 2]; inventorying the third-party material (hardware, open-source software, foundation models, open source data, proprietary software, proprietary data, etc.) required for system implementation and maintenance [NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 4.1 Action 3]; and reviewing redundancies related to third-party technology and personnel to assess potential risks due to lack of adequate support [NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 4.1 Action 4].
Acme Health must identify and document internal risk controls for components of the AI system, including third-party AI technologies.
The Vendor Risk / AI Risk team identifies and documents these controls.

NIST suggests, among its 4 actions for Map 4.2, tracking third parties that prevent or hamper risk-mapping as indications of increased risk [NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 4.2 Action 1]; supplying resources such as model documentation templates and software safelists to assist in third-party technology inventory and approval activities [NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 4.2 Action 2]; reviewing third-party material (including data and models) for risks related to bias, data privacy, and security vulnerabilities [NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 4.2 Action 3]; and applying traditional technology risk controls — such as procurement, security, and data privacy controls — to all acquired third-party technologies [NIST AI RMF Playbook Map 4.2 Action 4].
Acme Health must maintain contingency processes to handle failures or incidents in third-party data or AI systems deemed to be high-risk.
The Vendor Risk / AI Risk team owns these contingency processes and their execution.

NIST suggests, among its 2 actions for Govern 6.2, establishing policies for handling third-party system failures that include consideration of redundancy mechanisms for vital third-party AI systems [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 6.2 Action 1], and verifying that incident response plans address third-party AI systems [NIST AI RMF Playbook Govern 6.2 Action 2].
Acme Health must manage AI risks and benefits from third-party entities.
Risks and benefits from third-party resources must be regularly monitored, and risk controls must be applied and documented.
[NIST AI RMF Manage 3 | NIST AI RMF Manage 3.1]
The Vendor Risk / AI Risk team performs this monitoring, applies the risk controls, and maintains the documentation of both.

NIST suggests, among its 10 actions for Manage 3.1, addressing legal requirements [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 1]; applying organizational risk tolerance to third-party AI systems [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 2]; applying and documenting organizational risk management plans and practices to third-party AI technology, personnel, or other resources [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 3]; identifying and maintaining documentation for third-party AI systems and components [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 4]; establishing testing, evaluation, validation, and verification processes for third-party AI systems that address the need for transparency without exposing proprietary algorithms [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 5]; establishing processes to identify beneficial use and risk indicators in third-party systems or components, such as inconsistent software release schedules, sparse documentation, and incomplete software change management (e.g., lack of forward or backward compatibility) [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 6]; establishing processes for third parties to report known and potential vulnerabilities, risks, or biases in supplied resources [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 7]; verifying contingency processes for handling negative impacts associated with mission-critical third-party AI systems [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 8]; monitoring third-party AI systems for potential negative impacts and risks associated with trustworthiness characteristics [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 9]; and decommissioning third-party systems that exceed risk tolerances [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.1 Action 10].
Pre-trained models used for development must be monitored as part of AI system regular monitoring and maintenance.
The Vendor Risk / AI Risk team is responsible for including pre-trained models in this monitoring and maintenance activity.

NIST suggests, among its 5 actions for Manage 3.2, identifying pre-trained models within the AI system inventory for risk tracking [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.2 Action 1]; establishing processes to independently and continually monitor the performance and trustworthiness of pre-trained models, as part of third-party risk tracking [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.2 Action 2]; monitoring the performance and trustworthiness of AI system components connected to pre-trained models, as part of third-party risk tracking [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.2 Action 3]; identifying, documenting, and remediating risks arising from AI system components and pre-trained models per organizational risk management procedures, as part of third-party risk tracking [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.2 Action 4]; and decommissioning AI system components and pre-trained models that exceed risk tolerances, as part of third-party risk tracking [NIST AI RMF Playbook Manage 3.2 Action 5].
Compliance with this standard is verified by the Vendor Risk / AI Risk team, which is accountable for the end-to-end process described herein and for the handoffs between participating teams.
Deviations from this standard must be reported to the Vendor Risk / AI Risk team.

Network Security must use [Assignment: organization-defined security and privacy attributes] associated with [Assignment: organization-defined information, source, and destination objects] to enforce [Assignment: organization-defined information flow control policies] as a basis for flow control decisions.

Network Security must enforce the use of human reviews for [Assignment: organization-defined information flows] under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions].

Network Security must provide privileged administrators the capability to enable and disable [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] under [Assignment: organization-defined conditions].

Network Security must provide privileged administrators the capability to configure [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] to support different security or privacy policies.

When transferring information between different security domains, Network Security must use [Assignment: organization-defined data type identifiers] to validate data essential for information flow decisions.

When transferring information between different security domains, Network Security must decompose information into [Assignment: organization-defined policy-relevant subcomponents] for submission to policy enforcement mechanisms.

When transferring information between different security domains, Network Security must implement [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] requiring fully enumerated formats that restrict data structure and content.

When transferring information between different security domains, Network Security must examine the information for the presence of [Assignment: organization-defined unsanctioned information] and prohibit the transfer of such information in accordance with the [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy].
When transferring information between different security domains, Network Security must implement [Assignment: organization-defined security or privacy policy filters] on metadata.

Network Security must uniquely identify and authenticate source and destination points by [Selection (one or more): organization, system, application, service, individual] for information transfer.

analyze: This Standard establishes mandatory requirements for the use of cryptography and the management of cryptographic keys across all systems operated by Example Org.

It applies to all information at rest and in transit, all cryptographic modules and key material under Example Org control, and all use of cryptography by external service providers on Example Org's behalf.
Platform Security owns this Standard and is accountable for its implementation, operation, and review end to end.
Other teams may participate in individual steps as identified below, but all handoffs, reviews, and outcomes under this Standard are owned by Platform Security.

Platform Security must establish and manage cryptographic keys whenever cryptography is employed within the system, in accordance with organization-defined key management requirements `[Assignment: organization-defined key management requirements]` covering key generation, distribution, storage, access, and destruction, and consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
[NIST 800-53 SC-12 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SC-12 AE Mandatory]

Platform Security must maintain a key inventory and rotation log recording all cryptographic keys under Example Org control, including their generation, distribution, storage, access, rotation, and destruction.
[NIST 800-53 SC-12 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SC-12 AE Mandatory]

When cryptographic mechanisms are used, Platform Security must employ encryption products validated under the Cryptographic Module Validation Program (CMVP) for compliance with the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards, and must cite current key management references including NIST SP 800-56A, SP 800-56B, SP 800-56C, and NIST SP 800-57 for key management requirements.
Platform Security must maintain availability of information in the event that users lose their cryptographic keys.
Platform Security must produce, control, and distribute symmetric cryptographic keys using NIST FIPS-validated or NSA-approved key management technology and processes.

Platform Security must produce, control, and distribute asymmetric cryptographic keys using NSA-approved key management technology and processes; prepositioned keying material; DoD-approved or DoD-issued Medium Assurance PKI certificates; DoD-approved or DoD-issued Medium Hardware Assurance PKI certificates with hardware security tokens that protect the user's private key; or certificates issued in accordance with organization-defined requirements `[Assignment: organization-defined requirements]`.
Platform Security must maintain physical control of cryptographic keys when stored information is encrypted by external service providers.

Platform Security must determine the organization-defined cryptographic uses `[Assignment: organization-defined cryptographic uses]` and implement the types of cryptography required for each specified cryptographic use, in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
[NIST 800-53 SC-13 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP SC-13]

For each specified cryptographic use, Platform Security must implement at a minimum the latest published FIPS 140-compliant cryptography, consistent with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards.
FIPS 140-2 modules may remain active until September 21, 2026.
Platform Security must follow the FedRAMP Cryptographic Module Use rules.

Platform Security must encrypt all data containing sensitive information (e.g., Personally Identifiable Information, proprietary, financial, and legal information), wherever it resides in the system, using the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.

Platform Security must issue public key certificates under an appropriate organization-defined certificate policy `[Assignment: organization-defined certificate policy]` or obtain public key certificates from an approved service provider.
[NIST 800-53 SC-17 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SC-17 AE Mandatory]

Platform Security must include only approved trust anchors in trust stores or certificate stores managed by Example Org, covering certificates with visibility external to organizational systems as well as certificates related to internal system operations.
[NIST 800-53 SC-12 Moderate, High, SC-17 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SC-17 AE Mandatory]
Platform Security must protect the confidentiality and integrity of information at rest.
NIST permits a selection of one or both; ARC-AMPE requires both.
NIST scope is organization-defined information at rest `[Assignment: organization-defined information at rest]`; ARC-AMPE scope is all information at rest.
[NIST 800-53 SC-28 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SC-28 AE Mandatory]

Platform Security must implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of organization-defined information at rest `[Assignment: organization-defined information at rest]` on organization-defined system components or media `[Assignment: organization-defined system components or media]`.

Under ARC-AMPE, this must use the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards and includes, but is not limited to, Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and proprietary, financial, and legal information in accordance with applicable federal laws, Executive Orders, directives, policies, regulations, and standards.
[NIST 800-53 SC-28(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SC-28(1) AE Mandatory]
Platform Security must remove organization-defined information `[Assignment: organization-defined information]` from online storage and store it offline in a secure location.
Platform Security must provide protected storage for cryptographic keys using organization-defined safeguards `[Assignment: organization-defined safeguards]` or a hardware-protected key store.

Platform Security must implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to electronic protected health information being transmitted over an electronic communications network.
Platform Security must implement security measures to ensure that electronically transmitted electronic protected health information is not improperly modified without detection until disposed of.
Platform Security must implement a mechanism to encrypt and decrypt electronic protected health information whenever deemed appropriate.
[HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(e)(2)(ii) Addressable | HIPAA Security Rule 164.312(a)(2)(iv) Addressable]

Platform Security must implement technical policies and procedures for electronic information systems that maintain electronic protected health information to allow access only to those persons or software programs that have been granted access rights as specified in § 164.308(a)(4).
Platform Security must assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
Platform Security must establish (and implement as needed) procedures for obtaining necessary electronic protected health information during an emergency.
Platform Security must implement electronic procedures that terminate an electronic session after a predetermined time of inactivity `[Assignment: organization-defined inactivity period]`.
Platform Security must maintain the following evidence of compliance with this Standard:

| Artifact | Description | Owner | | ----------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------- | | Key inventory and rotation log | Record of all cryptographic keys, including generation, distribution, storage, access, rotation, and destruction activities | Platform Security | | Encryption-at-rest configuration | Configuration records demonstrating encryption of information at rest per Sections 3 and 5 | Platform Security | | Encryption-in-transit configuration | Configuration records demonstrating encryption of information in transit per Sections 3 and 6 | Platform Security |

Platform Security must review this Standard, the key inventory and rotation log, and the encryption-at-rest and in-transit configurations annually to confirm continued conformance with this Standard and the frameworks cited herein.
