analyze: This Standard defines the mandatory requirements for acquiring, developing, and managing systems at Example Org using a formally defined and documented system development life cycle (SDLC) that incorporates information security and privacy considerations.
The Application Security team is accountable for this process end to end.
Application Security performs, reviews, and answers for each step in this document, including all handoffs between participating teams.

This Standard applies to all systems, components, and services developed internally or acquired from developers, vendors, or service providers, throughout development, implementation, operation, and disposal.

Application Security shall define and document information security and privacy roles and responsibilities throughout the system development life cycle, and shall identify the individuals holding those roles.
Application Security shall integrate the organizational information security and privacy risk management process into system development life cycle activities.

Security and privacy offices must have an opportunity to ensure that requirements to protect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) are appropriately considered throughout the system development life cycle.
Application Security shall protect system preproduction environments commensurate with risk throughout the system development life cycle.
Application Security shall approve, document, and control the use of live data in preproduction environments.
Application Security shall protect preproduction environments at the same impact or classification level as any live data in use within them.

If PII is used in the test environment, the same controls required for systems containing PII must be applied to the test environment, and synthetic PII must be used to the maximum extent practicable when testing system functionality.
The creation, collection, use, and/or disclosure of PII must be limited only to the extent necessary to accomplish a specified and authorized purpose.
The senior official for privacy must approve the use of PII in testing, training, and research; synthetic or de-identified data is preferred for these purposes.
Application Security shall plan for and implement a technology refresh schedule for the system throughout the system development life cycle.

Application Security shall ensure that the acquisition contract for the system, component, or service includes, explicitly or by reference, using standardized contract language: - security and privacy functional requirements; - strength of mechanism requirements; - security and privacy assurance requirements; - controls needed to satisfy security and privacy requirements; - security and privacy documentation requirements; - requirements for protecting that documentation; - a description of the development environment and intended operating environment; - allocation of responsibility (or identification of responsible parties) for information security, privacy, and supply chain risk management; and - acceptance criteria.

Each contract and Statement of Work involving development of, or access to, systems containing PII must include language requiring adherence to the organization's security and privacy policies and standards (consistent with 45 CFR §155.260(b)), define security and privacy roles and responsibilities, and receive approval from the system owner.

When acquiring systems, components, or services used to store, process, or transmit PII, Application Security must include in the acquisition contract, in consultation with the privacy office: a list of security and privacy controls necessary to protect PII (and, if appropriate, enforce applicable privacy requirements); privacy requirements including privacy training and awareness and rules of behavior; and privacy functional requirements.
Application Security shall include organization-defined Privacy Act requirements in the acquisition contract for the operation of a system of records on behalf of the organization.

Application Security shall include organizational data ownership requirements in the acquisition contract, and must require all data to be removed from the contractor's system and returned to the organization within an organization-defined time frame.

A covered entity may permit a business associate to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on its behalf only if it obtains satisfactory assurances (in accordance with § 164.314(a)) that the business associate will appropriately safeguard the information; a business associate must obtain the same satisfactory assurances from any subcontractor before permitting it to handle electronic protected health information on its behalf.
The required satisfactory assurances must be documented through a written contract or other arrangement with the business associate that meets the applicable requirements of § 164.314(a).

The business associate contract must provide that the business associate will comply with the applicable requirements of the subpart, ensure that any subcontractors creating, receiving, maintaining, or transmitting electronic protected health information on its behalf agree to comply via a compliant contract or other arrangement, and report to the covered entity any security incident of which it becomes aware, including breaches of unsecured protected health information as required by § 164.410.
The requirements applicable to business associate contracts apply in the same manner to the contract or other arrangement between a business associate and its subcontractor.
Application Security shall require the developer to provide a description of the functional properties of the security and privacy controls to be implemented.

Application Security shall require the developer to provide design and implementation information for the controls — including security-relevant external system interfaces, high-level design documentation, and source code or hardware schematics — at an organization-defined level of detail sufficient to prove control implementation.

Functional properties of security controls describe only the functionality visible at the interfaces of the controls and specifically exclude functionality and data structures internal to the operation of the controls.

Application Security shall require the developer to follow organization-defined systems engineering methods, security and/or privacy engineering methods, software development methods, testing/evaluation/verification/validation methods, and quality control processes.

Application Security shall require the system, component, or service to be delivered with organization-defined security configurations implemented, and shall require those configurations to be used as the default for any subsequent reinstallation or upgrade.

Application Security shall employ only government off-the-shelf or commercial off-the-shelf information assurance (and IA-enabled) products that compose an NSA-approved solution to protect classified information transmitted over networks at a lower classification level, and shall ensure those products have been evaluated and/or validated by NSA or in accordance with NSA-approved procedures.

Application Security shall limit the use of commercially provided information assurance products to those successfully evaluated against a NIAP-approved Protection Profile for the technology type (if one exists); if no such profile exists but the product relies on cryptographic functionality to enforce its security policy, Application Security must require that the cryptographic module is FIPS-validated or NSA-approved.

Application Security shall employ only information technology products on the FIPS 201-approved products list for Personal Identity Verification (PIV) capability implemented within organizational systems.
Application Security shall require the developer to produce a plan for continuous monitoring of control effectiveness that is consistent with the organization's continuous monitoring program.
Application Security shall require the developer to identify the functions, ports, protocols, and services intended for organizational use.

Application Security shall obtain or develop administrator documentation describing the secure configuration, installation, and operation of the system, component, or service; the effective use and maintenance of security and privacy functions and mechanisms; and known vulnerabilities regarding configuration and use of administrative or privileged functions.

Application Security shall obtain or develop user documentation describing user-accessible security and privacy functions and how to use them effectively; methods for user interaction that enable more secure use and protect individual privacy; and user responsibilities for maintaining system security and individual privacy.
Application Security shall document attempts to obtain system documentation when it is unavailable or nonexistent, and shall take organization-defined actions in response.
Application Security shall distribute documentation to organization-defined personnel or roles.
Application Security shall follow the FedRAMP Secure Configuration Guide rules.

Application Security shall develop system documentation that describes the system and specifies its purpose, technical operation, access, maintenance, and required training for administrators and users.
Application Security shall maintain an updated list of related system operations and security documentation.
Upon changes in system functions or processes, Application Security shall update the relevant system documentation and shall ensure the documents include date and version numbers.

Application Security shall evaluate and protect documentation based on whether it aligns with the risk management strategy or is essential for the effective implementation or operation of security controls.

Application Security shall apply organization-defined systems security and privacy engineering principles in the specification, design, development, implementation, and modification of the system and system components.

Application Security shall implement the following NIST-defined security design principles in organization-defined systems or system components as applicable: [NIST 800-53 SA-8(1)–SA-8(32)] - clear abstractions - least common mechanism - modularity and layering - partially ordered dependencies - efficiently mediated access - minimized sharing - reduced complexity - secure evolvability - trusted components - hierarchical trust - inverse modification threshold - hierarchical protection - minimized security elements - least privilege - predicate permission - self-reliant trustworthiness - secure distributed composition - trusted communications channels - continuous protection - secure metadata management - self-analysis - accountability and traceability - secure defaults - secure failure and recovery - economic security - performance security - human factored security - acceptable security - repeatable and documented procedures - procedural rigor - secure system modification - sufficient documentation

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of least privilege in organization-defined systems or system components, consistent with the principle of least privilege as discussed in AC-6 and reflected in all aspects of secure system design.

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of trusted communications channels in organization-defined systems or system components, including restricting access to the communication channel and employing end-to-end protections for data transmitted over it.

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of accountability and traceability in organization-defined systems or system components, tracing security-relevant actions (subject-object interactions) to the entity on whose behalf the action is taken and creating a trustworthy infrastructure that records details of actions affecting system security.
Application Security shall implement the security design principle of secure defaults in organization-defined systems or system components.

Application Security shall implement the security design principle of secure system modification in organization-defined systems or system components; all system changes must be accompanied by a Security Impact Analysis (SIA) and a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA).
Application Security shall implement the security design principle of sufficient documentation in organization-defined systems or system components.

Application Security shall implement the privacy principle of minimization using organization-defined processes, driven by business needs, coordinated with the senior privacy officer, and consistent with PM-25, PT-2, and SI-12.
Application Security shall require the developer to perform configuration management during system, component, or service design, development, implementation, operation, and disposal.
Application Security shall require the developer to document, manage, and control the integrity of changes to organization-defined configuration items.
Application Security shall require the developer to implement only organization-approved changes to the system, component, or service.
Application Security shall require the developer to document approved changes and the potential security and privacy impacts of those changes.

Application Security shall require the developer to track security flaws and flaw resolution within the system, component, or service and to report findings to organization-defined personnel or roles.
Application Security shall require the developer to enable integrity verification of software and firmware components.
Application Security shall provide an alternate configuration management process using organizational personnel in the absence of a dedicated developer configuration management team.
Application Security shall require the developer to enable integrity verification of hardware components.

Application Security shall require the developer to employ tools for comparing newly generated versions of security-relevant hardware descriptions, source code, and object code with previous versions.

Application Security shall require the developer to maintain the integrity of the mapping between the master build data for the current version of security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware and the on-site master copy of that data.

Application Security shall require the developer to execute procedures ensuring that security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware updates distributed to the organization are exactly as specified by the master copies.
Application Security shall require organization-defined security and privacy representatives to be included in the organization-defined configuration change management and control process.
Application Security shall require the developer, at all post-design stages of the system development life cycle, to develop and implement a plan for ongoing security and privacy control assessments.
Application Security shall require the developer to perform unit, integration, system, and regression testing/evaluation at an organization-defined frequency, depth, and coverage.
Application Security shall require the developer to produce evidence of the execution of the assessment plan and the results of the testing and evaluation.
Application Security shall require the developer to implement a verifiable flaw remediation process.
Application Security shall require the developer to correct flaws identified during testing and evaluation.
No security-relevant modifications of the information systems should be made after the assessment.

Application Security shall require the developer to verify that the scope of testing and evaluation provides complete coverage of the required controls at the organization-defined breadth and depth of testing and evaluation.
Non-production data must be used when executing test scripts or in a test environment that is configured to comply with the security controls as though it were a production environment.

All systems supporting development and pre-production testing must be connected to an isolated network separated from production systems; network traffic into and out of that environment must be permitted only to facilitate system testing, restricted by source and destination access control lists as well as ports and protocols.
Application Security shall require the developer to employ static code analysis tools to identify common flaws and to document the results of the analysis.
Static analysis (SAST) results shall be produced per release and retained as evidence.

Application Security shall require the developer to perform threat modeling and vulnerability analyses during development and subsequent testing and evaluation, using organization-defined contextual information (impact, environment of operations, known or assumed threats, and acceptable risk levels), organization-defined tools and methods, at an organization-defined breadth and depth of modeling and analyses, producing evidence that meets organization-defined acceptance criteria.

Application Security shall require an independent agent satisfying organization-defined independence criteria to verify correct implementation of the developer's security and privacy assessment plans and the evidence produced during testing and evaluation, and shall verify the agent is provided with sufficient information or granted the authority to obtain it.
Application Security shall require the developer to perform a manual code review of organization-defined specific code using organization-defined processes, procedures, and/or techniques.
Application Security shall require the developer to perform penetration testing at an organization-defined breadth and depth of testing and under organization-defined constraints.
Application Security shall require the developer to perform attack surface reviews.
Application Security shall require the developer to employ dynamic code analysis tools to identify common flaws and to document the results of the analysis.
Dynamic analysis (DAST) results shall be produced per release and retained as evidence.
Application Security shall require the developer to employ interactive application security testing tools to identify flaws and document the results.

Application Security shall require the developer to follow a documented development process that explicitly addresses security and privacy requirements, identifies the standards and tools used, documents the specific tool options and tool configurations used, and documents, manages, and ensures the integrity of changes to the process and/or tools used in development.

Application Security shall review the development process, standards, tools, tool options, and tool configurations at least every one (1) year or as needed to determine whether they can satisfy organization-defined security and privacy requirements.

The organization-defined security and privacy requirements for the development process must be based on the ARC-AMPE security and privacy controls or their equivalent, and must include all applicable System Acquisition (SA) and Configuration Management (CM) security controls.
Application Security shall require the developer to minimize the use of personally identifiable information in development and test environments.

Application Security shall define quality metrics at the beginning of the development process and shall require evidence of meeting them at an organization-defined frequency, program review, and/or upon delivery.
Application Security shall require the developer to select and employ security and privacy tracking tools for use during the development process.
Application Security shall perform criticality analysis at organization-defined decision points in the system development life cycle and at an organization-defined breadth and depth of analysis.
Application Security shall require the developer to reduce attack surfaces to organization-defined thresholds.
Application Security shall require the developer to implement an explicit process to continuously improve the development process.

Application Security shall perform automated vulnerability analysis using organization-defined tools; shall determine the exploitation potential and potential risk mitigations for discovered vulnerabilities; and shall deliver the tool outputs and analysis results to organization-defined personnel or roles.
Dependency and supply-chain scan output shall be produced per release and retained as evidence.
Application Security shall require the developer to use threat modeling and vulnerability analyses from similar systems, components, or services to inform the current development process.
Application Security shall require the developer to provide, implement, and test an incident response plan.

Application Security shall require the developer to archive the system or component to be released or delivered together with the corresponding evidence supporting the final security and privacy review.

Application Security shall require the developer to provide organization-defined training on the correct use and operation of the implemented security and privacy functions, controls, and/or mechanisms.

Application Security shall require the developer to produce a design specification and security and privacy architecture that is consistent with the organization's security and privacy architecture (an integral part of the enterprise architecture), accurately and completely describes the required security and privacy functionality and the allocation of controls among physical and logical components, and expresses how individual security and privacy functions, mechanisms, and services work together to provide the required capabilities and a unified approach to protection.

Application Security shall produce, as an integral part of the development process, a formal policy model describing the organization-defined elements of organizational security and privacy policy to be enforced, and shall prove the model is internally consistent and sufficient to enforce those elements when implemented.
Application Security shall define security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware and shall provide a rationale that the definition is complete.

Application Security shall produce a formal top-level specification specifying the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware in terms of exceptions, error messages, and effects; shall demonstrate its consistency with the formal policy model, its complete coverage of those interfaces, and its accuracy as a description of the implemented components; and shall describe security-relevant mechanisms strictly internal to those components not addressed in the specification.

Application Security shall produce an informal descriptive top-level specification specifying the interfaces to security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware in terms of exceptions, error messages, and effects; shall demonstrate its consistency with the formal policy model, its complete coverage of those interfaces, and its accuracy; and shall describe security-relevant internal mechanisms not addressed in the specification.

Application Security shall design and structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to use a complete, conceptually simple protection mechanism with precisely defined semantics, and shall internally structure those components with specific regard for this mechanism.
Application Security shall require the developer to structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to facilitate testing.
Application Security shall require the developer to structure security-relevant hardware, software, and firmware to facilitate controlling access with least privilege.
Application Security shall design organization-defined critical systems with coordinated behavior to implement organization-defined capabilities.
Application Security shall use different designs for organization-defined critical systems to satisfy a common set of requirements or to provide equivalent functionality.

Application Security shall require that the developer of systems, components, or services has appropriate access authorizations as determined by the assigned Authorizing Official (or designee) and satisfies personnel screening criteria consistent with PS-3.
Application Security shall replace system components when support for the components is no longer available from the developer, vendor, or manufacturer.
Application Security shall provide alternative sources for continued support for unsupported components, such as in-house support or support from organization-defined external providers.

Where unsupported components are retained to satisfy mission/business needs, Application Security shall document the justification and approval in a risk acceptance form and shall update the related Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) finding.

Application Security shall establish plans to mitigate or remove unsupported systems, applications, operating systems, or software once identified, and shall upgrade, retire, or stop use of the component before end of life or vendor discontinuation of product support.
If removal is not feasible, Application Security shall maintain a governance process to review unsupported system components and make a risk-based decision on their continued use.

Application Security shall ensure the validity of all information inputs to web/application servers, database servers, and any system or application input that might receive a crafted exploit toward executing code or causing a buffer overflow, verifying that inputs match specified definitions for format and content.

When PII is entered, validation techniques that support data quality must be used (e.g., ensuring the PII entered is the expected type and format), and the system must provide the capability to limit or exclude entering PII in fields that should not contain it; reasonable steps must be taken to ensure PII is complete, accurate, and up to date as required by laws and regulations.

Application Security shall provide a manual override capability for input validation of organization-defined information inputs, shall restrict its use to organization-defined authorized individuals, and shall audit its use.
Application Security shall review and resolve input validation errors within an organization-defined time period.
Application Security shall verify that the system behaves in a predictable and documented manner when invalid inputs are received.
Application Security shall account for timing interactions among system components in determining appropriate responses for invalid inputs.
Application Security shall restrict the use of information inputs to organization-defined trusted sources and/or organization-defined formats.
Application Security shall prevent untrusted data injections.

Application Security shall generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective actions without revealing information that could be exploited — such as user name and password combinations, password-reset validation attributes, PII, biometric or authentication data, sensitive financial records, or content related to internal security functions.

Application Security shall reveal error messages only to organization-defined personnel or roles (documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan) — authorized individuals with a need for the information in the performance of their duties.

Application Security shall establish a process or processes to identify and address weaknesses or deficiencies in the supply chain elements and processes of organization-defined systems or components, in coordination with organization-defined supply chain personnel.

Application Security shall employ organization-defined supply chain controls to protect against supply chain risks to the system, component, or service and to limit the harm or consequences from supply chain-related events; these controls are not limited to those defined in ARC-AMPE and may include other NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 supply chain controls as appropriate.

Application Security shall document the selected and implemented supply chain processes and controls in security and privacy plans, the supply chain risk management plan, and any other organization-defined document.
The Chief Security Officer (CSO) must document and maintain supply chain custody, including replacement devices, to ensure the integrity of devices before they are introduced to the boundary.
Application Security shall employ a diverse set of sources for organization-defined system components and services.
Application Security shall employ organization-defined controls to limit harm from potential adversaries identifying and targeting the organizational supply chain.
Application Security shall ensure that the controls included in the contracts of prime contractors are also included in the contracts of subcontractors.
Application Security shall employ organization-defined acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks.
Application Security shall employ organization-defined controls to ensure an adequate supply of organization-defined critical system components.
Application Security shall assess the system, component, or service prior to selection, acceptance, modification, or update.
Application Security shall implement a tamper protection program for the system, component, or service.
Application Security shall employ anti-tamper technologies, tools, and techniques throughout the system development life cycle.

Application Security shall inspect organization-defined systems or system components (at random, at an organization-defined frequency, and/or upon organization-defined indications of need for inspection) to detect tampering.
Application Security shall develop and implement anti-counterfeit policy and procedures that include the means to detect and prevent counterfeit components from entering the system.

Application Security shall report counterfeit system components to the source of the counterfeit component, organization-defined external reporting organizations, and/or organization-defined personnel or roles.
Application Security shall train organization-defined personnel or roles to detect counterfeit system components (including hardware, software, and firmware).
Application Security shall maintain configuration control over organization-defined system components awaiting service or repair and serviced or repaired components awaiting return to service.
Application Security shall scan for counterfeit system components at an organization-defined frequency.

Application Security shall dispose of organization-defined data, documentation, tools, or system components using techniques and methods in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88, Guidelines for Media Sanitization, consistent with MP-6 Media Sanitization.
The Application Security team shall retain, on a continuous basis, the following evidence artifacts demonstrating execution of this Standard:

| Artifact | Produced By | Associated Controls | | --------------------------------------- | -------------------- | ------------------- | | SAST results per release | Application Security | SA-11(1) | | DAST results per release | Application Security | SA-11(8) | | Dependency and supply-chain scan output | Application Security | SA-15(7), SR-3 |
Application Security is responsible for the completeness and retention of these artifacts and shall make them available for audit and assessment activities.
heading_statements: Example Org — Secure Development Lifecycle Standard
4.2 Business Associate Requirements for Protected Health Information
weakened_citations: This Standard defines the mandatory requirements for acquiring, developing, and managing systems at Example Org using a formally defined and documented system development life cycle (SDLC) that incorporates information security and privacy considerations.
The requirements applicable to business associate contracts apply in the same manner to the contract or other arrangement between a business associate and its subcontractor.

Functional properties of security controls describe only the functionality visible at the interfaces of the controls and specifically exclude functionality and data structures internal to the operation of the controls.
No security-relevant modifications of the information systems should be made after the assessment.

analyze: | Field | Value | | --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Document type | Information Security Standard | | Owning team | Platform Engineering | | Process cadence | Continuous | | Required evidence artifacts | Change tickets with approvals; Baseline configuration and drift report | | Applies to | All Example Org systems, system components, and personnel who initiate, approve, implement, or audit changes to them |

This Standard establishes Example Org's requirements for configuration management, baseline configuration control, configuration change control, system component inventory management, software use restrictions, and integrity verification.
It applies to all systems and system components owned or operated by Example Org.
Platform Engineering is accountable for this process end to end, including all handoffs between participants.

- Platform Engineering owns and is accountable for the configuration management process described in this Standard, including baseline maintenance, change control, drift detection, and evidence production.

- Platform Engineering shall develop, document, and disseminate the configuration management policy and the procedures that facilitate implementation of the policy and associated controls to organization-defined personnel or roles.

The policy shall address purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and shall be consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
The policy shall be maintained at the organization level.
[NIST 800-53 CM-1 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP CM-1 | ARC-AMPE CM-1 AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall designate an organization-defined official (or officials) to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the configuration management policy and procedures.
[NIST 800-53 CM-1 | FedRAMP CM-1 | ARC-AMPE CM-1 AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall review and update the configuration management policy and procedures at an organization-defined frequency and following organization-defined events.

Review shall occur at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, including assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
- Platform Engineering shall follow the FedRAMP Significant Change Notification rules.

- Platform Engineering shall maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with these requirements in written (which may be electronic) form, and shall maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required to be documented.
- Required documentation shall be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
- Documentation shall be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.
- Documentation shall be reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
- Platform Engineering shall develop, document, and maintain under configuration control a current baseline configuration of the system.
The approved baseline configuration and the associated drift report constitute required evidence under this Standard.
[NIST 800-53 CM-2 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CM-2 AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall review and update the baseline configuration at an organization-defined frequency and when required due to organization-defined circumstances, and when system components are installed or upgraded.
Review shall occur at least every one (1) year, and the triggering circumstances are defined as major system changes/upgrades, critical security patches, and/or emergency changes.
- Platform Engineering shall maintain the currency, completeness, accuracy, and availability of the baseline configuration using organization-defined automated mechanisms.

Access controls shall be configured so the automation has the needed access; the automated mechanisms shall be run to gather hardware and software configurations as part of the Continuous Monitoring Program; and hardware/software asset management systems and centralized configuration management software are acceptable examples of such mechanisms.
The drift report produced by these mechanisms is required evidence under this Standard.
[NIST 800-53 CM-2(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-2(2) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall retain previous versions of baseline configurations of the system to support rollback.
At least one (1) previous version shall be retained — specifically, the most recent older generation of the baseline — to support situations such as emergency rollback.
Additional versions may be retained based on organizational risk tolerance.
[NIST 800-53 CM-2(3) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-2(3) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall maintain a baseline configuration for system development and test environments that is managed separately from the operational baseline configuration.
Separate environments shall be provided for development and testing to minimize risk to operational systems.

- Platform Engineering shall issue organization-defined systems or system components with organization-defined configurations to individuals traveling to locations the organization deems to be of significant risk, and shall apply organization-defined controls to those systems or components when the individuals return.
Applicable security safeguards include detailed inspection for physical tampering, purging, or reimaging of the hard disk drive/removable media.
Issued systems and components shall have stringent configurations, such as the latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards.
[NIST 800-53 CM-2(7) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-2(7) AE Mandatory]
Platform Engineering operates the configuration change control process on a continuous basis.
All approved changes shall be recorded in change tickets with approvals in the [Ticketing System]; these change tickets with approvals constitute required evidence under this Standard.
- Platform Engineering shall determine and document the types of changes to the system that are configuration-controlled.
[NIST 800-53 CM-3 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-3 AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall review proposed configuration-controlled changes and approve or disapprove them with explicit consideration for security and privacy impact analyses.
- Platform Engineering shall document configuration change decisions associated with the system.
- Platform Engineering shall implement approved configuration-controlled changes to the system.
- Platform Engineering shall retain records of configuration-controlled changes for an organization-defined time period; records shall be retained for no less than one (1) year after the change.
- Platform Engineering shall monitor and review activities associated with configuration-controlled changes to the system.

- Platform Engineering shall coordinate and provide oversight for configuration change control activities through an organization-defined configuration change control element that convenes at an organization-defined frequency or when organization-defined configuration change conditions occur.

Change request forms shall be approved by an organizational configuration change control board that convenes sufficiently frequently to accommodate proposed change requests, and the requirements of other appropriate organization officials shall be fulfilled.

- Platform Engineering shall establish a means of communicating significant changes to or developments in the information system or environment of operations that may affect business agreements/contracts with CMS and business partners and services to the business owner and associated service consumers.
The means of communication shall be approved and accepted by the system owner.
Platform Engineering shall follow CMS change reporting procedures using the CMS change notification form for the specific entity type.

- Platform Engineering shall document proposed changes to the system; notify organization-defined approval authorities of proposed changes and request approval; highlight proposed changes not approved or disapproved within an organization-defined time period ([Approval Response Deadline]); prohibit changes until designated approvals are received; document all changes to the system; and notify organization-defined personnel when approved changes are completed.
- Platform Engineering shall test, validate, and document changes to the system before finalizing the implementation of the changes.
[NIST 800-53 CM-3(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-3(2) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall implement changes to the current system baseline and deploy the updated baseline across the installed base using organization-defined automated mechanisms.
- Platform Engineering shall require organization-defined security and privacy representatives to be members of the configuration change control element/board.
These representatives may include Information System Security Officers, Chief Information Security Officers, and/or the Senior Official for Privacy.
[NIST 800-53 CM-3(4) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-3(4) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall implement organization-defined security responses automatically if baseline configurations are changed in an unauthorized manner.
- Platform Engineering shall ensure that cryptographic mechanisms used to provide organization-defined controls are under configuration management.

- Platform Engineering shall review changes to the system at an organization-defined frequency or when organization-defined circumstances occur to determine whether unauthorized changes have occurred.
- Platform Engineering shall prevent or restrict changes to the configuration of the system under organization-defined circumstances ([Circumstances Restricting Configuration Changes]).
- Platform Engineering shall analyze changes to the system to determine potential security and privacy impacts prior to change implementation.

Platform Engineering shall review and update the Security Impact Analysis (SIA) and/or Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA), record identified changes in a Change Notification (CN) form and SIA, and refer to entity-type CMS CN procedures and submit the entity-type CMS CN form and SIA to CMS for evaluation if appropriate.
[NIST 800-53 CM-4 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CM-4 AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall analyze changes to the system in a separate test environment before implementation in an operational environment, looking for security and privacy impacts due to flaws, weaknesses, incompatibility, or intentional malice.
[NIST 800-53 CM-4(1) High | ARC-AMPE CM-4(1) AE Mandatory]

- After system changes, Platform Engineering shall verify that the impacted controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with regard to meeting security and privacy requirements.
Any system (including development and test) containing or processing sensitive information (e.g., PII) shall verify security functions per this control.
Security functions shall be continuously monitored and evaluated to ensure they operate as intended and changes do not adversely affect system performance.
Actions shall be taken to verify that the provisioned security function implementation meets security function requirements and is an approved system configuration.
The SIA and/or PIA shall be reviewed and/or updated if necessary when a system change is made.
[NIST 800-53 CM-4(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-4(2) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to the system.

Only qualified individuals — those with appropriate technical skills and expertise within their job responsibilities — and authorized individuals, as determined and documented by the organization, are permitted access to systems for purposes of initiating changes.
[NIST 800-53 CM-5 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CM-5 AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall enforce access restrictions using organization-defined automated mechanisms to the fullest extent possible, and shall automatically generate audit records of the enforcement actions.
[NIST 800-53 CM-5(1) High | ARC-AMPE CM-5(1) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall enforce dual authorization for implementing changes to organization-defined system components and system-level information.

- Platform Engineering shall limit privileges to change system components and system-related information within a production or operational environment, and shall review and reevaluate those privileges at an organization-defined frequency; review and reevaluation shall occur at least quarterly.
- Platform Engineering shall limit privileges to change software resident within software libraries.

- Platform Engineering shall establish and document configuration settings for components employed within the system that reflect the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements, using organization-defined common secure configurations.

The most current security configuration guidelines shall be used per the following hierarchy: USGCB; NIST National Checklist Program Tier IV, then Tiers III, II, and I in descending order; DISA STIGs.
If formal government-authorized checklists do not exist, commercially accepted practices (e.g., SANS), independent testing results, or vendor/industry group checklists (e.g., CIS) may be used.
Checklists shall be SCAP validated or SCAP Compatible if validated checklists are unavailable.
Deployed configurations shall be supported for security updates.
[NIST 800-53 CM-6 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CM-6 AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall implement the established configuration settings.
- Platform Engineering shall identify, document, and approve any deviations from established configuration settings for all configurable system components based on explicit operational requirements.
- Platform Engineering shall monitor and control changes to the configuration settings in accordance with organizational policies and procedures.
- Platform Engineering shall manage, apply, and verify configuration settings for Information Technology products and organization-defined system components using automated mechanisms.
[NIST 800-53 CM-6(1) High | ARC-AMPE CM-6(1) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall take organization-defined actions in response to unauthorized changes to organization-defined configuration settings.
- Platform Engineering shall configure the system to provide only essential capabilities as defined by the organization.
[NIST 800-53 CM-7 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CM-7 AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall prohibit or restrict the use of organization-defined prohibited or restricted functions, system ports, protocols, software, and/or services.

This includes high-risk system services, functions, ports, network protocols, and capabilities across network boundaries that are not explicitly required for system or application functionality or are identified as unnecessary and/or nonsecure.
Platform Engineering shall maintain and document a list of specifically needed system services, ports, and network protocols in the applicable security/privacy plan, with all others disabled.
CIS guidelines (Level 1) shall be used to establish the prohibited/restricted list, or the organization's own list if USGCB is not available.
Configuration review information sources include systems, appliances, devices, services, and applications (including databases).

- Platform Engineering shall review the system at an organization-defined frequency to identify unnecessary and/or nonsecure functions, ports, protocols, software, and services, and shall disable or remove those deemed unnecessary and/or nonsecure.

Review shall occur upon encountering a significant risk, as incidents occur, upon major system/software updates, or at least every one (1) year; the one-year minimum permits a more frequent organizational standard.
[NIST 800-53 CM-7(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-7(1) AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall prevent program execution in accordance with organization-defined policies, rules of behavior, and/or access agreements regarding software program usage and restrictions, and/or rules authorizing the terms and conditions of software program usage.
Example policies include requirements that software be legally licensed, provisioned in approved configurations, and used only by users authorized for software program use.
[NIST 800-53 CM-7(2) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-7(2) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall ensure compliance with organization-defined registration requirements.

- Platform Engineering shall identify organization-defined software programs, employ an allow-all, deny-by-exception policy to prohibit the execution of unauthorized software programs on the system, and review and update the list of unauthorized software programs at an organization-defined frequency ([Unauthorized Software Review Frequency]).

- Platform Engineering shall identify software programs authorized to execute on the system, employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy to allow their execution, and review and update the list of authorized software programs at an organization-defined frequency.
Review shall occur at least quarterly or when there is a change.

Automated updates from a trusted source or authorized software whitelisting information sources (systems, appliances, devices, services, and applications including databases) are permitted, and authorized software may be limited to specific versions or to a specific source.
[NIST 800-53 CM-7(5) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-7(5) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall require that organization-defined user-installed software execute in a confined physical or virtual machine environment with limited privileges.
- Platform Engineering shall restrict code obtained from sources with limited or no warranty and/or without the provision of source code to execution in protected environments.

- Platform Engineering shall prohibit the use of binary or machine-executable code from sources with limited or no warranty or without the provision of source code, allowing exceptions only for compelling mission or operational requirements and with the approval of the authorizing official.

- Platform Engineering shall identify hardware components authorized for system use, prohibit the use or connection of unauthorized hardware components, and review and update the list of authorized hardware components at an organization-defined frequency.
Review shall occur at least every one (1) year or when there is a change, and authorized hardware components shall be defined and documented in the System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP).

- Platform Engineering shall develop and document an inventory of system components that accurately reflects the system; includes all components within the system; does not include duplicate accounting of components or components assigned to any other system; is at the level of granularity deemed necessary for tracking and reporting; and includes organization-defined accountability information.

The accountability information comprises, for each component: unique identifier and/or serial number; component type (e.g., server, desktop, application); manufacturer/model information; operating system type and version/service pack level; presence of virtual machines; application software version/license information; physical location (e.g., building/room number); logical location (e.g., IP address, position within the information system); MAC address; system/component owner; operational status; and information system/component administrators.
[NIST 800-53 CM-8 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP CM-8 | ARC-AMPE CM-8 AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall review and update the system component inventory at an organization-defined frequency; review and update shall occur at least every six (6) months, coordinated with the organization-defined continuous monitoring capability.
[NIST 800-53 CM-8 | FedRAMP CM-8 | ARC-AMPE CM-8 AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall follow the FedRAMP Continuous Collaborative Monitoring, Significant Change Notification, Vulnerability Detection and Response, and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules.
- Platform Engineering shall update the inventory of system components as part of component installations, removals, and system updates.
[NIST 800-53 CM-8(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-8(1) AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall maintain the currency, completeness, accuracy, and availability of the inventory of system components using organization-defined automated mechanisms.

- Platform Engineering shall detect the presence of unauthorized hardware, software, and firmware components within the system using organization-defined automated mechanisms at an organization-defined frequency, and shall take organization-defined actions when unauthorized components are detected.
Detection shall be continuous with a maximum five (5) minute delay.
Actions shall include disabling network access by such components, isolating the component, and notifying responsible personnel or roles (including for unauthorized provisioned configurations).
[NIST 800-53 CM-8(3) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-8(3) AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall include in the system component inventory a means for identifying, by name, position, or role, the individuals responsible and accountable for administering those components.
- Platform Engineering shall include assessed component configurations and any approved deviations to current deployed configurations in the system component inventory.
- Platform Engineering shall provide a centralized repository for the inventory of system components.
- Platform Engineering shall support the tracking of system components by geographic location using organization-defined automated mechanisms.
- Platform Engineering shall assign system components to a system and receive an acknowledgement from organization-defined personnel or roles of this assignment.

- Platform Engineering shall implement policies and procedures that govern the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media containing electronic protected health information into and out of a facility, and the movement of these items within the facility.

- Platform Engineering shall implement policies and procedures to address the final disposition of electronic protected health information, and/or the hardware or electronic media on which it is stored.
- Platform Engineering shall implement procedures for removal of electronic protected health information from electronic media before the media are made available for re-use.
- Platform Engineering shall maintain a record of the movements of hardware and electronic media and any person responsible therefor.
- Platform Engineering shall create a retrievable, exact copy of electronic protected health information, when needed, before movement of equipment.

- Platform Engineering shall develop, document, and implement a configuration management plan for the system that: addresses roles, responsibilities, and configuration management processes and procedures; establishes a process for identifying configuration items throughout the system development life cycle and for managing their configuration; defines the configuration items for the system and places them under configuration management; is reviewed and approved by organization-defined personnel or roles (e.g., Business Owner and System Owner, defined in the organization's SSPP); and protects the configuration management plan from unauthorized disclosure and modification.
[NIST 800-53 CM-9 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CM-9 AE Mandatory]
- Responsibility for developing the configuration management process shall be assigned to organizational personnel not directly involved in system development.
- Platform Engineering shall use software and associated documentation in accordance with contract agreements and copyright laws.
[NIST 800-53 CM-10 Low/Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CM-10 AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall track the use of software and associated documentation protected by quantity licenses to control copying and distribution.

- Platform Engineering shall control and document the use of peer-to-peer file sharing technology to ensure this capability is not used for the unauthorized distribution, display, performance, or reproduction of copyrighted work.
- Platform Engineering shall establish organization-defined restrictions on the use of open-source software.
- Platform Engineering shall establish organization-defined policies governing the installation of software by users.
[NIST 800-53 CM-11 Low/Moderate/High | FedRAMP CM-11 | ARC-AMPE CM-11 AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall enforce software installation policies through organization-defined methods; enforcement shall be through the organization-defined applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP).
[NIST 800-53 CM-11 | FedRAMP CM-11 | ARC-AMPE CM-11 AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall monitor software installation policy compliance continuously, per the FedRAMP-defined parameter via CM-7(5); continuous monitoring via CM-7(5) likewise applies.
- Platform Engineering shall monitor software installation policy compliance at an organization-defined frequency.
- User installation of software is allowed only with explicit privileged status.
- Platform Engineering shall enforce and monitor compliance with software installation policies using organization-defined automated mechanisms.
- Platform Engineering shall identify and document the location of organization-defined information and the specific system components on which the information is processed and stored.
Platform Engineering shall additionally identify and document information flows of that information to other components where it may be processed and/or stored (e.g., backups).
[NIST 800-53 CM-12 Moderate, High | FedRAMP CM-12 | ARC-AMPE CM-12 AE Mandatory]
- Platform Engineering shall identify and document the users who have access to the system and system components where the information is processed and stored.
[NIST 800-53 CM-12 | FedRAMP CM-12 | ARC-AMPE CM-12 AE Mandatory]

- Platform Engineering shall implement cryptographic mechanisms to detect unauthorized changes to software, firmware, and information.

- Platform Engineering shall implement policies and procedures to protect electronic protected health information from improper alteration or destruction.
- Platform Engineering shall implement electronic mechanisms to corroborate that electronic protected health information has not been altered or destroyed in an unauthorized manner.

- Platform Engineering shall implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to electronic protected health information being transmitted over an electronic communications network.

- Platform Engineering shall implement security measures to ensure that electronically transmitted electronic protected health information is not improperly modified without detection until disposed of.
- Platform Engineering shall implement a mechanism to encrypt electronic protected health information whenever deemed appropriate.

This Standard defines the requirements for malicious code protection, verification of security and privacy functions, spam protection, memory protection, media use restrictions, and mobile code controls on Example Org systems and endpoints.

It applies to all systems, system components, and endpoints within scope of Example Org's security program, including workstations, notebook computers, mobile devices, servers, and network entry and exit points.
Endpoint Engineering is accountable for this process end to end, including implementation, configuration, operation, verification, evidence production, and handoffs to other teams.

Endpoint Engineering must implement malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points — which can include firewalls, remote-access servers, workstations, email servers, web servers, proxy servers, notebook computers, and mobile devices — to detect and eradicate malicious code, using one or more of signature-based or non-signature-based technologies.
Endpoint Engineering must implement both signature-based and non-signature-based malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code.
Endpoint Engineering must automatically update malicious code protection mechanisms as new releases are available, in accordance with organizational configuration management policies and procedures.
[NIST SI-3 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SI-3 (AE Mandatory)]
Endpoint Engineering must update malicious code protection mechanisms only when directed by a privileged user.
Endpoint Engineering must configure malicious code protection mechanisms to perform periodic scans of the system at an organization-defined frequency of [Scan Frequency].
Periodic scans of the system must be performed at least every one (1) week.

Endpoint Engineering must configure malicious code protection mechanisms to perform real-time scans of files from external sources as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed, in accordance with organizational policy, at one or more of the endpoint or network entry and exit points.

Endpoint Engineering must configure malicious code protection mechanisms to perform real-time scans of files from external sources at both endpoints and network entry and exit points as the files are downloaded, opened, or executed, in accordance with organizational policy.

Endpoint Engineering must configure malicious code protection mechanisms to block or quarantine malicious code, or take an organization-defined action of [Detection Response Action], and send an alert to organization-defined personnel or roles of [Detection Alert Recipients] in response to malicious code detection.

Endpoint Engineering must configure malicious code protection mechanisms to both block and quarantine malicious code and send an alert to the administrator or organization-defined security personnel in near real-time in response to malicious code detection.
Endpoint Engineering must address the receipt of false positives during malicious code detection and eradication and the resulting potential impact on the availability of the system.
[NIST SI-3 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE SI-3 (AE Mandatory)]

Endpoint Engineering must test malicious code protection mechanisms at an organization-defined frequency of [Malicious Code Protection Test Frequency] by introducing known benign code into the system, and must verify that detection of the code and the associated incident reporting occur.

Endpoint Engineering must detect the organization-defined unauthorized operating system commands of [Unauthorized OS Command Definitions] through the kernel application programming interface on organization-defined system hardware components of [In-Scope Hardware Components], and must issue a warning, audit the command execution, and/or prevent execution of the command.

Endpoint Engineering must employ organization-defined tools and techniques of [Malicious Code Analysis Tools] to analyze the characteristics and behavior of malicious code, and must incorporate the results of malicious code analysis into organizational incident response and flaw remediation processes.
Endpoint Engineering must verify the correct operation of organization-defined security and privacy functions.

Verification of security and privacy functions must be performed upon command by a user with appropriate privilege, at an organization-defined frequency of [Verification Frequency], and/or during organization-defined system transitional states.
Verification of security and privacy functions must be performed upon system startup and/or restart, upon command by a user with appropriate privileges, or at least monthly.
Endpoint Engineering must alert organization-defined personnel or roles — at a minimum, the system/security administrator — to failed security and privacy verification tests.

Endpoint Engineering must shut the system down, restart the system, or perform an organization-defined alternative action of [Anomaly Response Action] when anomalies are discovered; under ARC-AMPE, any alternative action must be documented in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP).
Endpoint Engineering must implement automated mechanisms to support the management of distributed security and privacy function testing.
Endpoint Engineering must report the results of security and privacy function verification to organization-defined personnel or roles of [Verification Report Recipients].

Endpoint Engineering must employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry and exit points — which can include firewalls, remote-access servers, email servers, web servers, proxy servers, workstations, notebook computers, and mobile devices — to detect and act on unsolicited messages.
[NIST SI-8 (Moderate, High) | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 (AE Mandatory)]
Endpoint Engineering must update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available, in accordance with organizational configuration management policies and procedures.
[NIST SI-8 (Moderate, High) | FedRAMP SI-8 | ARC-AMPE SI-8 (AE Mandatory)]
Endpoint Engineering must automatically update spam protection mechanisms at an organization-defined frequency of [Spam Protection Update Frequency].
Spam protection mechanisms must be automatically updated at least every one (1) week.
Endpoint Engineering must implement spam protection mechanisms with a learning capability to more effectively identify legitimate communications traffic.

When Example Org sends email on behalf of the government as part of the business offering, Endpoint Engineering must implement Domain-based Message Authentication, Reporting & Conformance (DMARC) on the sending domain for outgoing messages as described in DHS Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 18-01.

Where DMARC is implemented, Endpoint Engineering must confirm the configuration to ensure the policy is set to reject and the rua parameter includes reports@dmarc.cyber.dhs.gov, document DMARC compliance in the SI-08 control implementation solution description, and list the FROM: domain(s) used when emails are sent on behalf of the government.
Endpoint Engineering must implement organization-defined controls of [Memory Protection Controls] to protect the system memory from unauthorized code execution.

At a minimum, Endpoint Engineering must implement the related controls within this control set to protect system memory from unauthorized code execution, using safeguards such as data execution prevention and address space layout randomization.
Endpoint Engineering must restrict or prohibit the use of organization-defined types of system media on organization-defined systems or system components, using organization-defined controls.

Endpoint Engineering must prohibit the use of personally owned media (e.g., flash drives, external hard disk drives, and other portable storage and media devices) on organization-defined systems and networks, using organization-defined security safeguards.
Endpoint Engineering must prohibit the use of portable storage devices in organizational systems when such devices have no identifiable owner.
[NIST MP-7 (Low, Moderate, High) | ARC-AMPE MP-7 (AE Mandatory)]
Endpoint Engineering must prohibit the use of sanitization-resistant media in organizational systems.
Endpoint Engineering must record the resulting removable media restrictions and safeguards in the Removable media policy configuration.
Endpoint Engineering must define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies, and must authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code within the system.
Under ARC-AMPE, Endpoint Engineering must define the acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies in the applicable System Security and Privacy Plan (SSPP).
Endpoint Engineering must identify organization-defined unacceptable mobile code of [Unacceptable Mobile Code Definitions] and take organization-defined corrective actions.
Endpoint Engineering must verify that the acquisition, development, and use of mobile code to be deployed in the system meets organization-defined mobile code requirements.
Endpoint Engineering must prevent the download and execution of organization-defined unacceptable mobile code.
Endpoint Engineering must prevent the automatic execution of mobile code in organization-defined software applications and enforce organization-defined actions prior to executing the code.
Endpoint Engineering must allow execution of permitted mobile code only in confined virtual machine environments.
Endpoint Engineering produces and maintains the following evidence artifacts in support of this Standard, on a continuous basis:

| Evidence Artifact | Associated Requirements | | ------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | EDR deployment coverage report | Malicious code protection mechanism implementation, scanning, real-time scanning, and detection response (Section 2) | | Removable media policy configuration | Media use restrictions (Section 6) |
Endpoint Engineering must retain these artifacts and make them available for audit and compliance review.
