analyze: This Standard establishes Example Org's requirements for risk assessment, security categorization, control assessment, authorization, continuous monitoring, penetration testing, risk response, and related contingency planning activities.

It applies to all Example Org information systems, system components, and services that process, store, or transmit organizational information, including electronic protected health information where applicable.
Security Program / GRC owns the risk assessment and authorization process end-to-end.

Security Program / GRC performs or coordinates risk assessments, security categorizations, control assessments, continuous monitoring, penetration testing coordination, risk response, and authorization support activities described in this Standard; maintains the risk register and the authorization decision record; and is accountable for ensuring the process operates at the cadence specified below.

Other functions — including system owners, authorizing officials, independent assessors, penetration testing agents, and workforce members generally — participate in individual steps as identified in each section, but Security Program / GRC is accountable for the process and for the handoffs between participants.
Unless a requirement below identifies a different responsible party, Security Program / GRC performs, reviews, or answers for the described activity.

- Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate an organization-level (and/or mission/business-process-level or system-level) risk assessment policy to [Designated Personnel or Roles] that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; Security Program / GRC must also develop procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated risk assessment controls.

- Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate an organization-level (and/or mission/business-process-level or system-level) assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy to [Designated Personnel or Roles] that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines; Security Program / GRC must also develop procedures to facilitate implementation of the policy and associated assessment, authorization, and monitoring controls.

- Security Program / GRC must designate an official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the risk assessment policy and procedures, and a designated official to do the same for the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures.
[NIST 800-53 RA-1 | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory | NIST 800-53 CA-1 | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

- Security Program / GRC must review and update the risk assessment policy and procedures, and the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures, annually and following [Defined Events] (such as assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents/breaches, or changes in applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, or guidelines), consistent with ARC-AMPE's requirement that this review occur at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.
[NIST 800-53 RA-1 | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory | NIST 800-53 CA-1 | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

- Example Org must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the applicable security rule requirements, taking into account specified factors; such policies and procedures may be changed at any time provided changes are documented and implemented in accordance with the rule.

- Security Program / GRC must maintain implemented policies and procedures, and any required documentation of actions, activities, or assessments, in written (which may be electronic) form; retain such documentation for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later; make the documentation available to persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains; and review the documentation periodically, updating it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
- Example Org must identify the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the required security policies and procedures.
- Security Program / GRC must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

- Security Program / GRC must categorize the system and the information it processes, stores, and transmits; document the security categorization results, including supporting rationale, in the system security plan and in the risk register; and verify that the authorizing official (or designated representative) reviews and approves the security categorization decision.
- Security Program / GRC must conduct impact-level prioritization of organizational systems to obtain additional granularity on system impact levels.

- Security Program / GRC must conduct a risk assessment that identifies threats to and vulnerabilities in the system, determines the likelihood and magnitude of harm from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of the system and its information, and determines the likelihood and impact of adverse effects on individuals arising from processing of personally identifiable information; risk assessment results and risk management decisions from organization and mission/business process perspectives must be integrated with system-level risk assessments.

- Security Program / GRC must document risk assessment results in the risk register together with security and privacy plans, a risk assessment report, or another organization-defined document; per ARC-AMPE, documentation must appear in the Information System Risk Assessment (ISRA), Security Assessment Report (SAR), and privacy plans (e.g., PIA).

- Security Program / GRC must review risk assessment results annually or when a significant change occurs, consistent with ARC-AMPE's requirement to review at least every one (1) year or when a significant change occurs, and must disseminate risk assessment results to [Designated Personnel or Roles].

- Security Program / GRC must update the risk assessment annually, or when there are significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact its security or privacy state; this satisfies ARC-AMPE's minimum requirement to update at least every three (3) years, before issuing a new internal/organization-specific authorization, or upon significant change.

- Security Program / GRC must document and implement a privacy risk management process that assesses privacy risk to individuals resulting from the collection, sharing, storing, transmitting, use, and disposal of PII.

- Security Program / GRC must assess supply chain risks associated with [Designated Systems, System Components, and System Services], and must update the supply chain risk assessment annually, when there are significant changes to the relevant supply chain, or when changes to the system, environments of operation, or other conditions may necessitate a change.

- Security Program / GRC must use all-source intelligence, including publicly available/open-source information, to assist in the analysis of risk, to inform engineering, acquisition, and risk management decisions, and to analyze risk of vulnerabilities from development, manufacturing, and delivery processes, people, and the environment.
- Security Program / GRC must determine the current cyber threat environment on an ongoing basis using [Designated Means].
- Security Program / GRC must employ [Advanced Automation and Analytics Capabilities] to predict and identify risks to [Designated Systems or System Components].

- Security Program / GRC must conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by Example Org.
- Security Program / GRC must implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.
- Security Program / GRC must ensure appropriate sanctions are applied against workforce members who fail to comply with security policies and procedures.
- Security Program / GRC must implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.

- Security Program / GRC must perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation, initially based on the standards implemented under the security rule and subsequently in response to environmental or operational changes affecting ePHI security, establishing the extent to which security policies and procedures meet the rule's requirements.

- Security Program / GRC must identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for [Designated Systems, System Components, or System Services] at [Designated Decision Points] in the system development life cycle; per ARC-AMPE, all system components within the CMS ATC/RTC boundary (or equivalent State AE/other ARC-AMPE user boundary) are considered critical.
- Security Program / GRC must select the appropriate assessor or assessment team for the type of assessment to be conducted.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- Security Program / GRC must develop a control assessment plan describing the scope of the assessment, including the controls and control enhancements under assessment, assessment procedures to determine control effectiveness, and the assessment environment, team, and roles/responsibilities; the plan must be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to conducting the assessment.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- Security Program / GRC must assess the controls in the system and its environment of operation to determine the extent to which they are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting established security and privacy requirements.

NIST and FedRAMP leave the assessment frequency organization-defined; ARC-AMPE requires assessment as specified in supplemental control requirements and guidance, including a complete independent assessment of all controls over a three (3) year period — via full reassessment at ATC expiration, annually-designated control subsets across years one through three, or per CMS guidance for significant system changes — with the final ATC package delivered no less than ninety (90) days prior to ATC expiration.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- Security Program / GRC must produce a control assessment report documenting the results of the assessment and provide the results to [Designated Individuals or Roles]; FedRAMP specifies this includes FedRAMP and agency customers; ARC-AMPE specifies results go to the Business Owner and personnel responsible for reviewing assessment documentation and updating security/privacy documentation, with updates made within thirty (30) days of assessment completion, and CMS notified within thirty (30) days of authorization artifact updates or significant role changes.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- Security Program / GRC must ensure an independent assessment of all security and privacy controls is completed before an authorizing official issues an authority to operate for any newly implemented or significantly changed system, as CMS requires.
- Security Program / GRC must employ independent assessors or assessment teams to conduct control assessments.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

- Security Program / GRC must include specialized assessment activities (announced or unannounced) as part of control assessments annually, such as in-depth monitoring, security instrumentation, automated security test cases, vulnerability scanning, malicious user testing, insider threat assessment, performance and load testing, data leakage/loss assessment, or other [Designated Forms of Assessment].

- Security Program / GRC must leverage the results of control assessments performed by [External Organization] on [Designated System] when the assessment meets [Designated Requirements]; FedRAMP specifies leveraging results from any FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service.

- Security Program / GRC must develop a plan of action and milestones (POA&M) for the system, tracked in the [Ticketing System] and reflected in the risk register, to document planned remediation actions to correct weaknesses or deficiencies noted during control assessments and to reduce or eliminate known vulnerabilities in the system.

- Security Program / GRC must update the existing POA&M based on findings from control assessments, independent audits or reviews, and continuous monitoring activities, at the frequency documented in Example Org's Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) strategy, per ARC-AMPE; the POA&M must be maintained throughout the system lifecycle starting with development, including scheduled completion dates, milestones with dates, appropriate risk levels, detailed weakness descriptions, and all findings (self-discovered or via assessment); ARC-AMPE further requires delivery of a fully updated and accurate POA&M to CMS quarterly (January 31, April 30, July 31, October 31).
- Security Program / GRC must ensure the accuracy, currency, and availability of the plan of action and milestones for the system using [Designated Automated Mechanisms].

- Security Program / GRC must ensure a senior official is assigned as the authorizing official (AO) for the system and a senior official is assigned as the AO for common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems.

- Security Program / GRC must ensure that, before commencing operations, the AO for the system accepts the use of common controls inherited by the system and authorizes the system to operate, recording the decision in the authorization decision record; the AO for common controls must authorize the use of those controls for inheritance by organizational systems.

- Security Program / GRC must ensure authorizations are updated at least every three (3) years for all entities (except Direct Enrollment Technology Providers, which must update at least every one (1) year), when significant security breaches occur, when there is a significant change to the system or its operating environment, or prior to expiration of a current authorization, per ARC-AMPE; Example Org must notify CMS of significant/major changes prior to making the change.
- Security Program / GRC must employ a joint authorization process for the system involving multiple authorizing officials from the same organization.

- Security Program / GRC must employ a joint authorization process for the system involving multiple authorizing officials, including at least one from an organization external to the organization conducting the authorization.

- Security Program / GRC must develop a continuous monitoring strategy (system-level, and consistent with any organization-level strategy) that establishes system-level metrics to be monitored, establishes frequencies for monitoring and for assessment of control effectiveness, and includes ongoing control assessments and ongoing monitoring of metrics in accordance with the strategy.

NIST and FedRAMP leave metrics and frequencies organization-defined; ARC-AMPE requires metrics based on organizational security/privacy goals and its ISCM strategy, scans of operating systems, databases, and web applications using a [Vulnerability Scanning Tool] at least once a month, and assessment of control effectiveness no less than at least every one (1) year.
[NIST 800-53 CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must correlate and analyze information generated by control assessments and monitoring, and take response actions to address the results of that analysis.
[NIST 800-53 CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must report the security and privacy status of the system to [Designated Personnel or Roles] at least every thirty (30) days (monthly), per ARC-AMPE.
[NIST 800-53 CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

- Security Program / GRC must follow the FedRAMP Continuous Collaborative Monitoring, Significant Change Notification, Vulnerability Detection and Response, and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules.

- Security Program / GRC must maintain continuous monitoring records until released by the investigating authority when a system is subject to a legal investigation (e.g., insider threat); must monitor systems, appliances, devices, and applications (including databases); and must provide oversight of information security and privacy for each system, including via a [SIEM Tool] as applicable.
- Security Program / GRC must employ independent assessors or assessment teams to monitor the controls in the system on an ongoing basis.
[NIST 800-53 CA-7(1) Moderate/High | ARC-AMPE CA-7(1) AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ trend analyses to determine if control implementations, monitoring frequency, or monitoring activity types need modification based on empirical data.

- Security Program / GRC must ensure risk monitoring is an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy, including effectiveness monitoring, compliance monitoring, and change monitoring; per ARC-AMPE, the continuous monitoring strategy must document processes and guidance defining effectiveness, compliance, and change monitoring as part of a holistic risk monitoring strategy.
- Security Program / GRC must employ [Designated Actions] to validate that policies are established and implemented controls are operating in a consistent manner.
- Security Program / GRC must ensure the accuracy, currency, and availability of monitoring results for the system using [Designated Automated Mechanisms].

- Security Program / GRC must conduct penetration testing at least every one (1) year on the documented system and its full boundary as agreed with testers in the Rules of Engagement, per ARC-AMPE, and must also perform testing when new risks/threats are identified or upon CMS request.
[NIST 800-53 CA-8 High | FedRAMP CA-8 | ARC-AMPE CA-8 AE Mandatory]
- Penetration testing must be treated as part of vulnerability detection and is subject to the FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response rules.

- The Penetration Testing Rules of Engagement must specify the scope of systems/components to be tested and any exclusions, and must be agreed upon and co-signed by both the system Authorizing Official and the penetration testing organization official; testing on production systems must minimize the risk of information corruption or service outage; scanning must include evaluation of embedded structures and interactive content; results must be searchable and provided in a CMS-compliant format; test information sources include systems, appliances, devices, services, and applications (including databases); organization-directed information collection requests must be fulfilled within the specified timeframe; and reports must be provided to CMS summarizing findings, significance, impact, risk, and remediation plans, including underlying raw security information/results in unaltered format.

- Security Program / GRC must employ an independent penetration testing agent or team, approved by Example Org's CISO or equivalent per ARC-AMPE, to perform penetration testing on the system or system components.
[NIST 800-53 CA-8(1) High | ARC-AMPE CA-8(1) AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must employ [Designated Red-Team Exercises] to simulate adversary attempts to compromise organizational systems in accordance with applicable rules of engagement.

- Security Program / GRC must employ a penetration testing process that includes announced and/or unannounced attempts, conducted annually, to bypass or circumvent controls associated with physical access points to the facility.

- Security Program / GRC must respond to findings from security and privacy assessments, monitoring, and audits in accordance with Example Org's risk tolerance, using options such as mitigating risk (implementing new or strengthened controls), accepting risk with appropriate justification/rationale, sharing or transferring risk, or avoiding risk, recording the decision in the risk register.
[NIST 800-53 RA-7 | FedRAMP RA-7 | ARC-AMPE RA-7 AE Mandatory]
- Security Program / GRC must follow the FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules.

- Security Program / GRC must discuss risk acceptance with CMS prior to actual acceptance to ensure agreement on approach and mitigations; risk-accepted findings must be documented and tracked in the POA&M and risk register with full detail in the risk acceptance form.

- Security Program / GRC must establish and implement, as needed, policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (e.g., fire, vandalism, system failure, natural disaster) that damages systems containing electronic protected health information.
- Security Program / GRC must establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information using the [Backup System].
- Security Program / GRC must establish and implement, as needed, procedures to restore any loss of data.

- Security Program / GRC must establish and implement, as needed, procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of electronic protected health information while operating in emergency mode.
- Security Program / GRC must implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans.
- Security Program / GRC must assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components.
Security Program / GRC maintains the following artifacts as evidence that this process is operating, and is accountable for their accuracy, currency, and retention:

| Artifact | Content | Generated/Updated By | | ----------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Risk register | Security categorization decisions, risk assessment results, supply chain risk assessments, POA&M items and remediation status, risk response and risk acceptance decisions | Sections 4, 5, 8, and 12 activities, performed by Security Program / GRC | | Authorization decision record | Authorizing official acceptance of common controls, system authorization to operate, and authorization update decisions | Section 9 activities, performed by Security Program / GRC in coordination with the authorizing official(s) |

Security Program / GRC must ensure both artifacts are kept current and available to support the reviews, reports, and notifications described throughout this Standard, and must review this Standard and its underlying process annually, consistent with the review requirements set out in Section 3.

[NIST 800-53 CA-2 | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

NIST and FedRAMP leave metrics and frequencies organization-defined; ARC-AMPE requires metrics based on organizational security/privacy goals and its ISCM strategy, scans of operating systems, databases, and web applications using a [Vulnerability Scanning Tool] at least once a month, and assessment of control effectiveness no less than at least every one (1) year.
[NIST 800-53 CA-7 | FedRAMP CA-7 | ARC-AMPE CA-7 AE Mandatory]

analyze: This Standard establishes the governance requirements for Example Org's information security program.
It governs how the program is planned, documented, resourced, and reviewed, and how the policies that constitute the program are developed, disseminated, and maintained.

The Security Program / GRC team is accountable for this process end to end: it owns the development, approval routing, dissemination, review, and update of the artifacts described in this Standard, and answers for the outcome of this process.
Other teams (e.g., Human Resources, Facilities, IT Operations, Legal) participate in individual steps as described below, but do not own the process.
This process runs on an annual cadence.
It is expected to produce and maintain the following evidence: - Approved policy set with review dates - Program plan and org chart

Security Program / GRC must develop and disseminate an organization-wide information security program plan that: - Provides an overview of security program requirements and describes the security program management and common controls in place or planned; - Includes identification and assignment of roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; - Reflects coordination among entities responsible for information security; and - Is approved by a senior official accountable for the risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
Security Program / GRC must review and update the plan annually and following [Organization-Defined Triggering Events].
The plan must be protected from unauthorized disclosure and modification.

Example Org must appoint a senior official (Senior Agency Information Security Officer / Senior Information Security Officer / security official) with the mission, resources, and responsibility to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain the organization-wide information security program, including development and implementation of required policies and procedures.
[NIST PM-2 | ARC-AMPE PM-2 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.308(a)(2)]

Security Program / GRC must develop a comprehensive, organization-wide risk management strategy to manage security risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, and privacy risk to individuals resulting from authorized processing of PII.
Security Program / GRC must implement the strategy consistently across the organization, and must review and update it annually or as required to address organizational changes.

Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate to [Designated Personnel or Roles] an organization-level, mission/business-process-level, or system-level planning policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, along with procedures to implement the policy and associated planning controls.

Security Program / GRC must designate a [Designated Official] to manage development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures, and must review and update the policy and procedures annually and following [Organization-Defined Triggering Events].

Additionally, Security Program / GRC must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with applicable requirements, taking into account specified risk factors; changes to policies and procedures must be documented and implemented in accordance with applicable requirements.
[NIST PL-1 | ARC-AMPE PL-1 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.316(a)]

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with system owners, must develop security and privacy plans for each system that: - Are consistent with the enterprise architecture; - Define constituent system components; - Describe the operational context in terms of mission/business processes; - Identify individuals fulfilling system roles/responsibilities; - Identify information types processed, stored, and transmitted; - Provide the system's security categorization with rationale; - Describe specific threats of concern; - Provide results of a privacy risk assessment for systems processing PII; - Describe the operational environment and dependencies/connections to other systems; - Provide an overview of security and privacy requirements; - Identify relevant control baselines or overlays; - Describe controls in place or planned, including tailoring rationale; - Include risk determinations for architecture/design decisions; and - Include security- and privacy-related activities requiring coordination with [Coordinating Individuals or Groups].
These plans must be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to implementation.

Security Program / GRC must distribute copies and communicate changes to [Plan Distribution Recipients]; review the plans annually or following significant changes; update the plans to address system/environment changes or problems identified during implementation or assessments; and protect the plans from unauthorized disclosure and modification.
Security Program / GRC must maintain required policies, procedures, and records of required actions, activities, or assessments in written form (which may be electronic).

Such documentation must be retained for 6 years from the date of creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later, made available to those responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains, and reviewed periodically, with updates made as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.

Security Program / GRC must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations, including: - Conducting an accurate and thorough risk analysis of potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information; - Implementing security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level; and - Implementing procedures to regularly review records of information system activity such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with Facilities, must implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and the facilities housing them, while ensuring properly authorized access is allowed.

These policies and procedures must: - Establish procedures allowing facility access to support restoration of lost data under disaster recovery and emergency mode operations plans; - Safeguard the facility and equipment from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft; - Control and validate access based on role or function, including visitor control and control of access to software used for testing/revision; and - Document security-related repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility.

Except where disclosure is limited to summary health information or enrollment/disenrollment data, or is otherwise authorized, a group health plan must ensure its plan documents provide that the plan sponsor will reasonably and appropriately safeguard electronic protected health information created, received, maintained, or transmitted on its behalf.

Plan documents must be amended to require the plan sponsor to: - Implement administrative, physical, and technical safeguards protecting the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of such information; - Ensure adequate separation is supported by reasonable and appropriate security measures; - Ensure any agent receiving the information agrees to implement reasonable and appropriate security measures; and - Report security incidents to the group health plan.

Security Program / GRC must establish and provide to individuals requiring system access the rules describing their responsibilities and expected behavior for information and system usage, security, and privacy.
Security Program / GRC must obtain a documented acknowledgment from such individuals that they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules before authorizing access.
The rules must be reviewed and updated annually.
Individuals who acknowledged a previous version must re-acknowledge when the rules are revised or updated.

The rules must include restrictions on use of social media/social networking/external sites and applications, posting organizational information on public websites, and use of organization-provided identifiers and authentication secrets to create external accounts.
[NIST PL-4 | ARC-AMPE PL-4 AE Mandatory | NIST PL-4(1) | ARC-AMPE PL-4(1) AE Mandatory]

Security Program / GRC must implement policies and procedures specifying the proper functions to be performed, the manner in which those functions are performed, and the physical attributes of the surroundings of workstations or classes of workstations that can access electronic protected health information.

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with system owners, must develop security and privacy architectures for each system that: - Describe the requirements and approach for protecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability of organizational information; - Describe the requirements and approach for processing PII to minimize privacy risk; - Describe how the architectures are integrated into and support the enterprise architecture; and - Describe assumptions about and dependencies on external systems and services.

The architectures must be reviewed and updated annually or following a significant change to reflect enterprise architecture changes, and planned architecture changes must be reflected in security and privacy plans, CONOPS, criticality analysis, organizational procedures, and procurements/acquisitions.
Security Program / GRC must select a control baseline for each system.
Security Program / GRC must tailor the selected control baseline by applying specified tailoring actions.

Controls included within the CMS ARC-AMPE baseline must not be removed or reduced, AC-2(8) must not be added to the baseline, and controls may be added only where they do not conflict with or create less stringent standards than the baseline, based on a risk-informed decision considering mission/business functions, operating environment, and threats/vulnerabilities.

Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate to [Designated Personnel or Roles] an organization-level, mission/business-process-level, or system-level personnel security policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, along with procedures to implement the policy and associated personnel security controls.

Security Program / GRC must designate a [Designated Official] to manage development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures, and must review and update the policy and procedures annually and following [Organization-Defined Triggering Events].

Human Resources, in coordination with Security Program / GRC, must implement policies and procedures to ensure workforce members have appropriate access to electronic protected health information and to prevent unauthorized access by those without it.

These policies and procedures must: - Provide for authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with such information or in locations where it might be accessed; - Include a workforce clearance procedure to determine appropriate access; and - Include termination procedures for revoking access when employment or another arrangement ends or as otherwise determined necessary.
Security Program / GRC must develop and document access agreements for organizational systems and must review and update the agreements annually.
Individuals requiring access must sign appropriate access agreements prior to being granted access and must re-sign them when updated or annually.

Security Program / GRC must implement policies and procedures for authorizing access to electronic protected health information consistent with applicable requirements, including: - Isolating health care clearinghouse functions within a larger organization to protect ePHI from unauthorized access by that organization; - Implementing access authorization procedures (e.g., for workstations, transactions, programs, or processes); and - Implementing procedures to establish, document, review, and modify a user's right of access based on the organization's access authorization policies.

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with IT Operations, must implement policies and procedures governing the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media containing electronic protected health information into and out of a facility, and movement of such items within the facility.

These policies and procedures must: - Address final disposition of the information and/or the media on which it is stored; - Include procedures to remove such information from media before reuse; - Require maintenance of a record of hardware/media movements and the responsible person; and - Require creation of a retrievable, exact copy of the information, when needed, before moving equipment.

Example Org (as a covered entity or business associate) may permit a business associate (or subcontractor) to create, receive, maintain, or transmit electronic protected health information on its behalf only after obtaining satisfactory assurances, documented through a written contract or other arrangement, that the recipient will appropriately safeguard the information.

The contract must: - Require the business associate to comply with applicable requirements; - Require the business associate to ensure its subcontractors agree by contract to comply with the same requirements; and - Require the business associate to report security incidents (including breaches of unsecured protected health information) to the covered entity.
Alternative arrangements satisfying the applicable requirements may substitute for a contract.
These requirements apply equally to contracts between a business associate and its subcontractors.

Security Program / GRC must establish personnel security requirements, including security roles and responsibilities, for external providers, and must require external providers to comply with the organization's personnel security policies and procedures.

External providers must be required to notify [Designated Personnel or Roles] of personnel transfers or terminations of external personnel possessing organizational credentials/badges or system privileges within 24 hours.
Security Program / GRC must monitor provider compliance with personnel security requirements.
Additionally, [Identity Provider] must clearly document any nationality requirements for any account type within its platform, or explicitly state that none exist.
[NIST PS-7 | FedRAMP PS-7 | ARC-AMPE PS-7 AE Mandatory]

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with Human Resources, must employ a formal sanctions process for individuals failing to comply with established information security and privacy policies and procedures, including applying appropriate sanctions against noncompliant workforce members.
[Designated Personnel or Roles] must be notified within 24 hours when a formal sanctions process is initiated, with notification identifying the individual sanctioned and the reason for the sanction.
[NIST PS-8 | ARC-AMPE PS-8 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(C)]

Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate to [Designated Personnel or Roles] an organization-level, mission/business-process-level, or system-level system and services acquisition policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, along with procedures to implement the policy and associated system and services acquisition controls.

Security Program / GRC must designate a [Designated Official] to manage development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures, and must review and update the policy and procedures annually and following [Organization-Defined Triggering Events].

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with system owners and finance/budget stakeholders, must determine the high-level information security and privacy requirements for a system or system service during mission and business process planning.

Security Program / GRC must determine, document, and allocate the resources required to protect the system or service as part of the organizational capital planning and investment control process, and must establish a discrete line item for information security and privacy in organizational programming and budgeting documentation.
Security Program / GRC must retain evidence of this process, including:

| Artifact | Description | | ------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Approved policy set with review dates | The current approved versions of the policies and procedures described in this Standard, each showing the date of last review/approval | | Program plan and org chart | The organization-wide information security program plan and the associated organizational chart reflecting roles, responsibilities, and coordination among entities |

These artifacts must be made available to those responsible for implementing the procedures to which they pertain and must be updated in accordance with the review requirements set out in the applicable sections above.

8. Prevention, Detection, Containment, and Correction of Security Violations

unanchored: Security Program / GRC must develop and disseminate an organization-wide information security program plan that: - Provides an overview of security program requirements and describes the security program management and common controls in place or planned; - Includes identification and assignment of roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance; - Reflects coordination among entities responsible for information security; and - Is approved by a senior official accountable for the risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation.
Security Program / GRC must review and update the plan annually and following [Organization-Defined Triggering Events].

Security Program / GRC must develop a comprehensive, organization-wide risk management strategy to manage security risk to organizational operations, assets, individuals, other organizations, and the Nation, and privacy risk to individuals resulting from authorized processing of PII.

Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate to [Designated Personnel or Roles] an organization-level, mission/business-process-level, or system-level planning policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, along with procedures to implement the policy and associated planning controls.

Security Program / GRC must designate a [Designated Official] to manage development, documentation, and dissemination of the policy and procedures, and must review and update the policy and procedures annually and following [Organization-Defined Triggering Events].

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with system owners, must develop security and privacy plans for each system that: - Are consistent with the enterprise architecture; - Define constituent system components; - Describe the operational context in terms of mission/business processes; - Identify individuals fulfilling system roles/responsibilities; - Identify information types processed, stored, and transmitted; - Provide the system's security categorization with rationale; - Describe specific threats of concern; - Provide results of a privacy risk assessment for systems processing PII; - Describe the operational environment and dependencies/connections to other systems; - Provide an overview of security and privacy requirements; - Identify relevant control baselines or overlays; - Describe controls in place or planned, including tailoring rationale; - Include risk determinations for architecture/design decisions; and - Include security- and privacy-related activities requiring coordination with [Coordinating Individuals or Groups].
These plans must be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to implementation.
Security Program / GRC must maintain required policies, procedures, and records of required actions, activities, or assessments in written form (which may be electronic).

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with Facilities, must implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and the facilities housing them, while ensuring properly authorized access is allowed.

Except where disclosure is limited to summary health information or enrollment/disenrollment data, or is otherwise authorized, a group health plan must ensure its plan documents provide that the plan sponsor will reasonably and appropriately safeguard electronic protected health information created, received, maintained, or transmitted on its behalf.

Security Program / GRC must establish and provide to individuals requiring system access the rules describing their responsibilities and expected behavior for information and system usage, security, and privacy.
Security Program / GRC must obtain a documented acknowledgment from such individuals that they have read, understand, and agree to abide by the rules before authorizing access.
The rules must be reviewed and updated annually.
Individuals who acknowledged a previous version must re-acknowledge when the rules are revised or updated.

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with system owners, must develop security and privacy architectures for each system that: - Describe the requirements and approach for protecting confidentiality, integrity, and availability of organizational information; - Describe the requirements and approach for processing PII to minimize privacy risk; - Describe how the architectures are integrated into and support the enterprise architecture; and - Describe assumptions about and dependencies on external systems and services.
Security Program / GRC must tailor the selected control baseline by applying specified tailoring actions.

Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate to [Designated Personnel or Roles] an organization-level, mission/business-process-level, or system-level personnel security policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, along with procedures to implement the policy and associated personnel security controls.

Human Resources, in coordination with Security Program / GRC, must implement policies and procedures to ensure workforce members have appropriate access to electronic protected health information and to prevent unauthorized access by those without it.
Security Program / GRC must develop and document access agreements for organizational systems and must review and update the agreements annually.

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with IT Operations, must implement policies and procedures governing the receipt and removal of hardware and electronic media containing electronic protected health information into and out of a facility, and movement of such items within the facility.

Security Program / GRC must establish personnel security requirements, including security roles and responsibilities, for external providers, and must require external providers to comply with the organization's personnel security policies and procedures.
These requirements must be documented.

External providers must be required to notify [Designated Personnel or Roles] of personnel transfers or terminations of external personnel possessing organizational credentials/badges or system privileges within 24 hours.
Security Program / GRC must monitor provider compliance with personnel security requirements.

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with Human Resources, must employ a formal sanctions process for individuals failing to comply with established information security and privacy policies and procedures, including applying appropriate sanctions against noncompliant workforce members.

Security Program / GRC must develop, document, and disseminate to [Designated Personnel or Roles] an organization-level, mission/business-process-level, or system-level system and services acquisition policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines, along with procedures to implement the policy and associated system and services acquisition controls.

Security Program / GRC, in coordination with system owners and finance/budget stakeholders, must determine the high-level information security and privacy requirements for a system or system service during mission and business process planning.

This Standard establishes the requirements for Example Org's workforce security and privacy awareness and training program.
It defines the policy, procedures, training content, delivery cadence, and documentation obligations that security and IT staff must implement and against which compliance will be audited.
The Security Awareness team is accountable for this process end to end, including all handoffs to participating teams.

This Standard applies to all members of the Example Org workforce, including management, senior executives, employees, and contractors, and to all individuals working on behalf of the organization who access, use, manage, or develop organizational systems.

Security Awareness shall develop, document, and disseminate to organization-defined personnel or roles an awareness and training policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
While NIST permits the policy to be organization-level, mission/business process-level, or system-level, this Standard adopts an organization-level policy.
Security Awareness shall develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate implementation of the awareness and training policy and the associated awareness and training controls.
The lead of the Security Awareness team is the designated official responsible for managing the development, documentation, and dissemination of the awareness and training policy and procedures.
Security Awareness shall review and update the awareness and training policy at least annually and following organization-defined events.
Security Awareness shall review and update the awareness and training procedures at least annually and following organization-defined events.
Security Awareness shall actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect awareness and training policies.

Security Awareness shall ensure awareness and training policies and procedures support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and the life cycle of the information on that system.

Security Awareness shall maintain the policies and procedures implemented under this Standard in written form (which may be electronic), and shall maintain a written (electronic permitted) record of any action, activity, or assessment required to be documented.
Security Awareness shall retain required documentation for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
Security Awareness shall make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

Security Awareness shall review documentation periodically and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
Example Org shall implement a security awareness and training program for all members of the workforce, including management.
The Security Awareness team owns and operates this program.

Security Awareness shall provide security and privacy literacy training to system users (including managers, senior executives, and contractors) as part of initial training for new users and thereafter at least annually.

Security Awareness shall provide additional literacy training when required by system changes or following organization-defined events (e.g., assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines).

Security Awareness shall employ techniques to increase the security and privacy awareness of system users, per organization-defined awareness techniques; these techniques shall include phishing email tests and other organization-defined techniques.
Phishing exercises shall be conducted through the [Phishing Simulation Platform], and their outcomes recorded as Phishing simulation results.
Security Awareness shall update literacy training and awareness content at least annually and following organization-defined events.
Security Awareness shall incorporate lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into literacy training and awareness techniques.

Security Awareness shall develop and implement an information security and privacy education and awareness training program for all employees and individuals working on behalf of the organization who access, use, manage, or develop systems; this program may be integrated with general cybersecurity training.

Security Awareness shall include, within the information security and privacy education and awareness training, an individual's responsibilities associated with sending sensitive information in email.

Security Awareness shall provide privacy training before granting access to organizational systems and networks, for all employees and contractors, for all systems that collect, maintain, store, use, or disclose Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
Security Awareness shall provide practical exercises in literacy training that simulate events and incidents.
Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.

This training should include how to communicate employee and management concerns regarding potential insider threat indicators through appropriate organizational channels in accordance with established organizational policies and procedures.
Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on recognizing and reporting potential and actual instances of social engineering and social mining.

This training should include how to recognize and report, through appropriate organizational and defined channels (e.g., applicable security and privacy plans), potential attempts to trick an individual into revealing information or taking an action that can be used to breach, compromise, or otherwise adversely impact a system.
Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on recognizing suspicious communications and anomalous behavior in organizational systems using organization-defined indicators of malicious code.

This training should include how to recognize and report, through appropriate organizational and defined channels (e.g., applicable security and privacy plans): potentially suspicious email or web communications (e.g., receiving an unexpected email, receiving an email containing strange or poor grammar, or receiving an email from an unfamiliar sender who appears to be from a known sponsor or contractor), and anomalous behaviors in systems.
Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on the advanced persistent threat (APT).

This training should include techniques for recognizing suspicious emails, use of removable systems in non-secure settings, the potential targeting of individuals at home, and the various ways APTs can infiltrate the organization (e.g., through websites, emails, advertisement pop-ups, articles, and social engineering).
Security Awareness shall provide literacy training on the cyber threat environment and reflect current cyber threat information in system operations.
Security Awareness shall implement periodic security updates (security reminders).
Security Awareness shall implement procedures for guarding against, detecting, and reporting malicious software.
Security Awareness shall implement procedures for monitoring log-in attempts and reporting discrepancies.
Security Awareness shall implement procedures for creating, changing, and safeguarding passwords.

Security Awareness shall provide role-based security and privacy training to personnel with organization-defined roles and responsibilities before authorizing access to the system or information or performing assigned duties, and thereafter at least annually.
This requirement applies to significant information security and privacy roles.

Security Awareness shall provide role-based security and privacy training when required by system changes; when an employee enters a new position that requires additional role-specific training; and when significant information system or system environment changes occur.
Security Awareness shall update role-based training content at least annually and following significant changes to the system or the system environment.
Security Awareness shall incorporate lessons learned from internal or external security incidents or breaches into role-based training.

Security Awareness shall disable the user accounts of employees and contractors with significant information security and privacy roles and responsibilities who have not completed the required role-based training within the mandated timeframes, until they have met the role-based training requirement.
Account disablement shall be coordinated with the [Identity Provider] administrators.
Security Awareness shall provide organization-defined personnel or roles with initial and annual training in the employment and operation of environmental controls.
Security Awareness shall provide organization-defined personnel or roles with initial and annual training in the employment and operation of physical security controls.
Security Awareness shall provide practical exercises in security and privacy training that reinforce training objectives.

Security Awareness shall provide organizational personnel (including vendors, contractors, and employees) with initial training — and thereafter at least annually — in the employment and operation of personally identifiable information processing and transparency controls.

Security Awareness shall develop and implement a privacy education and awareness training program for all employees and individuals working on behalf of the organization involved in managing, using, and/or processing PII.
Security Awareness shall include responsibilities associated with sending PII in email within the privacy education and awareness training.
Security Awareness shall ensure privacy communications and training are job-specific and commensurate with the employee's responsibilities.

Security Awareness shall ensure initial training of employees (including managers) on their privacy responsibilities is completed before permitting access to organizational information and systems, with refresher training completed every one (1) year thereafter.
Security Awareness shall ensure any additional or advanced training provided is commensurate with the employee's responsibilities.
The Security Awareness team shall produce and retain the following artifacts as evidence of program operation:

| Artifact | Description | | --------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Training completion report | Record of workforce completion of initial, refresher, and role-based training, maintained in the [Learning Management System] | | Phishing simulation results | Outcomes of phishing email tests conducted under Section 5.4 |
These artifacts are subject to the retention requirement in Section 4.2.

The Security Awareness team is accountable for this process end to end, including the development, delivery, tracking, review, and updating of all training and awareness activities defined in this Standard, and for the production and retention of the evidence artifacts listed in Section 10.1.

Other teams participate in individual steps (e.g., [Identity Provider] administrators for account disablement under Section 8.5), but ownership of the process and its handoffs rests with Security Awareness.

analyze: This Standard establishes requirements for the maintenance of Acme Health information systems and the physical security of facilities housing those systems, to ensure the continued secure operation of systems processing protected health information and to maintain compliance with applicable regulatory requirements.

This Standard applies to all Acme Health information systems, system components, facilities housing information systems, and personnel performing maintenance activities on or near those systems, whether performed on-site or remotely.
Acme Health shall designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the maintenance policy and procedures.
[NIST 800-53 MA-1 Low | NIST 800-53 MA-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-1 High | ARC-AMPE MA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health shall develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the maintenance policy and associated maintenance controls.

Acme Health shall review and update the maintenance policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.
Acme Health shall review and update the maintenance procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].
[NIST 800-53 MA-1 Low | NIST 800-53 MA-1 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-1 High]
Acme Health shall review and update the maintenance procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.

Acme Health shall schedule, document, and review records of maintenance, repair, and replacement on system components in accordance with manufacturer or vendor specifications and/or organizational requirements.

Acme Health shall require that [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] explicitly approve the removal of the system or system components from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement.

Acme Health shall sanitize equipment to remove [Assignment: organization-defined information] from associated media prior to removal from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low | NIST 800-53 MA-2 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-2 High]

Acme Health shall sanitize equipment to remove all organizational information from associated media prior to removal from organizational facilities for off-site maintenance, repair, or replacement, in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88.
Acme Health shall check all potentially impacted controls to verify that the controls are still functioning properly following maintenance, repair, or replacement actions.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low | NIST 800-53 MA-2 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-2 High | ARC-AMPE MA-2 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall include [Assignment: organization-defined information] in organizational maintenance records.
[NIST 800-53 MA-2 Low | NIST 800-53 MA-2 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-2 High]
Acme Health shall include maintenance-related information in organizational maintenance records.
On organizational systems where Personally Identifiable Information (PII) is stored or accessed, Acme Health shall document all repairs and modifications to the system components.

Acme Health shall schedule, conduct, and document maintenance, repair, and replacement actions for the system using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms]; and produce up-to-date, accurate, and complete records of all maintenance, repair, and replacement actions requested, scheduled, in process, and completed.
Acme Health shall approve, control, and monitor the use of system maintenance tools.
[NIST 800-53 MA-3 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-3 High | ARC-AMPE MA-3 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall review previously approved system maintenance tools [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].

Acme Health shall inspect maintenance tools used by maintenance personnel for improper or unauthorized modifications.
[NIST 800-53 MA-3(1) Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-3(1) High | ARC-AMPE MA-3(1) AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall check media containing diagnostic and test programs for malicious code before the media are used in the system.

If malware or unauthorized changes are discovered during inspection of maintenance media, Acme Health shall treat this discovery consistent with organizational policies and procedures for incident handling.

Acme Health shall prevent the removal of maintenance equipment containing organizational information by: (a) verifying that there is no organizational information contained on the equipment; (b) sanitizing or destroying the equipment; (c) retaining the equipment within the facility; or (d) obtaining an exemption from [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles] explicitly authorizing removal of the equipment from the facility.

Acme Health shall monitor the use of maintenance tools that execute with increased privilege.

Acme Health shall monitor maintenance tools to detect unauthorized access to information and assets as a result of increased system privileges to information that would otherwise be inaccessible to individuals.
Acme Health shall inspect maintenance tools to ensure the latest software updates and patches are installed.
To the extent possible, Acme Health shall install software updates and patches on organizational systems to minimize vulnerabilities and maintain cyber hygiene on organizational systems.
Acme Health shall ensure the organization's installation of updates in support of daily operations has minimal impact to organizational systems.
Acme Health shall approve and monitor nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic activities.
[NIST 800-53 MA-4 Low | NIST 800-53 MA-4 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-4 High | ARC-AMPE MA-4 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall allow the use of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic tools only as consistent with organizational policy and documented in the security plan for the system.

Acme Health shall ensure authentication and authenticators used during nonlocal maintenance are in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-63B, Digital Identity Guidelines.

Acme Health shall maintain records for nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic activities.

Acme Health shall terminate session and network connections when nonlocal maintenance is completed.
[NIST 800-53 MA-4 Low | NIST 800-53 MA-4 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-4 High | ARC-AMPE MA-4 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall sanitize media used during remote nonlocal maintenance in accordance with the latest published NIST SP 800-88, Guidelines for Media Sanitization.

Acme Health shall log [Assignment: organization-defined audit events] for nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions, and review the audit records of the maintenance and diagnostic sessions to detect anomalous behavior.
Acme Health shall log organization-defined audit events, as defined in the organization's formal audit policy, for nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions.
Acme Health shall ensure audit events for nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions are logged and collected.
Acme Health shall review the audit records of the maintenance and diagnostic sessions to detect anomalous behavior.

Acme Health shall require that nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic services be performed from a system that implements a security capability comparable to the capability implemented on the system being serviced; or remove the component to be serviced from the system prior to nonlocal maintenance or diagnostic services, sanitize the component (for organizational information), and after the service is performed, inspect and sanitize the component (for potentially malicious software) before reconnecting the component to the system.

Acme Health shall protect nonlocal maintenance sessions by: (a) employing [Assignment: organization-defined authenticators that are replay resistant]; and (b) separating the maintenance sessions from other network sessions with the system by either (1) physically separated communications paths or (2) logically separated communications paths.

Acme Health shall require the approval of each nonlocal maintenance session by [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles]; and notify [Assignment: organization-defined personnel and roles] of the date and time of planned nonlocal maintenance.
Acme Health shall implement [Assignment: organization-defined cryptographic mechanisms] to protect the integrity and confidentiality of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic communications.
Acme Health shall verify session and network connection termination after the completion of nonlocal maintenance and diagnostic sessions.
Acme Health shall verify that non-escorted personnel performing maintenance on the system possess the required access authorizations.
[NIST 800-53 MA-5 Low | NIST 800-53 MA-5 Moderate | NIST 800-53 MA-5 High | FedRAMP MA-5 | ARC-AMPE MA-5 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall ensure non-escorted personnel performing maintenance on the system possess the required access authorizations and security credentials.

Acme Health shall follow organization-established visitor logging and escort security protocols and ensure that any organizational personnel who supervise maintenance activities of personnel without access authorizations have been trained on supervisory and escorting responsibilities.

Acme Health shall implement procedures for the use of maintenance personnel that lack appropriate security clearances or are not U.S. citizens, requiring: (1) maintenance personnel who do not have needed access authorizations, clearances, or formal access approvals are escorted and supervised during the performance of maintenance and diagnostic activities on the system by approved organizational personnel who are fully cleared, have appropriate access authorizations, and are technically qualified; and (2) prior to initiating maintenance or diagnostic activities by personnel who do not have needed access authorizations, clearances or formal access approvals, all volatile information storage components within the system are sanitized and all nonvolatile storage media are removed or physically disconnected from the system and secured.
[NIST 800-53 MA-5(1) High | FedRAMP MA-5(1) | ARC-AMPE MA-5(1) AE Mandatory]
Acme Health shall develop and implement [Assignment: organization-defined alternate controls] in the event a system component cannot be sanitized, removed, or disconnected from the system.
[NIST 800-53 MA-5(1) High | FedRAMP MA-5(1) | ARC-AMPE MA-5(1) AE Mandatory]

Acme Health shall verify that personnel performing maintenance and diagnostic activities on a system processing, storing, or transmitting classified information possess security clearances and formal access approvals for at least the highest classification level and for compartments of information on the system.
Acme Health shall verify that personnel performing maintenance and diagnostic activities on a system processing, storing, or transmitting classified information are U.S. citizens.

Acme Health shall ensure foreign nationals with appropriate security clearances are used to conduct maintenance and diagnostic activities on classified systems only when the systems are jointly owned and operated by the United States and foreign allied governments, or owned and operated solely by foreign allied governments; and ensure approvals, consents, and detailed operational conditions regarding the use of foreign nationals to conduct maintenance and diagnostic activities on classified systems are fully documented within Memoranda of Agreements.

Acme Health shall ensure that non-escorted personnel performing maintenance activities not directly associated with the system but in the physical proximity of the system have required access authorizations.
Acme Health shall obtain maintenance support and/or spare parts for [Assignment: organization-defined system components] within [Assignment: organization-defined time period] of failure.

Acme Health shall obtain maintenance support and/or spare parts for organization-defined information system components within the applicable Recovery Time Objective (RTO) specified in the system Contingency Plan of failure.
Acme Health shall perform preventive maintenance on [Assignment: organization-defined system components] at [Assignment: organization-defined time intervals].
Acme Health shall perform preventive maintenance on system components at applicable Recovery Time Objective (RTO) time intervals specified in the system Contingency Plan.
Acme Health shall perform predictive maintenance on [Assignment: organization-defined system components] at [Assignment: organization-defined time intervals].
Acme Health shall transfer predictive maintenance data to a maintenance management system using [Assignment: organization-defined automated mechanisms].

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to limit physical access to electronic information systems and the facilities in which they are housed, while ensuring properly authorized access is allowed.

Acme Health shall establish and implement as needed procedures that allow facility access in support of restoration of lost data under the disaster recovery plan and emergency mode operations plan in the event of an emergency.
Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to safeguard the facility and equipment from unauthorized physical access, tampering, and theft.

Acme Health shall implement procedures to control and validate a person's access to facilities based on their role or function, including visitor control, and control of access to software programs for testing and revision.

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to document repairs and modifications to the physical components of a facility which are related to security (for example, hardware, walls, doors, and locks).

Acme Health shall implement policies and procedures to ensure that all members of the workforce have appropriate access to electronic protected health information, and to prevent those workforce members who do not have access from obtaining access to electronic protected health information.
Acme Health shall implement procedures for the authorization and/or supervision of workforce members who work with electronic protected health information or in locations where it might be accessed.
Acme Health shall implement procedures to determine that the access of a workforce member to electronic protected health information is appropriate.

Acme Health shall implement procedures for terminating access to electronic protected health information when the employment of, or other arrangement with, a workforce member ends or as required by determinations made under workforce clearance procedures.

Acme Health shall maintain policies and procedures implemented to comply with applicable security requirements in written (which may be electronic) form, and maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any required action, activity, or assessment.
Acme Health shall retain documentation for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
Acme Health shall make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.
Acme Health shall review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.

All Acme Health personnel, contractors, and third parties performing maintenance activities or having access to facilities housing information systems are responsible for understanding and complying with this Standard.
