This standard establishes the requirements for conducting risk assessments, categorizing systems, performing security and privacy control assessments, authorizing systems to operate, and monitoring security and privacy posture at Example Org.

It applies to all systems, system components, and system services owned or operated by Example Org, and to all personnel involved in the risk assessment, authorization, and continuous monitoring processes.
The **Security Program / GRC** team is accountable for this process end to end, including all handoffs described in this document.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop, document, and disseminate to [Designated Personnel or Roles] a risk assessment policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
[NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the risk assessment policy and the associated risk assessment controls.
[NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall designate an official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the risk assessment policy and procedures.
[NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the risk assessment policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following [Organization-Defined Events] (such as assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines).
[NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop, document, and disseminate to [Designated Personnel or Roles] an assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
[NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and the associated controls.
[NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall designate an official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures, named in the appropriate security and privacy documents.
[NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following [Organization-Defined Events] (such as assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines).
[NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

- Example Org shall implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the applicable standards and requirements, and shall document any changes to those policies and procedures.
- The Security Program / GRC team shall maintain required policies, procedures, and documented actions, activities, or assessments in written (which may be electronic) form.
- Required documentation shall be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
- Documentation shall be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall periodically review documentation and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
- Example Org identifies the head of the Security Program / GRC team as the security official responsible for the development and implementation of the required security policies and procedures.
- The Security Program / GRC team shall categorize the system and the information it processes, stores, and transmits.
[NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall document the security categorization results, including supporting rationale, in the security plan for the system.
[NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]
- The authorizing official or the authorizing official's designated representative shall review and approve the security categorization decision.
[NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall involve the senior official for privacy, or their designee, when conducting the security categorization process.
- The Security Program / GRC team shall conduct an impact-level prioritization of organizational systems to obtain additional granularity on system impact levels.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall conduct a risk assessment that includes identifying threats to and vulnerabilities in the system; determining the likelihood and magnitude of harm from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of the system and the information it processes, stores, or transmits, and any related information; and determining the likelihood and impact of adverse effects on individuals arising from the processing of personally identifiable information.
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory | HIPAA 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A)]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall integrate risk assessment results and risk management decisions from the organization and mission or business process perspectives with system-level risk assessments.
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall document risk assessment results in security and privacy plans, a risk assessment report, the risk register, and any additional organization-defined documents.
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall review risk assessment results at least every one (1) year or when a significant change occurs.
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall disseminate risk assessment results to [Designated Personnel or Roles].
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall update the risk assessment at least every three (3) years for internal, organization-specific authorization, and whenever there are significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact the security or privacy state of the system.
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall document and implement a privacy risk management process that assesses privacy risk to individuals resulting from the collection, sharing, storing, transmitting, use, and disposal of personally identifiable information.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall assess supply chain risks associated with [Defined Systems, System Components, and System Services], and shall update the supply chain risk assessment at [Supply Chain Risk Assessment Frequency], when there are significant changes to the relevant supply chain, or when changes to the system, environments of operation, or other conditions may necessitate a change in the supply chain.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall use all-source intelligence, including publicly available or open-source information, to assist in the analysis of risk, including the risk of vulnerabilities (both intentional and unintentional) from development, manufacturing, and delivery processes, people, and the environment, and to inform engineering, acquisition, and risk management decisions.
- The Security Program / GRC team shall determine the current cyber threat environment on an ongoing basis using [Defined Means].
- The Security Program / GRC team shall employ [Advanced Automation and Analytics Capabilities] to predict and identify risks to [Defined Systems or System Components].
- Example Org shall implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level.
- Example Org shall apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures of the covered entity or business associate.
- The Security Program / GRC team shall implement procedures to regularly review records of information system activity, such as audit logs, access reports, and security incident tracking reports.
- The Security Program / GRC team shall respond to findings from security and privacy assessments, monitoring, and audits in accordance with organizational risk tolerance.
[NIST 800-53 RA-7 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP RA-7 | ARC-AMPE RA-7 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall follow the FedRAMP Vulnerability Detection and Response and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules when responding to risk findings.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall discuss risk acceptance with CMS prior to actual acceptance, and shall document and track risk-accepted findings in the Plan of Action & Milestones (POA&M) with full detail in the risk acceptance form.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall identify critical system components and functions by performing a criticality analysis for [Defined Systems, System Components, or System Services] at [System Development Life Cycle Decision Points].
[NIST 800-53 RA-9 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-9 AE Mandatory]
- The Security Program / GRC team shall treat all system components within the CMS Authority to Connect (ATC)/Request to Connect (RTC) boundary as critical.

- Example Org shall establish (and implement as needed) policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (for example, fire, vandalism, system failure, and natural disaster) that damages systems containing electronic protected health information.
- Example Org shall establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information, maintained by the [Backup System].
- Example Org shall establish (and implement as needed) procedures to restore any loss of data.

- Example Org shall establish (and implement as needed) procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of electronic protected health information while operating in emergency mode.
- Example Org shall implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans (addressable).
- Example Org shall assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components (addressable).
- The Security Program / GRC team shall select the appropriate assessor or assessment team for the type of assessment to be conducted.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop a control assessment plan describing the scope of the assessment, including the controls and control enhancements under assessment, the assessment procedures to be used to determine control effectiveness, and the assessment environment, assessment team, and assessment roles and responsibilities.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]
- The control assessment plan shall be reviewed and approved by the authorizing official or designated representative prior to conducting the assessment.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall assess the controls in the system and its environment of operation at [Control Assessment Frequency] to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting established security and privacy requirements.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall conduct a complete independent assessment of all security and privacy controls over a three (3) year period — either via a full controls assessment, annual assessments of the controls designated for years one through three, or per CMS guidance on testing for each significant system change — with the complete and final ATC package delivered to CMS no less than ninety (90) days prior to ATC expiration.

- Example Org shall perform a periodic technical and nontechnical evaluation, based initially upon the implemented standards and subsequently in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information, that establishes the extent to which the entity's security policies and procedures meet the applicable requirements.
- The Security Program / GRC team shall produce a control assessment report that documents the results of the assessment.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall provide the results of the control assessment to [Designated Individuals or Roles], which for FedRAMP include FedRAMP and agency customers, and for ARC-AMPE include the Business Owner responsible for the system and personnel responsible for reviewing assessment documentation, in writing within thirty (30) days after the assessment's completion.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall update relevant security and privacy documentation to reflect any changes to the system within thirty (30) days of the changes or within thirty (30) days of the control assessment results, and shall notify CMS within thirty (30) days whenever updates are made to system security and privacy authorization artifacts or when significant role changes occur.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall employ independent assessors or assessment teams to conduct control assessments, following the CMS Framework for Independent Assessment of Security and Privacy Controls where applicable.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2(1) Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-2(1) AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall include as part of control assessments, at [Specialized Assessment Frequency], announced or unannounced specialized assessments such as in-depth monitoring, security instrumentation, automated security test cases, vulnerability scanning, malicious user testing, insider threat assessment, performance and load testing, data leakage or data loss assessment, or other organization-defined forms of assessment.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall leverage the results of control assessments performed by [External Organizations] on [Defined Systems] when the assessment meets [Organization-Defined Requirements]; for FedRAMP, any FedRAMP-recognized independent assessment service qualifies.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop a plan of action and milestones (POA&M) for the system to document the planned remediation actions of the organization to correct weaknesses or deficiencies noted during the assessment of the controls and to reduce or eliminate known vulnerabilities in the system.
[NIST 800-53 CA-5 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall update the existing POA&M in accordance with the frequency documented in the organization's Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) strategy, based on findings from control assessments, independent audits or reviews, and continuous monitoring activities.
[NIST 800-53 CA-5 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-5 AE Mandatory]

- The Security Program / GRC team shall establish and maintain the POA&M throughout the system lifecycle starting with development, including scheduled completion dates, milestones with dates, appropriate risk levels, as-detailed-as-possible weakness descriptions, and all findings whether self-discovered or identified through assessments.

- The Security Program / GRC team shall develop the POA&M based on the CMS Standard for POA&M Management and Reporting using the CMS-provided template, and shall remediate POA&M entries consistent with SI-2.
- The Security Program / GRC team shall deliver a fully updated and accurate POA&M to CMS quarterly on 31 January, 30 April, 31 July, and 31 October.
- Example Org shall ensure the accuracy, currency, and availability of the plan of action and milestones for the system using [Automated Mechanism].
- Example Org shall assign a senior official as the authorizing official for the system.
[NIST 800-53 CA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]
- Example Org shall assign a senior official as the authorizing official for common controls available for inheritance by organizational systems.
[NIST 800-53 CA-6 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-6 AE Mandatory]

analyze: This standard establishes the requirements for risk assessment, security categorization, assessment and authorization, and continuous monitoring of information systems at Acme Health.
This standard applies to all information systems that process, store, or transmit electronic protected health information and other organizational information assets.

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate a risk assessment policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
[NIST 800-53 RA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-1 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the risk assessment policy and the associated risk assessment controls.

Acme Health must review and update the risk assessment policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events], and review and update the risk assessment procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

Acme Health must review and update the risk assessment policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, and review and update the risk assessment procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate an assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy that addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and that is consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

Acme Health must develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate the implementation of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and the associated assessment, authorization, and monitoring controls.

Acme Health must designate an [Assignment: organization-defined official] to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures.
[NIST 800-53 CA-1 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE CA-1 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events], and review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring procedures [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] and following [Assignment: organization-defined events].

Acme Health must review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events, and review and update the assessment, authorization, and monitoring procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events.

Acme Health must implement reasonable and appropriate policies and procedures to comply with the standards, implementation specifications, or other requirements of this subpart, taking into account those factors specified in § 164.306(b)(2)(i), (ii), (iii), and (iv).
Acme Health must implement policies and procedures to prevent, detect, contain, and correct security violations.

Acme Health must maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with this subpart in written (which may be electronic) form, and maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment required by this subpart to be documented.
Acme Health must retain the documentation required by paragraph (b)(1) for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
Acme Health must make documentation available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.
Acme Health must review documentation periodically, and update as needed, in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of the electronic protected health information.
Acme Health must categorize the system and information it processes, stores, and transmits.
[NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health must document the security categorization results, including supporting rationale, in the security plan for the system.
[NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health must verify that the authorizing official or authorizing official designated representative reviews and approves the security categorization decision.
[NIST 800-53 RA-2 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-2 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must conduct a risk assessment, including: (1) identifying threats to and vulnerabilities in the system; (2) determining the likelihood and magnitude of harm from unauthorized access, use, disclosure, disruption, modification, or destruction of the system, the information it processes, stores, or transmits, and any related information; and (3) determining the likelihood and impact of adverse effects on individuals arising from the processing of personally identifiable information.
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of electronic protected health information held by the covered entity or business associate.
Acme Health must integrate risk assessment results and risk management decisions from the organization and mission or business process perspectives with system-level risk assessments.
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must document risk assessment results in security and privacy plans, risk assessment report, and any additional organization-defined documents.
Acme Health must review risk assessment results [Assignment: organization-defined frequency].
Acme Health must review risk assessment results at least every one (1) year or when a significant change occurs.
Acme Health must disseminate risk assessment results to [Assignment: organization-defined personnel or roles].
[NIST 800-53 RA-3 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE RA-3 AE Mandatory]

Acme Health must update the risk assessment [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] or when there are significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact the security or privacy state of the system.

Acme Health must update the risk assessment at least every three (3) years at a minimum or when there are significant changes to the system, its environment of operation, or other conditions that may impact the security or privacy state of the system.
Acme Health must use all-source intelligence to assist in the analysis of risk.

Acme Health must implement security measures sufficient to reduce risks and vulnerabilities to a reasonable and appropriate level to comply with § 164.306(a).
Acme Health must respond to findings from security and privacy assessments, monitoring, and audits in accordance with organizational risk tolerance.

All system components within the CMS Authority to Connect (ATC) / Request to Connect (RTC) boundary are considered critical, and all system components within the CMS State AE Authority to Connect (ATC) or the other ARC-AMPE User's Request to Connect (RTC) boundary are considered critical.

Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (for example, fire, vandalism, system failure, and natural disaster) that damages systems that contain electronic protected health information.
Acme Health must establish and implement procedures to create and maintain retrievable exact copies of electronic protected health information.
Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) procedures to restore any loss of data.

Acme Health must establish (and implement as needed) procedures to enable continuation of critical business processes for protection of the security of electronic protected health information while operating in emergency mode.
Acme Health must implement procedures for periodic testing and revision of contingency plans.
Acme Health must assess the relative criticality of specific applications and data in support of other contingency plan components.
Acme Health must select the appropriate assessor or assessment team for the type of assessment to be conducted.

Acme Health must assess the controls in the system and its environment of operation as specified in the supplemental control requirements & guidance to determine the extent to which the controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome with respect to meeting established security and privacy requirements.

A complete independent assessment of all security and privacy controls must be conducted over a three (3) year period by: (a) undergoing a full controls assessment at the end of the ATC lifespan and delivering the complete and final ATC package no less than ninety (90) days prior to the ATC's expiration; or (b) undergoing independent assessments of the annually required controls designated by CMS for years one (1), two (2), and three (3) such that all ARC-AMPE controls are assessed within the three (3) year period and delivering the complete and final ATC package no less than ninety (90) days prior to expiration; or (c) by responding to CMS guidance on what, if any, documents or independent testing must be completed for each significant system change based on CMS' determination of any impact to the ATC.
Acme Health must produce a control assessment report that documents the results of the assessment.
[NIST 800-53 CA-2 Low, Moderate, High | FedRAMP CA-2 | ARC-AMPE CA-2 AE Mandatory]
Acme Health must provide the results of the control assessment to [Assignment: organization-defined individuals or roles].
Acme Health must provide the results of the control assessment to individuals or roles to include FedRAMP and agency customers.

Acme Health must employ independent assessors or assessment teams approved by the organization's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or equivalent to conduct control assessments.

Acme Health must leverage the results of control assessments performed by any FedRAMP Recognized independent assessment service when the assessment meets organization-defined requirements.

Acme Health must develop a plan of action and milestones for the system to document the planned remediation actions of the organization to correct weaknesses or deficiencies noted during the assessment of the controls and to reduce or eliminate known vulnerabilities in the system.

Acme Health must update existing plan of action and milestones [Assignment: organization-defined frequency] based on the findings from control assessments, independent audits or reviews, and continuous monitoring activities.

Acme Health must ensure that the authorizing official for common controls authorizes the use of those controls for inheritance by organizational systems.

Acme Health must follow the FedRAMP Continuous Collaborative Monitoring, Significant Change Notification, Vulnerability Detection and Response, and Vulnerability Evaluation and Reporting rules when implementing continuous monitoring.
Acme Health must employ independent assessors or assessment teams to monitor the controls in the system on an ongoing basis.

This standard establishes the mandatory requirements for configuration management policy, baseline configuration, and configuration change control at Example Org.
It applies to all systems, devices, appliances, and applications owned or operated by Example Org, throughout the system life cycle.
Platform Engineering is accountable for this process and its handoffs end to end; other teams named in this document participate in individual steps but do not own the process.

- **Platform Engineering** owns the change and configuration management process end to end, including baseline maintenance, change review and approval workflow, drift monitoring, and evidence production.
- **The Change Control Board**, convened and chaired by Platform Engineering, reviews and decides configuration-controlled changes.
It must include security and privacy representatives, which may include Information System Security Officers, Chief Information Security Officers, and/or the Senior Official for Privacy.
- **The designated official** for configuration management policy is designated by Platform Engineering and named in the appropriate security and privacy documents.
- **System owners and business owners** participate as required by the change coordination and communication requirements in Section 5.

- Platform Engineering shall develop, document, and disseminate a configuration management policy to organization-defined personnel or roles at the organization level (as required by ARC-AMPE) and/or the mission/business process and system levels.

The policy shall address purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and shall be consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
- Platform Engineering shall develop, document, and disseminate procedures that facilitate implementation of the configuration management policy and the associated configuration management controls.

- The configuration management policy and procedures shall support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and for the information on the system.
- Example Org shall follow the FedRAMP Significant Change Notification rules for configuration management policy and procedures.
- Platform Engineering shall review and update the configuration management policy and procedures at least every one (1) year, and following organization-defined trigger events.

- Trigger events include, per ARC-AMPE: assessment or audit findings; security or privacy incidents; and changes to applicable laws (including privacy laws), executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.
- Example Org shall actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws and regulations that affect configuration management policies.

- The policies and procedures implemented to comply with the HIPAA Security Rule, and any written (which may be electronic) record of an action, activity, or assessment required to be documented, shall be maintained in written (which may be electronic) form.
- That documentation shall be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date it was last in effect, whichever is later.
- The documentation shall be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which it pertains.
- The documentation shall be reviewed periodically and updated as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.

- Platform Engineering shall develop, document, and maintain under configuration control a current baseline configuration of the system, applicable to all systems, devices, appliances, and applications and including security updates.

- Platform Engineering shall review and update the baseline configuration at least every one (1) year; when required due to major system changes/upgrades, critical security patches, and/or emergency changes (e.g., unscheduled changes, system crashes, replacement of critical hardware components); and when system components are installed or upgraded.
- Platform Engineering shall maintain the currency, completeness, accuracy, and availability of the baseline configuration using organization-defined automated mechanisms.
Access controls shall be configured so the automation has the information it needs, and the automated mechanisms shall run as part of the Continuous Monitoring Program.
Examples of such mechanisms include hardware asset management systems, software asset management systems, and centralized configuration management software.

- Platform Engineering shall retain at least one (1) previous version of baseline configurations — the most recent older generation — to support situations such as emergency rollback; additional previous versions may be retained based on risk tolerance.

- Platform Engineering shall maintain a baseline configuration for system development and test environments that is managed separately from the operational baseline configuration, and shall provide separate environments for system development and testing to minimize risk to operational systems.

- Example Org shall issue organization-defined systems or system components with organization-defined configurations to individuals traveling to locations the organization deems to be of significant risk, and shall apply organization-defined controls to those systems or components when the individuals return from travel.

Issued systems and components shall carry stringent configurations (e.g., latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption); return safeguards may include detailed inspection for physical tampering, purging, or reimaging the hard disk drive/removable media.
The configuration change control process operates on a continuous basis.
Platform Engineering shall: - Determine and document the types of changes to the system that are configuration-controlled.
- Review proposed configuration-controlled changes and approve or disapprove them with explicit consideration for security and privacy impact analyses.
- Document configuration change decisions associated with the system.
- Implement approved configuration-controlled changes to the system.
- Retain records of configuration-controlled changes for no less than one (1) year after the change.
- Monitor and review activities associated with configuration-controlled changes to the system.

- Platform Engineering shall coordinate and provide oversight for configuration change control activities through the Change Control Board, which convenes sufficiently frequently to accommodate proposed change requests.

Change requests shall be submitted on change request forms approved by the Change Control Board, and the requirements of other appropriate organization officials shall be satisfied when configuration change control activities occur.

- Security and privacy representatives (which may include Information System Security Officers, Chief Information Security Officers, and/or the Senior Official for Privacy) shall be members of the Change Control Board.
- Platform Engineering shall test, validate, and document changes to the system before finalizing the implementation of the changes.
- Platform Engineering shall implement changes to the current system baseline and deploy the updated baseline across the installed base using organization-defined automated mechanisms.

- Proposed changes shall be documented in the [Ticketing System], which shall be used to notify approval authorities and request approval, highlight proposed changes not approved or disapproved within [Approval Time Period], prohibit changes until designated approvals are received, document all changes, and notify organization-defined personnel when approved changes are completed.
Each change ticket must capture its approvals; these change tickets with approvals constitute required evidence of the process.
- Platform Engineering shall implement organization-defined security responses automatically if baseline configurations are changed in an unauthorized manner.
Platform Engineering shall produce and retain a baseline configuration and drift report as evidence of baseline monitoring and unauthorized-change detection.
- Cryptographic mechanisms used to provide organization-defined controls shall be under configuration management.

- Platform Engineering shall review changes to the system at the organization-defined frequency or when organization-defined circumstances occur to determine whether unauthorized changes have occurred.

- Platform Engineering shall establish a means of communicating significant changes to or developments in the information system or environment of operations that may affect business agreements/contracts with CMS and business partners and services to the business owner and associated service consumers (e.g., electronic bulletin board or web status page).
The means of communication shall be approved and accepted by the system owner.
Example Org shall follow CMS change reporting procedures and utilize the CMS change notification form for the specific entity type.

analyze: This Standard defines the requirements for measuring, evaluating, and tracking the risks and trustworthiness characteristics of AI systems at Acme Health.
It applies to all AI systems developed, deployed, or operated by Acme Health, across the AI lifecycle from pre-deployment evaluation through production monitoring.
The requirements in this Standard are drawn from the NIST AI Risk Management Framework (AI RMF) Measure function.

The AI / ML Engineering team is accountable for the AI evaluation and measurement process end to end, including the selection and application of metrics, the execution and documentation of evaluations, the tracking of identified risks, and the handoffs between evaluation activities and other teams.

Domain experts, end users, AI actors external to the developing or deploying team, affected communities, and subject-matter specialists (for example, in privacy, security, human factors, and socio-technical analysis) participate in individual evaluation steps as specified in the sections below, but AI / ML Engineering owns the process and answers for its outcomes.

Appropriate methods and metrics for measuring AI risks must be identified and applied by AI / ML Engineering, with approaches and metrics for the risks enumerated during the Map function selected for implementation starting with the most significant AI risks.
[NIST AI RMF Measure 1 | NIST AI RMF Measure 1.1]
AI risks or trustworthiness characteristics that will not — or cannot — be measured must be properly documented by AI / ML Engineering.

Internal experts who did not serve as front-line developers for the system and/or independent assessors must be involved by AI / ML Engineering in regular assessments and updates, with domain experts, users, AI actors external to the developing or deploying team, and affected communities consulted as necessary per organizational risk tolerance.

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Measure 1.3, utilizing separate testing teams to enable independent decisions and course-correction for AI systems with tracked processes and documented change in performance, planning and evaluating AI system prototypes with end user populations early and continuously in the AI lifecycle, assessing the independence and stature of TEVV and oversight AI actors to ensure they have the required levels of independence and resources, and evaluating the effectiveness of external stakeholder feedback mechanisms for eliciting, evaluating, and integrating input from diverse groups.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.3 Action 6]

NIST suggests, among its 12 actions for Measure 1.1, establishing approaches for detecting, tracking and measuring known risks, errors, incidents or negative impacts, identifying testing procedures and metrics to demonstrate whether the system is fit for purpose and functioning as claimed and to demonstrate AI system trustworthiness, defining acceptable limits for system performance with course-correction suggestions when the system performs beyond those limits, documenting metric selection criteria including considered but unused metrics, and documenting risks or trustworthiness characteristics identified in the Map function that will not be measured, including justification for non-measurement.

[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 8 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 1.1 Action 12]
AI systems must be evaluated for trustworthy characteristics by AI / ML Engineering.
Test sets, metrics, and details about the tools used during TEVV must be documented by AI / ML Engineering.

NIST suggests, among its 3 actions for Measure 2.1, leveraging existing industry best practices for transparency and documentation of all possible aspects of measurements, such as data sheets for data sets and model cards, regularly assessing the effectiveness of the tools used to document measurement approaches, test sets, metrics, processes and materials, and updating those tools as needed.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.1 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.1 Action 3]
Evaluations involving human subjects must meet applicable requirements, including human subject protection, and must be representative of the relevant population.

NIST suggests, among its 8 actions for Measure 2.2, following human subjects research requirements established by organizational and disciplinary requirements, including informed consent and compensation, during dataset collection activities, analyzing differences between the intended and actual population of users or data subjects including likelihood for errors, incidents or negative impacts, utilizing disaggregated evaluation methods (for example by race, age, gender, ethnicity, ability, region) to improve AI system performance in real-world settings, and evaluating data representativeness through investigating known failure modes, assessing data quality and diverse sourcing, applying public benchmarks, traditional bias testing, chaos engineering, and stakeholder feedback.

NIST suggests, among its 9 actions for Measure 2.3, measuring AI systems prior to deployment in conditions similar to expected scenarios, measuring and documenting performance criteria such as validity (false positive rate, false negative rate) and efficiency (training times, prediction latency) related to ground truth within the deployment context of use, measuring assurance criteria such as AI actor competency and experience, and documenting differences between the measurement setting and the deployment environment(s).

[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 4 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 6 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 2.9 Action 11]

[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.2 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.2 Action 3]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 3.3, measuring efficacy of end user and operator error reporting processes, categorizing and analyzing the type and rate of end user appeal requests and results, measuring feedback activity participation rates and awareness of feedback activity availability, and analyzing end user and community feedback in close collaboration with domain experts.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 3.3 Action 6]

Measurement approaches for identifying AI risks must be connected to deployment context(s) and informed through consultation with domain experts and other end users, with the approaches documented by AI / ML Engineering.

Measurement results regarding AI system trustworthiness in deployment context(s) and across the AI lifecycle must be informed by input from domain experts and relevant AI actors to validate whether the system is performing consistently as intended, with the results documented by AI / ML Engineering.

Measurable performance improvements or declines — based on consultations with relevant AI actors, including affected communities, and field data about context-relevant risks and trustworthiness characteristics — must be identified and documented by AI / ML Engineering.

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 4.1, supporting mechanisms for capturing feedback from system end users — including domain experts, operators, and practitioners — conducted in settings where end users are able to openly share their doubts and insights about AI system output in connection to their specific context of use, identifying and documenting approaches for evaluating and integrating elicited feedback in collaboration with human-factors and socio-technical domain experts to actively inform continual improvement, and identifying and implementing approaches to measure effectiveness and satisfaction with end user elicitation techniques and documenting results.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 2 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.1 Action 6]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 4.2, integrating feedback from end users, operators, and affected individuals and communities as inputs to assess AI system trustworthiness characteristics and ensuring both positive and negative feedback is assessed, evaluating feedback regarding end user satisfaction with, and confidence in, AI system performance including whether output is considered valid and reliable and explainable and interpretable, and measuring the frequency of AI systems' override decisions, evaluating and documenting results, and feeding insights back into continual improvement processes.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.2 Action 5]

NIST suggests, among its 6 actions for Measure 4.3, developing baseline quantitative measures for trustworthy characteristics, utilizing qualitative approaches to augment and complement quantitative baseline measures in close coordination with impact assessment, human factors and socio-technical AI actors, and performing and documenting sensitivity analysis to characterize actual and expected variance in performance after applying system or procedural updates.
[NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.3 Action 1 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.3 Action 3 | NIST AI RMF Playbook Measure 4.3 Action 5]

This Standard establishes the requirements for the processing, transparency, minimization, sharing, retention, quality management, and inventory of personally identifiable information (PII) and protected health information (PHI) at Example Org.
Data Governance is accountable for this process end to end, including all handoffs to participating teams.
All personnel and roles identified by Data Governance must comply with this Standard.

Data Governance must develop, document, and disseminate to organization-defined personnel and roles a personally identifiable information (PII) processing and transparency policy at the organization level (NIST also permits mission/business process-level and system-level policies).

The policy must address purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination among organizational entities, and compliance, and must be consistent with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines.

Data Governance must develop, document, and disseminate procedures to facilitate implementation of the PII processing and transparency policy and the associated PII processing and transparency controls.
Data Governance must designate an organization-defined official to manage the development, documentation, and dissemination of the PII processing and transparency policy and procedures.
These officials must be named in the appropriate security and privacy documents.

Data Governance must review and update the current PII processing and transparency policy and procedures at least every one (1) year and following organization-defined events (e.g., assessment or audit findings, security or privacy incidents, breaches, or changes to applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and guidelines).
Data Governance must actively monitor for changes to applicable privacy laws, regulations, and overarching policy that affect these policies.

The PII processing and transparency policies and procedures must support cybersecurity and privacy safeguards to the greatest extent feasible throughout the system's life cycle and the information on that system.

- Data Governance must maintain the policies and procedures implemented to comply with the rule in written (which may be electronic) form, and must maintain a written (which may be electronic) record of any action, activity, or assessment that the rule requires to be documented.
- Required documentation must be retained for 6 years from the date of its creation or the date when it last was in effect, whichever is later.
- The documentation must be made available to those persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

- Data Governance must review the documentation periodically and update it as needed in response to environmental or operational changes affecting the security of electronic protected health information.
Data Governance must determine and document the organization-defined authority that permits the organization-defined processing of PII.
Personnel must consult with the senior agency official for privacy and legal counsel regarding such authority, particularly where multiple jurisdictions or sources of authority apply.

The organization-defined processing of PII must be restricted to only that which is authorized, including through training personnel on authorized processing and monitoring and auditing organizational use of PII.

Policies and procedures regarding the creation, collection, use, and disclosure of PII must, at a minimum, be documented and available to appropriate authorities upon request, and must identify the applicable law governing collection, use, and disclosure of PII.
[ARC-AMPE PT-2 AE Mandatory | ARC-AMPE PT-3 AE Mandatory]
Data tags containing the organization-defined authorized processing must be attached to organization-defined elements of PII.
Enforcement of the authorized processing of PII must be managed using organization-defined automated mechanisms ([Automated Mechanism]).
Data Governance must identify and document the organization-defined purpose(s) for processing PII.

The processing purpose(s) must be described in the organization's public privacy notices and policies and in related privacy compliance documentation, such as privacy impact assessments and system of records notices.
The organization-defined processing of PII must be restricted to only that which is compatible with the identified purpose(s).
Changes in PII processing must be monitored, and organization-defined mechanisms must be implemented to ensure that any changes are made in accordance with organization-defined requirements.

Per ARC-AMPE, authorized purposes for processing PII in accordance with the ACA include determining eligibility for enrollment in a qualified health plan, determining eligibility for other insurance affordability programs (as defined in 45 CFR §155.300), and determining eligibility for exemptions from the individual shared responsibility provisions in Code section 5000A.

Per ARC-AMPE, the Exchange may only use or disclose such PII to the extent necessary to carry out functions described in 45 CFR §155.200; other functions the Secretary determines to be in compliance with the ACA and for which the individual provides consent; or other functions pursuant to the substantive and procedural requirements in 45 CFR §155.260(a)(iii).
Data tags containing the organization-defined processing purposes must be attached to organization-defined elements of PII.
Processing purposes of PII must be tracked using organization-defined automated mechanisms ([Automated Mechanism]).

Authorized users must be enabled to determine whether access authorizations assigned to a sharing partner match the information's access and use restrictions for organization-defined information-sharing circumstances.

ARC-AMPE scopes this to circumstances where user discretion is required, as defined in data sharing agreements such as Computer Matching Agreements or Information Exchange Agreements, and consistent with 45 CFR §155.260(e).
[NIST 800-53 AC-21 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-21 AE Mandatory]
Organization-defined automated mechanisms — or, per ARC-AMPE, manual processes — must be employed to assist users in making information-sharing and collaboration decisions.
[NIST 800-53 AC-21 Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE AC-21 AE Mandatory]
PII may only be shared when authorized, there is a need to know, and adequate assurances of protection have been provided.

Information search and retrieval services ([Information Search and Retrieval Service]) must be implemented that enforce organization-defined information-sharing restrictions.

Information within the system and information output from the system must be managed and retained in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, guidelines, and operational requirements, covering the full information life cycle.
Data Governance must record the applicable retention requirements for each data category in the Retention schedule.
[NIST 800-53 SI-12 Low, Moderate, High | ARC-AMPE SI-12 AE Mandatory]

System output — including but not limited to audit records, system reports, business and financial reports, and business records — must be retained for ten (10) years (per 45 CFR §155.1210 and 45 CFR §156.705) or in accordance with organizational policy; NARA policy applies to the retention of federal data held by Enrollment Partners.

For systems processing, storing, or transmitting protected health information (PHI), the following must be documented and retained for at least six (6) years from creation or last effective date, whichever is later: [ARC-AMPE SI-12 AE Mandatory | HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(i)] - Decisions regarding addressable implementation specifications (including why a particular implementation specification would not be reasonable and appropriate); - A user's right of access to a workstation, transaction, program, or process; - Security incidents and their outcomes; - Satisfactory assurances that a business associate will appropriately safeguard PHI (recorded in a written contract or other arrangement meeting business associate agreement requirements, with documented attempts and reasons if satisfactory assurances cannot be obtained); - Repairs and modifications to physical components of a facility related to security (e.g., hardware, walls, doors, locks); - Changes to organizational policies and procedures.
[ARC-AMPE SI-12 AE Mandatory | HIPAA Security Rule 164.316(b)(2)(i)]
The PII being processed in the information life cycle must be limited to the minimum PII elements necessary to accomplish the legally authorized purpose of collection (organization-defined elements).

Organization-defined techniques — in accordance with organizational standards and applicable federal and state laws and regulations — must be used to minimize the use of PII for research, testing, or training.
The creation, collection, use, and/or disclosure of PII must be limited only to the extent necessary to accomplish a specified and authorized purpose(s).

If PII is used in the test environment, the same controls required for systems containing PII must be applied to the test environment, and synthetic PII must be used to the maximum extent practicable when testing system functionality.
The senior official for privacy must approve the use of PII in testing, training, and research; using synthetic or de-identified data is preferred.
Organization-defined techniques must be used to dispose of, destroy, or erase information following the retention period, in a manner that prevents loss, theft, misuse, or unauthorized access.
The latest published NIST SP 800-88, *Guidelines for Media Sanitization*, must be referred to for guidance on information disposal techniques.
The latest published FIPS 140-compliant encryption standards must be used to ensure secure deletion or destruction of PII (including originals, copies, and archived records).
The accuracy, relevance, timeliness, and completeness of PII must be checked across the information life cycle at least every one (1) year.
Data Governance owns this review and must record its results in the Data inventory and classification register.
Inaccurate or outdated PII must be corrected or deleted.

An individual's record must be maintained in accordance with the Retention schedule regardless of that individual's activity or inactivity; correcting or deleting inaccurate data does not violate retention rules provided a log of those changes is maintained.

PII that is inaccurate or outdated, incorrectly determined regarding impact, or incorrectly de-identified must be corrected or deleted using organization-defined automated mechanisms ([Automated Mechanism]).
Data tags must be employed to automate the correction or deletion of PII across the information life cycle within organizational systems.
PII must be collected directly from the individual.

PII must be corrected or deleted upon request by individuals or their designated representatives, noting that organizations may not be permitted to delete certain PII regardless of an individual's preference.
Organization-defined recipients of PII and the individuals whose PII has been corrected or deleted must be notified.
If an individual requests deletion of PII that the organization is legally required to maintain, that reason must be communicated in the denial of the individual's request.
Data Governance must develop and update an inventory of organizational systems at least every one (1) year or when there is a significant change to the inventory.
This inventory must be maintained as the Data inventory and classification register.

Data Governance must establish, maintain, and update — continuously or when there is a significant change to the systems, applications, and projects involved (organization-defined frequency) — an inventory of all systems, applications, and projects that process PII.
This inventory must be maintained in the Data inventory and classification register.
The policies and procedures required by PM-1 must include operational guidance for compliance with the PII inventory control.

Data Governance must produce and maintain the following evidence artifacts in support of this Standard: - **Data inventory and classification register** — maintained under Sections 9.1, 10.1, and 10.2, recording organizational systems, applications, and projects that process PII, their classification, and the results of annual PII quality reviews. - **Retention schedule** — maintained under Section 6.1, recording the applicable retention requirements for each data category across the full information life cycle.

All documentation and records required by this Standard must be maintained in written (which may be electronic) form, retained in accordance with Sections 2.6, 6.2, and 6.3, and made available to the persons responsible for implementing the procedures to which the documentation pertains.

analyze: This Standard establishes requirements for the governance, risk management, operational oversight, and lifecycle management of artificial intelligence (AI) systems deployed or under development at Acme Health.
This Standard applies the NIST AI Risk Management Framework to ensure AI systems achieve their intended purposes while managing risks to patients, staff, and organizational operations.
This Standard applies to all AI systems developed, procured, deployed, or operated by Acme Health, including AI components embedded in clinical, administrative, or operational systems.
This Standard applies to all personnel involved in the specification, development, deployment, operation, monitoring, or decommissioning of AI systems.

Before an AI system proceeds to production deployment or to the next stage of development, a determination must be made as to whether the AI system achieves its intended purposes and stated objectives and whether its development or deployment should proceed.
This determination must be documented and retained as part of the AI system's governance record.
Treatment of documented AI risks must be prioritized based on impact, likelihood, and available resources or methods.
The prioritization methodology must be documented and applied consistently across all AI systems within scope of this Standard.
Responses to high-priority AI risks must be developed, planned, and documented, with risk response options including mitigating, transferring, avoiding, or accepting.

Each documented response plan must identify: - The specific risk being addressed - The selected response option (mitigate, transfer, avoid, or accept) - Actions to be taken - Responsible parties - Success criteria
Negative residual risks (defined as the sum of all unmitigated risks) to both downstream acquirers of AI systems and end users must be documented.
This documentation must be made available to relevant AI actors, including downstream acquirers and representatives of affected end-user communities.
Risk treatments, response and recovery plans, and communication plans for identified and measured AI risks must be documented and monitored regularly.
Resources required to manage AI risks must be taken into account, along with viable non-AI alternative systems, approaches, or methods, to reduce the magnitude or likelihood of potential impacts.
The alternatives assessment must be documented and included in the planning materials for any proposed AI system deployment or major modification.
Mechanisms must be in place and applied to sustain the value of deployed AI systems.
These mechanisms must address ongoing verification that the AI system continues to meet its intended purposes and业objectives as operational conditions and data distributions change over time.

Mechanisms must be in place and applied, and responsibilities must be assigned and understood, to supersede, disengage, or deactivate AI systems that demonstrate performance or outcomes inconsistent with intended use.

The deactivation procedures must include: - Criteria for determining when performance or outcomes are inconsistent with intended use - Authority and decision-making process for deactivation - Communication requirements to affected users and stakeholders - Procedures for transitioning to alternative processes or systems - Documentation requirements
Procedures must be followed to respond to and recover from a previously unknown risk when it is identified.
These procedures must be documented and accessible to personnel responsible for AI system operations.

Post-deployment AI system monitoring plans must be implemented, including mechanisms for capturing and evaluating input from users and other relevant AI actors, appeal and override, decommissioning, incident response, recovery, and change management.
Each deployed AI system must have a documented monitoring plan that addresses all elements listed above.

The monitoring plan must establish mechanisms for: - Capturing input from system users - Capturing input from other relevant AI actors - Evaluating captured input for potential risks, performance issues, or improvement opportunities
Incidents and errors must be communicated to relevant AI actors, including affected communities.
Communication must occur through [Communication Channel] and must include sufficient detail for affected parties to understand the nature and potential impact of the incident or error.
Processes for tracking, responding to, and recovering from incidents and errors must be followed and documented.
All incidents and errors related to AI systems must be recorded in [Incident Tracking System].

The record must include: - Description of the incident or error - Date and time of occurrence - Affected AI system(s) - Impact to users or operations - Response actions taken - Recovery actions taken - Responsible personnel - Resolution status
Measurable activities for continual improvements must be integrated into AI system updates and include regular engagement with interested parties, including relevant AI actors.
These activities must be planned and tracked as part of the AI system's lifecycle management process.
Engagement with interested parties must occur at [Review Frequency] and must be documented.
Responsibilities for the activities described in this Standard must be assigned and documented.

At minimum, the following roles must be explicitly assigned for each AI system: - AI System Owner: accountable for the AI system's performance and compliance with this Standard - Risk Manager: responsible for risk assessment, prioritization, and treatment planning - Operations Manager: responsible for day-to-day monitoring and incident response - Deactivation Authority: authorized to supersede, disengage, or deactivate the AI system

All documentation required by this Standard must be retained for [Retention Period] and must be accessible to personnel responsible for AI system governance, compliance audits, and post-incident analysis.
